title: Better Than The Competition - But!
text:
First let me say that I've owned a lot of routers over the years (Belkin, DLink, Lnksys/Cisco, Netgear) and generally speaking I prefer Belkin for their ease-of-use and overall value for the dollar. I have a "mixed" network with both wired & wireless devices. I have a network-attached-storage (NAS) unit and frequently stream both movies and music; plus my phone service is a voice-over-Internet phone system. Dependability and speed are the two most important things I look for in a router. I do not do online/network gaming and cannot speak to that environment.

Things I Like:

All the basic functions are there for the average user plus a couple of features you don't necessarily see on the competition. Self healing is one such function. Basically, routers (any network device really) benefit from a periodic "restart/reset" a few times a month. The Belkin allows you to schedule that restart to automatically occur (say, in the middle of the night). Nice!. Belkin also employs the staefull-packet-inspection methodology for inbound transmissions which is an added level of protection from hackers. Some but not all of the competition does. Coverage is good for an internal antenna router. My environment has a single-level 2000 square ft. footprint and the signal strength is full "N" in all locations. My network also registers with usable strength for neighbors within a few hundred feet (no, they don't actually use my network).

Setup is extremely easy and you do not have to use the supplied software if you don't want to. I set mine up manually in about 15 minutes. A non-confusing interface with "help-bubbles" has always been a Belkin strength. For the most part (in a simple setup) you really don't have to do much other than plug it in and setup your wireless password & network name.

For those that require fast LAN speed (ie: non-wireless), this router is faster than several more expensive routers I've compared it to. Since I frequently stream movies over the network this was an important consideration. Streaming movies (wireless or wired) while others surf the net, talk on the phone, or use smartphone features is becoming an everyday requirement for multi-user households and the Belkin's seem to handle things pretty well.

Things Belkin Could Have Done Better:

These items may not matter to you, and they don't necessarily constitute a show-stopper. I like the N450 and it meets my immediate needs but I thought they deserve mention (nothing's perfect, right?). Maybe in the future Belkin will address them.

The N450 has a single diagnostic light as opposed to the multiple lights on previous Belkin models. I can't believe these would add anymore than a few dollars to the cost and they are a valuable addition for troubleshooting. If the thinking was "simpler is better", it is definitely not in cases of providing adequate performance indicators for troubleshooting. Belkin needs to spring for a couple more LED's.

I haven't found a way to reserve IP addresses for a specific device. Reserving addresses for network printers & some NAS units is a valuable tool in setting up a complex network. There are ways around it for the most part but it can be time consuming. Previous Belkin routers had this feature and its removal is a mystery to me.

In comparing the N450 to the more feature-laden N600, I find it curious that the N450 has Gigabit LAN ports and the pricier N600 does not. Normally you don't see features removed as the price goes up. Belkin Marketing needs to take another look it's targeted user base. I doubt most users needing faster wireless speeds would be willing to put up with slower LAN speeds for that benefit.

All things considered:

The N450 is a great value router for those that need good wireless coverage and very fast wired speeds for an affordable price. If you're seeking the fastest wireless speeds, have a multilevel house, or do not have a need for Gigabit LAN speeds, the N600 would be a better alternative. The N600 has 2 additional wireless antennas which make it a better wireless performer. The N450 with the Gigabit ports strikes a better balance for those that are both wired & wireless.

title: No Problems At All
text:
I have two of the 2TB Seagate GoFlex Desk USB 3.0 drives. One was an earlier USB 2.0 drive that has been converted to a 3.0 via the Seagate GoFlex Adapter, and one purchased initially as a 3.0 drive.

In both cases, I have been very happy with performance. Although external drives will never be as fast as internal drives, they do have their advantages in terms of flexibility & portability - and for most applications are more than fast enough for their intended purpose. In my case, that purpose was streaming (or accessing) DVD, Bluray, and music files across a home network. I also use a Netgear NAS with internal Seagate drives for the same purpose and the speeds via the external Seagate's are much, much faster (obviously processor speed of the NAS vs. my laptop is a factor).

The converted (2.0 to 3.0) drive was benchmarking 28MB/sec before the conversion and 132MB/sec afterwards (4.7X greater). The recently purchased 3.0 drive was similar with a speed of 142MB/sec. Cached speeds between 2.0 & 3.0 USB showed about a 5.4X speed bump. Will you realize the "10X faster than 2.0 USB" advertised bump? Not a chance. Is a 5X bump worth the move? You bet, and in my opinion well-worth the relatively small cost premium. Across my wired network (or directly attached to a PC/Laptop), this has been more than enough for seamless playback of everything I've thrown at it.

I haven't looked inside either case but assume both drives are 5400rpm or 5900rpm. Some of the complaints about speed between different brands could be related to the rotational speed differences (say 7200 vs. 5400/5900); or on-board cache. Although not in all cases, both faster RPM and larger cache size can involve more noise, more heat, and greater expense. Pretty much everything's a trade-off so decide what your priorities are. I'm willing to trade-off raw speed (not needed in my case) for reduced noise and heat but understand completely that some may not.

Several of the reviews mention image backup problems. Some were MAC-related so I can comment on those. It is possible something else is going on for those people experiencing PC backup issues. Chipset, OS, partitioning, and imaging software all come into play. Modern equipment and software should be comfortable with traditional 512/512e and 4096 sector drives. All I can say is that on my Windows 7 HP laptop & Dell desktop (plus my Gateway XP laptop), making system image backups work perfectly for me. The statement that you cannot make image backups on a Windows 7 PC is simply not true.

In summary, personally I'm happy (so far) with the Seagate external drives. I also have Western Digital internal/external drives and they work well also. I do find all the included software (backup, Dashboards, etc.) to be pretty lame so I never install any of it. There are much better alternatives, free and otherwise.

text:
Since there are a huge number of reviews that go over the details, I'll just quickly comment on my experience. I've had JBOD and NAS units in the past and am very comfortable with anything having to do with computers / electronics. My goal with this unit was to consolidate three external drives (1 Seagate, 2 Toshiba) into 1one box. They each seemed to have different spin down settings plus the wall-wart issue was becoming a pain. NAS units have too much overhead for what I needed. I have several hundred movies (DVD + Bluray + Music) I stream throughout the house so I just needed a little consolidation before adding more drives.

The box is fairly well constructed. Others have commented on the flimsy front door but I don't see that as a problem. After you get the drives in you never touch the door anyway. It doesn't rattle at all. The box & inner door are all metal and the drives fit snugly. The power supply is better than most boxes in this price range. The lights are probably a little brighter than they need to be but I have mine in my office so it's never a distraction when I'm watching TV. I do like the fact that each drive has an LED that blinks during activity. The buttons have a nice, firm feel.

The Orange / Blue sync modes are well-documented here so I won't comment except to say I use the Orange setting so it syncs with my PC's sleep mode. Works fine - sleeps and wakes up with the computer. I do occasionally power the box down when I'm not working with the movie stuff. There are some comments about fan noise. It is definitely there but I did find that removing the fan shield quiets it down quite a bit. I run the fan on low but just as an experiment I turned the fan off and copied a few hundred Gigabytes back & forth between all the drives (several hours) and the drives never got very warm. I think the metal case may act as a heat sink. Anyway, on low speed the exhaust air is always cool even with multiple drive activity. Can't see any reason to run the fan on Auto, High, or Medium. Low is all you need and you may be able to get away with OFF. Replacing the fan with a higher quality quieter one would be extremely easy as it's a standard 80cm PC fan held in by 4 screws.

WARNING: IF your existing drives are MBR-type and 2TB or less in size, they should just plug in and all your data will be fine. IF your drive(s) are 3TB or 4TB they should be GPT-type (or have partitions 2TB or less). This box does NOT seem to like a 3TB or 4TB MBR partitions plugged into it and you may very well lose your data. Mixed drive types & sizes are fine. I am currently running a Seagate 2TB, Toshiba 2TB, Toshiba 3TB, and a WD 500GB. All are formatted NTFS with the 3TB defined as a GPT single partition

I'm running mine via USB 3.0 so can't comment on the eSATA. I think it's nice they give you cables for both. I'm easily hitting read speeds in the 125 - 130 range with write speeds slightly less. Obviously it's slower if you are going drive-to-drive withing the box but overall I'm very happy with the speed. It's pretty much the same as my direct connect speeds.

So far I'm very happy with the Mediasonic. It may not be a 5-Star box in the sense that it's a "marvel of quality & features" and "beats everything out there" but on the other hand its fairly well-constructed, is a 4-bay - not a 2-bay, has USB 3.0/2.0 plus eSATA, includes cables for both, does not seem to degrade transfer speeds, and cost less than $100 (it seems to have jumped since I bought it). That's why it's a 5-Star box to me. It's all relative folks.

Heat / Noise - The NUC would save me desk space over the always-on laptop plus generate less heat, energy use, and noise.

Other - Most off-the-shelf computers have a lot of 3rd party add-ons & drivers (3.0 USB, video, useless support firmware, etc). I wanted a pure Intel configuration to start with.

I ordered the i5 version because I do a lot of video encoding plus the i5 has the Intel 5000 graphics instead of the 4400 graphics. I think the i3 version would be just fine for everyday use. I already had a Kingston 120GB SSD drive on the shelf so I went with the larger NUC that supports a standard 2.5-inch HDD or SSD. title: OK With A Couple Shortcomings
text:
I have the 2015 Roku 2 model and mostly use it for Amazon Prime watching. I also have an Amazon Firestick. As background, I run both through an A/V receiver, connected via a dual-band router to my cable provider (50+ download speeds). My TV is a 60" Panasonic Plasma. There are zero buffering issues with either device and the picture quality is excellent so it really boils down to interface preferences.

I specifically bought the Roku 2 because of the IR remote. I map all my remotes to an IR universal remotes so the RF-based Roku 3 wasn't an option. Supposedly the processor speed is the same for both. Firstly, I think the biggest drawback for me is the lagging response time with the Roku 2. This is especially apparent on the pause/play function, and especially problematic with the fast forward function. At first I assumed the supplied remote was underpowered so I tried several others. That moved it up to acceptable but not great. Perhaps the Roku 3 with RF would be better but to me at least, the problem appears to be the speed at which the processor acts on the command rather than the speed it receives it.

My only other "nitpick" is the Miracast and Android App from Roku. I have a year old LG G3 phone so it's pretty current. It's running Lollipop and has a Miracast function built in. I was unable to get screen mirroring to work. The phone see the Roku but the Roku seems to block/reject the connection. Not sure what's going on there. The Roku App works well for general control & search works great. It also streams music & pictures from the phone very well. Unfortunately it does not do video. Strange given that the Roku is primarily a video device. So unless I'm missing something, without Miracast & Roku App video streaming, the advertised "local content streaming" is extremely limited (for me, anyway).

In summary, the above two issues are not show-stoppers for most people, and my Amazon Fire does both so it's manageable for me. Regular streaming from Amazon, Hulu, Crackle, Vudu, etc. work fine. I would guess both drawbacks are addressable via firmware upgrades (although Roku should consider a better IR remote or stick to RF).

title: Incredible sound, easy set-up, and great features!
text: This Onkyo NR838 replaced an older Denon AVR-3805 in my home theater system. I was expecting the Onkyo to be far easier to set up than the older Denon (it was) but I was not expecting such a dramatic improvement in sound and functionality! Wow! I am an audiophile from way back and am very fussy about sound quality. I will leave it to others to detail each and every feature of this receiver. Let me just say that after you set this receiver up, using the excellent guided on-screen set-up menus, and the automatic speaker set-up using the supplied mic, hit the THX button and be prepared to be blown away. There may be better sounding receivers on the market, but I haven't heard any. Another favorite feature is the network connection (WiFi or hard-wired) which allows you to connect to lots of different Internet radio stations. If you're a Top 40 kind of person, you can skip this comment. So within minutes, using the "Tune-In" app on the receiver, I had found my favorite stations from RadioTunes, and from KEXP Seattle, KCSM San Mateo jazz, etc. The sound quality of these radio streams is excellent, and it's free. So if you are a music junkie like me, and you'd like to listen to radio stations from around the country or around the world, look no further. The only suggestion I'd have for Onkyo is that some kind of a backlit remote would be nice. The remote buttons are tiny and numerous, but in the dark, it's impossible to see which is which. Other than that, this receiver is nearly perfect. Nice job Onkyo.

title: DOES NOT WORK WITH KODAK Zi8
text:
These are my initial impressions, I have only had the smoothie a couple days now. I will post updates.

I have read a lot of reviews from many different websites with the word "Flip cam". Thinking that if it could work with the flip cam why not the zi8? Well, the iphone attachment comes off and other attachments can be put on, like the flip attachment, sold separately. The way it comes off is similar to a tripod. A tripod like mine (Sunpack Plat + 5800D) has a top piece that un-latches and has the screw on the top to screw your camera into it. These tops seem to be universal but I am not sure. Anyway, I thought I could take the top from the tripod and put it into the top on the Smoothie. No. The opening is too small. Did they do this on purpose so that you only purchase their attachments? Why couldn't they design the smoothie with a piece that just has the (Universal) screw on top so that you can use any small camera? Stupid. I ended up taking the top from the tripod and shaving the sides down with an exacto knife until it fit into the smoothie. that piece also has a level on it to help with the balancing. (Something that should probably be on the smoothie to begin with!)

Balancing is a little difficult, and getting used to this thing is indeed challenging. But with time I know it will pay off.

Walking in a straight line is easy and you will see improvements 100%. Without it you can "See" me walking. Every step and the camera would shake with my movements. With the smoothie it seems as though you are gliding. It looks a little unnatural at first when watching the video. But keep in mind this is walking in a straight line. It gets tricky when you want to zoom because you really don't want to be touching any part of the camera or smoothie. Panning from left to right and looking up and down is tricky too. If you just hold the handle your shot will be the smoothest. But the camera tends to wander and most of the time you need to control the camera to look at things, so you need to touch the smoothie to control it. This is the tricky part that will come with practice.

I like to hold it in one hand with my thumb and index finger lightly holding the collar. Hold too loosely and the camera is a wild mustang, hold too tightly and you defeat the purpose of the smoothie.

4 stars because it is a quality piece and It's MUCH cheaper than the Merlin!
-1 star because I hate when companies make their products and accessories "Exclusive". Like I said before, unless you have an iphone or flip cam, this won't work for you unless you are willing to rig something yourself. But you really can't do anything too wild because you will throw off the balancing and the whole unit won't work. i.e. I initially though I could attach the Zi8 to the iphone mount with velcro/rubberbands. Who would pay this much for the mediocre videos the iphone records anyway? They should have included a thread at the top. Most camera's have this for mounting on "UNIVERSAL" equipment!

text:

Transfer of a single 1.5GB AVCHD video file. Compared with a Transcend 32GB Class 6 SDHC card :

From hard drive to class 6 card: 13MB/s
From hard drive to Class 10 card: 39MB/s
From class 6 card to hard drive: 22MB/s
From class 10 card to hard drive: About a sec. 1.43GB/s. I don't understand how it is so fast.

Using the class 6 card with another card reader= no difference in transfer speed.
Copying to and from ssd (500MB/s) or 5700rpm hard drive = no difference in transfer speed.

So, to sum up, The class 6 card will transfer at USB2 speeds regardless of what card reader you choose. title: front fan= NOISY
text:
Big QC flaw that is the front fan. The front panel of the case has a metal plate that is perforated with holes, to allow the air to flow through. Behind the front panel, built into the case, is the front fan. There is not enough room between the metal plate and the front fan which causes the fan noise. It is a pulsating "whirring" noise that I find unbearable. The case is about 4 feet from me on my desk at work. I contacted Corsair and told them about this and their response was to mail me a new front fan. I do believe they are aware of the problem but are unwilling to do anything about it. Do a web search for "Corsair 650D front fan noise" and you can read up about it. Best solution is to cut the metal mesh plate out of the front panel is your handy with tools. IMO, for the $ of this case I find this unacceptable. My case model is CC650DW-1. I have an Antec 1200V3 at home. Aside from the front dust filter being a pain to get to, I really have to recommend that case over this one.

Anyway.....here is what I did. I took the top HDD cage off. I left the bottom cage where it was. I removed the top 2 front fan screws completely. For the bottom 2 screws, I unscrewed them almost all the way. I left a couple threads to grab the fan. Without the top HDD cage this allows the fan to tilt back and rest on the bottom hdd cage. It does not fall because the bottom 2 screws are still holding the fan, slightly. This provides enough clearance between the fan and the front mesh. The fan does not rattle and it still provides cooling to the HDD's. The only draw back is that you have to sacrifice a HDD cage.

title: It's a winner [for me]- until I had problems
text:
***EDITED on 4/8/14***Dropped 2 stars.
2 new problems.

1. Popping. Played backup BD rip, Bad popping throughout movie. Some were low, others were very loud. Like a static pop. Very bad. Hooked up the wdtv live smp to the same gear and it did not pop. Also playing on the pc it's being served from in PDVD & VLC and no popping.

2. Audio cutting out. Whenever I pause, RW, FF, or jump to a scene the audio cuts out and all I hear is this faint buzzing. I blamed it on my receiver. While this buzzing was going on I would power-cycle the receiver and the audio came back on. Used the wdtv live smp with that gear and it did not cut out.

Not sure if my kdlinks 720 is defective or if it's this new firmware. It could also be some of my equipment is not playing nice with the kdlinks. What is clear is that the kdlinks is no longer working for me.

Gonna retire this unit to the bedroom. At least I could use it as a poor man's NAS or something.

***EDITED ON 1/9/14****

I started an official forum for this player on audio video science forums. You can read my trials and tribulations there. I have my media backup files stored in my pc and I stream everything to this kdlinks 720 via my gigabit network via Windows network shares. I put a 1TB HDD in the unit and it works great with that method too.

Pros:
It plays dvds with menu support. (straight VIDEO_TS rips) via Network shares. Media streamer programs like Serviio/plex do not support dvd menus (because it's using DLNA).

***If you rip your BD discs to straight BDMV folders****
Some BD rip movies are split among multiple .m2ts files (seamless branching). Other media players might only play the first or largest .m2ts file. The kdlinks 720 will play the movie with all the .m2ts files in order! I did notice that you will experience a slight pause/stutter when it switches between the files. This also happens when playing the movie from the hard drive too. With a movie that only has a couple .m2ts files it doesn't really matter. Some movies though have a lot. Sometimes over 100. In this case I would recommend using a program that combines all the .m2ts files into one. Most of the movies only have one .m2ts file and thus you won't see any pauses.

***If you rip your BD into ISO***
Same playback as the above method. You will not be able to use the menu of the BD (this goes with ANY format you rip BD to). Regardless of what the specs say. Almost all movies today have java-menus and almost all players have had this functionality removed. You can access the subtitles and audio streams however.

It will bitstream full DD True HD & DTS-HD.

Fast Forward & Rewind works great! It is rather slow doing this through network streams but it does work. Also, the top of the round button (around "ok") will jump 1 minute ahead, as will the bottom of the button jump back 1 minute. Overall, the player did not freeze or crash at all.

It uses the Realtek 1186 chipset. This is, as of now, the newest version. The other popular competing chipset is the Sigma chipset (which is in the WDTV live smp).

I use the "mymovies" program to provide all the metadata and cover art (folder.jpg) which is located in the root of each movie folder. The KDL 720 will use those jpegs in the thumbnails when browsing your movie collection. The KDL720 will also provide this cover art as well but you have to do this manually for each movie. ***UPDATE- This player will read "about.jpg" movie sheet images. These have all the metadata (artist, director backdrops, etc)on a single .jpg. When browsing your movies, hit "info" on the remote and you will see this on screen. Programs like Mymovies and Thumbgen can create these about.jpg files, also known as "Moviesheets" or "Linksheets".

Cons:
The interface is downright ugly as hell. It does not have popular apps other than Youtube. In fact, it probably would have been better if it didn't include any apps at all rather than give us some of the strangest apps I have ever seen.

With all these media players out there, and all the different ways people organize their media, you really have to find the player out there that works for you!

If your looking for a player that has a slick looking interface and all the popular apps, this is not it. If you are just looking to play your backup rips on the local hard drive or through your computer networked to this device, this might just fit the bill for you.

title: Finally got SONOS!  and I'm on the fence
text:
EDIT 5/7/14
Another cool find is that when the system is off (on standby) you can just press the play button on the speaker to resume listening to what you were listening to last. This is pretty huge since sometimes I want to turn it on but am too lazy to get the phone or can't find it. If you just want quick music you can hit this button.

EDIT 4/21/14
Sonos recently got Google Music functionality. Great news! You can use the Google music manager installed on your pc to automatically monitor and upload your music to the cloud. It stores a sick amount of music for free. Apparently, SONOS is also going to be phasing out their BRIDGE unit. They found a way to make the system work without it. That's also great news. Hope they actually do it. But kind of sucks for the people who already bought the thing. I have been bringing my play1 inside and outside all the time so far this spring. It's been great. Might get a second play1 to leave in the garage. Sometimes the connection is flaky. Not sure if it is because I keep unplugging the thing. Sometimes it takes a while for the app to "find the speaker". Sometime I have to switch my iphone from back and forth from/to 5G wifi. And yes, when you want to change/lower music it does take some time to pull out the phone, touch the app, ect...Best feature by far: My wife and I each have an iphone and ipad. At anytime we can open one of these 4 devices and control the music regardless of who started the app. VERY COOL!

EDIT 4/10/14-
So, I brought these two speakers outside (Play1 & Play3). Have to admit they both sounded awesome outside. I put them side-by-side and listened to the same song over and over with each speaker. The play1 has much sharper highs. It seems to drown out a lot of everything else but not really in a bad way. The play 3 has much more mids and a slightly better low-end bass response. The lows hit a little harder, deeper and cleaner, but it was slight and really not a "wow what a difference" moment. The mids seem to overtake everything here. I messed around with the eq setting for each speaker. Funny, the play3 has a setting for Left/right. Really? The speaker might be stereo itself but it is not a stereo listening experience. Being that I had to really go back and forth between the 2 speakers to really get a sense of their differences tells me they are not that much different. To my ears anyway. Worth the extra $100? I don't know. Some music sounds a little better and the rest sounds the same. Considering that I would just use sonos to add background sound to a room, I think the play1 is absolutely fine. It is also much easier and lighter to carry the thing around than the play3. Again, I think the Sonos stuff is really overpriced. The bridge should be free since you cannot do anything with it alone. Ultimately, I need a speaker I can bring all around the house and outside. The play1 & bridge is a $250 setup. I had a $100 gift card. So, $150 sits easier with me. I think it's the price it should be anyway. ***I discovered you can use different apps on your phone and pc (like Windows Media Player) to send songs (Play-to) to the sonos speaker, bypassing the Sonos app. Really cool.
******************************************************************************end of update.

So, been thinking of sonos for years. (I am just interested in music, not the home theater aspect of Sonos). Currently have a Yamaha receiver w/ Airplay in the living room. All my music is on google play online, where I can store all of my 50GB of music. Pull it up on the iPad, hit "Airplay" and it sounds great on my home theater speakers. The only thing is that Airplay does tend to drop-out sometimes. This is a pretty big deal. But, this setup is costing me zero dollars, I can attach a pair of speakers outside to the "B" outputs on my receiver too. But that requires running the lines.

So, I got the Play1 with the bridge and then a week later got the Play3 to test that out for comparison. With these, you get a speaker with an amp built in and it's wireless. But it is still a lot of $ for the gear. They don't give the specs for their speakers or amps. I don't like that at all. I hate it when companies tell the consumers what they think we should care about.

I am just not sure about the sound quality of the Play1 and 3. Here is my problem, I'm used to listening to music in stereo. When I listen to a single play1/3, the sound is very direct (obviously), and there is no separation. It is also a "treated" sound, similar to Bose. It sounds a bit unnatural. As if the speakers are just trying too hard to produce sound that they physically cannot reproduce. Do they sound good? Sometimes. Sometimes there is too much mids, bass or lack thereof. It all sounds very small. And the louder they play the worse it gets. I have a moderate HT setup. Klipschs FR speakers connected to a $600 Yamaha receiver. Nothing too fancy. Maybe I am spoiled.

Also, besides having a NAS or leaving your computer running when playing music, there is currently no free online storage method of streaming your music. This would change if Sonos gets google music or if Amazon cloud storage suddenly removed their 250-song limit.

The play 1 is in my kitchen & living room (open floor plan house). And I think to myself, why not just use the Airplay?
There are options though. Getting 2 play1 speakers, now this is getting pricey. Forget their speakers and just get the Connect or the Connectamp. Way overpriced. If the connect was $100, now that would be a game changer. I just can't see spending $350 for something that just acts as a conduit to play my music on their app. And $500 for the Connect amp?

I think perhaps Sonos is just too overpriced. I'll continue to listen in hopes of discovering something that makes this all worth it. But for now, this is what I have come up with, for what it is worth:

Sonos excels at:
Playing music that does not drop out at all! (not sure if this alone justifies the price tag)
Whole-house (background) audio. If someone has a lot of separate rooms and wants audio in each, yes this would fit the bill. But really only for background music IMO. They start to show their limitations the louder they get. You're not going to rock a dance party with any of the Sonos speakers, unless you are running multiple pairs of (maybe) the play 5's.
Having a wireless speaker that you can take around the house/outside.

title: It will do the job but strange design choice. No side to side adjust.
text:
This thing is heavy. Period. Used a 15/64 drill bit for pilot holes. Tightened as much as i could using a screwdriver. Paired this with the powerbridge one-pro. Hung a 50" vizio e500ib1. The bolts supplied to attach arms to back of tv were too long. Had to use own washers.

Pros: super strong, no sag whatsoever. Easy to adjust tilt. It rotates too so that if you screw up, you can adjust it so it is level. Very good directions. Comes with free hdmi cable.

Cons: here we go. Bolts on top make it hard to rest level on. Had to level the holes in the wall. Im 6' 230lbs and i struggled a bit to hold this on the wall to get the first bolt in. They could have detached the plate to make mounting easier. Arms are stiff! You really have to grip the tv to move it. Makes me uncomfortable to do. Tvs nowadays are made cheap with thin bezels. Cable management is a joke. No way to not pinch wires when collapsing arms. I just used twisties on the upper arms.

Heres a big one: no side to side adjust. With studs 16" apart, tv is 4" off center of wall. Bolts on back of tv were narrow meaning that when the tv was placed on the mount there was no play to adjust side to side. Big design flaw. Yes, i could move the tv out and away from wall to move it over, but im talking about when it is collapsed. If the wall plate was wider it would solve this. Each outer hole is 16" apart.

Overall it works. But some of the design choice made me say "what were they thinking?".

title: Great!  Worth the money.
text:
IMO speaker manufacturers are the biggest source of snake oil on the planet. They literally tell you that a speaker is going to sound great because it costs 30k. I mean it it's gotta right? And $45 speakers must sound terrible. The only test is blind. We then find out that compressed mp3s don't actually sound that bad and Radio Shack wire sounds no different than Monster's $600 speaker cable.

In my theater room i hav Klipsch reference speakers all around and IMO, they sound good, but not worth the $500 a piece price tag. I don't like the narrow sweet spot and harshness of a horn tweeter. My sweet spot for speakers are about $100 each, and receivers around $500-$600. I have a discerning ear and outstanding hearing sensitivity. Its hard to judge reviews on speakers because everyone hears things differently, and there is soooo much hoopla in marketing with name brands and price. I have a pair of cerwin vega ls12s that sound great to me and Bose is great if you like "treated" music, which sometims i do. Anyway.....

Upstairs i have a modest yamaha v673 receiver with klipsch quintet speakers i replaced with these Micca speakers and matching center, and a BIC h-100 sub. I have to say, out of the box, these things sound great! They have a very crisp and "airy" sound to them. Music, and br movies (HD audio) sound very good. I have the xover on the sub set at 120hz. The highs are especially spacious and the mids are pretty soft. I dont generally like a lot of mids. Cymbal crashes sound very open. They sound really good to me.

To me, i have found that with speakers, bigger is better. No matter how much people say that these speakers have great bass, i would not agree. These speakers do sound a bit "small". Thats not a con though, they ARE small. The size is really just right for my tv stand. I like that the box is oversized for the cones. They kind of remind me of recording studio monitors (audioengines, etc).

It could be that since these speakers are inexpensive, the sound is much better than expected. Would i still like the sound if i had paid $500 per speaker for these? Lets not think about it. These fit the bill and sound great to me. That's all that matters. Give em a shot. You can always return them.

I have a klipsch reference series set of home theater speakers wired to a $600 Yamaha receiver. After moving, I didn't want the clutter of big box speakers in my den and didn't want the hassle of mounting the tv so I could fit the massive klipsch center channel speaker. title: What is the deal? 3 minute standby auto-shutoff and mine came with Live streaming.
text:
[[VIDEOID:fe16bf664e627724891eacf2a50bdb9e]] Update----— it would not turn on. After about six times holding down the button it finally did turn on. Battery was fully charged. Tried again later at home and the same thing happened. Holding down the power button just did not turn this thing on until after about five times. It's going back. ------end update.

I had such high hopes for this to be my "cheap mans gopro". I used it for a 2 hour session at the local bmx trails yesterday. I'll start with the good.

Footage looks great. Image stabilization is good enough to keep the video steady while jumping on a bmx bike.
Simple to use. Not a lot of settings to get overly complex.
Small.
The magnet is a great feature. It stayed on my helmet with just the magnet and did not move while jumping on my bike. I used the metal sticker that was in the packaging and stuck that to my helmet.

Here is the bad:
- Standby auto shutoff
When the camera is on and ready to record, after 3 minutes it beeps 3 times and then shuts off. I called Polaroid and they confirmed this is normal. There is no way to turn this off or adjust the standby time. This can be good or bad depending on your needs. In order to see if it's on which requires taking off my helmet, I would then have to turn it on and then start recording. If I need the app I would have to press the button for 3 seconds, then press the wifi for 3 seconds and wait for the app to connect. Nothing is mentioned ANYWHERE about the auto-shut off in the manual or anything. It prevents me from being spontaneous with shots. As a trade off it does prolong battery life.

Mine came with live streaming?!?
Currently there a 3 cubes offered by Amazon. One without wifi, one with wifi (The one I purchased), and then one with live streaming. On my box was written "Now with live streaming". Is this something they just added? What's with the more expensive version that seems the only difference is that it comes with live streaming?!?
UPDATE: I just called Polaroid and they confirmed there are only 2 cameras, the cube and the cube+. The cube does not have wifi while the cube+ has wifi and live streaming. Live streaming if provided by the app, not the camera. This is a problem on Amazons website. THERE ARE NOT 3 different Cube cameras.

Field of View
Not wide enough for bmx riding. It's good for overall shooting, but I want something more wide. As you can see in the video clip below, while watching my footage, it seems a bit too "close" for comfortable viewing. I hear the gopro has adjustable FOV options.

- The app (Iphone 6).
Oh boy. You can connect your phone to the Cube and see a live preview, then record, and play the video it just recorded all on the phone. However, if I lock my phone and then unlock it and go back into the app, the preview screen goes black. The wifi disconnects when you lock/turn screen off your phone. Then you have to either restart the app or hit random buttons until it brings you to the : "Looks like your cube isn't connected" screen, and then have to "connect" and then it works. You need to either have your phone open all the time, or just preview the video every now and then. You are not going to want to record, watch, record, watch, etc.
- I could not see anywhere on the app where I could trim the recordings.

- Accessories
They are limited. The handlebar mount they offer is fixed and only accepts 1" bars.
The helmet mount does not have any tilt adjustment. This is HUGE since you have to put a lot of thought on where to mount it on your helmet. It took me about 5 times to get the angle right. (*I used the metal sticker that was in the packaging and stuck that to my helmet.*)

Battery:
It was just ok. I was able to record around 20-25 minutes of 1080p 60fps video. The camera was used for about 2 hours and took up about 3.5GB of space on my card. Charging took a LONG time, about 3 hours.

Memory card issues
There seem to be a lot of problems with the cube being picky about memory card brands. If your memory card is formatted to fat32 you are only going to be able to use a MAX of 32 GB. That is all the fat32 file system will allow. It worked with my 64GB card formatted to fat32 (but only allowed 32GB). I restored my 64GB card to its factory xfat file system and cube was then able to record the full 64 GB.

title: NOT for serious situations ***UPDATED 12/18/18
text:
UPDATE 12/18/18
6 months with this camera and the #1 problem that I couldn't get over was the inability to deter anyone. I ended up getting the Arlo Pro2 cams. The base unit has a VERY loud alarm that you can set off from the app. I feel a bit more secure knowing that in the event I saw something, I can sound the alarm and hope to deter the threat. The Arlo also provides near-instant push notifications (reliably serving as a doorbell cam), and I can watch the feed on my firestick.

Blink recently added activity zones, but the doorbell has been delayed indefinitely (not a good sign), and now I have a green band on my videos. I demoted my blink cams to indoor duty only.
END UPDATE
-----------------------------------

First the pros, and then the reasons why I cannot recommend these cameras for any type of serious surveillance situations.

PROS:
They are less expensive then their competition (Arlo, Ring). No monthly fees for cloud storage.
Footage quality is good. There is not a lot of exposure compensation so be sure to position your camera so that your subjects are not under/overexposed.

Access from phone when at/away from home is great. Always able to connect. Audio is ok, with frequent drop-outs.

I use these camera to check on my pets and *if* something criminal were to happen, maybe I could have some footage of the event. It's nice to see when packages get delivered.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CONS:
I cannot recommend these cameras for any type of serious surveillance situations. Bottom line - you cannot use these cameras to DETER anyone. It will not record during live mode (actively watching camera). All you will have is recorded footage to take to the police.

After having used this camera for 5 months, here is a list of real problems:

It will send you phone notifications AFTER it is done recording. That's right. It will detect movement and then record (based on your length setting). After it is done recording you will then get a notification on your phone. By this time, someone has either done the damage or has been waiting at your door for a while. Forget using this as a doorbell cam. Hoping for better results when they finally get around to releasing their actual doorbell cam. Because of this, I set the recording length to 5 seconds. I timed it. When someone approaches my door, I will get the notification after about 10 seconds. Wish it was sooner, since I then have to get the phone, watch the footage, and then go to the door.

There is no siren or way to talk to the person whom you want to leave. There is a blue light that comes on when it detects movement. Maybe that would scare them away. For comparison, The RING cam lets you talk through the camera, sound a loud siren, or turn the camera light on. To be clear, the BLINK cam does not do any of these things.

It doesn't record during live view. To make the matter worse, if the thing causing the detection stays there, you will get caught in the "system busy" loop. It goes like this: You will get a notification. If you don't click on it right away it will start recording again. You won't be able to watch the video since it will be recording and it will say "camera busy", and once it is done, you can either watch the first video, or view live mode but then it won't record during live mode anyway. And this is only if you catch it before it starts recording a third time. Better off waiting until all the action is over, or adjust the time of how soon it records again after detecting motion.

Side to side detection is ok, but it will struggle to detect someone walking straight toward the camera. Yeah. It will start recording when they are about 1-2 feet from it. My driveway cams purpose is to just trigger movement (I can never see people clearly enough because they are always walking straight towards the camera).

Watching the camera in live mode will last about 15 seconds and then it asks you to "Continue?", which will then give you another 15 seconds, and so on. Too bad. My hopes of monitoring when people show up (pizza?) in my driveway were crushed. I now need to rely on the notification. Please give me the option to waste my battery how I see fit.

With I could view my cameras on a FireTV product. Isn't Blink owned by Amazon?

I have cameras about 30 ft from each other, one on my garage monitoring my driveway, and the other at the front door. The front door cam detection is delayed due to the driveway cam is busy recording that movement which it detects first.

Would a cat5 wired from the base station to my router help to reduce the delay? They don't offer wired ethernet. I wish they did since my base is sitting on top of my router.
--------------------------

I bought the 3 pack and I do enjoy the free cloud storage. I think I would have enjoyed the MUCH better features of the Ring spotlight/doorbell cam, but I didn't want to spend the $ on cloud storage. If I had to start over - I'm still not sure which one I would get. BUT, If I lived in an area with frequent security concerns, it would be a no brainer - Ring.

title: Possible defective unit, soap opera effect, & thoughts on VRR & THX gaming
text:
I got this tv for the VRR & THX gaming for my xbox one x. I have the 2019 4 series tv and I'm familiar with TCL.

-----Defects-----
When connecting my xbox the screen would flash to black, game mode and the dolby vision logo would flash on and off. Going through all the option in the xbox and tv, finally using HDMI port 3 was the only thing that worked. I still had strange flashing every now and then, but it was enough to experience the VRR & THX.

-----VRR & THX----- (fyi the tv will only do 120hz @ 1440p res on the xbox one x)
I set the xbox to 1440p, 120hz, game mode on, tv using thx game mode. My opinion - it depends on the game. I played Far Cry 5, The Outer Worlds, and Alice Madness Returns (to see what older gen games would look like) and I did not notice any difference from my 4k TCL 4 series from 2019. When spanning left to right I saw the same juddery choppy images. FC5 color looked a bit washed out, similar to what others are saying about the THX mode. Outer Worlds color and detail looked amazing. The lag experience (thumbstick to tv action) was similar to my TCL 4 from 2019, which is responsive enough for me. I tried these games with vrr turned off and at 4k 60hz and it all looked the same to me. TOW seem a tiny bit choppier, but nothing concerning at all.

I noticed a BIG difference with COD WW2. Panning around was FLUID! It seemed to take advantage of the 120hz. It was very impressive!

-----Movie, apps, general watching-----
My wife and I have been binging on LOST for the past month on my 7 year old 60" Sony 1080p tv. So, we resumed watching Lost on this tv. My wife hated it. I struggled to get this set to display a picture that looked good to my eyes. I even went into the Roku app and tried the expert picture settings. It was overly bright and the colors were not right.

It also has some sort of permanent SOAP OPERA EFFECT. I experienced the same exact thing on the 6 series TCL from 2019. I turned off ALL the related settings. But it was still there.

My panel was PERFECT! No clouding or banding or anything. No dark or light corners.

-----eARC-----
According to the TCL rep on AVSFORUM, this tv will pass DD True HD & DTS MA via the eARC. I was hoping to pass this hi-res audio from the Plex app on the tv to my receiver but I did not have any luck. I tried turning off all transcoding on Plex but perhaps it is a setting issue. Someone from the Plex forum mentioned that an app on the tv will not pass these audio formats, it has to come from a set top box like an Nvidia Shield or a Dune player or something.

-----FINAL THOUGHTS-----
For gaming, it seems like it is up to the individual game to take advantage of VRR and 120hz, which is a bummer. Perhaps TV tech is ahead of the gaming hardware/software. THX is an endorsement for list of requirements that a tv needs to have. Seems like marketing tom foolery but we will see what RTINGS has to say when they finally review this set. The soap opera effect and the terrible color (though I'm sure you could tweak the color.) I cannot live with. I'd rather just buy the TCL 4 series. Sometimes fewer picture options is better. I want to watch the show, not fool around with all the adjustments trying to find the perfect picture quality. The tv was returned.

title: Frustrating Alexa, CEC, Stutter.
text:
For me, a TV is 50/50 picture/convenience. This is a zero on convenience. (Update 3/19/23 I'll Never buy an LG tv again).

Forget the nonsense about "oleds don't get that bright". People are just saying stuff that they hear the pros saying because it's a couple hundred nits lower than an LED set. It's plenty bright for HDR highlights and daytime viewing. I have to squint my eyes. And if you're like most people who work a 9-5 and mostly watch tv in the evenings - you'll find it bright enough. Come on people.

Let's start with the UGLY:

CEC: NIGHTMARE
I have a PS5, XBSX, Shield Pro. Whether these devices are all plugged into tv then ARC-> Yamaha receiver, -OR- everything plugged into a new Denon 760H receiver then eARC-> tv, it's equally faulty. The tv likes to turn on my PS5 whenever I hit the input button (it shows the row of inputs first like it should, but then turns on and switches to PS5, also whenever I hit the back button from the ThinQ menu (I need to remember to hit the HOME button instead) and other odd buttons it fires up the PS5. Last night it did this when I hit the settings button ?!? Cannot get the Shield Pro to turn the tv on when it powers on. Yet, it will turn the tv on when it's connected to my 10 year old Yamaha receiver (eARC to tv).
The Universal Control Management is terrible. So much bloated crap on this TV.

Auto-resume?!? Pause while watching netflix. 3 minutes later it starts playing. Watching something on plex- exit to home screen. 5 min later it switches to Plex and resumes movie.

ALEXA: HORRIBLE
This has to be the WORST Alexa integration EVER. My 3 year old Sony 900h connected on day one and has been FLAWLESS. Same with my $400 TCL roku tv. I say "Alexa, turn off xxx tv" and it would work 100% of the time. NOT ON THIS TV. It took me a week to troubleshoot, uninstalling apps, reinstalling (why are there 2 different LG devices on the Alexa app?!?). I'd say it works 10% of the time. Usually it says "LG tv is not responding, please check it's network and power connection). If I grab the LG remote and hit the Alexa button and tell it to turn off it will work. But I could obviously just hit the power button on the remote.

UPDATE: try calling the Tv "tv" instead of "lg tv" . ALSO-" the tv has its own Alexa built in. Our echo dots are all named "echo" so this actually works quite well. Try calling "alexa" to the tv and issuing command. This has been working lately rather than telling my dot "echo, pause the tv". We'll see tomorrow. /update. (This still only works 50% of the time. Usually says " network error". 3/19/23)

LEARNING CURVE: STEEP AF
Make sure to register at AVSFORUM and read up/post your questions. The menu settings are very confusing and oddly placed. Read the manual, do your research. Go onto RTINGS.

REMOTE: LOVE/HATE
The pointer wheel is kind of cool and probably quicker most of the time. It's like using a Wii remote but far more accurate and stable. The problem is when you just want to click over and select something (by pressing the wheel in). But my finger slips and instead of pressing the wheel in it turns the wheel which brings up the pointer and takes much longer to do what I need to do. There's also no Play/Pause button, you need to press in the wheel.

I consider myself a person of average intelligence but it's 2023 All remotes should have 3 things MANDATORY:
1. ALL buttons need to light up when lifted (like the Shield remote).
2. There ABSOLUTELY NEEDS to be a sliding LOCK BUTTON to prevent accidental button press (and kid mischief).
3. It needs to have a remote finder. Go into the app, hit a button, the remote makes a sound.
(4). It would be nice to have a few learning buttons and customizable app buttons, not just Netflix.

"Gallery" feature is a missed opportunity. It only appears if you are on an external input after the device has been powered off. Or you can select the gallery app manually. Here's a stellar idea - why not use the gallery as the screensaver instead of the ugly fireworks or clock?

GAMING: SUPERB
Playing Horizon Forbidden West on PS5 at 60+ FPS in 4K is absolutely ASSAULTING on the eyes. It looks incredible! TV is responsive in regards to input lag and response time. When the tv is in GAME MODE, hitting the options button on the TV brings up the GAME menu which shows you all the gaming-related options and displays the current FPS on screen. Very nice.

MOVIES: OBJECTIVE
No TV is perfect. Side viewing angle is big for me. I can see the color washout sitting 12" over on the couch while watching my Sony 900h LCD tv. Unacceptable. This TV has an AWESOME VIEWING ANGLE. Go to RTINGS to view and compare. There is no discernable color/luminance washout in any seat in my living room. You need to go off to the extreme right/left to notice it.

My dvd backups played via PLEX app on TV look incredible, thanks to the rich OLED blacks. 1080p BD rips also look fantastic (compared to my LCD SONY 900h). And of course 4k content looks great. We all know about the "inky" blacks of OLED, no need to talk about it. Image quality is the best I've seen.

STUTTER/(Judder?):
This is a big one for me. During panning shots, usually when there is something tall and thin not moving on the screen there is a HORRIBLE STUTTER effect. It's jaggy and looks like the picture can't keep up. It's extremely jarring and takes me right out of the experience. This is due to the extremely fast response time of OLED technology. I find it extremely undesirable and a flaw. Options to mitigate this will introduce the Soap Opera effect, which is worse IMO.

SOUND OUTPUT
Sound on the tv is fine. The usual. Sound output via ARC/eARC will only output the basics: stereo, Atmos, Dolby Digital and (DD+) to your receiver. And there is a difference between this DD and the DD you will find on a DVD/Blu Ray. It's a much more boring, stripped-down version (as with the Atmos I have heard) It's a lower bitrate signal. But it will suffice if you're going for a true 1-remote system. The TV will NOT OUTPUT DTS, DTS-MA, DD True HD via ARC/eARC. ***UPDATE: RECENT NEWS INFORMED THAT LG MIGHT START OFFERING DTS OUTPUT VIA ARC. IT'S UNSURE WHETHER THIS TV WILL RECEIVE THIS UPDATE*** Go onto RTINGS to check this info. Most TV's these days do not support outputting hi res audio signals which is unfortunate. The Nvidia Shield Pro is the recommended set-top box if hi-res audio is important to you.

webOS: fine
Everyone seems to hate on the webOS. Look, they ALL have ads. I much prefer the Google Android (SONY tv, Shield) OS. But this one is fine. It offers all the apps I need: Netflix HBO MAX, Hulu, Disney +, and all the other ones, and displays them in a row at the bottom of the screen. You can easily go to what you want without looking or noticing all the other ads and crap on the tv. There is also another "ThinQ" app home screen where you can look at more crap you will probably never use. I stay away from all of this and hit my buttons very precisely otherwise one wrong move and I will launch the PS5 or some other device via CEC.

HINT: If your PS5 (maybe other devices too) does turn on, hit the (...) button on the LG remote to bring up a menu where you can put the PS5 back into sleep mode.

EYES
It took about 6 weeks for my eyes to adjust to this tv. Not sure of it was the detail, the brightness (it's plenty bright for me) or the blue light - whatever - my eyes got strained. It felt like a dull pressure behind my eyeballs. I'm 43 and perhaps I have some eye issues, so this is objective. I'm sort of used to it now, however I do start to feel eye strain in excess of 2/3 hours. Sooner if gaming.

BOTTOM LINE: WOULD I BUY THIS TV AGAIN?
I don't think so, especially now with other brands (SONY) offering OLED. I just don't think I should have so much to complain about with a $2500 tv. I would expect it with HiSense, TCL, Westinghouse basement bargain garage sale tvs, but not with a top shelf LG OLED.

I would NOT choose OLED if there was another tech that offered similar gaming response time, decent black levels, and NO STUTTER during panning shots. This is like right on the edge of being a deal-breaker for me.

1/30/23 - I will update when/if things change. 3/19/23. I still hate this tv. Love the picture quality but just HATE the way it operates and all the shortcomings. No more LG for me.

title: No good for Raspberry Pi
text:
I intended to house a 3.5" 10TB WD drive in this and connect it to a Pi 4 8GB. Having added to fstab I expected it to reappear after rebooting the Pi, except it didn't, and won't until the enclosure is turned off and on again. It is apparently down to the JMicron chipset (vendor/device id = 0080:a001) in the enclosure and its UASP implementation vs Linux drivers.

I have reluctantly given up and on the advice of Pi forums ordered an enclosure with a ASM1153e chipset instead as apparently this works properly with the Pi.

title: Excellent headphones for those who know what they're looking for
text:
It's "almost" (see my edit below) impossible to find a negative review of the Audio-Technica ATH-M50x Closed Back Headphones. And I have to agree. Probably the best headphones I've ever owned. They've been available now for 10 or so years. You can't get this high end quality audio anywhere else for this price point. I got an excellent deal. The headphone purchase also included 3 high quality extra items for just about the same price as the headphones alone. My package included an extra cable, a solid hard plastic carrying case, and a FiiO A1 headphone amplifier.
The headphones live up to all the positive reviews, and the extras included made for a very good total price.
I would definitely recommend this product.
Updated 2/4/2021, 4 months later.
I still love these headphones. I have to laugh when I occasionally check the customer reviews and find that most of the criticisms are based on how these headphones were purposely engineered. Let me be more specific. Some of the negative comments include:
-others around you can hear what you're listening to. Oh well. Too bad. They should probably put on their own noise cancelling headphones. Which brings me to my next point:
-they're not noise cancelling. Yup, that's right. When I did my search for headphones, I specifically did NOT want noise cancelling OR Bluetooth. Much prefer putting the money saved when not buying these options and putting it toward better cans.
-there is no microphone on the cables. Correct again. These headphones were not necessarily intended for those who want a set of cans primarily to support their cell phone addiction.
-they must be used with the company's proprietary cables to attach to the headphones. I'll take that and love it. Why? Because they twist and lock into the bottom of the can. How many times, with other headphones, have I moved too far, or stood up or whatever, and the cord would be ripped out of the cans!!
-too much bass, not enough base. Midrange too pronounced, or not enough. And they go on and on and on.
-the "best" (tongue in cheek) criticism stated that none of the included cables, nor the included adapters fit his computer. I don't know what kind of a computer this person has, but, if Bill Cosby appears in TV commercials for your computer, headphones should not be your #1 focus right now
-and finally, and I quote, "I needed to add an EQ to make them sound like I wanted them to". Precisely! These cans were designed and manufactured specifically for those who are looking for an accurate, unadulterated representation of the original recording. The way the musicians and the recording engineers intended it to sound. If one doesn't find that acceptable, and that's fine, include an EQ somewhere in the mix. As a matter of fact, I have more than my share of sound shaping hardware and software all over my system in order to tailor the music to my liking.
You need to like the sound quality reproduced through headphones and speaker systems alike. And this is very subjective. One person's likes are another person's hates, especially when it comes from those who love to sound like they "might" know what they are talking about.. I bought and returned a number of headphones because I didn't care for how they sounded. I kept these.
I do agree with one common complaint. The earpads do get uncomfortable after a while. I checked for aftermarket replacements, but many included their own negative reviews that they changed the sound quality from the originals. That's the last thing I want.

title: I was Skeptical
text:
I live in the rural mountains of Virginia, where I get limited coverage. A few months ago I purchased an iPhone 4S and a Verizon MiFi for my phone and internet. I typically was getting one to two bars, enough to get and make calls, but data on the iphone would usually time-out and the MiFi connection was so frustrating that I was pulling my hair out!

I'd been looking at the Wilson products for a while, and finally decided to bite the bullet because I was wasting monthly fees on a MiFi I could hardly use. I was extremely skeptical of this product. When it arrived I was pleasantly surprised with all that was included, and I decided to do a professional style install, mounting the antenna at the highest point in my roof. I followed the instructions explicitly, and had to do some adjustments to the 800 Mhz Gain. Once I adjusted it, BAM! My iPhone went from one bar to five. I then watched some You Tube videos on it, and they loaded quickly with no buffering.

Now for the true test: using my MiFi internet. For the first time my Verizon MiFi was keeping a steady five bars. I went online and was able to watch videos and load web-pages with barely any noticeable latency. I did some speed tests, and before I was lucky to get 400 Kbps, which wouldn't stay connected for long. Now I am consistently getting between 800 Mbps and a high of 2400 Kbps... Wow! And it rarely disconnects.

I am incredibly impressed with how this performs. If you decide to purchase this, you should be aware of its limitations. It can only boost a signal where one exists. If you have zero bars to start with, it has nothing to boost. The antenna works best mounted outside and high-up, mounting it on the inside of a window might not work because modern window laminates can interfere with the signal (if you mount it on a window, mount it on the outside of the window). This unit only provides 10 to 12 feet of coverage, enough for one room, which I found to be the case. If you want whole-house coverage, you need to pay at least $125 more for the 841263 Kit.

When you do the install, the antenna on this unit needs to be at least 20 direct feet away from the amplifier, or you will get feedback and it will shut-off. The Desktop antenna needs to be at least 18 inches from the amplifier or it will not work, and it needs to face the room in a direction opposite that of the antenna. The instructions are clear and easy to understand, so I think those disappointed with this unit didn't install it correctly, or didn't understand the limitations. Lastly, this will not boost 4G LTE signals, only 3G. Where I am it's not an issue, because 4G is not available, at least not yet. If ever 4G becomes available, Wilson will need to create a new unit for that, which would be a new unit I would need to buy (currently they have them as attachments for phones for use within vehicles).

title: Practical and Functional Dash Cam but Instructions Could be Better
text:
I installed this Dash Cam on a Hatchback. This is my first Dash Cam, and although I like it, it took me a long time to figure-out how to properly use all its features. It does come with everything you need to use it, including an SD card; Nothing else needs to be purchased separately. But the included instructions are 20-pages long, and I constantly had to refer to the booklet because the navigation on the Cam is not very intuitive (and it requires the use of buttons, it is not a touchscreen model). I can’t imagine I’ll ever memorize everything and will be needing to use the instructions time and time again. Be aware that to properly use all the functions, it requires the downloading and use of a Smartphone App. Although the App is basic, it is not intuitive even though it appears at first that it would be. It can, however, be used in place of the buttons on the camera for using the settings. It took me forever to figure-out how to download recordings from the Cam to my phone’s camera roll. I had to get a separate instruction sheet for the App from the manufacturer to figure it out, and I still had to re-read the App instructions several times before I realized what it was telling me to do (it’s unfortunate that these additional instructions are not included in the box).

The installation went smoothly, and both cameras work well with great definition. If you are installing on a hatchback, mount the camera high-up on the rear windshield’s interior, and make sure you leave enough wire so that when the hatch opens, the wire will be long enough. I used cable ties on the loose wire at the hatch’s lift-point to attach it to the windshield’s strut and wiring harness boot. Hiding the remaining wiring in my vehicle’s headliner worked well and looks clean and professional. This model does not have an interior cabin camera, so I would not recommend it for drivers who would want recordings of passengers as well as of the exterior. It does have a microphone so that in can record the sounds within your vehicle, but that can be turned-off if you wish. One thing of note: the adhesive on the wiring clips did not stick properly to the glass or on the plastic interior of my vehicle.

The Cam comes preset with all kinds of warning settings, reminders, and startup and power-down sounds that have very annoying chimes that sound like a mix of a harpsichord and an early 2000’s ringtone. Fortunately, I was able to turn them all off from the settings menu, but it would have been nice to have been able to have other sound options that weren’t so abrasive.

The Smartphone App works via a Wifi type network that is generated by the Dash Cam. It is not Wifi in the sense that it connects to the internet, rather the Cam uses a Wifi style network to connect with your smartphone (instead of Bluetooth), so that you can not only control the settings of the Cam from your phone via the App, but so that there is enough bandwidth to download large files from your Cam to your phone. The App won’t work at all unless your phone is near your Cam (that is, in your vehicle) and connected to the Cam via the Cam’s Wifi style network.

Downloading the camera’s recordings to your phone via the App does take some steps. Once you locate a recording you want to download, you must download it to the App’s local storage album folder. Then you have to find said Local Storage Folder, select the downloaded recording, and from there you then have to go back to the App’s main screen and find a smartphone-icon that would now be visible and tap that icon to actually download the recording to your phone’s photo album. Once I figured out the multi-step process to download the recordings to my phone’s camera roll, I was finally able to then upload them to my computer. I was impressed with the image quality for both daytime and night recordings, but annoyed with the large yellow Z and brand name stamped onto the upper left side of every recording. I don’t believe that there is a way to disable that feature.

Despite several gripes, it works as advertised, but if you purchase this, be aware of the limitations and processes to make it work as you want it to.

title: This Security Camera Exceeded my Expectations
text:
I wasn’t sure if this would work on my home Wifi connection. My ISP indicated that I have what they call a mesh system that works by meshing both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz together. Since this camera works on only 2.4 GHz, I wasn’t sure if the mesh network would complicate things. To my relief, it works on my network, and it works great. So, if you live in Central to Southern Virginia and are on the Firefly Broadband network, this unit will work for you.

This unit is much smaller than I expected which made it easier to install in tight places and I was able to get it setup better than I had expected. The camera body itself is only 5-inches long, 3-inches tall, and 2.5-inches wide. The antennae ears are adjustable in case it is mounted close to something like the top of an eave. Be aware that this is a fixed camera in that it will not pan or tilt on its own.

I installed a 32GB Micro SD Card, that I ordered separately, into the unit, and it works great with plenty of storage for my needs; So, I won’t be bothering with a cloud subscription. Playback of recordings is easy, resolution is great, and nighttime recording works well. For live viewing, I will say, however, that there is a 1 to 3 second delay from what you see on the screen to what is actually happening.

Setting up the camera and linking it to my Wifi was a breeze. I will admit that I was quite apprehensive that I would have a lot of difficulty, but I was pleasantly surprised to find the required Smartphone App easy to navigate and setup went without a hitch. The App can tell you the battery percentage status so that you know if your solar panel is charging properly. You can also set the App to send you a notification whenever it senses motion; When I’m working in my home office, it’s nice to receive an alert that a package was just delivered. The motion sensor seems to work quite well without missing anything and without false alarms when the wind is blowing.

Something of note: the solar panel attaches to the camera via a Micro-USB connection, and a Micro-USB to USB-A cord is included for pre-charging your camera if needed before installation. I like the fact that if I decide to forgo the solar panel one day, that I can run a Micro-USB cord from the camera to a USB charger to keep it charged. I also like that you can add additional cameras to your network to use through the same app (they must be the same brand and type, or one that specifically works with the CloudEdge App).

Is there anything I find lacking? Yes, but not something worth deducting a star over. I wish I could do live camera viewing on my computer monitor and not just on my smartphone, as there is no way to do that. I also wonder about the long-term viability of a product that relies on a Smartphone App to work (will there be support and updates for the App for the foreseeable future, and what if the company goes out of business and/or the App stops working, will my camera become a brick?). But otherwise, this is a great camera that is easy to setup, easy to use, that doesn’t require a cloud subscription, and that works on a 2.4 GHz/ 5 GHz mesh network (does NOT work on a standalone 5 GHz network).

title: Great Option for Rural Living but Range is Limited if Driveway Goes Down a Hill
text:
I ordered these because I live in the rural Appalachian Mountains of Virginia, and sometimes I am far away from my doorbell and don’t know when someone is coming to my home. It’s also nice to be notified when a delivery truck has come onto my property.

My driveway is 1/8-mile long down a ridge, and I wanted to know when someone both enters my drive, as well as reaches the parking area at the top by my home. Because these require a direct line of sight from the transmitter to the receiver, I found that I could only put a sensor at the top of the driveway and another one about a quarter of the way down. The one I tried to install close to the bottom of the driveway, although within the 328-foor range, was not able to transmit to the receiver. So, keep in mind that hills will limit 328-foot range.

Having two receivers is a plus, as I keep one in my home office, and the other in my basement. Although I had to position the one in my basement high-up on the wall in an area of my basement that is not completely underground.

It took me a few moments to figure-out how to open the sensors to get to the battery compartment… I kept thinking I was going to break them, and the instructions weren’t clear. You have to slide the sensor to the right within its shroud housing, and then you can pull it out from the shroud housing and remove the battery cover that is behind it.

Although these have around 40 different chimes you can choose from, most of them seemed hokey and annoying to me. I wish there were more basic tones or beeps rather than a lot of musical chimes. The receiver illuminates when it receives information, and one nice feature is that you can turn off the sounds and have it solely illuminate when it receives the sensor information.

A curious thing of note, there is a micro-USB port on the side of each sensor. The instructions make no mention of it and there is no supplied cord, and I’m not sure why it is there, other than to maybe hook in a battery backup in case of power outages.

I put the third sensor by the railing of my back deck, so that I know if someone has popped out of the woods and come to my back door. I also have discovered that deer and bears also trip the driveway sensors. Keep that in mind because if you live rural as I do, you may have it trip multiple times during the night.

These are very useful sensors that have some quirky sounds and a more limited range than is really described, but overall, I recommend them. If you found this review helpful, please click the “Helpful” button under this review so that I know I am providing useful feedback.
