title: It’s a Good Security Camera but the App has Some Limitations
text:
I already have a similar security camera mounted on my front door, manufactured by Codnida that uses the CloudEdge App, and I purchased this second unit to mount on my detached garage. I rated my other camera that I already own as five-stars as compared to the 4-stars of this one.

I thought maybe this camera would run on the same App, but it doesn’t, and it only runs on the O-Kam App, which is fine and it is not the reason I deducted a star. It synced fine to my mesh Wifi network that works by meshing both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz together, and if you live in Central to Southern Virginia and are on the Firefly Broadband network, this unit will work for you.

This unit is nice and small which makes it easier to install in tight places. The camera body itself is only 5-inches long, 3-inches tall, and 2.5-inches wide. The antennae ears are adjustable in case it is mounted close to something like the top of an eave. Be aware that this is a fixed camera in that it will not pan or tilt on its own. The solar panel is quite small but adequate to recharge the camera’s battery with enough sun; It’s 7-inches long by 4.5-inches wide.

I installed a 32GB Micro SD Card, that I ordered separately, into the unit, and it works great with plenty of storage for my needs; So, I won’t be bothering with a cloud subscription. Playback of recordings is relatively easy, but not as easy as on the App for my other camera. On this App, because I haven’t setup or purchased Cloud storage, I can’t use the playback button; Instead, I have to go to messages and find the recording I want in order to play it from the micro SD Card from a snapshot of the moment it started recording, which is somewhat annoying. There is another way to find the recordings on this App without having Cloud Storage, but it takes more steps and doesn’t have an identifying snapshot to help locate the correct recording. My other camera’s App is much easier to navigate for this function.

Resolution is great, and nighttime recording works well. For live viewing, I will say, however, that there is a 1 to 3 second delay from what you see on the screen to what is actually happening, just like on my other camera. One problem I’ve noticed with this camera compared to my other, is that it seems to record sound only intermittently, and when it does, it only captures sound when the subject is very close to the camera.

Setting up the camera and linking it to my Wifi was easy, but not quite as easy as my other camera was. The App has a lot of features, and it can tell you the battery percentage status so that you know if your solar panel is charging properly. You can also set the App to send you a notification whenever it senses motion; When I’m working in my home office, it would be nice to receive an alert when someone has driven to the top of my driveway. However, unlike the App for my other camera, even though I have badge notifications enabled on this App for my phone, if I miss a notification, there have been no badges to alert me, which is a bummer. The motion sensor seems to work just ok, without missing most things and with few false alarms when the wind is blowing. But unfortunately, it only works for motion close-up. I wanted to adjust the sensitivity on the camera so that it was more sensitive and able to pickup cars moving furthest from the camera, but I can’t find any such setting in the App. It does have a mapping feature on the App that you can highlight for areas for it to not sense motion so that it focuses better on other areas, but that didn’t seem to help. That is frustrating because I was able to adjust the sensitivity on the App of my other camera from anywhere from 1 to 10, and I found that it was a very helpful feature on my other camera as it could pick-up motion far away. Unfortunately, on this camera you must be fairly close to it for it to pick up motion, which defeats much of the point of this unit for me.

Something of note: the solar panel attaches to the camera via a Micro-USB connection, and a Micro-USB to USB-A cord is included for pre-charging your camera if needed before installation. I like the fact that if I decide to forgo the solar panel one day, that I can run a Micro-USB cord from the camera to a USB charger to keep it charged. I also like that you can add additional cameras to your network to use through the same app (they must be the same brand and type, or one that specifically works with the O-Kam App).

Is there anything else I find lacking? Yes, in addition to the previously mentioned limitations to the App and lack of sensitivity, sometimes the App tells me information, such as Wifi strength and battery power remaining, in Chinese characters instead of in English, but other times it is fine and in English; It seems like the App has quite a few bugs. I wish I could do live camera viewing on my computer monitor and not just on my smartphone, as there is no way to do that. The user manual is also very spartan compared to that of my other camera. I also wonder about the long-term viability of a product that relies on a Smartphone App to work (will there be support and updates for the App for the foreseeable future, and what if the company goes out of business and/or the App stops working, will my camera become a brick?), that’s why I ordered this camera of a different brand for my garage than the one by my front door, so that if App support goes away for one, it won’t disable my entire security network. Otherwise, this is a nice camera that is easy to setup, relatively easy to use, that doesn’t require a cloud subscription, and that works on a 2.4 GHz/ 5 GHz mesh network (does NOT work on a standalone 5 GHz network). But because of the limitations of the App for this camera as compared to the App I use for my other camera, and because I can’t adjust the sensitivity of the camera or do as easy playback from the SD card, I am deducting one star on this review.

title: Practical and Functional Dash Cam but Has a Few Limitations
text:
I installed this Dash Cam on my 2nd Gen Toyota Tacoma, which is a base model and has no working rear camera. This is my second Dash Cam as I have a different model installed in my Hatchback, and although I like this one a lot, it did come-up short on a couple of things. It comes with most everything you need to use it, excluding an SD card. The touchscreen and voice commands are excellent, and I find navigating the menus easy and intuitive.

The installation went relatively smoothly, and both cameras work well with great definition. On the rear of the truck, I installed the camera next to my license plate. I thought about putting it on the handle of my liftgate, but I frequently use a Tailgate pad for hauling bicycles, and I didn’t want to have the camera covered when I did so; The location also allows me to keep tabs on the trailer hitch when towing. I ran the cable through the floor of my cab, following the taillight loom back to the bumper.

When I pulled out the main power cord, at first, I was annoyed to see it is supplied power by a cigarette lighter plug and not a USB plug, but fortunately the lighter plug has a built in USB socket, so you won’t lose a spot to plug in other cords. I ended-up not hooking the rear camera to my reverse lights, as I didn’t want or need the backup assistance, I wanted only a rear camera since I frequently tow with my truck. I also didn’t hook-up the GPS module, as I don’t need to track my routes, which apparently can only be viewed on a computer, and I didn’t want extra wiring cluttering up my dash.

Using the camera as a rear-view mirror is just as sharp as my actual mirror from which I see reflections through a tinted rear window. So, if your rear windshield is not tinted, you may find images a little darker than your actual rear-view mirror.

This model does not have an interior cabin camera, so I would not recommend it for drivers who would want recordings of passengers as well as of the exterior. It does have a microphone so that in can record the sounds within your vehicle, but that can be turned-off if you wish.

So why did I give it four stars instead of five? Here are the reasons:

- The cord for the rear camera was barely long enough to run from the cab of my truck to the bumper (I have a 6-foot bed). If I had wanted to install the camera on my liftgate, I would not have had enough length of cord to do so. My truck is a Standard Cab, so I don’t think there would be enough cable for anyone with an Access Cab or Double Cab with 6-foot bed, or any truck with an 8-foot bed.

- I discovered the rear camera can only be mounted one way, and there is nothing marked on it to indicate which way is up. When I first did the installation, I found that I had mounted the camera upside down because the image on the screen was upside down.

- The camera is supplied power by a cigarette lighter plug. Many newer vehicles don’t have cigarette lighter style sockets anymore and instead have USB ports, so make sure you can plug this into your vehicle before purchasing it (the camera’s power input is USB-C, so theoretically you can power it with a cord that has a USB-C plug to another USB plug).

- The Dash unit is a bit heavy. My mirror can droop with the weight when I hit bumps, and I have my mirror tightened as much possible. I also wonder how the straps will hold-up to sunlight degradation.

- My last gripe is the most frustrating, which is how to download the Cam recordings. You can view them on your camera screen at any time but removing the recordings from the camera is not the easiest. On my other unit, I can transfer them to a phone App while in my vehicle. That way if I am involved in a vehicle accident, I can immediately download the recording to my phone and show it to an officer or instantly send it to my insurance company. Unfortunately, with this model, you must remove the micro-SD card and insert it into a card reader hooked-up to a computer. My laptop doesn’t have a card reader, so I had to order one separately to be able to download my camera’s recordings; Therefore, if you don’t have a computer, then you won’t have a way to download the recordings. The micro-SD slot is also not in a convenient location for removing it for downloading purposes, it’s on top, right between the cord inputs. It would have been better to have had it on the side or on the bottom, but I really wish there was a smartphone App so removal of the SD card was not necessary.

Despite several gripes, it works as advertised, but if you purchase this, be aware of the limitations and processes to make it work as you would like.

title: Really nice bookbag with features rivaling those of packs that cost three times as much
text:
I am really impressed with this bookbag, as it has features of packs costing three times as much. It is a true 30L sized pack. For reference, the filled-out pack in my pictures has a fluffy standard sized pillow stuffed inside, so that should give you an idea of the room available. I will make this review simple by listing the pros and cons.

Pros:

- Has a laptop sleeve which is against the back-panel, which in my opinion is the best place to put it, as it keeps the weight close to your back, protects the laptop better, and has the most padding by your back. It does indeed hold a 17-inch laptop.

- Has a secret outer pocket on the outside of the pack under the lumbar pad, which is a great place to put items such as plane tickets, boarding passes, travel wallet, and passport. You can swing it around and access the pocket without removing the pack from your back, but no one else can access it when you are wearing the pack.

- Has a sewn-in strap so that it can be slid over the handle of rolling luggage.

- Has a thickly padded durable grab handle on top of the pack.

- Has a generous deep accessory pocket on the outside of the pack.

- Generous side pockets are large enough to hold a quart sized water bottle.

- Has reflective piping on the back of the pack.

- Lots of nice organizational compartments and key clip.

- Very well-padded back-panel.

- Has charging cord and port for affixing a battery bank.

- Nice lighter color lining on the inside so that it is easier to find contents.

- Made of durable water-resistant nylon materials and the stitching appears robust and durable.

- Large zipper pulls that are easy to grab.

Cons (these cons are minor, but combined they are enough of an issue to deduct one star):

- There is no waist strap, so if you need to run through an airport or across campus, the pack will bounce against your back.

- Although the straps are padded, I would have liked to see them have thicker padding, such as the thickness of the carry-handle for when you are carrying a lot of weight.

- The back-panel does not really have the advertised breathability. Yes, there is a touch of airflow and breathability, but you will sweat a lot on hot days.

- Although there are touches of reflective piping, there is no place to attach a blinky light.

- The well-padded laptop sleeve is missing some padding in one critical area, on the bottom. So, if you are holding the grab-handle or pack strap, and you then you set the bottom of the pack down hard, the bottom of your laptop will have no padding against the floor.

All in all, a really nice pack at this price-point that is great for on the travelling, on campus, or for commuting, but with a few limitations you should be aware of if you decide to purchase this pack.

title: Great Ball-Head style Tripod for the Price that is Packed with Features
text:
Although I have a higher quality tripod than this one, it is heavier and has lock-stops on the legs so that they can fold out just so far. I wanted a lighter weight tripod that I could take to the range and affix my monoscope spotting scope for sighting in optics and watching groupings. This fit the bill because the range is quite hilly and having extendable legs that also pivot up to 180-degrees allows much more versatility.

I am used to a pan tilt head with lever arm, as that is what I have used for nearly 40-years, so adjusting to this ball head takes a little getting used to. I will likely not use the monopod / hiking pole feature, but it is an interesting concept for versatility. The instructions are very spartan, and it took me a minute to understand where to put the carry strap: unscrew the hook on the bottom of the center shaft and slide it on, then reaffix the hook, and you will have a nice carry strap affixed to the tripod.

Pros:

- Very compact at 15-inches by 4-inches, and very light at approximately 3.5-pounds.

- Has the ability to convert to a monopod or hiking pole.

- Legs pivot out up to 180-degrees, allowing for use on uneven and hilly terrain.

- Bubble level aids in micro adjustments to the 360-degree ball-head.

- Legs are in four sections to aid in compactness but allow for extended height.

- Spring-loaded clip on the bottom of the tripod allows for low angle macro shots, or you can flip the legs so that the ball head is close to the ground.

- Ball head is aluminum and not plastic and comes with a protective velvet bag cover.

- Conforms to the Arca Swiss standard ball-head dovetail mount, so you can replace the quick release plate with another one of any brand of the same specs if you need to.

- Comes with a zippered carry bag that is easy to get the tripod back into.

Cons (not enough to deduct a star, especially at this price point, but items to be aware of):

- The tripod is a little wobbly, that is, the slightest vibrations do make it shake a bit when fully extended.

- Only rises to a maximum of 4.5-feet (55-inches) at its highest setting, so if you are of average height or taller, you will likely need to stoop to use it (in monopod mode you can extend it higher by only a couple of inches).

- The friction knob (with the numbered markings) and the locking knob for the ball head seem to work indistinguishably. That is, the friction knob is supposed to have more finesse in the tightening/loosening of the head than the locking knob, but it appears they have been machined to the same tolerances; I’ll just be using the locking knob. Also, the numbers on the friction knob don’t seem to really correspond to anything.

- There is quite a bit of plastic in non-stress areas, so be careful not to have them impacted.

- The carry bag is very crinkly sounding, like crinkling newspaper inside.

- Does not come with a smartphone mount.

- The included larger diameter 3/8-inch screw is not for mounting cameras or equipment utilizing 3/8-16 UNC threads, but it is only for connecting the shaft sections into a monopod.

- I question the longevity of the spring-loaded shoulder adjustment clips that allow the legs to pivot out the 180-degrees.

The cons are relatively benign based on the low cost and light weight of this tripod. I think it is a great deal and recommend it for all but the discerning of professionals.

title: Decent Binoculars for the price but with some QC issues
text:
I was really excited to receive these binoculars and I really wanted to love them, especially when I read some of the other reviews, but they came-up short for me and I was somewhat disappointed in the quality. I have a pair of 40-year-old 7x35 Nikons that I compared this to, and the quality of the sight picture on this was severely lacking as compared to the Nikons. Granted, I recognize that this pair is budget minded, but the manufacturer’s claims of optical clarity are somewhat exaggerated.

Pros:
- Very compact at only 6-inches by 5-inches and weighs only 22-ounces with the caps, which is very light for a 12x42 binocular.

- Nitrogen purged waterproof and textured tactile coating is easy to hold.

- Has a tripod thread mount, although it is lacking (see cons section).

- Focus knob is smooth with no grittiness.

- Has rotatable eyecups for eyeglass wearers.

- Has a Diopter adjustment knob so that each eye can be focused independently if necessary.

- Comes with a storage pouch, although it has no belt loop, and the neck cord is not removeable.

- Images are bright and color is distortion free.

Cons:

- I don’t consider myself as having narrow or close eyes, but I have to push the binoculars together to the closest setting to get a sight picture with the proper interpupillary distance.

- The tripod thread-mount is plastic, not metal, and I put a magnet to it to make sure. I can’t see the threads holding-up to long term use, and cross threading could easily damage the threads, rendering the mount feature useless. Also, when the interpupillary distance is at the closest setting, there is no room for a tripod mount to fit anyways.

- Now for my biggest gripe, the optical clarity. I live right in front of a mountain and ordered these for viewing the mountain and related wildlife because of the 12x42 power and lens opening and supposed optical clarity. When looking dead center, the very center of the sight picture is very clear, but the fringes of the sight picture get blurry as you move towards the edges, effectively shortening the field of view. The farther away you view, the worse this effect becomes. I spent an hour looking every which way to make sure it wasn’t me, and compared it to the Nikons, and sure enough there is a blurry ring around the sight picture. Upon further inspection, it seems that the edges of the picture are focused differently, even if they are the same distance as the center of the viewing area. If I bring the edges into focus, then the center of the picture blurs. This ended-up being a huge disappointment, as now I can only really look at the very center of the actual field of view. My old 7x35’s has a much better field of view than this pair.

I think I will be relegating this pair to become my beater-upper and looking for something else with better clarity. For the price of around 60 bucks they are certainly not bad, but they are certainly not professional grade and do not expect them to have a true clear large field of view as the manufacturer claims, and if you have a narrow face or eyes, then I don’t recommend them. I was going to deduct two stars but am only deducting one because of the price. If this was an 80-dollar binocular or more, then I would say it is only a 3-star model.

title: A Well Designed Bino Case but with a Couple of Minor Shortcomings
text:
This is an impressive Binocular case with a lot of thoughtful features, but at a price of $150 I expected a bit more function and fit & finish.

First, let’s talk about the pros:

- Very well thought out design that allows quick deployment of binoculars one-handed.
- Has a lifetime warranty.
- Case is very compact at 9.5-inches tall, 6.5-inches wide, and 3.5-inches thick at the thickest point.
- Keeps your Binos close to the chest so they don’t bounce around.
- Harness is lightweight but very comfortable and durable and has retention bungie so that the ends of the strapping don’t dangle.
- Harness has a nice breathable mesh with extra stitching at stress points, and there is the same mesh on the back of the case where it rests against your chest.
- Shoulder pads on harness have additional clip points for attaching gear.
- Case is easily removeable with durable detachable clips.
- The case is completely waterproof to keep valuables dry and secure.
- Thick and durable fabrics that appear will withstand the test of time.
- Organization compartments within to secure small items such as SD cards, smartphone, or a GPS.
- External Clip sleeves for attaching items like rangefinders, flashlights, or knives.
- Has a Belt loop on the back for when chest carry is not feasible, which can accommodate belts or straps up to 3.5-inches wide. When I am doing tactical training I either clip it to my chest rig with a large biner or attach it to my rigging belt.

Don’t get me wrong, it is a very nice case, one of the best out there. But for the price I would say it should be top notch. Here are the cons for which I am deducting one star.

- There were a lot of loose threads along the internal seams which I had to cut away and then burn the ends to prevent fraying, which can be seen in the photo of it open and empty.
- At this price I assumed it was manufactured stateside, but that is not the case.
- It has two sleeves on either side for hooking items to it, but it comes with only one hook with 3M adhesive. I really think it should have come with two hooks to affix to your accessories in case both accessories you want to use don’t have hooks themselves. Apparently additional hooks can be purchased from their website for $5 plus shipping.
- The belt loop, while in use, interferes with complete closure of the case.
- The listing indicates that the interior pockets can be used for accessories like rangefinders, but I can’t fit both 12x42 binocs and a rangefinder inside and still be able to close the case.
- Its only available in Grey, you can’t get black, tan, or camo.

Despite the cons it really is a very nice chest rig for your binoculars and accessories. If you decide to purchase this, just make sure you are aware of the limitations before you do so.

title: Decent Binoculars for the price with some nice accessories
text:
I recently received a pair of comparable binoculars from Rexmeo and was disappointed in the optical clarity of that model, so I ordered this model in hopes it would be a better unit since it retails for a bit more money. It is marginally better in a few regards, but still a 4-star model as based on some of the items I list below. I am not planning on using my smartphone with this, so I don’t have a review of the smartphone mount.

Pros:

- Very compact at only 6-inches long and 5-inches wide and it weighs a mere 16.2-ounces with the caps, which is extremely lightweight for a 12x42 binocular.

- Argon gas purged waterproof and rubbery tactile coating is easy to hold (I did not test the waterproof feature).

- Has a metal tripod thread mount that is fully accessible even when the binoculars are folded at the closest interpupillary distance (this was a problem with my Rexmeo’s).

- Focus knob is smooth with no grittiness, although not quite as nice as my other pair.

- Has rotatable eyecups for eyeglass wearers, and they are 23mm which makes finding the sight picture easier than on binoculars with smaller eyepieces (like on my other pair).

- Has a Diopter adjustment knob so that each eye can be focused independently if necessary.

- Comes with a storage pouch, although it has no belt loop, and the neck cord is not removeable.

- Images are bright and color is distortion free.

- The interpupillary distance on this model is great. On my other model I could not get it to fold close enough for my narrow eyes, but on this one I don’t have to fold it all the way in order to get a good sight picture.

- The accessory package is quite nice for these binoculars, as I have received a similar set for a monocular scope that I ordered, and the other accessory set was very cheap compared to these. Granted, these are not even remotely considered top shelf, but they are not bottom shelf either. The tripod has metal legs, which surprised me, but everything else on it is plastic. It extends to 20-inches tall, which is very respectable for a tabletop tripod. The tripod-to-binocular mount is all metal.

Cons:

- The optical clarity is better than on my Rexmeo’s, but still not as good as I would expect for a pair that is in this price range. When looking dead center, the sight picture is very clear, but the fringes of the sight picture, specifically on the bottom right and left, at the edge of the sight picture, are a little blurry. Granted, on the Rexmeo model the entire fringed edges are blurry all the way around, and it creeps inwards much more than on these, so this is a vast improvement; but I don’t think there should be any edge blurriness at all.

- Just about everything on these binoculars excluding the lenses and tripod mount, are made of plastic. That’s probably why it is so lightweight. Even the hinge is plastic, so I am concerned that if I drop it, it will easily break.

- Can we talk about the brand name for a moment, Dazftiey, that is a tongue twister!

For the price of around 90 bucks these binoculars are certainly not bad, but they are not as high a grade as other brands in this price range as it does not have optimal optical clarity. title: Binoculars with Quality Optics but a few shortcomings
text:
I have a couple of other similarly powered binoculars, 10x42 and 12x42, and with those I was somewhat disappointed with the quality of the optics. This Hontry model is marginally better in a few regards, but still a four-star model as based on some of the cons I list below. Pros:

- Fairly compact at 7-inches long and 5.45-inches wide, but not as compact as my other brand that even has a higher magnification.

- Rubbery tactile coating is easy to hold, and it has an IPX6 waterproof rating and is shockproof (I did not test the waterproof or shockproof features).

- Has a metal tripod threaded mount that is mostly accessible even when the binoculars are folded at the closest interpupillary distance (this was a problem with one of my other pairs).

- The tripod mount is deep enough to get the mount tightened all the way (this was also an issue with one of my other binoculars).

- Focus knob is very smooth with no grittiness.

- Has rotatable eyecups for eyeglass wearers, and they have a 22mm diameter, which makes finding the sight picture easier than on binoculars with smaller eyepieces (like on my other pair).

- Rotatable eyecups have the best rubber sockets I have seen on a pair like this, they are extremely comfortable.

- Has a deep 22mm deep eye-relief, which is great for folks that wear glasses. I don’t wear glasses, but I apparently have deep eye-sockets and I found these easier to use as a result.

- Has a Diopter adjustment knob so that each eye can be focused independently if necessary.

- Comes with a storage pouch, which has a belt loop, although the shoulder strap for the pouch is not removeable.

- Images are bright and the color is distortion free.

- The interpupillary distance on this model is adequate. On one of my other models, I could not get it to fold close enough for my narrow eyes, but on this one I can get it folded enough to get a good sight picture, but it still needs to be folded inwards completely (Although I have somewhat narrow eyes, they are not that narrow, and anyone with narrower eyes than I would not be able to get the eyepieces close enough for proper viewing).

Cons:

- A little hefty at 25.4-ounces as compared to my other models (but it does feel sturdier).

- Unsure if it is Nitrogen or Argon gas purged, which would prevent fogging, as there is no mention of this in the specifications.

- The optical clarity is better than on my other binoculars, but still not as good as I would expect for a pair that is in this price range. When looking dead center, the sight picture is very clear, but the lower edges of the sight picture, specifically on the fringes at the bottom right and left at the edge of the sight picture, are a little blurry. They’re better than my other pair that has a similar issue, but these are twice the cost and I expect perfect clarity on the fringes; there should not be any edge blurriness at all. Most binoculars in the C-note-plus-a-Grant price range do not have this drawback.

- When I installed my tripod mount, I could not get the binoculars folded all the way to get the eyepieces close enough for me to see a proper sight picture. Granted, this may be because the tripod mount I am using is only 2.75-inches long and .75-inches wide with only a 1.25-inch-long scallop, so it may not be an issue so much as with the binoculars, but it may be an issue with the tripod mount. I have ordered a longer skinnier tripod mount to see if that solves the issue.

For the price of around 150 bucks these binoculars are certainly not bad, but they are not as high a grade as other brands in this price range since it does not have comparable optical clarity on the fringes of the viewing picture. If you are someone with narrow eyes this may be a good model to pick-up, and if you want a model that works with a tripod, this may also a good selection. If you wear eyeglasses or have deep eye sockets, the eye relief on this pair is ideal.

title: Entry-Level telescope with Several QC Issues
text:
I was really excited to order this telescope but was disappointed with the build quality upon receiving it. Although I am an amateur, I recall the days of my youth looking at the stars with a similar spec’d telescope and was excited to be able to use this for not only stargazing, but as a spotting scope to view the mountains around my home.

I recognize that this is a budget entry-level model, so I wasn’t expecting anything stellar, but this telescope was more akin to a toy than a precision instrument. Out of the box the finder scope was in pieces and the camera mount was broken as well.

Pros:

- It very lightweight and portable and comes with a carrying storage bag.

- Assembly is straightforward and instruction manual is easy to navigate.

- Works well for viewing the moon.

Cons:

- This telescope is made almost entirely out of plastic, including the housing and tube.

- My finder scope was in pieces upon arrival. It took me sometime, but I was able to finally get it back together again, but I stabbed myself to the point of drawing blood in doing so, as the crosshairs are made of a needle-thin wire that extends out from its housing.

- The finder scope does not have a diagonal image corrector, so all images are upside-down in the finder scope, which is not useful for finding terrestrial objects.

- My Camera Mount also arrived in pieces, which does not attest to the durability of this item even if it arrives for you intact.

- The tripod is a bit short for an adult at 48-inches, and the lens tray only works with this tripod, so if you switch to a taller tripod, you likely won’t be able to use the lens tray. In addition, I couldn’t get all the tripod adjustments to fully lock tight.

- The storage bag, although a nice addition, is very cheap and it sounds like crinkling newspaper when touching the interior.

- As I was setting-up this telescope, my fingernail grazed the painted logo and brand name, which scraped right off where touched. I ended-up just removing those altogether.

- As expected with the use of a 70mm telescope, when using the eyepieces, very little light gets to the eye. Although the moon is crisp and bright, this telescope is really just too dim for properly viewing most other celestial bodies.

I think this telescope should really be selling for half of its going rate. I have ordered some higher quality magnifying eyepieces to see if I have any better luck viewing celestial bodies other than the moon, but I do recognize the limitations of the 70mm aperture. I think your money would be better spent getting something else that is a leg-up in quality.

title: It does what it claims, but getting it there is no small feat
text:
Let me start by saying that it works, but getting it to work took some effort, as the instructions were not written by someone with a command of the English language, and they were written for someone that is probably a professional in the tech industry… and I don’t think they could have made the writing on the instruction manual any tinier.

My router is on one side of the house, my office in the middle, and spotty reception is on the other end of my house near my kitchen where I installed an outdoor security camera outside the kitchen door. I picked-up this unit so that I could not only use my phone in my kitchen, but so that my security camera could get a strong enough signal to work properly. I chose this unit because it said you could set it up via a phone or laptop, and not necessarily using an Ethernet cable. I also live very rural where cell phone coverage is spotty at best, so I use my phone over my wifi connection for dependable calls.

First off, trying to decipher the manual gave me a headache. Secondly, I could not get the extender to work on my phone to get it setup. When I entered the password, which is “admin” by the way, nothing would happen. Using an ethernet cable was not an option with my particular router and laptop, so I was extremely frustrated.

I did eventually get it setup, and this is how I did it. I plugged it into the wall, and then looked for it as a Wifi connection on my laptop. Once I found it, I connected to it and used the “admin” password. Once I entered the password I was connected to a menu where I was able to select my home network and enter that password, and it was then connected to my home network and its name changed to my home network’s name plus “Ext”.

I then took the extender and plugged it in to an outlet in my kitchen. The plug is obtrusively in the middle of the extender, so it unfortunately takes-up the space of two outlets. But I was finally able to stream videos in my kitchen and the signal strength of my security camera went from 54-percent all the way up to 100-percent. I also can now make and receive phone calls from my kitchen. The IMPORTANT thing you need to know, is that you must connect to the Extender as if it is a separate network, or you’ll just be connected to your router. For example, if your Network is called “My Home”, the Extender will have a Network name of “My Home EXT” and be listed as a separate network which your device will need to connect to INSTEAD of to your router’s connection.

So, if it works, why am I deducting 2 stars? Because setting it up was way more difficult than it should have been. The instructions are terrible, and I just couldn’t get it setup from my smartphone. The listing indicates that the unit has two ethernet ports, but in actuality it has only one, and it is so lightweight that I question the long-term durability of this extender. Lastly, you must connect your device to the Extender “network”, it’s not a Wi-Fi booster, but a separate network device for which your phone or other personal device will need to be configured to.

title: High Quality Security Camera with Lots of Features at a Great Price
text:
I already have a few security cameras mounted around my home, that also use the CloudEdge App, and I purchased this unit to mount above my side-yard specifically because it works on the same app. This completes the security network I’ve setup around my homestead, and I am very pleased with this camera. I live very rural, and an alarm system isn’t viable for me because no one would be around to hear it, and the police wouldn’t respond for hours, so having security cameras at least lets me monitor my homestead and record any intruders. This camera is one of the better ones I have added to my network and am giving it 5-stars.

Setting this up on the existing CloudEdge App that is on my smartphone was easy and it synced without an issue to my mesh Wi-Fi network that works by meshing both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz together; if you live in Central to Southern Virginia and are connected to the Firefly Broadband network, this unit will work for you. Having several cameras on the same App simplifies viewing my security network, and I can view all the cameras simultaneously on a split screen on my phone if I wish.

This unit is nice and small which makes it easier to install in tight places; it’s the smallest of all the cameras I added to my network. The camera body itself is only 3.5-inches tall, just under 2-inches wide, and a hair over 2-inches deep including the lenses. Some of the other cameras I own are larger but have adjustable antennae ears for better Wi-Fi reception. Fortunately, this isn’t mounted too far from my router, so a model with antennae was not necessary for me this time. If you’re going to be mounting your camera more than 20-feet from your router, you may want a model that has antennae ears instead. Also understand that this is a fixed camera and that it will not pan or tilt on its own.

Be aware that this camera does not come with a charger or solar panel, it comes with just a short micro-USB to USB-A charging cable. I’ve hooked this camera up to a 3W solar panel with micro-USB connection, that is mounted facing South, and it keeps this camera charged perfectly fine.

I installed a 32GB Micro SD Card, that I ordered separately, into the camera, and it works great with plenty of storage for my needs; So, I won’t be bothering with a cloud subscription. Playback of recordings on your phone is relatively easy using the App, and you can also live-record to your phone’s camera roll.

Resolution is great, and nighttime recording works very well. One of my other cameras records in only 1080 resolution, but this one is in 2K resolution and so much better; I wish I had all my cameras in 2K. For live viewing, be aware that there is a 1 to 3 second delay from what you see on the screen to what is actually happening, just like on my other cameras.

I really like that as a feature of the App, you can adjust the sensitivity on the camera so that it is more or less sensitive to picking up motion. I’m able to get it sensitive enough that it picks up movement from the periphery of the sight radius.

Is there anything I find deficient? Like with my other cameras, I wish I could do live camera viewing on my computer monitor and not just on my smartphone, as there is no way to do that; I can only view recordings on my computer that I’ve uploaded from my smartphone’s camera roll. As I mentioned on the reviews of my other cameras, I also wonder about the long-term viability of a product that relies on a Smartphone App to work (will there be support and updates for the App for the foreseeable future, and what if the company goes out of business and/or the App stops working, will my camera become useless?), that’s why I ordered this camera of a different brand than those of my other cameras, but they are still all dependent on continuous support and updates to the same App.

Amazingly this camera is half the cost of the similar camera that I ordered which is in only 1080 resolution, and it is this is the smallest of all my cameras and has been the easiest to install and setup. The only drawback to this camera as compared to most of my other cameras, is that it is not as powerful for picking-up a Wi-Fi signal, but knowing that upfront, I think this is one of the best deals out there on a security camera. It is easy to setup, easy to use, doesn’t require a cloud subscription, and works on a 2.4 GHz/ 5 GHz mesh network (does NOT work on a standalone 5 GHz network). If you’re looking for a security camera, I highly recommend this one!

title: Multipurpose Tripod that has Decent Features at this Price Range
text:
I specifically ordered this tripod to use with a spotting scope that I have, because the tripod that came with the Spotting scope is too short and I find I must stoop or sit to use it. The height of this tripod is what caught my attention for this unit.

This tripod is a bit heavy for its size, probably because of the ability to reorient the center support rod, at over 3.35 pounds (53.6-ounces), but most everything else about it works well enough.

Pros:

- Flick Lever Lock adjustments on the legs.

- Foam lining on one leg for easier carrying in cold weather.

- Included zippered carrying/storage case with strap instead of a cheap storage sack with drawstrings.

- Broad range of adjustability.

- Quick-release plate for quick removal or re-installation of camera.

- Built in Bubble Levels at both the leg shoulders and by the camera mount.

- Self-adjusting/leveling feet on ball sockets work well on uneven ground.

- Can get very low to the ground in the lowest position: 22-inches and extends camera up to nearly 75-inches high.

- Has a hook on the bottom of the tripod for hanging a camera for macro shots.

- Does not have the spring-loaded shoulder adjustment clips that are common to other tripods, which so easily break.

- Large panning handle is easy to use for scopes, binoculars, and telescopes.

- Comes with a spare mounting plate as well as a smartphone mount and metal ground spike feet adaptors.

- The entire head on the tripod is easily removeable if you want to upgrade it with something more robust.

Cons (Deducting one star for these):

- A little on the heavy side at over 3.35 pounds (53.6oz) for its size.

- Excluding the leg shafts, most of the tripod is made of plastic components that could cause long-term durability issues. Even the head and camera mount are plastic.

- The tripod is a little wobbly when fully extended, and the slightest vibrations do make it shake a bit, but that is probably because the legs are in four sections and the bottom sections are very thin as a result. It probably would have been better if it were a three-section legged tripod.

- The center shaft is entirely made of plastic. Which means the teeth on the center column for engaging the hand crank can easily wear out.

- The height adjustment hand-crank knob for the center shaft is also plastic. A lot of torque is put on this knob, so I am concerned it may break. I also hate crank arms on tripods, as it is not smooth or quick to use. I would have preferred a flick lever or tightening turn-knob for quick adjustments of the center shaft.

- The pan/tilt handle/bar does not actually control the tilt tightening like on all my other tripods. It’s just a handle. There is a separate knob to the left of it for tightening and loosening the vertical tilt adjustments. This is somewhat annoying and cumbersome, requiring two-handed operation for vertical tilt adjustments.

The cons are not so bad since this is a tripod of around fifty bucks at the time of this writing. I think it is a decent deal and recommend it for anyone looking for a compact tripod that is not of the ball-head style as long as you understand its limitations and annoyances before making the purchase.

title: Wonderful Wi-Fi Projector that Easily Adds Big Screen Entertainment
text:
This is my first Wi-Fi projector, and I am very excited to have received this. We don’t have a large-screen TV in our home, so this allows us to have big screen entertainment without the bulk or cost of a big screen TV. It also allows us to easily change the location of where we want to watch a movie, such as taking it outside, and because it is so portable, we can take it with us on vacations to mountain cabins or to the beach.

Setup was fairly straightforward and easy to navigate, although you will need to use the remote to do so. When you turn-on the projector, a menu is displayed from the lens to your wall or screen, and you have to navigate through the menu to do things like enable Bluetooth connections and to connect the projector to your Wi-Fi for Airplay enabling. I have been using this by mirroring my iPhone screen through my Wi-Fi connection, and it has worked very well. I was happy to see that there is a built-in speaker in the projector, but I did hook-up an external speaker for better audio clarity and volume.

When using the remote, remember to point it at the projector and not the screen; I kept forgetting about that. This unit has a standard throw ratio of 1.38, so it may not give you a large enough screen if using it in a very small room (you would need something else with a short throw or ultra-short throw for very small room use where you want a large image but can’t have the projector far enough away from the screen).

The 1080p resolution looks sharp and I was impressed with the image quality. This projector has a contrast ratio of 10,000:1, which has deeper blacks in the images than lower quality projectors, but understand that in reality, this is only realized in a darkened room. Although a Polyester/spandex screen is provided, it is not the best for indoor viewing, so we used an old slide projector screen that we had, and it worked very well for getting a nice image.

Pros:

- Image quality is very sharp and bright. Works well in a darkened room (but not so well if there is a lot of daylight). Has native 1080p resolution. If you want more resolution, you’ll need a pricier unit that has 4k UHD, but 1080p is more than adequate for most needs and it supports a wider range of inputs.

- Color transmission is great and looks true to type and is not washed out or too blue.

- The light source is a long-lasting LED, which does not get as hot as a bulb and lasts longer (this is not a laser light source).

- Focus uniformity is very good, although I wouldn’t call it great. There is a little blurriness and distortion at the very edges of the viewing image, although at this price-point it is not enough of an issue to bother me.

- Wireless streaming and connections will work both on 2.4G and 5G wireless networks.

- The projector has a built-in speaker, but you can connect external speakers as well, either via Bluetooth or through a 3.5mm audio jack connection.

- Has multiple input/output ports, such as 3.5mm headphone and AV ports, HDMI ports, USB-A port, and even the older VGA port.

- Supports wireless connections such as IOS Mirroring and Airplay, as well as Android Airplay.

- The AV ports allow you to connect Gaming Consoles and DVD players to the projector (although the input lag is not listed, so I don’t know how well gaming that require fast inputs will work).

- It is very lightweight and portable at just under 3-pounds (but there is no internal battery, it must be plugged-in to use). It is 8.5-inches wide, by 6.5-inches deep, and 3.25-inches tall.

- Has a tripod/wall/ceiling mount screw hole. Although it is not centered on the bottom of the unit, so if using a tabletop tripod, the projector can be somewhat unbalanced.

- Comes in a nice, padded storage case, with an HDMI-to-HDMI cable, an AV Cable, and a remote that uses two AAA batteries (batteries are *not* provided).

- Has a removeable/cleanable cooling fan filter on the outside of the projector.

- Comes with a bonus 100-inch cloth spandex style screen that can be hung from the wall via grommets and adhesive tabs. Although the material, which feels like polyester, is very thin, and if hung against wall hangings, you will be able to see the outline of what is behind it. This screen really is best for doing temporary outside yard setups where there is no wall where it can be stretched-out with no creases or folds visible, rather than using it as a dedicated indoor screen.

Cons (I am deducting one star for these):

- I was surprised that at this price-point (at the time I ordered it was advertised at $370, but has since dropped to $230), that it does not support Dolby Sound. If a movie is playing in Dolby, the device it is playing from must have the Dolby turned-off, or else no sound will come out of the projector or any connected speakers. If the device the movie is playing from cannot turn-off Dolby, then the movie cannot be played at all because you won’t be able to get any sound.

- Claimed Lumen Brightness in not in ANSI Lumens, which gives a true sense of how it would work with Daylight in the background. The light source lumen output is listed as 9000-lumens, which is just an indication of the brightness of the LED chip within the projector, and not the brightness of the actual projected image. Viewing with daylight pollution washes-out the image quite a bit. I did a search for the ANSI lumens for this unit, and all I could find was something that said it had a brightness of 1800 Lumens, which means it is best viewed in a semi-dark to fully darkened room. Using it outside in the day won’t work, and in a bright room it will be washed-out quite a bit.

- You need to use the remote to be able to use most of the projector functions. If you lose the remote or if the remote breaks, you won’t be able to do most connection functions to the projector.

- The optical Keystone adjustment knob has a very limited range of adjustment. You really need to keep the base of the projector as parallel to the ground as possible, or else your image will be trapezoidal, narrower at the bottom at wider at the top (or reverse that if projected from the ceiling). So, putting it on a table or tripod may be required depending on how high the screen is.

- If using a Bluetooth connected speaker, when you power down the projector after you are finished using it, you need to remember to turn off the Bluetooth function from the projector first. Otherwise, the next time you turn-on the projector, it will automatically look for the same Bluetooth device and no sound will be emitted from the projector at all no matter what audio source you try and connect unless you go in and turn off the Bluetooth setting, and then turn it back on if connecting a Bluetooth device again.

- Apparently, this projector does not support all types of Bluetooth devices. Older Bluetooth devices may not work, and the manual does not indicate what versions do or do not work.

- You can hear the fan on the projector, which is a little louder than I expected. I had to turn-up the volume on what I was watching to drown it out.

- It claims to support 4k viewing but be aware that it does not actually project in 4k. It will take a 4k video and downscale it to 1080p in order to project it.

- Does not have a USB-C input port, which I expect these days.

Understand that this projector is only as good as the screen it is projected on. The supplied fabric screen is a nice addition, but it’s not the best for optimal viewing. To take advantage of the true colors, ratios, and illumination of the projector, you need a screen that will have the proper gain for the room in which it is viewed and the amount of ambient light that you are using it in, to realize the benefits of the projector’s specs. At the current advertised price, I think it is a decent deal on a well thought out projector, but make sure you understand the limitations of this unit before committing to ordering this particular projector.

title: Sturdy Metal Phone Tripod Mount with a Multitude of Configurations
text:
The other day I accidentally tipped over my tripod and broke yet another plastic phone mount. So, I decided to get a metal phone mount as a replacement, as I already have one made by Ulanzi that I like very much. I am really pleased with the phone mount as well. It is configurable both horizontally and vertically, as well as forwards and backwards, which when combined with the multitude of adjustments on my tripod, makes it easy to get my phone in the exact position I would like. Also, because it tilts forward and back, it will work well on a tabletop tripod or selfie stick that does not have those adjustments.

Pros:
- Durable metal construction lends to longevity of the unit.

- Fairly Stiff Spring-loaded arms extends to 3.5 inches (8.9cm, which is 89mm) to accommodate most phones within a case (but not all of them!), and it will keep good tension on the phone so that it doesn’t fall off.

- 5/8-inch 0.63 inches deep so that it can grab a phone within a thick case.

- It fits my iPhone 6s which is in a life proof case, that also has a Nite-ize steelie socket on the back of it, without any problems.

- Rubberized foam type texture on the back and on the arms to get s good hold on the phone without scratching or damaging it.

- You can adjust the tension of the joint/hinges using a supplied Hex wrench.

- Has two Cold Shoe mounts for adding accessories to either side of the phone, such as lighting and a microphone.

Cons:

title: Quality Binoculars that are Comfortable and Well-Constructed
text:
I have a couple of other similarly powered binoculars that have the same price-point, and with all but one of those I was somewhat disappointed with the quality of the optics. This Hidegazer model is quite a bit better in a few regards, and what I would consider a 4.25-star model, so the best one I have tested so far.

Hidegazer apparently has for sale a couple of other similar models that are also 10x42. One is eighty-nine dollars (model HD110), and the other is two-hundred and forty-nine dollars (model ED580). The eighty-nine-dollar version is not waterproof or fog-proof and has a smaller ocular lens. The only differences I can tell between this model and the pricier model are in the diameter of the ocular lens (this one has the largest at 24mm), and the other model has a shorter eye relief, 15mm as opposed to the 18mm on this model. The other model can also focus on nearby objects that are a couple of feet closer. This model is the ED350.

Pros:

- Nicely compact at 6-inches long and 4.75-inches wide.

- Rubbery tactile coating is easy to hold, and it has an IPX7 waterproof rating, which means it can be submerged up to 1 meter in water for 30 minutes (I did not test the waterproof feature).

- It is nitrogen filled which keeps the internal side of the lenses fog-proof.

- Has a metal tripod threaded mount that is accessible even when the binoculars are folded at the closest interpupillary distance (this was a problem with some of my other pairs).

- Focus knob is very smooth with no grittiness, but I do wish it had a bit more resistance as it spins a little too easily.

- Has rotatable eyecups for eyeglass wearers, and they have a 24mm diameter, which are the largest I have seen on a 10x42 model, and which makes finding the sight picture easier than on binoculars with smaller eyepieces.

- The rotatable eyecups have very comfortable rubber sockets; they aren’t quite as nice as those on the comparably priced Hontry model that I have, but they are certainly better than anything else I have seen.

- Has a deep 18mm eye-relief, which is great for folks that wear glasses. I don’t wear glasses, but I apparently have deep eye-sockets and I found these easier to use as a result. They’re not quite as nice as my Hontry model, but very close.

- Has a Diopter adjustment knob so that each eye can be focused independently if necessary.

- Comes with a very well-constructed storage pouch, which has a robust belt loop, and the shoulder strap for the pouch is removeable. The neck strap for the binoculars is wide and made with a very comfortable padded neoprene type material.

- Images are bright and the color is distortion free.

- The interpupillary distance on this model is the best I have encountered, even better than my Hontry model. On some of my other models, I could not get them to fold close enough for my narrow eyes, but on this one I can get it folded more than enough and it still has room to be folded quite a bit further. This will work well for anyone with narrow eyes and even some children.

Cons:

- A little hefty at 25.3-ounces as compared to my other models (but it does feel sturdier).

- The tripod mount is not deep enough to get the mount tightened all the way (this was also an issue with one of my other binoculars).

- The optical clarity is better than any of my other binoculars, but still not quite as good as I would expect for a pair that is in this price range. When looking dead center, the sight picture is very clear, but on the lower left and right edges of the sight picture, just a bit on the fringes, there is a little bit of distortion/blurriness.

- The lens caps on the objective lenses are hard to get snapped into place so that they don’t flop out. Fortunately, they have tails that keep them affixed to the housing so that they are not easily lost.

- I’m not sure how shockproof / impact-resistant these are, and there is no mention of that as a feature in the listing or manual.

For the price of around 150 bucks these binoculars are certainly a well-made pair of optics, but they are not as high a grade as some other brands in this price range since it does not have comparable optical clarity on the lower fringes of the viewing picture, and because the tripod threaded socket is not as deep as it should be. If you are someone with narrow eyes then this model would be ideal for you, and if you wear eyeglasses or have deep eye sockets, the eye relief on this pair is great.

title: Quality Binoculars But They Do Not Stand-Out
text:
I have a few other similarly powered binoculars, and with some of those I was somewhat disappointed with the quality of the optics. This Birds of Prey model is quite a bit better in a several regards, but it is certainly the most expensive of the lot, and I don’t see it any better than some models that go for half as much. Is it worth the asking price of nearly three Franklins? I will let you be the judge, but there are many other pairs out there that cost far less that I feel are just as good as these.

Pros:

- Nicely compact at 6-inches long and 5-inches wide and weighing in at 20-ounces.

- The rubbery tactile coating is easy to hold, and it claims to be waterproof (I did not test the waterproof feature).

- It has a metal tripod threaded mount that is accessible even when the binoculars are fully folded to the closest interpupillary distance (this has been a problem with some of my other pairs).

- The knurled metal focus knob is very smooth with no wobble or grittiness.

- Has rotatable eyecups for eyeglass wearers, and they have a 19mm diameter, which are a decent size for a 10x42 model, which makes finding the sight picture easier than on binoculars with smaller eyepieces, although I have some 10x42 models that do have larger eyepieces, up to 24mm.

- The rotatable eyecups have fairly comfortable rubber sockets, but they are not nearly as comfortable as those on a Hontry model that I have which is half the price.

- It has the standard Diopter adjustment knob on the right eye so that each eye can be focused independently if needed.

- Images are bright and the color is distortion free. There is no blurriness or deformation of the images around the fringes of the sight picture.

- The interpupillary distance on this model is excellent. On some of my other models, I could not get them to fold close enough for my narrow eyes, but on this pair, I can get it folded far enough with still a bit of room to fold it further. This pair should work well for those with narrow eyes and even some children.

Cons:

- I am unsure if these binoculars are Nitrogen or Argon gas purged, which would prevent internal fogging, as there is no mention of this in the manual or the listing’s specifications.
- The finish could have been better for a pair of this cost. There was glue slop on the focus knob that was difficult to remove.

- Although these are advertised as waterproof, there is No IPX rating given, so it is hard to know if they are just safe in a light rainstorm or something more severe.

- Eye relief is not specified. I don’t wear glasses, but I apparently have deep eye-sockets and I found these fairly easy to use, but someone who wears glasses would want to know the specific eye relief so that they would know if it might strain their eyes.

- It comes with a very basic storage pouch which does not have a belt loop and the neck strap is not removeable. I would have expected a better storage pouch at this price point.

- The instructions are not written by someone with a command of the English language. Not that instructions are really needed for these, but for the price of this unit, I would have expected proper proofreading of any supplied manual.

- I’m not sure how impact-resistant / shockproof these are, and there is no mention of that as a feature in the listing or manual. The hinge is also plastic, and I question the durability of that critical spot if these are accidentally dropped.

For the price of around three-hundred dollars these binoculars are certainly a well-made pair of optics, but I don’t see them as any better than pairs selling for half the cost. If you are someone with narrow eyes, then this model would work well for you, and if have deep eye sockets you will find these comfortable. But I would take a hard look at the Hontry and Hidegazer brands that seem every bit as good as these but at half the asking price.

text:

The smaller Plossls and the color filters need both better atmospheric conditions than what most folks have access to, as well as a telescope with a wide aperture that brings in a lot of light to really be useful. You might be better off saving some money and just getting the larger Plossl, Barlow Lens, and Moon Filter because realistically 99% of folks won’t need or be able to use the majority of the items in this set, and if you can utilize all of what’s in this case, then you likely have a telescope that would be better suited to a much higher quality set.

title: It Works but it Does Have Some Drawbacks
text:
I’d been wanting a digital picture frame for a while and was excited to receive this one. Once you get it setup and working, it is a nice frame, but I will say that setup and instructions are lacking, and the App needs work. Fortunately, you can bypass the App and upload pictures to the frame using either a USB stick, memory card, or the supplied mini-USB to USB-A cord that I assume you can connect directly to your computer (I have not tried that last option).

Once you have your pictures uploaded to the frame, you can have the frame either display one picture or cycle through as many selected photos as you wish, and a selected speed/duration of time for each photo. You can increase or decrease the intensity of the brightness, and you can even use the frame as a display for time, date, and weather, which you can have take up the whole frame, or share it with a photo.

Despite how much I like this frame, there are several drawbacks to be aware of if you decide to order this:

- This needs to be plugged-in using the power adaptor all the time to work. There is no battery.

- To upload photos using Wifi, you must use their App or email the photos to the frame to an email address in the settings menu of the frame (I have not tried the email option).

- To use the App, you must register an account using your personal email address, and it requires you to upload an avatar photo. There is no way around this if you decide to use the App.

- The included instruction manual only refers to using the frame in conjunction with the App. There is little to no information on using the frame without the App, which you can do, but you’ll have to figure it out on your own using the touchscreen on the frame.

- When I first started using the frame, the images were too bright. The manual has no reference as to how to change it. After some time I figured it out. I went to “Settings” on the frame’s screen, and then to “Customis” (yes, it is spelled that way), and was able to change the brightness, and the volume for the touchscreen clicks.

- The App is clunky and not easy to navigate, even if following the instruction manual. On my iPhone, I wanted to crop a few photos, but when I got to the cropping page on the App, all the buttons were in Chinese characters. Fortunately, I found a crop function on the frame’s menu settings without using the App.

- The Weather function requires you to select a city from the frame’s list of cities. I am in the rural Appalachian Mountains of Virginia, and it didn’t have any nearby cities or towns listed, not even Charlottesville, VA. I ended-up finding a city in the list that is on the other side of the mountains, so my weather information is not accurate to where I actually live. If you live in or near a big city, this feature will likely work for you, but if you are rural, it will be disappointing.

- The cord to connect to a computer uses a mini-USB connection to the frame. This is a very outdated connection. I would have preferred it be USB-C so that it would be easy to use another cord if you lose the included cord.

I did upload photos both using the App and using a USB stick. I prefer the stick for simplicity and so that I don’t have to use the App. I am only using this as a picture frame, I did not try music or videos, which can be uploaded using the App, and possibly uploaded using the other non-App methods. So to sum up, this frame works, but with a slew of caveats. Based on the drawbacks, I would consider this a 3.5-star item, but since Amazon doesn’t allow half-star ratings, I am rounding-up to 4-stars.

title: Trouble-Free Installation
text:
I installed this card on a Dell Dimension 8200 desktop PC. I am running a network using equipment from various manufacturers. The router is made by Netgear, that is compatible with both 802.11b and 802.11g standards. In all, I have four dekstop PCs and one laptop sharing a DSL connection. My intention is to eventually upgrade to a router with higher speed. Most likely the Linksys with Speedbooster.

The installation itself was quite easy. My only complaint is that the long antenna of this adapter gets tangled with all of the other wires/cables that are connected on the back of my computer. Perhaps the best installation technique is to put this adapter on the top-most PCI slot. That way, all of the other wires and cables will be underneath the unit and will not tangle with the antenna above the adapter.

This PC is the farthest one from the router. Therefore, it receives the weakest signal. This adapter is no better than my older D-Link 520 adapters at receiving the signal. With a weak signal, the adapter is running at 5.5 Mbps. However, when it is getting good signal, it does run at the highest speed that "standard" 802.11g is capable of. With a router upgrade, that speed should increase.

For your information, my computer system has a Pentium 4 processor, 512MB of RDRAM, and Windows XP Pro. The device driver that came with the adapter is working fine with this system. Users with Windows XP and Windows 2000 will get the most benefit from this adapter. The Speedbooster capability is only available to those using these operating systems. Soon, I will upgrade my router to a Linksys unit with the Speedbooster ability.
item_title: Cisco-Linksys WMP54GS Wireless-G PCI Card with SpeedBooster

title: Nice!
text:
This router is basically the WRT54G, with the addition of Linksys' Speedbooster technology. It can service all 802.11g, as well as the older 802.11b, based networks. Or it can serve a network consisting of a mixture of those two standards. In short, this is a very versatile router to have.

The Speedbooster technology provides an additional increase in network speed over the typical 54mbs of the 802.11g standard. This is very useful if you like to transfer large files between your computers. The extra speed should help things move along just a little quicker. But keep in mind that this will probably not give you any additional increase over the internet. Probably because the wireless connection between the router and your computer is not the bottleneck. The Speedbooster capability can only be fully utilized if your operating system is either Windows 2000 or Windows XP.

Setting up this router was easy. My PCI wireless desktop adapter is also made by linksys. The ethernet card on my older computer is a standard issue IBM.

I highly recommend this wireless router to anyone who frequently transfers large files from one computer to another. I have had the router in operation for over a week, and so far, it has not dropped my internet connection.

For your information, my current network consists of two desktop computers (Dell 8200 and an IBM 300PL). The Dell is connected wirelessly, using a Linksys wireless adapter with the Speedbooster capability. The IBM has the original IBM network card. Speedstream DSL modem. The Dell is running on Windows XP Pro and the IBM has Windows 2000 Server.
item_title: Cisco-Linksys WRT54GS Wireless-G Broadband Router with SpeedBooster

title: Solid Adapter
text:
This is another solid product from Linksys. The adapter functions like an adapter should function. The installation was simple and free of complications. I have not experienced any break in communication between the laptop and the router.

For your information, this card is installed on a Dell Latitude C610 laptop. The operating system on the laptop is Windows 2000. The other components of my network are as follows: A Dell Dimension 8200, with a Linksys desktop adapter(with Speedbooster also). The Dell is running with Windows XP Pro. The second PC in the system is an old IBM 300PL, which is connected directly to the router through ethernet. A Linksys WRT54GS (Speedbooster) ties it all together. The network has been solid. No drop-offs.

There is really only reason that this adapter did not get five stars from me. In my opinion, the range of the card should have been greater. Even with a straight line of sight from the router, I cannot go far without losing a high percentage of the signal. So far, that has not caused any issues. However, I probably cannot go to the garage and surf the internet, for example.

I can recommend this card to a home user. In a home environment, the limited range of the card should not be an issue at all. For business use, I would probably try to find a Cisco Aeronet.

title: Awesome Microplayer
text:
The IPod Shuffle is the smallest member of the IPod family. It is also a single-purpose device. It is only a music player. And just like the other IPods, a lot of thought went into its design as far as aesthetics are concerned.

The Shuffle comes with a small dock that serves multiple duties. The dock allows the Shuffle to connect to your computer or laptop. It is also the charging cradle. The same jack, or port, that powers the headphones also serves as the charging port and the pc connection port. The USB port also supplies the current to recharge the Shuffle's battery. Basically, this is a very efficient, and a very minimalists design.

Loading songs from iTunes is very easy. Just make sure that you have the latest version of iTunes on your computer. The 1 GB capacity is more than adequate for my intended use of the system. And, since the system will only hold songs (no video), that should be plenty of space for most users. Sound quality is quite good. Perhaps you can even improve that by upgrading and buying a more expensive set of headphones.

Perhaps the biggest attraction of this system is it's small size. Perfect for those situations that call for you to be discrete. What is an example of a situation that might call for having a very discrete music player? Ok, picture this scenario. You're a college student and you already have a 4.0 grade point average. But you still have to attend that boring lecture on tax laws in order to fulfill the attendance requirement for your business law class. Ok, obviously, you wouldn't want to get caught listening to your music instead of paying attention to the professor talking about how, in his opinion, graduated income taxes affect the emotional cycle of the average housewife. This little shuffle is perfect for that, especially for those large classes that are held in auditoriums instead of traditional classrooms. Please understand, Citan does not encourage this type of irresponsible behavior. The pursuit of knowledge, and your desire for intellectual development, are more important uses of your time than listening to your IPod. That is, unless you're old man promised you, in writing, that you're gonna inherit ten million dollars.

Do you like to listen to music while working out? The Shuffle is the perfect size for that. The built in clip can attach to just about any part of your clothing. Well, ok, there are exceptions. No doubt some people enjoy working out, while wearing as little as possible. You know, that Jessica Biel lookalike with a perfect body that hangs out at the local gym? The Goddess that has a "bareable" physique? Yeah, that's the one. The one whose outfit can compete with the Shuffle's minimalists design? Perhaps even the Shuffle won't find an attachment point in her outfit. Ok, ok, we've gotten sidetracked. Back to the Shuffle.

The Shuffle itself feels durable. And there are no moving mechanical parts to wear out. The headphones might not last the life of the system though. Especially if you use the system while working out. In my experience, sweat will eventually destroy the headphones. Sweat gets inside the phones, dries up, and perhaps leaves a buildup that will prevent them from functioning after a while. But they are easily replaced. I believe that it will be the battery that will determine the life of the system. As long as the battery continues to function properly and hold a charge, the system will be useful.

I recommend this system for anyone who needs to be able to listen to their music in a discreet manner. The Shuffle also makes a good workout companion for those who like to listen to music while they sweat away the pounds. Users who need to have a multi-function device will obviously have to look elsewhere. Consider a Zune or a Nano if you want to show off pictures of your children, sweetheart, or pet.
