title: Among the best of the dash cams I've tested.  Great functionality, easy to operate - even while driving!
text:
First, please note that in the photos I’m posting, none of the blurriness at the side of the photos appears on the videos in any videos I’ve shot. In the videos the entire image is very clear, no blurriness anywhere. I would post a video, but so far as I’ve been able to determine the Amazon system degrades hi-res video, and uploading video that I’ve res’d down seems counterproductive when I’m trying to convey the quality of an HD camera.

I’ve reviewed several of these dash cams at this point, and I now know fairly well what attributes I want them to have. Different people will have different requirements as to the features they’re looking for, e.g., video cycling, locking files, battery back-up (in case of a crash), etc. However, while I recommend looking at and considering those things, keep in mind that if the cam isn’t easy to operate while you’re driving those features might as well not even exist. This cam has only four large buttons and is very easy to operate.

I’ll try to put somewhat random thoughts in an order that makes sense:

Attachment to the windshield is easy, and the suction mechanism provides among the best hold I’ve encountered while still being easy to remove. This is important in the event of a crash, but also because there can be the extra weight of the power cord pulling on the cam. The cam swivels in all directions, X, Y, and Z axis.

The power cord and the (required) micro SD card are installed on the right side of the cam. There is also a “Reset” button on that side. It hasn’t happed for me yet with this cam, but an easy reset is great if the camera ever freezes. (That’s happened to me with a cam I have used but did not review – long story - and it was a big problem.)

The four control buttons are along the bottom, facing toward you as you drive. They’re limited to “back,” “up,” “down,” and “OK,” but the functionality of those four buttons is expanded by the symbols/icons that appear on the screen just above each button. That is, the icons and menu choices on the screen change based on your input, but the basic function of the four buttons remains essentially the same. I’m not sure what I just wrote will make sense, but I think it will when you use the cam. Regardless, AUSDOM has got a system that provides full control and settings within a framework that’s very easy to follow. You won’t get lost in the menu items and you won’t have a hard time finding the settings you need.

I was able to simply plug-and-play right out of the box. Power it up and it starts recording, although of course you can change that, and the red dot on the screen makes recording very clear. I like very much that you can power the cam not only through the cigarette lighter, but also by USB cable, including USB cable to a battery pack, the type used for charging cell phones, etc. That means you’ve also got full video function away from the car.

With some cams the controls have been complicated enough, especially while driving, that I’ve controlled the recording on/off by plugging in or unplugging the cigarette lighter. With this cam that function is so easy it’s actually easier to use the single touch of the “OK” button to start or stop recording.

This cam can also take still photos with a single touch of a button; you’ll even hear the artificial shutter sound. However, unless I haven’t found the way yet, I don’t think you can take snapshots while recording video. It is of course, easy to capture still images during playback on your laptop or whatever you use.

This cam has so many features I could right five times this amount, but I’m already over 650 words so I should stop. The only potentially negative thing I can even come up with to mention is that this cam does not have GPS. However, while I found that to be initially interesting in one cam I used, it did not really prove to be very useful, and in the cam I used but did not review the GPS didn’t work properly.

I received this dash cam at a discount in exchange for testing and writing this review, but as I wrote, at this point I know what to look for in one of these, and this cam has just about every feature I’ve come across. It does not have the rear-view camera, i.e, you can swivel the cam to a rear view but it does not record front and back simultaneously. While I initially thought that was a great idea, in practice the way to record front and back in a way that’s actually useful is to mount a second cam in the back window and run it off of a battery pack. Shooting backward from the front windshield gives you a very small rear view in video. That seems to be because these cams shoot at a very wide angle, and the portion of that wide angle that’s represented by the rear window is tiny sliver of the entire view being recorded. (I hope that makes sense. Just know that you don’t get a good rear view when shot from the front windshield.)

Anyhow, I can easily give this camera my highest rating. That’s based on its features, the quality of the video (and audio), ease of use, the ability to shoot still photos, and whatever else I’m forgetting. Easiest five stars I’ve awarded in a while!

title: Very high quality video and stills combined with easy operation
text:
I like this camera a LOT, based primarily on the quality of the video and simplicity of use.! However, especially as I received it in exchange for testing and writing this review, I prefer to let the photos I'm posting do the talking for me. As you can see, they're crisp and clear, as is the video. The Amazon system degrades posted video, not a good thing when you're trying to convey what quality a camera is capable of, but to show that the video quality is equal to the quality of the still photos I'm posting both stills and screen-shots taken from videos. You can tell the screen-shots from the stills by the date and time stamp, which show on the video screen-shots but not on the stills (although I assume, but am not sure, that this is controlled by a setting I haven't noticed so far). The video is exactly as clear as the stills. What I can't convey with the still is the quality of the sound. It's quite good with the windows rolled up - music and conversation comes through clearly - although with windows down it's naturally quite a bit less clear.

A few things about operation:
Straight out of the box you simply insert a micro-SD card, mount the suction cup holder onto the windshield, and plug the cable into the camera and the cigarette lighter/power port (or matched power pack). If you want to set the date and time and the various other settings in advance you can do that before getting into your car by plugging the USB cable into a power source. Scrolling through the menu and settings is easy and really don't require the use of the instruction booklet, but the instructions are helpful in explaining some of the terms you may need to know to select the specific settings you want. If you're using a new micro-SD card I think you'll be asked to format the card, but as my card was already formatted I did not get that question. With the camera mounted and plugged in, recording will start automatically, with the red icon on the screen indicating that it's recording. You can immediately stop, or stop and start recording as you like, with the push of a single button on the side of the cam. To take single shots you simply press a different button on the side of the cam.

With some other dash cams I've found it easiest to start and stop recording by plugging in and unplugging the power cable, but with this cam and its one-button recording control it's so easy I haven't bothered using the power supply to control the recording.

Viewing and handling the photo/video files is as easy as with photos from your smart-phone.

The windshield suction clamp is very strong and secure, with the angle of the camera easily positioned, and it stays in position very well. The instructions describe how to tuck the power cable out of the way, but as I prefer to not leave the cam in my car I simply tuck the cable under the passenger side sunscreen, then dismount the suction-cup mount when I leave the car, taking everything with me or stashing it all somewhere in the car out of sight.

I know some people are skeptical about the integrity of reviews when a product is received in exchange for testing and writing a review, but other than what I can substantiate with the photos I'm posting, I've tried to stay away opinion/qualitative descriptions. What I've written truly reflects my experience with using the cam. I'm very happy with it and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to friends. I can literally think of no cons/negatives to mention. Please see the photos to get a real feel for the quality of the images.

title: Easy to install
text:
I just received this today. Fast shipping. Ordered Sunday night, received Thursday morning.

I did a lot of research to find a 802.11N WiFi USB that would work with both Windows 7 and Ubuntu 10.10 Linux.
This one came the closest. Although there were reviews suggesting that I would have issues on both OS's, they would be resolvable.
Those doubts were wrong. There were no issues on either OS.
I unplugged my old Belkin Basic 802.11n ($35) and plugged this one in. Windows 7 found it and installed the drivers immediately and at once I was able to surf the net at 2-3 times the speed. I verified this with CNET's Speedtest. It showed a 65Mbs connection.
I planned to install Ubuntu on this same box once I found a reliable 802.11n WiFi USB. So, as a test, I booted Ubuntu from CD (64bit version) and voila!
It found the dongle and I connected to my D-Link 802.11n Wireless network using WPA with no problems whatsoever. It showed a 54mbs connection. Surfing was quite quick. I could not test via CNET due to an Adobe Flash Issue that will be resolved when I install the OS on my hard drive. But, it appeared quicker on the same pages that I tested on Windows 7 (which I expected).
So, bottom line, I am extremely satisfied with this purchase.

Update: After using the product for several days, I have discovered a minor inconvenience. If the computer goes to "sleep" due to inactivity, when I "awaken" it then Windows 7 cannot find it. I have tried adjusting the Power management options, including disabling "allow the computer to turn off this device to save power" to no avail. The solution is simple but somewhat inconvenient. I can either shutdown and power back up, or unplug the dongle and re-plug it, at which point Windows 7 finds it immediately and activates it. I did read in one review about a similar issue with Ubuntu but cannot verify at this time.

title: Best specs for the price
text:
First the bad:
Does not have 5ghz WiFi connectivity.
Built in keyboard, word prediction and suggested word is flaky.
Bloatware, too much stuff you can't remove.
Not the brightest screen.
Speakers are too low in some apps and crackles in some.
Screen gets dirty fast, picks up fingerprints and dust.
Wider than most 8 inch tablets so difficult to hold one handed.
Small selection of cases available for this model tablet.
Battery life is much shorter than others in this class of tablets.
Apps cannot be moved to the SD card.

The good:
More memory and twice the storage of other tablets in this price range.
Fast switching between apps.
Thin and very lightweight.
Bloatware for managing apps and files is better than add on apps that I use on other devices.
The wider screen is an advantage when using portrait mode, especially ebook reading.
Different, so it takes getting used to, but the Settings screen is better organized and easier to use.
It automatically upgraded to Android 6.0
Charges quickly and uses standard micro USB.
They've maximized the 2.4ghz WiFi connection, so while connecting at 72mps it outperforms devices connected at 150mbs on 5ghz using a Speed test app.

Ways to minimize the bad:
Ordered a universal strap, will update if it doesn't help when holding it one handed.
Added a screen protector.
Use Ear buds for movies and music.
Replaced installed keyboard app with SwiftKey app.
The screen is very crisp and excellent indoors, find a shady spot if you need to use it outdoors.

All in all an excellent tablet for the budget conscious. It's specs rival competitors that cost 2-3 times as much.

Turns out that up until a short while ago v1.10 that uses Atheros drivers was what was being shipped for many years and worked perfectly. They are now producing and selling v2.1, it uses rtl8188eu drivers and they are not included in recent kernels. Your best bet is to search the forums for your distro for specific instructions.They are easily obtained from github and installed IF you have an alternative method to connect to the Internet with Linux. title: Happy Purchase
text:
I loved the TCL Roku Smart TV that I bought my wife so much that I decided to buy a second one. My wife's TV has cable input and is the sole monitor for her Lenovo desktop. Mine uses antenna input and is the second monitor on my Asus desktop. In both cases they replaced 5 year old 26” 1080p TVs. Her old TV was an Emerson, mine was an RCA.
First the things I don’t like:
■ The legs, not only only a bit of a pain to attach, they are too far apart and the TV sits too low. Since the speakers face downward this effects sound quality. I replaced them on both with universal VESA legs. Her TV is now 6 inches off the surface and mine is 12. Sound quality and volume is much better, as is viewing angle. Also, the wide spacing of the legs may mean you will need to replace them, as I did, if the table or stand they will sit on is narrow.
■ Input Switching. Since Input Switching takes place through the Roku menu you lose where you were when you switch. If you are watching say a YouTube video, a Netflix or Amazon movie and want to jump over to the Computer to check on say a long running update, it exists those channels rather than leaving them paused on what you were watching. This is especially a hassle on a sole monitor system when setting up those channels or the Roku itself. The same goes with using Pause Live TV.
■ No VGA input. Only a problem if using an older desktop/laptop that only has VGA output. The HDMI works perfectly, even with a Display Port to HDMI cable. Audio transference is flawless.
■ Antenna Tuning. Not all TV tuners are the same. I have worked with about 6 different brands all connected to the same antenna. The number of OTA channels have ranged from 28-46. The RCA being the best. The TCL sits in the middle with 34. If I wasn’t missing the local PBS I wouldn’t care. A second antenna on a splitter improved the signal enough for the TCL to find it, I now have 36 OTA channels. Unlike every other brand there is no way to manually add/delete individual channels.
■ Channel Switching on Antenna. No number pad. Up/down only.
■ Line of Sight Remote. This may be a bit of nit picking as 99% of all remotes are LoS. The remote that comes with the standard Roku is not. It uses 2.4tghz so you don’t have to point it at the device.
If you are used to that you will need to adjust.

Things that I really like:
■ Low Power usage. Mine is in my “man cave” which is powered by Solar, so this is a big thing to me. When turned off it uses less than 5 watts. Other brands are in the 10-15 watt range. I had those on a separate switch, now at 5 watts I don’t bother. When on it ranges 20-25 watts. Half of what the RCA used.
■ Physical Size. Being newer I knew that it was going to be thinner and lighter than anything 5 years old or more. What pleasantly surprised me is that it is the exact same dimensions as my previous 26” models. Just less edge, more screen. If you are replacing an older 26” inch and placing it in a cabinet it will fit in the same space.
■ Picture quality. This is 720p but unless it is sitting right next to a 1080p you will probably not notice the difference. My wife insists that it is a better picture and sound then any previous model she has used. When compared side by side to my 1080p monitor when watching a 1080p movie, I can see the difference, but it is very slight, and it is the only time I can see any difference. Of course I don’t play high-end graphic intense games on it.
■ Excellent Monitor. Not all TV’s work well as a computer monitor. Screen flickers, few resolution choices, to name two issues. The TCL doesn’t have those issues and functions fine as a monitor for daily use. Probably not for gaming though.
■ Turn off LED indicator. If it is in a room where you sleep being able to turn that off is a great feature it has.
■ Antenna TV. I mentioned two issues I didn’t like in this area, but these two areas make up for those two.
▪ Live Pause TV. I love this feature. Watching a sporting event, can’t wait for the commercial break, hit pause, come back and start up where you left off. You’ll need a 16gb USB stick and if you switch channels or input you’ll lose the saved programming. I’ll adjust. This feature is amazing and was an unexpected bonus.
▪ OTA Programming Guide. This is fantastic. Up to now I’ve had to use an online Programming guide like TV Guide. Now it looks just like Cable TV. The “More Ways to Watch” feature shows if that same program is available on a Roku channel as well. Another unexpected bonus.

In case you are wondering, it is the legs that I took a star off for. I had to spend $20 to remedy that.
If those are not an issue for you than you should consider this a 5 star purchase. I highly recommend.

I plan test it on the latest Manjaro, I am running the 4.14 kernel there as it is the most stable for the system it is on. I will also test on LMDE Cindy.

text:
Update: You will see below my original 5 star review. I was so pleased with my purchase that I bought a second one. I was greatly disappointed. While it looks exactly the same, it's an entirely different product than the first one that I bought. The one is an rtl8818fu chipset. Not the "eu" the first one was. It's too cheap to bother returning it. Lesson learned. Won't be buying from this seller again.

Original 5 star review:
I have found my new favorite CHEAP USB WiFi adapter for use on older systems running Linux with very slow internal WiFi . Or ones that just can't be made to work properly on Linux. It says it uses the MT7601 chipset and that may be the way Windows sees it. But Linux sees it as a RTL8188EUS and it uses the r8188eu driver. That driver has been in the Linux kernel since 3.12. I personally tested it on kernels from 4.4 through 5.2. On Arch, RHEL, and Debian based distros. On all the Ubuntu and Linux Mint flavors. On every one it worked out of the box without any drivers needing to be installed. Only Debian 9 itself required drivers to be installed. But heck, does any WiFi work out of the box on Debian? If you want to spend more money and get better speeds, the Panda PAU07 is my recommendation for the most Linux friendly AC600 WiFi adapter. It is 3 times faster than this one, but also 3 times the cost. To compare this AC150 routinely got download speeds in the 20-24Mb/s and the Panda AC600 was in the 60Mb/s. If your Internet service is around 25Mb/s then the faster adapter provides no additional benefit.

title: Stay Young, Look Professional
text:
I suffer from powerfully strong "young face" genes. I know I'll appreciate it in my 30's, but having recently graduated college and joined the professional work force I get lots of "young guy" and "kid" comments that can be borderline embarrassing at times. I had been using my college backpack for my work laptop and documents, but then realized that my basic black Herschel was only adding to my already youthful appearance. I didn't want to go full corporate black laptop messenger bag, so I thought I'd give this a shot.

As far as stylish satchels go, this one is a clear winner in functionality and finesse. The strap feels comfortable around the shoulder and the leather is soft against your side. The front lid (flap? whatever its called) closes by two magnets attached to the leather AS WELL AS the two belt straps on the front. Those straps aren't just for style points, which can be a pro/con depending how quickly you like opening your bag. You don't really need to secure the straps because of the magnets, but if you have a second I would recommend doing both.

On the inside you find two small pockets on the front side of the bag separate from the main compartment. The main compartment is secured by a sturdy zipper that feels well made and won't break after multiple uses. Diving further you find the typical laptop divider on one side and an empty slot for files/notebooks on the other. There are also a few small pockets for pens and small items. The interior has padded canvas material which again is soft on the skin and keeps scratches off your laptop. The 15.6" size fits my Lenovo ThinkPad P50 15.6" laptop perfectly. Although your laptop feels big, the bag doesn't because of how comfortable it is to carry around.

I was half joking about myself in the first paragraph, but I really do like this bag and feel more professional using it. I am in no hurry to get old, and this satchel is a good in-between for any young professional looking to keep their liveliness in a cubicle office.
item_title: Lifewit Genuine Leather Flap Vintage 15.6 Inch Laptop Canvas Messenger Satchel Bag (Grey)

title: Best low cost DVD recorder!
text:
I've been using dvd recorders for several years. This one is great. It makes excellent quality recordings with no hassle. I think the fact that it doesn't have a tuner makes it easier to operate. It has a nice option that will allow it to start recording if it senses a signal if a satellite or cable box turns on so you don't have to set up any timers if you use the timer feature on your cable box.

1) Put in a blank DVD
2) Pick the quality (I use 2 hour for most everything
3) Push the red record button to start recording (you can press pause during commercials)
4) When you're done push stop. If you don't want to add anything else to the dvd, go to the dvd menu and choose finalize to make the dvd compatible with other dvd players.

That's it. My 8 year old makes recordings with it.

Here are my only minor criticisms:
- It would be nice if there was a 3 hour recording mode instead of having to jump from 2 hour to 4 hour but I would still describe the 4 hour as quite good quality.
- I wish the remote had a finalize button on it.
- The menu it creates is text with no picture/preview on DVD+R. I think preview/picture icons appear when using a DVD+RW.

title: You'll be happy with this unit
text:
Got it today and drove around town (Austin, Texas) and loved listening to my MP3 music on my GM car radio. Much lower cost than replacing the radio. Just plug it in the cigarette lighter and set tune it and the radio to same empty frequency. Decent sound quality (better than a cassette tape). I had no problems whatsoever with the unit despite the crowded FM dial because of our proximity to San Antonio and small towns. The sound was clear with no hiss no buzz. The transmitter is powerful and even works over frequencies that have a weak station. I've tried other transmitters and by far this is the best I've heard and nice looking and small in size.

If you can accept cassette tape quality that you'll be perfectly happy with this unit. You can't get CD quality through an FM transmitter but this is about as good of quality as I think you can get. I did adjust the tone and volume controls on the unit (had too much bass and not enough treble). Now when I turn it on it sounds almost identical in loudness and tone to any other FM station on the dial. The remote is nice as is slim and has raised buttons so you can control the unit without taking your eyes off the road. I have to use the remote to turn the unit off because my cigarette lighter is always powered even when the car is off. The unit flexes to put the display at a convenient angle. It uses basic red LED display bright enough to see in sunlight. Forget the crappy owner's manual and go to their web site and watch the demo video.

title: Buy it, you'll be happy!
text:
Don't believe the naysayers, this is an outstanding product and very well integrated into the Prime ecosystem. The fact that you can download movies or tv shows and watch them offline itself is amazing. Plus you can add up to 200GB (FAT 32 or EXFAT format) MicroSD card if you want. It's super simple to get started and is pre-registered to your name and amazon account. The display is great, the keyboard and touch is very good. The technology they employ to make the Silk browser lightning fast is incredible. Pages load faster than on any computer. There is a built in map app (you can also install google maps) is twice as fast as google maps and great for just casual browsing. I was surprised that the stereo speakers did make a difference when watching music videos and it streamed nicely to bluetooth receiver that I already had.

After I had it on for an hour there was a system update and that is when "Alexa" was installed. After it's installed you press and hold the circle button at the bottom of the screen to use it.

I leave it connected to the internet all the time as the power feature that disconnects from internet slows me down if engaged and I want to jump right on the net. Battery life in idle mode is great and lasts for days without a recharge just idling with screen off. I love the built-in blue shade feature (optional) you can have it automatically filter out blue light between certain hours (good to avoid sleep disruption.

The desktop does support folder creation and there are multiple pages of icons for each category (Movies, music, etc.). You can also slide the categories by just putting your finger on the category itself and sliding it. This eliminates the need to swipe one page at a time.

A nice built-in feature (that can be disabled) is called On-Deck. Basically it pre-downloads a random movie so you'll always have something to watch. I was about to disable it but it actually picked some decent movies and it says if you start running out of space it will delete them automatically so I left it on. Who knows when I might get stuck somewhere and need to be entertained without having to have wifi access.

Here are my minor issues:

-It only uses Amazon Underground and not Google Play so not every app is available but most of the usual ones are. There is not a built-in YouTube app but there is a shortcut link you can install (it's tiny) and I think launches YouTube in the browser and it works perfectly. I also use Tune-in radio app, works great and gives free radio stations from around the world and free CNN audio feed so you can listen to for free. Microsoft apps are available and are good

-The Silk browser is native, it's very good, extremely fast, but does have one missing feature: you can't import bookmarks. Still I mainly use this to casually browse my favorite 10 websites so not a big deal to re-bookmark them. If it's really an issue you can use a commercial free bookmarking service. The browser does not support flash as Adobe is no longer supporting a version for tablets. You might want to check to see if your favorite browser and other apps are available from Amazon Underground. As of now Firefox is not available

- Don't think this particular version supports the use of VPN which is strange because earlier versions did.

-Touching the power button always locks the screen and no way to override it. What you can do is to set the delay until screen turns itself off. If it turns itself off you don't need to enter the PIN. The exception is that it will eventually lock after the user preset time forces it to lock.

- The virtual keyboard works well, no typing errors like I get with my phone....BUT....the built-in virtual keyboard does not support swiping. You have to tap each character. Not a big deal given how well it works. However the tablet, can be easily paired with a generic physical bluetooth keyboard.

title: Amazing difference on four year old computer
text:
For ordinary use, my four year old budget laptop now runs almost as fast as my new computer. The startup time is the huge difference, under a minute rather than minutes. Laptop came with a 500GB drive but this 240GB was plenty big enough as I was only using 80GB (I checked before I bought this drive). Crucial also has an easy to use scanner on their website that will tell you if the drive is compatible with your laptop and I ran it to make sure. Easy to install and I recommend a clean install and not cloning the old drive.

1) Backup your data files onto the cloud, USB, etc.
2) Download the Microsoft USB recovery drive creator and install it. Then run it. It will need a 16GB or larger USB flash drive in order to make the Windows 10 recovery drive and takes about an hour for it to run.
3) With my computer, a single screw holds the cover to remove the old hard drive. Remove the cover, slide out the old hard drive case and slide out the old hard drive from within shock-resistant case (you'll reuse it so be mindful).
4) Slide the new hard drive in the case, then slide the assembly into computer and attach cover and screw.
5) Plug in Windows 10 recovery drive you created earlier and start up the computer and follow the prompts to install the latest version of Windows 10.
6) Once installed, a good idea to turn on Windows system protection and create a recovery point. If you have problems, you can always reinstall the old hard drive and get tech support (which I didn't need).

It's that simple and now my old computer is dramatically faster and am very happy with the purchase!

title: Great value, much better than I expected it to be
text:
If you have reasonable expectations you'll be very happy with this. It is NOT a replacement for high-end home theater projector.

Excellent, low-cost device that you can use casually like take with you on trips, use in a child's bedroom, or in your backyard etc. It's smaller than most projectors, about the size of a dictionary and weighs about a pound.

The unit is brighter than I expected but you need a dark environment. If you can't make your environment darker than make the picture smaller. Colors are vivid. Motion is fluid and natural

I plugged in a FireStick, sound could be surprisingly loud but has the flat tonality of an alarm clock. Not a problem for listening to the news or sports game. You can plug in portable speaker or soundbar if you want better sound.

Fan does make some noise but just don't sit right next to it. Not a deal-breaker for me.

Could use it for PowerPoint if font was decent size. Don't expect to show Excel spreadsheets unless you zoom in.

To get good sharpness make sure the unit is level and parallel to the wall it's projecting on. While you can angle the unit and use keystone correction I found that only the center of the picture is sharp and the corners won't be that sharp. Best way I found is to focus the center then use the keystone dial to adjust till corner is sharp. Note that there is a focus range and it does work well to wall size. if you try to make a 20 foot image you won't be able to get it in focus.

Includes 12 volt 3.5A power supply. Remote needs two AAA batteries (not included). Inputs: Two HDMI, computer, USB flashdrive, MicroSD. Output: Headphones and audio. Threaded metal tripod socket on bottom.

I've already ordered another as a gift. I think you'll be very happy with this if you have reasonable expectations.

text:

For indoors, you could mount this to a piece of wood (about a square foot) and set atop a bookcase next to your TV which is what I did.

It will fit on a closet shelf so you could put it in a closet (assuming you get a good signal) and run a wire to the TV. The higher you mount it the better so if you can put it upstairs in an attic or closet you'll get the best results. Optionally, you can use a signal amplifier (about $20) and they're simple to setup and plug into an outlet.

Once you get the correct antenna direction, it's VERY IMPORTANT to have your TV re-scan for channels so that it fine-tunes the stations.

For years I have had DLNA capability but no easy way to play these music files on my high fidelity equipment. The bottom line: Wow! I'm using the SPDIF directly to my receiver's internal DAC which is too old to be state of the art. It doesn't matter. The music whether streaming Amazon Prime or my DLNA server files is pleasing. I noticed the difference immediately compared to the analog output of my Amazon Echo Input. The software finds the DLNA server easily. This is fantastic. title: They have always impressed me until now.
text:
This is my 9th Soundblaster product, and 12th Creative product. They have always impressed me until now. I run audio out via SPDIF to a NAD pre-amp, then to 4 NAD power amps, finishing at mixed brands of in wall speakers and subs throughout the house. The level of the SPDIF out was weak compared to my previous sound card(s), and required more than twice the amplification. I am not going to be running my amps full tilt all the time to make up for a weak input signal. The built in headphone amp is a joke. Volume level/power was no better than plugging direct into the laptop's factory soundcard. No EQ is bundled with this unit, I had to install old Creative software. Burn option in Creative MediaSource 5 magically disappeared, I consulted customer service, and was told this product does not support MediaSource (MediaSource won't burn unless a qualifying Creative device is connected). How can YOUR software not support YOUR hardware?! How does the Creative sound card model I am using have anything to do with transferring files to a CD?!?! Creative did not respond to further inquires on this compatibility issue. Sound quality lacks as compared to previous SoundBlasters, it was dull and flat. Overall sounded poor, through a mix of Klipsch, Polk, Boston Acoustics, and even a single pair of Martin Logan Edges. Out of no where, a click and pop appeared between tracks in MediaSource. Said clicks/pop not present with previous PC/Soundcard. I have submitted for a refund. I am going back to my desktop PC, with a Soundblaster X-Fi Titanium until I figure out a better laptop option. Considering the Cambridge Audio DacMagic Plus or axing the computer all together for a network media center.

Everyone is entitled to a flop. Creative proved themselves to me over years of use and many products. I can get over a single flop. But not responding to additional inquiries regarding product quality and compatibility issues is TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE. I have used SoundBlaster exclusively since my 8bit ISA mounted "Game Blaster" card purchased from Radio Shack in the late 80's early 90's. Creative has lost a decades long customer not from product quality, but from poor customer service. Shame on you, and good riddance.

This was run on:
Dell Latitude E6540
Intel Core i7-4810MQ @ 2.8ghz
8Gb RAM
Win7 64 bit

Sound card was purchased direct from the Creative website, not through Amazon. However, Amazon fulfills their orders...

**UPDATE** Creative has finally responded, and is accepting the return/refund. They are NOT paying for shipping.

title: Delivers great bang for the buck
text:
If you have decent powered sub(s), this puts out more than enough power for the surround channels in the average home theater. Auto set-up with the included microphone is pretty cool. Manual set-up on your TV via HDMI is awesome! Manual set-up from the unit itself is clunky and a hassle. TONS of HDMI inputs. HDMI switching is really nice. A couple switched 120v outlets on the back would have been nice. I also would have preferred an S/PDIF out to zone 2 instead of the analog out. Frequency response is as accurate as I am capable of reproducing. One of my subs is capable of 18Hz, and through a test tone delivered via S/PDIF in from my PC out, the Onkyo fed the signal through the sub line out as expected. I did not test high freq signals as I value my hearing and did not want 27 dogs in my yard, but I can say a jazz ride cymbal sounds as clean as the the drum kit in my basement. I am also utilizing the built in sub crossover, set to 120Hz, so I suppose that 18Hz test is not demonstrating the amplifier, rather it just passed the signal through. This is my 3rd Onkyo, and it once again delivers great bang for the buck.

This item is now discontinued, but new old stock is available for $899!! *gasp* buy a used model ($225), or the new replacement NR525 ($299). This really is a great receiver, but not worth $899. I paid $299 in Feb of 2013....

title: Good clean signal to at least 90% of volume
text:
I purchased 4 of these from outside of Amazon. I use them as amps for a huge outdoor party I do each summer. I am not a DJ, so this route is cheaper than buying a DAC and pre-amp, not to mention all kinds of XLR and SpeakOn cables. Besides that, it lets me control volume independently in all 5 zones. I run a single TosLink out from my soundcard to a powered 4 way optical splitter (39.99 from Specialty-AV here on Amazon), then to each of the 4 STR-HD550's. They really sound spectacular for the price ($160ea with qty4 discount from Jet). Power is adequate. 90w x 2 stated into 6Ohms, at 8Ohms it is probably about 70w x 2. Good clean signal to at least 90% of volume. So I would guess 60ish watts of usable power. 60x2 is more than adequate to cover the areas I need with clean power but without people having to scream at one another over the music. TosLink input jacks have a real weak "snap" to them - I am hoping cables falling out isn't a problem. Both sub pre-out RCA jack have a similar issue. It's like they are a couple of thousandths too small, and my RCA cables fit very loose. I tried several cables, including a new one, all with same result. I will have to crimp cable ends to ensure a good fit/connection. Both issues worthy of docking a star, but not enough to complain about the purchase. Setting crossover levels, bass/treble, speaker size all pretty easy through the remote. One remote controls them all, so common settings I can set to all 4 at the same time. With one on at a time, I can even name each receiver after the zones they will cover, and it shows up on the display. It came with a microphone to do an auto calibration, but I am not bothering with that for now. I might go through that in the woods, we'll see. I will play with these over the next 5 months, and really push them at the outdoor party in July. I suspect I will not need to push them to the limit as the sub out is set to 160Hz, and I have a totally unnecessary amount of subwoofer power. I will update my review with my findings until and thru then. 2.23.16

There will be no review on HDMI or analog I/O, nor surround sound as I am not using those features. These are only being used as stereo amplifiers. I could not find a stereo receiver with a TosLink input at this price range.

***UPDATE*** I replaced my SoundBlaster X-Fi Titanium with a SoundBlaster Zx. The Zx either has much stronger output signal, or the X-Fi was just weak with age. Either way, what required 90% of the Sony's volume is now achieved with 30%. WAAAAY louder than necessary. So, when coupled with adequate input signal strength, the Sony POUNDS!! Assuming they can stand the test of time, I cannot see any reason to ever replace these.....

***UPDATE 2*** These guys just thundered the annual party in the woods. Our neighboring campers, whom we affectionately refer to as "The Swamp People", visited camp after the annual fireworks war. I was told by one that their camp is 3/4mi away, and they could hear our tunes. Although he did mention he heard bass over anything.. For most of the weekend, the entire system was played at a level that was comfortable so folks didn't have to yell at one another. The last couple hours Saturday night I opened up all the amps and subs, and it was just absurd. It sounded like a live show - everyone was screaming at each other, but thoroughly enjoyed it. These receivers performed beyond my expectations. No need for an upgrade next year, the Sonys are going back to the woods. 07.13.16

***Update 3 10.2.2020*** I only have one left. One died in the woods, but I can't fault Sony. They were subject to high humidity, and tiny red ants that seemed to love the inside of these. I suspect an ant shorted a trace on one of the PCBs. 1 was sold, 1 was given away. I still blow the north woods up once a year, but it evolved in high power amps and stage speakers. The remaining Sony still runs a pair of Onkyo satellites, combined with a 10" Sony sub in my garage. It has been run in temps below zero, to over 90 and oppressive humidity. I always keep it in standby, not off in hopes that it will keep any kind of condensate out from within. Keep in mind it is NOT designed for this. But... Still work just fine, still pounds if I want to. Usually it now runs from an analog aux in from either my laptop or Alexa. Rarely, but I do sometimes listen to FM and AM as well....

title: More volume, more bass, more treble.....
text:
After a poor experience with an external SoundBlaster, I vowed to never be a Creative customer again. Problem with that is, their internal cards are tried and true. And I have found when comparing specs to other brands, Creative meets or beats them for the most part and comes in at quite a bit cheaper. Finger crossed I never need warranty or support, as dealing with Creative is like pulling teeth.

Seems to be a nice upgrade from my X-Fi Titanium, although it is possible my 6yr old X-Fi's output was not what it once was. I use the digital TosLink out to an 4x optical splitter, then on to 4 receivers. The output level seems like it is 3 times what the X-Fi put out (again, my X-Fi may have just plain been old and tired). The final output from the speakers is WAY louder than it once was. What used to be 90% of amplifier output is now achieved with 30%. For that, I absolutely love it!! Anything that can keep my amps running cooler is of course welcome.

As far as the sound quality goes, it sounds as clean and clear as most Creative products. I cannot say it sounds any better or worse than the X-Fi. What it does have, is a higher bass ceiling. With an available sub gain, selectable crossover boost from 10Hz to 1Khz, and a 10 band EQ, there is way more bass available to my subs than I need. I have also found the treble has a higher ceiling too. Way brighter than I care for. As a result, the EQ now has the top and bottom couple bands pulled back as compared to the X-Fi.

The SBX control panel is fair, but it did take a while to figure out how to get Dolby out of the Toslink. It also took a while to figure if I wanted stereo direct or 2.1 and if I wanted Dolby or DTS. 2.1 was the answer. Dolby also won over DTS as the final output was louder. In short, it took some screwing around to get it to settle down and sound like my X-Fi, but it was fun to play with and learn all the features, and the end result was worth it.

The Audio Control Module (ACM) I won't use much. The 'phone amplifier in my receiver produces more volume and better bass. However, the ACM is well built. It is a nice heavy base with full rubber foot to keep it from sliding around. I also thought it was cool to include both 1/4" and 1/8" jacks, instead of an adapter that you can never find when you need it. The volume rheostat is super silky and smooth, although it lacks a soft stop. You can hear and feel the wiper arm hitting something when it has reached the end of its stroke. Should be fine as long as you are conscious of it and not slamming the volume to 11 every time.....

I cannot comment on the cool LEDs, as I use a horizontal HTPC chassis with no windows.

Most of the complaints I have read on this card appear to be driver related. It looks like they may have released this card prematurely, and the firmware guys had not yet ran it through the ringer in each available Windows option. It also appears they now have those bugs worked out. I am running on Windows 7, and the included CD-ROM had everything I needed in its most current revision. A Creative update check after installation revealed nothing more current, other than a couple of options and a trial I was not interested in. It should also be noted that Windows 7 found all the drivers it needed to run the card on its own. So if you don't care for or need any of the included software to further control sound quality, you won't even need the CD.

**UPDATE*** 04.08.16 This could be some kinds gear glitch, idk..... But headphone through the ACM sounds like ass. Receiver 'phone jack, no issue. QC issue? - maybe something on the board, maybe my gear, idk... But it's prevalent through the ACM.... Best suggestion is - if your primary final driver is a headphone, do what you can to preview output prior to purchase. I, personally, give a rat's A*&. Through standard drivers, it is truly insane. Dolby Digital Live may as well be on stage......

***UPDATE*** 0928.2021 - Retired, abandoned in the still in use HTPC tower. I now use an external DAC, a Schiit Gungnir. SOOOOOOOoooo silky smooth. As close as I can get to tubes with a digital source and solid state amps. The only downfalls is I don't have as much audio control as I had. The Creative software doesn't work with the DAC. I had to buy audio software so I at least had a 10 band EQ to play with.....

title: Sounds great, but not without flaws....
text:
I cannot comment on bass, as these were used in conjunction with a 15" powered Behringer subwoofer. Used for an annual party in the woods. Getting too old to drag the amps and stacks up north, and these worked well with the big sub. Powered by a Sony STR-DH550. They sounded great - clean mids and crisp highs with a wide sound stage. They sounded no different before/during/after the 20 hour rain we rec'd. Pine sap wiped off the plastic cabinet with some Goo Gone (Goo Gone is citrus based and safe, Goof Off would surely melt the plastic case - be sure whatever you use to wipe them clean is safe for plastics!) I wish they could have handled the full power of the Sony receiver, but they produced adequate volume for a large area before they started to distort. Crisp highs, clean mids, and a WIDE sound stage. They really filled the area with music. The stage was wider than the Behringer tops and mid-bass cabinets I used to use.

I don't like the super fragile grills. I see in a couple place stated they are stainless steel - they are not. these a mild steel and bend/ding super easily. They also do not come on and off as you would expect your average removable grill to. The steel mesh edge fits into a groove in the cabinet. A tight fit, so perfect alignment is req'd or you'll find yourself forcing one corner in. Bend the edge (which is VERY easy to do), and it will no longer fit until you reform the edge with a pair of pliers.

I also didn't like the color. It shows virtually everywhere as a bright white, which they were not. They are an off-white/ivory color. Possible these are new old stock, and the color degrades over time, but that would equally undesirable.

Once again, they get used for annual party in the woods, so while I have some minor complaints, they really aren't very valid for my purposes but may be for yours. Outside of the party, they will see very low power levels in my garage. I expect them to last for years. I will update here as necessary, as I do all my reviews....

***UPDATE*** 11.11.2021 - These have moved in to my 2004 Jeep Grand Cherokee, so they will see much more use than originally intended. Combined with an 1100w 12" sub/amp combo. The Klipsch's are powered by a 250w Sony amp. The OEM speakers are powered by a JVC head unit. I have not pushed them to the limit, but I can say they get loud enough with the Sony amp to hurt my ears without distorting. I added them to the rear of the Jeep, so I can rotate the speakers out of the open hatch when I am working/camping on the property up north. Really fill the property with sound - I have no trouble hearing clean/clear tunes on the front few acres. They still sound great driving the Jeep too, despite being in such a small space. title: Great speaker for the price!
text:
For the price, this really is a great little speaker. I run patio speakers in the back of my Jeep so I can open the tailgate and flip them out to play tunes when I am camping/working on my "up north" property. The all-weather design leaves me with no concerns if it rains. If I am staying up there for more than a couple of days, I even hang them in the trees and run speaker wire back to the Jeep. I purchased these as a downgrade from my Klipsch KHO-7 pair, simply because they were too big and got in the way when I am loaded down with gear.

They sound pretty good. The highs are clear and crisp without being too bright. The mids were a tad strong and "squawky" at first, but I was able to correct with an EQ adjustment. Bass lines are strong, but don't expect to be blown out of you seat with a 4.5" woofer. I can't speak of deep bass, as my sub woofer takes over at 120Hz. The sub is another reason for the downgrade from the Klipsch's - there really wasn't much need for a large enclosure when the sub takes all the big hits. They are being driven by a 250w amp, which is probably realistically a 150w amp that I only use 100w of at peak. They take the power fine, but do of course have a limit before they distort if I really try and push them That limit is beyond my useful range anyway. They are loud enough that they become uncomfortable after a few song up close, and project enough that I can hear the tunes clearly on the front 5 acres of my property. Overall, and considering the price, they are a surprisingly comparable to the Klipsch's in sound quality. While they do project well on my wooded lot, I have to give that win to the Klipsch’s and their horn-loaded tweeter. In closing, these were well worth the $50. With the abuse these see in the way of being bounced around in the Jeep, I expect to get 2-3 years out of them. If they fall short of that, I will update here as long as Amazon will let me….

title: Great ram from a great company
text:
Ok first off this is hynix die and it will reach 3600 but mine would crash so I turned mine down to 3533 and is stable at that frequency. I do wish it was stable at 3600 but not that big of a deal as it would be very minimal gains to reach that. I did have 3200 ram installed by the same company and was running 32 gigs. So my take on this, is if you have 3200 and is stable save your money and keep what ya have as I feel it not worth the extra 400 mhz to get the top speed. The only reason I did this was I have the AMD 12 core Ryzen and wanted to know if I could reach 4.5 ghz with my cpu.

Update as I went into the bios I did a few tweaks to the settings and getting the ram stable at 3600 even in gaming and stress testing. I manually had to set the timing to 16 19 19 38. and voltage at 1.35 volts, hope this help others for some weird reason my asus motherboard wanted to auto to 16 18 18 38, and thats why in would crash as these timings are a bit too tight.

Update 2, As I've been working with this ram I have to say I really love it so well I bought another kit to add to my set up. It boots right up with the modded timing in the bios with no crashes with 32 gigs installed.

text: I have been running liquid cooled for 10 plus years now. I have used mainly 240mm and 280mm radiator's mainly in Corsair products. This is the first 360 mm I've owned. I decided on this one from online reviews. This one get things done and way better than what I've had in the past. I decided to keep my 3 140mm intake fans in the front and the added the radiator to the front then added 120mm fans to the back of the radiator for a push pull configuration. on the top of the case I use 3 140mm exhaust fans plus another 140mm for the rear. My set up is 12 core Ryzen and the graphics card is radeon RX 5700XL and while gaming I reach about 55-60 C. this is ultra setting in games. My next test was hand brake this will intrude all sorts of heat. This program is video rendering and runs all core as hard and fast as it can. with my old radiator it would reach temp of 89 c and down clocking the cpu to under 3.8GHZ.  or less, this set up will reach 75c now and the cpu does not down clock, it stays above 4.0 GHZ. because of the excessive heat. So what I'm saying here for the price you better pick one up and if you have the budget pick up some extra fans to configure a push pull. Your computer will love you for it!!!

title: Awesome Tablet!
text:
Let me start this with, no I’m not an amazon fan boy, work for amazon, or received this free for a review. I received this tablet in place of one that was an older model that had an issue in which the remedy was to replace it with the current 9th Gen tablet. The old one pretty much spent its life in the living room or on the treadmill for reading. So I decided to give this one a go in lieu of just getting money back.

In short, I’m pretty happy with it. Yes, the case is plastic and your married to the amazon ecosystem. But I will say, out of all the tablets I’ve had before this (yes...even the venerable HDX 8.9) the HD 10 with the octo-core processor is faster than them all. One could argue that it’s Android 9 (Pie) as the base OS, but it’s a definite improvement! The big plus for me is the micro SD slot, yes I have 64gigs on-board, but I also use a lot of storage for PDF’s and How-to videos. I like this unit for the price (which I will say is a heck of a deal)...and it’s not so crazy expensive that I’m scared to take it in the shop. Let me explain the “Shop” part. Aside from reading and consuming media like the masses, I house a ton of PDF manuals...service manuals to be frank. Some of these are 1000’s of pages of diagnostic information and electrical schematics. So being that it has expandable storage, it’s going to see more use than the last. I have this tablet in a hard case with a screen protector. I’ve been to the far reaches of the internet to gather a rather large collection of automotive material and it’s nice to be able to put almost 550gigs (OS and apps take up the rest) of stuff on a tablet that’s about $149-189 depending on base storage size. Big plus here.

Battery life is almost a work day, and that’s pretty hard usage (using it during a job), some days are much more with just light browsing and reading in my off time, depending on screen brightness. Falls inline with what they claim.

Alexa is surprisingly handy for cooking recipes, or just asking for some tunes (never used the assistant before) It’s decently responsive, kinda on the fence for the privacy aspect, but I like you can at least clear your history or view it, so kudos there.

Amazon, ya done did good;) Only thing I will add to this review, please design a really decent PDF viewer of your own design that’s more intuitive (searchable) than the baked in kindle version, and you’ll knock this unit outta the park!

Customer service needs a plug here, they handled my exchange to this unit quickly and I’m pretty dang happy with the outcome. Keep it up;)

title: Outstanding monitor and resolution!
text:
I've been looking for a portable monitor for a while since I tore up a knee pretty good. Unfortunately I can't sit in a chair or at a normal desk because my leg has to stay straight, so I'm relegated to a recliner. I needed a second screen for my surface pro 7 to work on cyber classes and telework while I'm at home recovering. This monitor is excellent in both color reproduction and brightness! 1440p is the only way to go for no eye-strain and a form factor that fits the surface pro perfectly since it's close to the resolution. It comes with a nice remote that with only hitting the up and down arrows lets you access brightness and volume quickly. You can adjust a multitude of advance settings as well in the menu that offers plenty of adjustments.

The screen at half backlight is about as bright as my surface at 60% brightness. So there is plenty of nits to be had if you want to go brighter. It is sRGB compliant according to windows display properties, and a good setting for text and app scaling is about 150% or so. Speakers are what they are, probably ok for those who don't have any options, but don't think tablet or iphone level audio richness.

There were a few quarks getting it to run on USB-C only, it might just be the goofy drivers on my surface since they are still working out the bugs on intel, but after some playing around in the device manager in windows, I must have scared it into working. No issues since on power up or down. Be mindful of your USB-C power draw, and middle brightness, it's about average watts you would expect from a lesser 1080p portable screen you may have used in the past, but when you crank up to full brightness, you may have issues with it turning off. This case only happened while I tested it first on a power supply I had laying around that was about 1amp and 5v. So the flexibility of voltages and outputs of USB-C should help here.

Overall, amazing little monitor, good build quality, and zero light bleed or dead pixels. Surprised the heck out of me;)

title: A great unit but not for beginners...
text:
After reading some of the other reviews, I wanted to provide my perspective as someone who has a couple of racks filled with RPi, Odroid, Banana Pi and Orange Pi's. Orange Pi's offer a great value for the money. But, they are not for beginners and there is no user support from the manufacturer. Also, the H3 processors run extremely hot and, in my opinion, they are dangerous as a burn and fire hazard if improperly operated. That said, I think it's a fun and useful board if you like a challenge and enjoy making things work.

For those not familiar with H3's, I suggest building a case for the Pi such that it is suspended by its mounting points. A heat sink and fan placed to circulate air above and below the suspended unit will bring the operating temperature down significantly. (Overclocking has not been a problem in 7 months of use.) I paired a sata drive from an old laptop with the Orange Pi and have found the extra storage to be useful. As for an OS, the closest thing to a community for Orange Pi users is Armbian. They have a good website and there is a fair amount of online documentation when running into challenges. If you want more adventure (things that need to be fixed in order to use it), try Lubuntu or Kali images -- each has a fair amount of online documentation. Just remember to 'dd' your card as you make progress and get features of the Orange Pi to work, because it is likely that you will have to rebuild everything from metal at least once along the way.

Overall, I think its just better to by a RPi because I can spend more time programming stuff. The price and features and performance of the Orange Pi make it really compelling. But unlike my RPi's that are on 24/7, my Orange Pi is shut down when not in use because of the excessive amount of heat it generates.

title: Week 1: So far so good.
text:
I purchased a smaller Cyberpower UPS a few years ago to protect a single desktop computer, and it is still working and has done a great job. So I added this unit to protect two additional systems on our network. My installation will draw just under 100w and provide ample time to shut down our systems after a power outage. This is week 1 and I can only provide the following review: The package arrived in a couple days after my order. I followed directions and charged it for 8 hours prior to use, downloaded the power panel management software and plugged in the systems. Everything powered as expected and the software panel provided some great options for power management. I am particularly happy about the integration of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) in these little units. The email notification was quick and easy to set up -- best of all it sent a successful email in a test. I hope that the automated settings in the software will actually work in a real power outage incident, but I'm not given to automatically believing the marketing in the materials. So far so good -- another recommend at this point (given my operational requirements).

Another reason for writing this review is that I have been disappoined by uninformed and unhelpful reviews for most UPS units while making my buying decision. Specifically, generic complaints that a unit "doesn't last as long as other units" is arbitrary and unhelpful. This type of review doesn't indicate the load placed on the unit during power loss. These types of reviews also don't indicate their operational requirements -- do customers use their UPS to give them time for an orderly shutdown or do they continue to use UPS power until the unit runs out of battery power? To make matters worse, other Amazon customers indicate that these general comments are helpful -- they aren't! Nor does anyone take the time to educate buyers that a UPS is not a substitute for a generator. My suggestion before buying a UPS, consider the power draw that will be placed on the unit during power loss, and review your operational requirements after a power loss. And I'll say it -- a UPS is NOT a generator. It's purpose is to inform you of a power loss and give you and opportunity for an ordered shut down to protect your systems. After a power outage, the purpose of a UPS is not to allow you to continue working until the end of battery life.

title: Noise cancelling headphone with decent performance and reasonable price.
text:
I buy this headphone to reduce background noise so that I don't have to turn the volume too high to hear it clearly (which is bad for hearing), and it does work!

Noise cancelling performance: ANC-33is does significantly cancels background noises, especially sounds like air-conditioner noise or traffic noise. It feels magical to quiet down the world around you with just one switch on the noise cancelling unit! Though it does not completely cancel all noises, I think the performance is good enough for its price. You can still hear the noise a little, but when music is played, the noise will become barely audible. I highly recommend it to people who listen to music in noise surroundings. (If you want something that blocks noise as much as possible when you are not listening to music, say sleeping, this is probably not what you are looking for. It does not reduce as much noise as my Mack's earplugs)

Sound quality: I am not a headphone expert, but I can clearly tell that ANC-33is is better than my 10 dollar Sony MDR-E9. The sound from ANC-33is is more stereo and clear. Though it is probably not as good as normal non-noise-canceling at the same price, I think the sound quality is good enough for me.

Build Quality: It is well build. The wire is covered with high quality rubber and noise cancelling unit is delicate. About the wire control, At first I find that it works on my iPod but does not work on my Android phone, but later I realized wire control was disabled in setting of my music app. After fixing the setting, it works perfectly.

Battery life: Impressive! I use it for about one hour per day and the battery lasted for almost three months before the lower battery LED started blinking! It even outperforms its specifications on Audio-Technica website, which says "up to 60 hours".

Wire length: The total length is enough, but the position of the noise canceling unit can be improved. There is about 50cm of wire between the plug and the unit and 80cm from the unit to headphone. If you prefer to clip the unit on the side of your pocket, the portion from the unit to the headphone may not be enough. I am 1.7m tall and the length is exactly enough.

EDIT: I am no longer perfectly confident about its durability. About one year after my purchase, it started to have problems when noise cancelling is on. At some positions the NC stooped working but if the cable was bent a little to some direction, NC worked again. So when I were running and the cable moved a lot, the NC sometimes worked and sometimes didn't, which is pretty annoying. I thought it was a cable connection problem. Then I sent it back to Audio Technica for repair and they sent back a new pair (good customer service!). Then it works perfectly for almost a year, and now same problem show up again. Now it is not as severe as last time and the impact is still tolerable (occasional slight noise in left ear), but I am not sure if it will worsen in the future. From my observation the problem comes from the part of cable connection the NC unit to actual headphones. If I remember correctly, this was also the part the failed in the previous pair. I am not sure if this has anything to do with that I often wear it to gym. Though I never stretch it, sweat may to damaging it.

title: Awesome headphones! Wonderful sound!
text:
I believe this is one of the best headphones you can get for this price. The sound is very good. I don't know how to analyze it technically like an audiophile, but it just feels good. It's not picky on input. Even a smartphone can drive it to a decent level (probably not to its full potential, but still good). Driving it with an amp is a little better, but not a big difference. But do note that due to its open back design, it offers virtually no noise isolation. I don't recommend using it in noisy environment. It's also very comfortable to wear, though it may get a little hot if the room temperature is high, just like all other over-head headphones. The build quality is also good. I can see this pair last for a very long time. In short, I highly recommend HD 558 if you want a pair of headphones to listen in a quiet environment. It's a real bargain for the price.

But there is one thing that I don't like about it. The cable. I am not talking about cable quality. The quality is very good. The problem is the plug. The cable comes with 6.3 mm plug. I don't understand what Sennheiser people are thinking, but this is a really stupid design. Though the package also includes a 6.3 to 3.5 mm adapter, but it extends the plug a lot and is very inconvenient (see the picture for how it looks when plugged into a Surface). First, I believe a lot of HD 558 users will drive this cans with a mobile source, such as a phone or a mobile player. There is no mobile device with 6.3 mm jack. Even for desktop amps, not all of them have 6.3 mm jack. Many amps also have 3.5 mm jack. I totally don't get what's the point of using 6.3 mm plug on this headphone. Ironically, HD 600, which is much harder to drive, comes with 3.5 mm plug. Second, even if in many cases this headphone will be plugged into a device with 6.3 mm jack, it still makes more sense to use 3.5 mm plug. An adapter from 6.3 to 3.5 is a disaster, but from 3.5 to 6.3 is perfectly fine. Eventually I replace the original cable with a Fiio one that has 3.5 mm plug, but it cost some extra dollars. It will be great if Sennheiser offers a 3.5 mm plug cable in the first place.

title: Good Gym Headphones. Could be better.
text:
I bought these headphones for listening to music in gym. I think they fulfill this purpose reasonably well. Here's some of my initial impressions.

- Active noise cancelling isn't that great. When turning on noise cancelling, I can tell it's there and it help muffle environment noise a bit, but it's nowhere near the level of good noise cancelling such as Bose QC20. QC20 can almost erase noise, while SP700N's noise cancelling can only reduce noise by a bit. On the other hand, QC20 is more expensive, larger, not wireless and not water resistant. It's not really a reasonable expectation for SP700N to match QC20. I would not buy SP700N just for its noise cancelling feature.

- Even though SP700N's noise cancelling is weak, it has pretty good noise isolation. It provides similar level of noise isolation as Shure SE215. This is an important reason for me to choose it over other truly wireless headphones like AirPods or SoundSport Free, which barely blocks any noise.

- Truly wireless. Water resistant. This is perfect for gym. No more cables in the way. No more cleaning off sweet from cables. No more worries about sweet damaging the headphones.

- There is some latency problem. When watching Youtube from Chrome on my Android phone, the latency can be over a second and makes the video barely watchable. However I find Youtube app has some optimization to reduce the latency to a fraction of a second. There's still some small latency, but much less noticeable. I have also tried MX Player and TED app on Android, and both have optimization similar to Youtube app. Overall I find video experience with SP700N bearable. I am fine with this because I mostly only listen to music in gym. As a side note, it also takes about a second to switch to next song, or change volume.

- Sound quality exceeds my expectation. It's not a Hi-Fi headphone, but the sound signature is pleasing. The sound stage is also pretty good. I can feel the music is around me, not just inside my head.

- Build quality of the headphones themselves is pretty good. Though charging case feels a bit cheaply made, especially the lid.

- I briefly tried ambient sound mode. It seems to does what it should do: let in ambient sound to counter noise isolation. I don't really use this feature. I think this might be what the noise cancelling hardware device is really for.

Overall, I am happy with this purchase. It's not perfect and has quite a few flaws, but none that bothers me a lot for my particular use case. I won't recommend SP700N as all-purpose headphones, but for gym use I think this is a nice option.

title: Unreliable heart rate, inaccurate floor count, but I can't find a better alternative
text:
Here's my review of Vivoactive 3 after 7 months of use.
Pros:
- Always on display transflective display that reads well under intense sunlight.
- Great battery life. I usually charge it once every 5 days or so when the battery level is below 20%. On full charge I think it can live up to 7-day battery life claim.
- Looks really good. The display is also pretty scratch resistant. I wear it 24/7 except charging and I see no scratch.

Cons:
- Heart rate measurement is unreliable. I'd say it works well about 75% of the time. However it's the other 25% of the time that makes me not able to count on it. Sometimes during my workout the heart rate measurement would stuck at 80-90, when my actual heart rate is in 130-140 range. It is very annoying.
- Floor count is quite inaccurate. I do a lot of floor climbing exercise. For climbing from 1st floor to 27th, it usually counts anywhere from 15 to 22 floors. It does particularly bad if I'm running up the stairs. I have seen it count 0 floors when I run from 1st floor to 27th. Also the pace graph is pretty useless. Very often it shows a mysterious spike of over 100 floors/min. I have only seen the pace graph useable twice.
- Some minor annoyances. For example, when there's an update, it would installs and reboots automatically without giving me the option to choose when. There have been times when I wanted to use the watch, and all of a sudden it reboots itself to install update. Also, it does not display any characters outside English alphabet. I listen to some Chinese and Japanese songs. All characters in their names in Garmin music control are shown are blocks.

Overall I'm not very happy with Vivoactive 3. However, it doesn't seem like there's a much better alternative on the market. My friend has a Fitbit Versa and has similar heart rate measurement issue from time to time. And the Fitbit has shorter battery life.

- It doesn't rattle like PD does when the plate is in the clip.
- I find occasionally PD plate and clip can bind in a bad way that makes it hard to put the plate in or take it out. PGYTech is way less prone to this.

There is one con compared to PD, but given the pros I still choose PGYTech over PD.
Con:
- The release button is on the opposite side of the camera grip. With PD I can often press the unlock button and take out the camera with one hand. With PGYTech it takes two hands. Alternatively I can press the button and take out the camera with my left hand, and then transfer the camera to the right hand, which is still less convenient than PD.

title: Sonos can get you hacked if you stream from a PC
text: I think that Sonos products are pretty cool, except their poor cyber security.  In short, if you store your music on a PC or a similar device like NAS and want to stream the music, you will no doubt share the folder.  When you do that, you will need to use SMB1 protocol for Sonos to work.  SMB1 makes it really easy for your computer to be hacked into.  Unfortunately, unless you have SMB1 turned on, Sonos device will not "see" the music files.  SMB1 was created by Microsoft and was replaced in 2007, yes 13 years ago.  Microsoft discountinued any sort of support for SMB1 in 2014, yes 6 years ago.  Unfortunately, SMB1 is the only way Sonos allows for music to be shared from a PC.  It is 2020 and Sonos does not seem to care that your PC will be super easy to hack into when SMB1 is turned on.

This is a budget gaming laptop, keyword being budget, so it can be quirky but it's a fantastic deal imo and with the gpu market still taking a hit from cryptocurrency, getting a prebuilt pc or laptop seems a lot better than paying 900+ for a gtx 1080....

It runs Nioh, Witcher 3, FFXV at medium settings, the specs sits at minium requirement, upgrading the ram, and possibly adding/replacing the ssd with a bigger one would improve overall performance and storage (the 5400rpm hdd is meh). Eh.... I don't know if this is a good workaround personally, even if OPTICAL gives better audio you're not getting the features you paid for. I have the newest firmware but it didn't fix it and if you google audio cutout or no audio and soundbar, the issue is still out there and hasn't been resolved for many.

It's hard to decide whether or not to send it back and get something different (JBL soundbar is what I'd consider instead) I'd research into how compatible it is with your TV (even if it's a Sony) before buying it. Sound wise, it's pretty epic when you crank it up (not so much when you're trying to watch something late at night and the volume is quiet, can't hear dialog) and Spotify, wow, sounds totally different on this.

I think you're better off committing to something more, like Sony's flagship, or their sub 300 soundbar. This is in the middle and it doesn't really bring a lot of value if you have inconsistent performance. Kinda ruins a movie if the sound cuts out randomly. If it works for you though, lucky.

title: surprising sound quality
text:
These speakers deliver surprisingly good sound for the price, and size. The sub woofer design does allow for more bass than anybody needs as many people have pointed out, but it is a very fulfilling sound.

For games it is awesome sounding, and teamed with a Creative X-Fi sound card, it's easy to configure the different output options other than switching the slide switch behind the woofer.

For music it sounds very crisp, clear, and still plenty more bass than ya need. The mids could be better, but tweaking the eq settings in your sound card software can patch that up. When I switch my X-fi from game mode to entertainment mode however, I do get some static-y crackling, as if somethings not shielded, that you can hear when there is no sound output, or very quiet music passages. Not sure where this is coming from, but since it doesn't happen in game mode, sounds like it's from the sound card.

The woofer enclosure is indeed VERY large, if you put it under your desk, you either have no room for your feet, or a nice footrest. Cables are adequate for putting around you as you sit at the computer, if you want them in the 4 corners of your room you can get extensions, they are just standard rca audio connectors, unlike others that hardwire them in, or use some weird plugs.

My first one arrived with the center channel not working, it was the amp, not speakers. Amazon sent me a replacement right away, before I sent the defect back even. Very nice, although I was told my cost for shipping back would be credited back, and it hasn't.

Replacement works fine, fraggin and crankin the tunes for about a month now, and glad I made the purchase.
