title: Better than any speakers you'll find in a computer monitor
text:
These are decent sounding speakers for their size. They are small and lightweight. They come in a glossy white finish, which I suppose is to make them match an ipod. The black speaker grills which are magnetically attached, blend in more with the more stylish and trendy black computer monitors and keyboards that most people buy these days.

You can get decent bass out of these when using anything with an eq, just don't crank the low frequencies up too high, nor the volume. They definitely sound better than any speakers you'll find in a computer monitor, and better than most their size. But there is no fear of rattling anything on your desk, or thumping things off the wall.

When used with an mp3 player, your at the mercy of whatever eq settings it has, since these speakers offer no tone controls at all. You get a nice blue glow around the on/off volume knob, and that's it. There is no mounting holes in the back of the speakers, so they can't go on the wall.

If they do sell for the $149 price, then you'd probably be better off looking for something else. That is surely too much for what they offer in my opinion. Heck, my 280 watt Logitech 5.1 system with so much bass you HAVE to turn it down didn't cost much more than that.

And speaking of wattage, 18 per speaker is the usual stretching of the truth. The little foldout that comes with it says the hi frequency amplifier is 7, and the lower is 11. Figure about half that, 9 watts per channel is more reality. Loud enough for your desktop, don't think you'll be getting room filling sound with these though.

Edit: After a couple weeks of use, they give static when moving any of the wires, the one attached to the other speaker or the one attached to the computer. Unplugging all and replugging seemed to lessen it, but still present.
item_title: Creative GigaWorks HD50 2.0 Multimedia Speaker System

title: Not bad for what it does
text:
I've been using this combo for about a week, and it does a pretty acceptable job. I won't know how the battery life is for awhile, so I can't comment on that now.

The keyboard is fine, some reviewers say it is loud, but they are probably younger, or newer to computer people who grew up on the soft touch keyboards that are relatively silent. I have been using computers for quite awhile, and like the tactile feel and clicky sounds a keyboard makes, let's you know when they have been pressed. This isn't as loud as the old ibm clackers of yesteryear, but is a bit louder than your average softouch.

The function keys are a bit smaller than I would like, but usable, even though they are covered with symbols for all the other funky things they do, and the F numbers are barely readable as though an afterthought. There is also the usual conglomoration of multimedia and programmable keys that are now all the rage, though I personally find most of them just annoying. I do like the volume being able to be adjusted, as well as the one touch key to bring up the calculator.

I usually don't install the software to make all the fancy keys do their fancy tricks, but I did on this one. It has some Windows 7 specific keys and functions in it, and since I am running that OS, thought I'd give it a go. You get 5 special keys that open the first 5 programs in your taskbar, no big deal, think I've used them once to see if they work. They do, but... for me... no biggie...

The mouse.... now that is a good news bad news issue for me. It works great, on multiple surfaces like they claim, and the buttons have a nic click and feel, not too easy to accidently press down, not too hard. The scroll wheel.... that's the sticky point so to speak. It scrolls fine, but it doesn't have and clicks to feel while you are scrolling, it is totally smooth. Whoever thought that was a good idea must have had too many coffee's or redbulls, or something. It's not hard to use, but it does scroll pages while your reading if your not careful, not to mention for gaming it is horrible if you use that to switch weapos as you don't know when to stop and it shoots past the one your trying to get.

It's definitely a step up from 1000 series, the keyboard actually has a rubber pad on the wrist rest for one, not as cheap feeling either. But the smooth scroll on the mouse HAS to be changed.

title: A good wireless combo
text:

It feels more natural and the usb receiver that plugs into your computer is very small, which makes it great for laptops/notebooks/netbooks. I tried it in both my desktop and my laptop and they worked fine. Of course I don't need the keyboard for the laptop, but I imagine there could be times you could kick back with the wireless keyboard in yyour lap instead of the whole laptop computer if it's on a table or desk in front of you.

The mouse is responsive enough, but I would use it for fast action twitch shooters. It was fine for my Everquesting though.

The keyboard has enough keys for everyone, with a slew of extra accessory keys which I generally don't use. I prefer not to install all kinds of drivers just to have a few programmable keys, although the option is nice for those who want it.

I mentioned the usb receiver is small, it is TINY, which could be bad if you take it out and set it on your desktop. It could get easily lost if not careful. In the computer it's great though, doesn't block another usb port or anything.

All in all a nice product. I can't comment on the life of the battereies as I've only used it a few months and they are still going strong. The box advertises up to a year, time will tell..

All in all a good little audio device.

title: Good solution to a common problem.
text:
This kit works pretty well for those that need to get internet access to devices in your home without having to run additional cables, or relying on an iffy or slow wifi connection.

You plug one unit into an ac outlet near your router, then run an included cable from it to your router. You then plug the other unit into an ac outlet near the device you want to hook up to the internet such as your computer, gaming console, tv etc..... and plug another included cable from the unit to your device.

You are now hooked up and ready to go. The speed is very quick, and it works with any outlet in the house. You can even hook up more units if need be to get to other devices.

This works great if you have a large house, multi floors, or other issues which would prevent wifi from getting to your devices, and some devices don't have a wifi connection anyway. If you have to have an internet cable hooked up, this will be what you need and get the job done well.

The one bad thing I can say about these units is that they need to be plugged into the ac outlet directly. They can't be plugged into a power strip. You can plug a powerstrip into the unit itself, it does have a pass through outlet. But the downside is these units then aren't surge protected. They would take the hit first.

So if your not in an area prone to lightning strikes or big power surges, this kit is ideal for you.
item_title: Netgear Powerline AV+ 200 Adapter Kit (XAV1501)

title: Awesome router
text:
This is truly an awesome router. With it's coverage of both frequencies, signal boosters, no cd installs, what's not to like.

This router will not only get you a great signal throughout your house, it will get it across the street with ease. I get 5 bars in every room of the house as well as poolside in the backyard. My neighbor across the street says he can see it with 4 bars in his house.

It was easy to setup and install, I am pretty knowledgeable about computers and networking, but even for non techies it should be no problem getting it hooked up and running.

I really like the 2 usb ports to hook up a printer and an external hard drive. You can plug just about any regular printer into it (as long as it has a usb cord) and any computer in the network can use it. Much cheaper than buying a wifi specific printer. And adding an external hard drive is good for sharing files and being able to watch videos or whatever without having to share every computer with each other on the network.

It is built with more specs and features than most wifi adapters can presently use, so it's going to be best in class for a good long time to come. It's extremely fast and looks sharp as well.

The only downside is that it is a bit expensive, but it is pretty much the best router you can get in my opinion. If you want strong signal everywhere in your location, and the benefit of using one usb printer for everyone,this will do it for you, and do it very well.

title: Works well and a nice small package
text:
This unit works well. It supports both the 2.4 and the 5 ghz bands, and the a/b/g/n flavors of wifi. It's pretty small, about the size of 2 packs of cigarettes.

I tried it first in 2.4 ghz mode, and used it with my laptop and a friend tried his xbox, both worked fine with nice range and no drops. I was able to get a nice 3- 4 bars at the neighbors house with the extender just inside my house at a window in a wall closest to the neighbor.

I then switched it to 5 ghz. There is no interference in this band, very few people use it, or even know about it yet.... so this is a good thing, better bandwidth, no interference. However, the range is shorter, so it's kind of a trade off. I had just happened to get a 5 ghz capable card for my desktop, so I was able to test it with that. I do only get 3 bars whereas I can get 4 in the 2.4 ghz, but the lack of others in the band makes up for it. Your mileage will vary, just have to try it, do speed tests, or see what looks like it's faster in your instance.

Overall this is a solid product with some nice options, and it works like a charm.
item_title: WD My Net Wi-Fi Range Extender - universal dual-band wireless network range extender

title: Pretty cool drive
text:

I chose to download the driver and see how it goes, and it works well. We're using it with Vista on a laptop. The wife likes to edit old family photos, put frames and effects and stuff on em, and this is a great place to save and store the originals and her projects.

No need for power, it's powered off the usb port. It's nice n small, pencil thin and barely larger than a deck of cards. It's price won't hurt you too bad, the interchangeable feature, as well as no need for additional power makes this a damn good item in my opinion.

title: Works well, when it works
text:

It's pretty much plug and play, right out of the box. I don't like the fact that the warranty is only one year as many have said. I also don't like the propriety cord that plugs in the usb in your computer. The other end is some weird plug that will only fit the drive. It would be nice if it was a regular usb cord, so if/when the cord has a problem, only one place to try and get a replacement is Seagate.

The main issue I have with it is it seems to only want to work in on usb on my computer. I have 4 usb's in my HP laptop, the only one it works in is the combo usb/esata port. That means I can't use my other removable which only plugs into the esata port.

I tried it in my desktop. and it will only work in one usb in the back of the computer, won't even power up in either of the 2 in the front of the computer. With the usb devices I need to use, like keyboard, mouse, wifi dongle, and flash drives, it makes it a puzzle to get things working at times.

My computers are a couple years old, not sure if that has anything to do with it, maybe the usb 3.0 would eliminate the issue, maybe not.

title: Works pretty well
text:
I've had a few different models from TP-Link, and have been happy with them, this one is no exception. The others didn't have the 5 Ghz band option, but they did have a detachable antenna and a short cable on them that made them attractive to me. This one doesn't have a high gain antenna on the outside, but still does a pretty darn good job of picking up a signal.

If you have a router capable of 5 Ghz, you should try to use that band, as not many people are, and it has less congestion. It does have a shorter range however, there always is a tradeoff. But I think a 3 bar connection on the 5 Ghz is better than a 4 or even 5 bars on the 2.4 band......

I have a number of tp-link products, and they work well with other brand routers, and maybe a little better when matched with their own routers.

Semi minor complaint, they do seem to be extremely slow with drivers. Well, actually the drivers are fine, it's the utility provided which is lacking. It says it's only compatible with Windows XP and Vista...... really..... when 7 has been available for years already..... good thing you really don't need it, but it would be nice to provide something a little more up to date one would think.

title: Nice little device
text:
This works great for what it is. It IS NOT a router, it is a switch that will allow you to hook up multiple devices WITH WIRES to each other and/or the internet.

Wireless is convenient and all, but for best speeds wires still rule. This switch stays cool to the touch which is nice, and works as advertised.

I have run 1 cable from my wireless router from the house to the guest house, then hooked this up. Now I can hook up the desktop, a couple of laptops to it and get much better connection than just the wifi. And when I want I can disconnect it from the internet and just use it as an intranet, connecting the computers together without having to worry about privacy settings and sharing over the wifi network which can be hacked into even with passwords.

Can't go wrong with this, if you have the need for a switch.
item_title: TP-Link 5 Port Gigabit Ethernet Network Switch | Plug and Play | Desktop or Wall-Mount | Plastic Case Ethernet Splitter | Fanless | Traffic Optimization | Unmanaged (TL-SG1005D)

title: Whats not to like?
text:
Like the title says, what's not to like about this router?? It does both 2.4 and 5.0 bands at the same time, it has a button to turn off wireless, QOS settings, detachable antennas so you can add higher gain ones if you want, plus a usb port for printer or storage.

It's easy to set up, works pretty much out of the box if you don't want to mess with configurations, and has good signal strength.

I like to use the 5 ghz band when possible because not many people use it, so there is much less interference on that band. The 2.4 is always congested with your neighbors wifi, cordless phones, microwaves, etc. The only downside is that the 5 ghz has a shorter range than the 2.4, so your mileage may vary.

I have quite a few tp-link products, wifi/usb dongles, routers, wifi PCIe card for the desktop, all work great with each other, and no issues when connecting to other brands.

title: Solid keyboard, a bit pricey, designed for gamers not typists
text:
This is the lower end of the 3 (at this time) different models of keyboards that Turtle Beach are introducing. They are well known for their headsets and sound cards, and seem to be branching out. In my opinion, so far it's hit and miss.

This keyboard as I previously mentioned is the lower cost of the 3. It is your basic keyboard layout, without being cluttered up with a bunch of 'shortcut keys' that I never use. It's got 4 indicator lights, the usual numlock and capslock, as well as a scrlk and a winlk. It's heavier than your average keyboard, seems more solid, and they say the imprint on the keys won't rub off which is nice, since I'm not a touch typist and need to look at the keys now and again, even while gaming. They are labeled nice and big in white on the black keys so they can be seen easily. It is not backlit, except for a logo on the spacebar, so if you game in complete darkness you might have a little issue, maybe not, your milage will vary.

They are marketing this as being in between a mechanical and a membrane type keyboard, I think it definitely leans towards feeling like a membrane. It doesn't have any mechanical clicky feel at all. The keys do seem relatively firm, but nothing game changing. It says it comes with a braided usb cord, which a lot of people assume means the outside of the cord would be braided. It really means it uses a braided shield under the outside wire instead of just foil, which does provide better shielding against signal loss and interference. I didn't slice mine open to see if it was true, we'll have to take their word for that.

Being the entry level option, it has no extras like backlighting, extra usb slots etc like the higher end models have. It is designed for gamers, and the biggest feature for them/us is that you can press up to 30 keys at a time and have them all register. I don't know anyone who would or could do that, but it will assure you that playing with 2 hands on the keyboard and pressing multiple combo keys at once will be recognized. Most keyboards will register an certain number of keys being pressed at tone time, and could be an issue for serious gamers. That seems to be it's only really unique function to me.

The only downside I see is the lack of a backlight for the keys, and the price. At it's $60 introductory price, seems a bit much for what your getting. Maybe if it lasts for 5 to 10 years with no letters rubbing off and no keypress degradation, it could be a value, but only time will tell on that front. Still, a solid keyboard, you could pay more, you could pay less. It does look kinda cool with the red trim and spacebar logo, but my system is blue accented so it looks out of place.

text:

We have our router at one end of our long ranch style house, close to the bedrooms/computer rooms. They seem to get the 'N' wifi just fine. At the other end of the house, and the garage that's been converted to a den/playroom, different story. Too far to get a reliable signal, and too far to run a cable, switch/hub/2nd router etc. Brick walls and metal soffets or whatever the heck they are called block and/or send the signal elsewhere.

As others have noted, these are really easy to install and use. Plug into wall outlet near routere, plug in provided ethernet cable. Go other end where you need the internet device/computer, do the same. Bing Bang Boom, instant connection. It's fast enough to deliver video and music from my network storage device plugged into the router with no skips, stutters or pauses. I don't have a fast enough connection to test the 1200 Mbps speed claim, we're rural and have a Verizon LTE connection at the house, and only a 2-3 bar signal at that. But as I said, no stutter or pauses, and things load as quickly if not quicker than the 'N' wifi connection the other rooms have.

Only downside (as others have also stated), needs to go into the wall outlet, and usually blocks the other plug.

title: Good system, good price, and it comes with 2 ps2 ports for us old folks to gaze at and remember the ole dayz
text:
This is a pretty good system for gaming or video editing. It's the first already built computer I have owned in at least 25 years. I have always built my own from scratch. I prefer to get each part that I want, for every single piece. That way I know I'll be happy with it, and it should last quite awhile with room for upgrades. My last computer was bought in 2009, and about the only things that weren't swapped out in that time were the cpu (cuz the motherboard couldn't take any faster), the power supply (it was 750 watts, way overkill for back then and a little even now), my trusty soundblaster x-fi sound card that still works to this day, and the optical drive which should have been replaced, but I just couldn't be bothered with it with the advent of flash drives.

Anyway, it was past time for something new, and I got the opportunity to test this system. FINALLY usb 3.0 and sata 3! There are PLENTY of usb ports 2.0 and 3.0 along with a usb 3.1 type c, which I don't even have a use for yet. Right up front you get 2 - 2.0 and 2 - 3.0 slots. Why do they even bother with 2.0 anymore? The 3.0 are backwards compatible. On the back there are 4 more 3.0 and 2 more 2.0. Oughta keep me happy for awhile and I can retire my 4 port usb hub.

The supplied rx 570 video card has 1 hdmi and 3 display port outputs, which caused me a little issue. My monitor is also from 2009, and has vga and dvi ports. Luckily one of the video cards I bought in the past came with an hdmi to dvi adapter. Otherwise I would have had to buy one to use the system at all. I still need another adapter so I can plug in the tv to watch downloaded videos and whatnot on the bigger screen. The 4 gigs of ram on the card is adequate, and it does a nice job.

The ryzon 5 cpu and the 1 stick of 8 gigs ram are plenty for the games I play and the photo editing as well. There only 2 ram slots, but the system will support up to 32 gigs.

The case is nice, all plastic on the outside, but solid metal frame inside. The blue led light is very cool, and it can be turned off via a software switch from Dell if ya don't like it.

My only peeve would be that it's not that expandable, but most Dell aren't. It only has 1 bay for SSD, and 2 for mechanical HDD, one of which contains a 1 tb drive already. I mounted an ssd in here for my boot drive, and also added a ssd adapter that holds 2 drives in the last HDD bay. I only used one laptop HDD in it, had some of my old stuff I still wanted to use on it. If I want to add another small drive or SSD on that adapter, I'll have a hard time getting power to it. There were only 3 power connectors right there at the bays. It seems like there might be one or 2 hiding in the harness but they are far away from the drive bays.

There are 2 slots on the m/b for m2 ssd drives which is a surprise, but they are more expensive than the regular ssd's owing to their smaller size. Something to look at in the future perhaps.

They include a keyboard and mouse, nothing to write home about. They are usb, I thought they might be ps2, since there are 2 ps2 ports on the back as well. NO idea why. Haven't used those type of ports for more than a dozen years or so ago.

All in all a pretty good system for a pretty good price, and upgradable for a few years into the future.

title: Great features, great price, and very helpful people in support and forums
text:
These travel routers are pretty cool. They are primarily designed to carry around with you (and they are very small) and you can hook up to a hotel ethernet connection and share wifi with all your devices, or connect wirelessly to any wifi and connect through the travel router and get an extra layer of protection, since you are on a subnet, not hooked up directly to the same network as everyone else is, say in a Starbucks, airport or wherever.

They work very well for that, a few clicks and your online. They also work well to extend your network throughout your house and cover any weak spots you may have. This model has 2 ethernet ports, 1 for WAN and 1 for LAN, as well as a usb port that you can plug usb modems, tether your phone or hotspot through it, and also plug a storage device like a hard drive or flash drive to it and share it on your network. It can be used as a repeater, a bridge and in WISP mode, so it can handle MANY different situations. And in advance mode in the web admin interface, you can reprogram it it to do almost anything you need. It runs on a custom openwrt firmware, with a nice gui, or you can flash many other firmware as well.

The forums are very helpful if you need assistance or have questions, and you really can't beat the price. They have other models with more and different configurations to meet pretty much any kind of network need or task. If/when I need another, I will not hesitate to purchase another, and I would recommend them to everyone.
I am using mine at home right now. I am tethering a Netgear Explore cellular hotspot/modem/router to it, and then plugging into my 5 port switch via the LAN port so my 2 desktops and NAS are connected, all via ethernet cables. I am so rural I can only get decent internet thru cellular, and I wanted to eliminate using wifi because wires are always faster, and no interference like with wifi.And I can still connect with my phone via wifi, so all is well.

I tries a bunch from Acronis, Casper, which was supposed to work, and almost did, but my start menu wouldn't come up and kept crashing the system, and a few more that didn't work either, Macromium being one that was supposed to, but didn't.

Took me over a month to move, finally did, and hooked up the monitor. it's a HUGE size, even coming from a 27", still a huge step up in size. For a TV, small, but for gaming on a PC it's massive. But I love it. The curved screen is a little easy to lose your cursor at times, but I'm sure I'll get used to it.

After running for a couple hours, a band of about 3" worth of lines appeared on screen, and wouldn't go away. Happened in both inputs and when there was nothing plugged into the monitor except power. And it was past the return date for Amazon so I had to deal with Samsung repair. Was an easy enough process, they even sent me a UPS return label to print to send it back 2nd day air. They did keep it over a week though, and I think they actually repaired the same monitor and sent it back. Wasn't a reconditioned unit off the shelf. At least it was the same box I sent it in.

All works well, and I really wish it was brighter, I have it set to full brightness and almost full contrast, and there are still some darker/muddy area when watching movies or playing some games. I'm sure if I mess with more settings I can improve it some, but mostly ok. The response time is fine, the 2k resolution is awesome, and my poor lil rx 570 can push this many pixels just fine.

A lot of games make it work really hard, and have had to turn some settings down. When playing in 1680x1050, I could have a lot of games on Ultra, and some in 1080. But popping the monitor on to it's full 2560x1440 it dropped frames to about 8-10. Had to go down a couple notches to Very High on most games to get playable again. Better video cards will handle better, but with prices the way they are, I'm happy with this for now.

title: Good receiver
text: I got this as a factory refurb and so far it has been working fine.  Good sound, excellent set of features.  Really enjoying the network play options, such as Pandora and Internet Radio.  Setup was a bit more complicated than I would have liked.  Most of the setup requires attaching a display (TV).  Once the TV was attached, I had to update the firmware of the unit.  This required downloading a file from the Internet and putting it on a USB stick and plugging the USB stick into the receiver.  The firmware update completed without issue.  Next step was configuring the auto-surround, which involved putting a (included) microphone where I normally sit.  The receiver then played some noise on each of the speakers, and automatically adjusted the surround sound.  Surround sound was good afterwards.  Configuring Pandora was somewhat of a pain.  The interface for inputting user name and password really sucked and required me to press the up arrow button like 60 times per character, and I have a long user name and password, so it took a long time to input.  Once inputted, it failed to connect because the - and the _ characters are hard to distinguish on the OSD, so I had to start all over again from the beginning.  Sigh.  But I got it done and was listening to Pandora.  The OSD for Pandora really sucks.  For a HD receiver, the OSD is very low rez and looks terrible on a 47-inch TV.  Pandora also doesn't display track information properly, for example it will show the name of the band and the album, but not the song.  Hopefully they will fix this.  But who cares, since I'm more concerned that the music plays ok vs .looking at the OSD.  I don't like CDs so I have my record player plugged into one of the audio inputs.  Kind of lame that there was no audio input labelled for Phono, so I had to plug it into the port labelled CD.  (So I have to press CD on the remote to listen to records.)  Sound is fine though.  Overall, this receiver has some faults, but nothing that would stop me from buying it again, and none of the faults have been related to sound quality or basic functionality.  Given the choice to spend the money elsewhere, I would still pick this receiver again, especially since I got it at half-price because it was a factory refurb.

title: The other details
text:
I bought this drive because it was rated as top of the line. While I am please with the drive, there are a few concerns and additional details that you might not find in other reviews:

If you are like me and bought this drive to speed up a system that is a few years old, there is a fair chance that you have an older Sata6 controller on your motherboard. Specifically a Marvell controller. Well it turns out those old Marvell controllers suck and give BSoD with SSD drives. So I had to plug it into a Sata 3.0 port, and it still runs pretty fast, but if you want Sata6, check compatibility and make sure you don't have an old Marvell controller. You don't really lose a lot running on Sata3, but still, that sucks.

I only gave this drive 4 stars because it does not ship with hard drive rails. Rails cost manufactures almost nothing, whereas a consumer can have a hard time finding a set locally. Seems like a no-brainer to include a set of rails, 4 screws, and a sata cable. Whatever happened to the good old days when those were standard.

Another issue, and it's not really about the drive, but more about Windows 7: Windows 7 is often pre-configured to run a defrag every week. It's hidden and runs in the background. You should disable this. SSDs don't need or like to be defrags. The instruction manual should mention this since a majority of their customers are using Win7.

All that said and done, this drive gives me a 7.9 Windows rating. Frankly, it's nice to see those numbers maxed, but I'll be frank: I didn't really notice a screaming fast difference with my computer. It does boot faster, but I don't care much about that because I only reboot every few weeks. My system already has a fast processor, memory, video, etc... So the performance jump with a faster hard drive isn't mind blowing.

I'd have no problems buying this drive again, but in hindsight, I would have lowered my expectations.

title: A solid mobo but overclocking has some issues.
text: I'd love to give this one all 5 stars but there were some issues:  First, the BIOS needs more work.  The auto-overclocking feature doesn't really work well.  It basically increases the speed until it crashes and then uses the last stable setting.  However it doesn't stress test it enough to get a proper analysis.  For example, when overclocked it works ok under a normal load, but at full CPU usage (such as encoding a video via handbrake) it will crash after a few minutes, where as the stress test only lasts a minute or less.  Later BIOS revisions might be able to fix this.  Also, I think it could use an extra USB 2.0 header.  While it has plenty of on-board USB ports, it only has 1 or 2 USB2.0 headers which are used in the panels of my Corsair Obsidian 900d case.  I have an entire Corsair system including power supply, case, cooling, and with all these Corsair parts, I wanted to use the Corsair Commander Mini control module so I could power all the necessary fans.  But the Corsair Commander Mini requires a USB2.0 header connection and I didn't have an available one.  So I had to buy a USB3.0 to USB2.0 header adapter so I could connect it to the 3.0 instead.  So what it comes down to is that this top-end motherboard isn't 100% compatible out of the box with the top end Corsair system, as would be expected.  I doubt most others will have this issue, but it was a problem for me.  I gave it 4/5 stars because of the poor overclocking function, not lack of 2.0 headers.

title: Sennheiser CX300-B Earbuds
text:
Early on, I bought these earphones because people stated on various reviews that they were great!

Well... my experience was completely different!

The cords have a J-type cable so one end is shorter than the other and is meant to wrap around the user's neck while the cord travels down one side of the body instead of the middle.

Also, the cable is SO thin that there is (forgot the technical term for it but there is one) an echo and vibration that travels through the cable. MANY people on various forums have noted this, probably the result of thin metal cables, light rubber insulation or both.

The reverberation of the cable feedback is SO annoying and can be quite load, even if you're walking slowly. The noise is heard even when the cable gently sways lightly.

The earbuds do NOT isolate noise, as compared to earphones from Shure or other high earphone brands!

Also, the construction is so light that the cable and wiring tore near the earbuds that I had to send them back for a replacement.

I've since put the new and sealed replacements away and it's sitting somewhere gathering dust! I've lost my investment as the value of the earphones dropped. Most people can buy it online for ~$20 but I bought it when it was near retail ~$50!

Shure earphones are my preference now, especially the SC-4, now called the SCL-4 model. It cost much more but worth every penny! Literally!
The guarantee is terrific and the sound isolation is one of the best!

The Sennheiser CX300-B(lack) Earbuds should be avoided at all costs!

Be very skeptical of other people's reviews as many reviewers get carried away with their emotions instead of putting an unbiased review of how products actually function!

title: Seagate 1TB SATA External Hard Drive
text:
Very simple to install especially if it's used as a secondary drive. The retail box includes the SATA cable and power cord connector cable and Cloning CD.

If used as primary drive, then the Cloning software isn't that good.
Sure, it cloned the original hdd but it kept the partition! NOT good when you upgraded from 250GB to 1T since the Cloned drive is recognized as a 250GB drive NOT a 1T drive!!

2 Solutions:

1. Buy a partitioning software to remove partition and resize the hard drive so it'll be recognized properly as a 1Tb drive

OR....

2. Do what many PC users do annually - RESTORE THE ENTIRE PRIMARY DRIVE with a Fresh installation of Windows! Sure, it'll LITERALLY take HOURS for a Fresh install (including other software not just Windows) but you'll have a Clean PC that runs faster and smoother since it's not loaded with software garbage that accumulated over time!

I chose Option 2 which took literally 1 entire day but, in the end, it was worth it! My 3 year old computer now runs smoother, faster and has lots of room on the primary drive. I now have a computer with 2 1Tb hard drives but I still perform backups to external drives.

BTW... my external harddrives are now becoming 1Tb hard drives since I build them myself with 1Tb internal drives and external Hdd enclosures.
It's very simple to assemble then plug and play for additional (MASSIVE) storage! It's better to build your own External hard drives than buy one of those pre-bulit ones that don't even include an on/off switch!!

Price is pretty good now ~$117 sale price (at B*****y).
Better than the $125-130 sale price about 1 month ago so it's SLOWLY dropping in price!

One caution:
Not sure about the reliability so keep your receipts and register the product!

Seagate used to be TERRIBLE years ago but when it bought Maxtor, then their HDD quality actually improved since the company must have obviously incorporated Maxtor's engineering designs into their own designs!

title: Sandisk 64Gb SDXC
text:
The Sandisk 64gb SDXC card does work on the GTab tablets including the 7" versions (as I have the GT7Plus).

You'll need to format it with software to Fat32 as Windows can't format it if the card >32Gb due to a Windows limitation from what I've read elsewhere. Try EaseUs Partition Master Home Edition as it's free and it works.

Too bad Android doesn't recognize NTFS as many movies have to be formatted specially to <4Gb to fit onto the card.

Also, the 64Gb card does have problems as many people on various forums have reported corruption issues. I just experienced this same corruption issue as the card couldn't read >30Gb. I contacted Sandisk support to have it returned and exchanged for a newer card which I received and reformatted just now.

Be aware that the 64Gb card may have some Quality issues if more owners are reporting quality issues with their card.

The return took ~1 week to ship prepaid to Sandisk then another week or two for a returned new card which also includes an SD adapter and case.

The price for the 64Gb card is currently ~$60USD. During certain holiday sales (i.e. Black Friday), the price dropped to ~$35USD so buy it if you need one as that's a good price. Unfortunately, many retailers are backordered like mine so I had to cancel my order since there was no word on when newer shipments would be arriving!

For a supposed Class 10 card, the speed is relatively slow when transferring files, especially large files, though I haven't formally tested it, but watching the transfer of files and the time it took to transfer. Some other reviewers have tested the speed but with differing results so who knows which is correct.

The main point of the card is its relatively large storage capacity which was the main reason of buying it, though having it on sale at a lower cost would also help in the buying decision ;)

Otherwise, I have the 32Gb version Sandisk cards available as backup cards.

Remember to keep your receipt for warranty purposes especially if the card becomes corrupted for whatever reason.

text:
Bought it new.

The noise isolation function isn't that great. It's suppose to work with LOW frequency (repetitive) noise such as noise from airplane engines.

It does NOT block out peoples' voices or LOUD noises as it was NOT designed for that! When using it in a library, I could still hear peoples' voices (which is another problem itself considering it's in a library!) but it reduced, not completely cancel, the AC system and voices which sounds muffled with the NC feature on.

One can still use the headphones WITHOUT using the NC feature but the volume and quality of the sound is low not rich and somewhat lively when the NC is turned on.

There is pressure to the ears when the. NC feature is turned on.
Also, it's very loud while wearing the headphones outside esp. on windy days as you will hear whooshing sounds from the wind even with the NC feature turned on.

I have the regular version, mdr-zx110, and it's really not much, if any, difference. it's not really worth the extra money to spend on the mdr-zx110NC version. Buy it at reduced cost online than paying full price if you insist in buying this model.

FYI... if you only want sound Isolation without listening to anything, then consider ear plugs or a sound isolation headset that outside (ie construction) workers use as either blocks out noise much better.

Active isolation headphones are designed to emit sound waves to block out low frequency noises (hum from airplane engine) not higher frequency noise like voices or road noise.

Better to use passive sound insulation devices (foam headsets or earplugs) to block out most other noises.

Nothing blocks out 100% of noise but may reduce it.

Like other subscription services, you'll have to PAY to get other media content like movies or TV series.
Some TV broadcast companies do have their own channels and will provide free viewing of their CURRENT shows generally a few days AFTER of it's release date. CBS CHARGES for its shows.
There are some other channels that will allow you to view the tv shows as it's aired to circumvent those limitations.
Basically, some older shows/movies are available depending on the channel available.
If you want the 'premium' access like current tv shows or movies, then you'll have to subscribe to them.

If people really want to 'cut the cord with cable' then that truly means going back to 'over the air' FREE channels IF it's available in your location!

Roku is a streaming service which provides access to many channels that cable providers provide and is NO different than those providers.
All people are doing is switching from one type of provider to another except that streaming services provides channels that allow people to just cancel their services unlike cable which locks you into a contract, usually a 1 year minimum contract, provide lousy customer/tech support and charging you a monthly equipment rental fee.

Ironically, the streaming channels are NO different than cable's stations except you may not get local stations and that many times, even with so many different much things to watch, there's really Nothing 'worth' watching at times.

Wish that Roku would change it's remote to include some dimples on the back cover to make removing the battery slot easy and that the remote had more functions and that's functionality was better when selecting and moving about in channels as well as getting local television contracts so people can actually watch their local tv stations (directly or indirectly through some channels).

text:
Just received them. Opened the package and charged the case which charges the earbuds inside.
The instruction booklet is Tiny and you could barely read it as the lettering (in difference languages) were also small.
Pairing was simple... take the earbuds out of the case and wait a few seconds for them to find each other to pair up then turn on Bluetooth on your smartphone. Look for the BT device ending in -R which pairs both earbuds.

The only controls on the earbuds:
1. Answer on/off for the microphone for calls
- Haven't tried the microphone feature yet.
2. Fastforward and play but No reverse
3. NO Volume control as you use the smartphone's volume control for that.

Had to set my iPhone's volume indicator on the LOW side since the volume was loud.
Also, you should also hear the difference in file quality if you have higher bitrate files encoded at 320k than 128k/256k.

Adjust the ear tips to fit your ears so it forms a proper seal to block out most external noise, lower the volume and enjoy. Would've been better if foam ear tips were included instead of the cheap rubber-like plastic tips.
You'll need to make sure you get a good seal or you won't hear well. So far, the music quality is fine but noticed that is bass heavy.

The earbuds are thick with a bulbous design but the fit was acceptable and you'll have to get used to wear wireless earbuds in your ears as these are my set of wireless earbuds. It's not bad for the price at $30 but not if it's near $50.

Update:
The cheap, plastic eartips do Not form a good seal in the ear as you still hear outsides noises and the earpieces don't feel snug. As you try to wiggle the earpiece to get a good fit, you almost always press the buttons so you know it wasn't designed well.
The plastic ear tips need to be replaced with foam tips for a good fit and to block out outside noise.
Since the fit isn't that snug, you will increase the volume to hear anything so be careful not to hurt your hearing.
Don't leave it anywhere where it gets hot as the battery life drops.
The case is bulky as heck and not comfortable to carry around which you must do to store the earpieces when not used. You can barely fit the recharging cable in the box which is terribly designed. You'll also need to carry a wall charger adapter Separately to use the charging cable.
Double clicking does Not work that well as it's designed to go both Forward AND Reverse but you do NOT know which direction it goes when you double click! Stupid design!
Foam eartips would be much better but you can't even get them from anyone like Comply.

Update:
Wearing and listening with the earphones have started to give me a slight ache in the ears and above my eyes.
The bass is TOO heavy. Sometimes the sound is weak in the left earpiece.
You really have to set the volume on the low side.
Will use the device sparingly.

Update:
The left earpiece has started to fritz out whenever the volume changes or trying to connect.
The right earpiece has started to go out as the sound is weaker than the left earpiece. The bass is on the left side which is louder compared to the right side.
There's barely any noise isolation that you'll need to increase the volume to hear the audio.
Also, the earbuds don't really fit and there's NO replacement parts so you better keep it clean!

title: No Vidbox Capture Device error
text:
"No Vidbox capture device detected!" error SOLVED.
I had to call support to get this, so I figured I'd post it. Specifically Windows 10
1. Open the Start Menu
2. Click the Gear icon ⚙️
3. Scroll down to Privacy and click it
4. On the left hand side, scroll down to "Camera" (under "App permissions")
5. On the right hand side, go to "Allow apps to access your camera" and turn it on.

If the issue persists, it's probably a bad driver. Their tech support is helpful and responsive if you need them.

title: Zi8 is a thoughtfully designed pocket HD video camera
text:
The only reasons I purchased the Zi8 was for the external microphone input, the tripod socket, the HD video and price; in that order. The optional remote control sealed the deal for this pocket video camera. Even if the videos or pictures weren't perfect the convenience and accessories would make up for it. However the videos are great for the price, the sounds syncs up perfectly, and it has a digital zoom which is not extremely effective but does exist, without the mechanical noise (and effectiveness)of a lens zoom.

I purchased a mono external microphone (ATR3350) and it worked perfectly once I adjusted the microphone volume on the Zi8 (remember the Zi8 will NOT provide extra power to your mic if it requires it). There was a small ringing in the background of the video, not very noticeable and I suspect it can be remedied.

I've read that for Mac users it's seamless with iMovie but Windows users may have more difficulty. If you have problems editing .mov files with your editing program, you may be a little frustrated. It works fine in CS4 if you got it. It also comes with a basic editing program (cut and filter) when you install the MediaImpressions media player (it installs when you first plug the Zi8 into your computer).

I used a class 10 16gb SDHC card although a class 6 would work just fine.

The Zi8 also shipped with the current firmware (1.06)

The Zi8 also plugs right in to your USB port with it's built-in flexible USB plug. It also ships with an HD-video cord and audio cables so you can play video from it to your TV with sound. Use it with the optional remote and you have a nice little handy video player and card reader for your HDTV or projector.

You can charge the battery from the wall, from your USB port to the charging inlet or even just plugging the Zi8 directly into the computer with that built-in USB plug.

One negative thing was the poor still-picture quality. On the "scenery" setting, from a range of 3' to 20' indoors, in a brightly lit area, the images were quite bad (blurry), with or without the "face detection" or even the "EIS" which are some of the few settings options available. There is a handy macro switch which gives crystal clear images at exactly 6" away at even low-light; but I'm unable to get images this clear using the other setting. I will experiment with the recommended light and distance; outside during the day, over a much farther distance.

The extremely minimized settings menu was surprising at first, there are literally only 8 things to change:

Time
NTSC/PAL
Brightness
Audio on/off
Microphone volume
EIS on/off
Face-detection on/off
Re-format SD card.

All this makes it as easy to use as a phone camera. When you turn it on, you simply choose video size or still picture and start recording. A little zoom and that's all you get. Perfect if it's all you need!

title: A feel-good 50mm fast shooter... That's sensitive to impact.
text:
OVERVIEW:

You can read any number of reviews about the 50mm 1.8 and how it's the greatest thing for the money, which it is, but this 1.4 isn't a chump either.

As I removed my 50mm 1.8 and put on this one, The first thing I noticed was the build, it doesn't have that cheap look and feel and it's a bit bigger and heavier. The USM and full time manual (in Auto-focus mode you can easily manually override the focus)is a great feature that adds to the value as well. As far as the double brightness in stepping up to the 1.4, well it certainly doesn't hurt, well not usually. You might find times where 1.4 gives you just too shallow of an image on a subject too close, and if you're pointing too close to the bright sun with that extra wide aperture it might play some tricks on you, but these are all things you work out for yourself as you learn.

REPAIR:

I'd really like to comment on the issue that seems to come up frequently with this lens in that some people say that a medium bump to the side of this lens can cause the focus to fail. Well, I got news for you, it happened to me.
But if you're concerned about this or if you have a 50mm 1.4 stuck between 10' and infinity, it's not as bad as you think. The motor didn't fail, the sensor didn't break, but the inside of this lens is the same material as the outside of the 50mm 1.8, cheap shiny plastic. The tolerance is pretty tight in there and a small bump in the right place can easily bend the plastic piece inside and cause it to have too much resistance to let it spin and focus smoothly.

Yes, I did disassemble my 50mm 1.4. I do not recommend anyone try this without the full intention to take it completely apart, sand down the interfering parts, clean it and put it back together. You'll need a clean work place, a small screwdriver set, plenty of patience and I encourage you to video tape the process so you can put it back together correctly. Also this is a prime lens, don't try this with a zoom lens.... WAYYYYY more parts that you'll never get back together properly nor aligned.

I realize that many people are not as mechanically inclined and patient as I, so I will not post how to do this here, I do however encourage you to go to your nearest camera repair shop with the knowledge that your problem is not a catastrophic one. My first time (with nothing but very concise and detailed illustrated instructions) took me 2 hours and I had a perfectly fixed 50mm 1.4 that I had thought was ruined.

title: Neat. Cheap, Can't beleive there isnt anything better at the moment.
text:
Let me first mention that Foscam isn't too pleased with all these critical reviews on here of their best selling product, so on their website they say that their cameras sold on Amazon are fakes which is obviously not the case.

The trouble is the camera software is lousy, the technical aspect to get beyond the functionality of a basic webcam is beyond most people's expertise and often, in certain network conditions, there just isn't going to be a solution to get it to work fully. If you have a dedicated IP address and knowledge of how to port forward your router and both ends have a great network connection, yes, you can actually view your camera from a remote location. My new smartphone was able to connect but even with wifi it was not even close to being able to display the streaming video.

Ok so if you got this far, you now have basically a choppy, discolored streaming webcam from your home without the need for it to be plugged into the computer... Hurray!

Now what?
You want to be able to record right?
You want there to be motion detection so when there is someone moving around in front of your camera you get alerted about it or at the very least have it recorded so you can review it later right?

SORRY, not with this purchase. Oh sure you can go buy some additional software to try and figure out how to integrate the two but show me one person who successfully did that who doesn't have an IT degree.(I got an IT person and the results are BELOW)

Basically I have far better results running Skype with a $20 webcam; better picture, smoother streaming, better sound.... I think it's time these guys or SOMEONE came out with a product that is not outdated by 10 years, my smartphone can record video, with effects, with motion detection and all wirelessly with ZERO effort or technical B.S., so why can't this camera do it better, when that is it's ONE AND ONLY function?

Bottom line, if you're gonna get one call your IT friend to help you and maybe just mount it over your front door so you can check in to see if you have UPS packages at your door... of course that's what tracking is for... it's not like you will be able to record the neighbor stealing it off your porch.

UPDATE:

So a week or so later and after many conversations with the most knowledgeable people I can find, and the result is this:

You CAN record, but only locally (to a computer plugged into the same network that your camera is on) which makes it normally inaccessible to you when you're not home not to mention your evidence videos are on-site waiting for your would-be thief to steal.

You CAN have it upload to a different place, via FTP or even email but only SNAPSHOTS which usually capture the picture way too late (a motion sets an alarm then it takes a moment to record a picture.
You can set the interval which it will continue to snap pictures, which can become overwhelming if you have your camera outdoors, near a breeze, the sun, shadows etc...) I set mine at my front door and it uploaded 8000 photos of nothing except a leaf blowing in the wind.

Then I set the sensitivity lower and it just took that much longer for it to recognize a movement, you won't catch someone walking by or even dropping off something unless the person is milling around in front of the camera for a while. You will have however a 45 minute video of the scene after they left.... and snapshots too... not helpful. The alternative is turning up the sensitivity but this resulted in the 8000 photos I mentioned and of course 17GB of videos 45 minutes long each filling my hard drive.

To those of you who have the skills and software and know-how to fiddle with these things, that's great, you can probably build a cyber network through a proxy and VPN to your home network to make all your dreams come true with this camera.. However as a consumer grade camera which advertises "quick and easy set-up" and all the wireless wonders it is capable of, in this day of apps and iPhones, why would anyone want to use something that is so counter-intuitive and poorly designed with such archaic settings management.

text:
I use an old metal Manfrotto tripod that is a couple inches taller and heavier duty for real estate photos. I needed something that had a shorter collapsed size but still had a stable footing.

The cool places I can get this tripod to go really is great but if I extend it taller using the center column, even a 2-second timer isn't quite long enough to stop if from shaking for a longer exposure shot with a dslr. Probably perfect for small cameras but a 6d and 16-35mm is too much to stop it from shaking in a slight breeze with the neck extended.

I also find the twist leg-locks to be cumbersome, but having the ability to make the tripod "squat" down lower is a great advantage. However, for now I will have to use it as a second tripod for hard to reach places only.

I know I'm focusing on the negative aspects as they impact me specifically, so take all the good reviews into consideration because it is a very cool tripod.

title: Not an adequate update for a Manfrotto 3055

I had high hopes for this, but for professional commercial real estate photos this is not better. The slight improvements to weight and smoothness of controls are outweighed by the slow knobs and slight movement to the levelness of the head when tightening. I wish they used their old 3055 ball head as a prototype for this instead of rebuilding from scratch.

Like my other photography equipment reviews, I have a very specific purpose for my equipment and if yours is not commercial, architectural or real estate photography then IT SHOULD WORK WONDERFULLY FOR YOU.

For me, level accuracy and time-not-spent-fiddling-with-knobs are very important, so this is a step backwards. Don't get me started on the switch to the 200pl quick release...

Sony is new to this Full Fame camera field and I guess they aren't using their heads in their attempt to be a competitor with the big boys. Maybe ask actual photographers which setting to remove, that literally every other camera in production has.

title: It's not the amazing deal it seems. It's exactly what it seems.
text:
I, like many other reviewers, was surprised by the cheap and light duty feel of this tripod. It is LIGHT DUTY (rated for like 3 LB cameras or as they say "entry level dslr"?) and it is CHEAP, we all generally expect to pay $200+ for even a modest tripod from Manfrotto. So don't be too disappointed when you get EXACTLY what you payed for.

What you may come to realize is not that you are disappointed by the tripod but more surprised that Manfrotto is taking on the entry level, throw-away or "i-phoneographer" market that everyone else has been getting rich from.

This is not a smoking hot deal, you haven't stumbled across an undervalued gem. It is what it is, plastic and metal and rivets with what I hope is years of experience in equipment design that won't disappoint for my light duty camera needs. And yes, you can shoot with the head upside down for low to the ground shots.

It deserves 5 stars but I take one away because despite it all, I'm a little disappointed anyway...

UPDATE after a week of use:
I am trying to make this work with 6d+35mm for videos and it is NOT the appropriate tool. Very shaky, impossible to make slight adjustments and overall the WRONG tool. This is the same results as when I tried a $30 tripod from best buy and expecting it to be something it is not. The only difference is when used properly (with a mobile device, not a dslr) it will probably last forever.

title: Decent sound, but not a thoroughly engineered product
text:
First issue: The unit has three different input jacks. Periodically, when I operate my cable remote, another input channel (e.g. 2) is randomly selected - seemingly for no reason. This kills the audio. Then I have to reach for the Polk remote to re-select the correct input channel (e.g. 1) to get the audio back.

Second Issue: Wireless subs are good in theory, but this one periodically stops working and has to be re-synched. They should provide a wire connect option, since those simply work. Also, a cheap plastic "cabinet" has no real place in a sub (that's what MDF Board is for) and the rubber legs on this one aren't tall enough to clear my carpet. I had to purchase and cut a sheet of 1/4" plastic to place under the sub's stubby feet in order to prevent the woofer from contacting the rug. That's just sad.)

Third issue: Turn the unit "off" and the sound-bar indicator lamp goes from green to red (to indicate "off") as it should. But the sub-woofer's indicator lamp keeps flashing green for at least 5 minutes because it's "searching" for the bar - as it would during the initial set-up. That light eventually turns to solid red. In other words, my living room looks like a fun-house after I shut this down, turn out the room lights and go to bed. This is just plain stupid on the part of the engineers who designed this. Now that I think of it, there are way too many lights on this thing...blue, green, red, flashing green, flashing red...My $2,000 SVS home speakers don't have any lights on them at all, yet they sound FANTASTIC.

Fourth issue: I had to call Polk to get my cable provider's remote to work with this, since the provided instructions were woefully lacking. (The good news is that I got a rep quickly and he was knowledgeable, friendly and helpful - a rarity in these times.) Most people will not be able to get their cable remotes working with this unit without experiencing major pain.

Fifth issue: My cat's whiskers are thicker than the skimpy optical cable that's provided with this. Go buy a real optical cable. BUT, if you do be prepared - the unit will tip (from back to front) due to the close proximity of the cable to whatever you set the unit on. I had two 3" tall plastic spool "feet" made up by a machinist friend of mine to get around this problem.

Sixth issue: Be ready to invest 1/2 an hour or so in properly removing (and cursing) the huge product information sticker that Polk sticks on the front grill. They specified a cheap adhesive (to save perhaps 1/2 cent per unit), so be prepared for a mess. I used Goo Gone (citrus based cleaner), a toothbrush and a rag to clean mine.

Summarily, this is basically a decent sounding unit for the money, but it's also a pain in the a** in many respect because Polk didn't bother to fully engineer this product.

UPDATE 2/25/12: The unit stopped working 9 days ago. I'm lucky enough to have a good dealer (privately owned) and they ordered me a new one, which I got today.

title: Dolby Vision is not ready for prime time
text:
I really wanted to like this product. On paper, it hit all the checkmarks. 7.1.4 system for the price of a 5.1.2? Check. Atmos on rear surrounds? Yes please. 4 inputs directly on the soundbar for true TrueHD 7.1 sound? Okay! I was coming from the Vizio 5.1.2 soundbar, and the reason why I was replacing that soundbar was the unstable firmware the company release and forced on all its users, thus rendering the soundbar worthless. I thought this soundbar was going to be the the solution for this. Sadly, it's not. My first experience of it not is that my Nvidia Shield Pro would not register as having Dolby Vision available. No amount of different HDMI cables (including an Ultra Fast 48 Gbps one) resulted in a having that feature available. Nor did the Nakamichi support have an answer to that problem. In fact, they stopped communicating with me completely. That, for me was a show stopper. Putting the Shield Pro on my TV and having sound to the soundbar via earc, did work, but at a sacrifice of TrueHD 7.1. Even that setup had its issues. Earc was not very stable and would cut in and out constantly. The ultra fast hdmi cable seem to relieve that, but not completely. Second, on my Apple TV 4k, I was able to get Dolby Vision passthrough working. There were problems there as well. Everything looked and sounded great on the apple tv until it didn't. After an hour or so of viewing, the tv would lose its picture and all you could hear was sound from the soundbar. Since both of these problems seem to stem from Dolby Vision, I could only conclude that the Dolby Vision implementation on the soundbar is not stable. Other quirks on the soundbar were related to HDMI-CEC. Even after a full HDMI reset, my devices had a hard time harmonizing together over HDMI CEC. Sometimes one device would take over when it wasn't supposed to, or I would be stuck in a loop trying to get my Shield TV Pro to activate. I ended up having to turn off HDMI CEC completely.
As far as the sound goes, I was really expecting Atmos and surround sound in genral to really sound amazing. Unfortunately it did not sound much better than my 5.1.2 Vizio soundbar. I have 9 ft ceilings, so I'm a prime candidate for good Atmos sound (bouncing off my ceilings). I struggled to pick out any height in my surrounds.
All in all, I was disappointed and had to continue my search for a replacement soundbar.

text:
The concept for this keyboard is not bad. The keyboard offers protection for your iPad while also giving you a versatile keyboard that can rotate and fold under itself (in order to allow you to use it like a tablet). Execution wise, there is room for improvement. First off, the weight of the keyboard does not support the iPad. So if you tilt it past 90 degrees, it will tip over. Second, the trackpad can use some major improvement. Scrolling is done with two fingers. However, zooming is done with two fingers pinching or expanding. The trackpad had a hard time distinguishing the two gestures. Webpage would constantly change size as you tried scrolling up and down the page. In addition, the palm check is either very bad or non existent. You choose. Any sort of typing would occasionally result in being sent to different parts of the page or worse.
Typing (when it wasn’t interrupted by palm redirects) feels fine. It’s already hard to type on such a cramped keyboard as it is, so this was helpful.
Quality control is a bit off. The first keyboard had to be replaced, because it never entered pairing mode. Luckily, Amazon’s replacement procedure was effortless, and a second, working keyboard was sent out immediately.
If you are looking for a way to get that laptop experience with your IPad, consider looking elsewhere for a keyboard that has better palm check and scrolling features.

title: Works well for audiobooks but hard to get Bluetooth headphones to connect
text:
I own another CD player of a similar type and got another because they work well for my purposes - I listen to a lot of audiobooks. This player is rechargeable, reads both audio CDs and MP3 CDs, and also has a memory feature that saves your place in the book even if you turn off the player. The sound quality is very good for books but probably only fair for music. There are some limitations to the volume - it is loud enough to hear if you are nearby, but not in the next room.

My only problem has been with getting the CD player to connect to Bluetooth headphones. The Bluetooth receiver feature works fine (I could play sounds from my computer through the CD player's speaker by using the FUN button to connect), but this does not work for the Bluetooth transmitter. I have tried to connect several sets of Bluetooth headphones with no success. The instructions are not detailed enough for me to figure out why; the answer to a posted customer question about it mentions a Mode button but there is no MODE button that I could find. If I understand the directions correctly, to get it to work requires the Bluetooth device be able to select the player – I don’t know of many Bluetooth headphones that have a screen to use to select the CD player device, so this might be my problem. I am hoping that more information is posted in response to the customer questions to clarify if this really will work with most Bluetooth headphones, and if so how.

I have taken one star off the overall rating to reflect the Bluetooth problem. If using Bluetooth headphones is important to you I would recommend looking for a different player. Otherwise, this is a very good CD player for audiobooks.

UPDATE - finally got my bluetooth headphones to work with this CD player. I had to play the CD, then press the FUN button until the tiny bluetooth symbol was blinking in the lower right corner, then turn on my headphones to make them discoverable. It took a while but the audio eventually switched from the CD speakers to the headphones. It doesn't always work, but it is nice to know it will if you don't lose patience.

text:
I got this because I wanted a camera for my backyard that did not require that you pay a monthly subscription fee for cloud storage. The free three-day cloud storage that comes with this is enough for my needs & allows me to view footage without having to access the microSD card. The solar recharging feature is icing on the cake – no need to worry about recharging it either.

Setting the camera up was relatively easy. You use a QR code in the instruction booklet to download their app, register, and then follow the add-a-camera instructions. You need to scan the QR code on the back of the camera to add it. Since this QR code label will be exposed to the weather, I was a bit concerned it might wear off over time. Just in case, I took a photo of it so I have it if I need it again.

There are two buttons at the base of the camera. The instructions call them the “switch” and “reset” buttons. The switch button is used to turn on the camera - it does nothing if you just press it and release, but works fine if you hold it down a few seconds before releasing. Picture and sound quality are very good – at least as good as my old Arlo Pro cameras.

Mounting the camera and solar panel took more time but is also pretty straightforward. Finding the best location for the panel, out of the shade, is hard to do in the winter with all the leaves gone, so I am hoping it works this well when spring arrives. I was able to mount it in the middle of my yard, well over 100 feet away from my house, and have had no problems with losing the WiFi connection. The instructions say it has a maximum range of 150 meters (490 ft!!!), but it could be much less as it depends on your local wifi setup and any obstructions. The app also works well but takes a little getting used to. Overall, I am very pleased with this camera.
item_title: BEENOCAM 3MP 2K Solar Security Camera Wireless Outdoor Rechargeable Battery Powered WiFi Surveillance Camera for Outside/Indoor with Spotlight Siren, Motion Detection, Color Night Vision

title: This seemed better than the mouse that came with my PC
text:

I find this to be very useful when using Excel, but there are also other features of this mouse I really like. It has a groove for your thumb, so I feel like I have a better grip on it than what I have on a generic mouse. It also has a small button that allows you to set the sensitivity of the mouse. The cursor initially moved too slowly, so I just hit the button and it moved faster/farther with the same amount of hand motion. This mouse requires no special setup – I plugged in the transmitter and it was recognized immediately on my Windows 10 PC.

With the extra features, this mouse seemed an improvement over my old one. However, upon continued use I find that it intermittently stops tracking well and I sometimes have to shake it to get it to work well again. I am not sure if this is due to the placement of the transmitter but it has led me to switch back to my old mouse except when using Excel. I deducted one star for this problem.

title: Some features don't work well (Eufy app / 2nd user)
text:
I have several Apple AirTags which work quite well but have the disadvantage that they can only be tracked by one user. I wanted a tracker that allows 2 people to track it and the product description for the Eufy SmartTrack Card states it has this feature. This is nice looking, very thin and it easily fits in a wallet. It is usable with the Eufy app and with Apple’s Find Me app. Unfortunately, it is does not work as well as I hoped.

The main problem I had was that the Eufy Security app does not work well for tracking the card. It is usually “out of range” or it spins while "connecting". It seems to only work well when it is in close vicinity. The Find My app works very well for tracking it on my iPhone. Unfortunately, the second user can not use the Find My app to track the card – they can only use the Eufy Security app (and they must use your Eufy account signin). Since the Eufy app has connection/out of range issues, it makes this feature pretty useless for me. The find my phone feature works, but it plays a loud tune for too long a time - I was unable to turn it off but it eventually stopped. I would not want that to happen around others as it was very annoying.

Unfortunately I can’t recommend this due to the problems with the Eufy app and the 2nd user feature. The card does work with the Find My App for a single user, just like Apple's AirTags do, so I am giving it 3 stars. It just doesn’t really offer any advantages over the AirTag other than the card shape, and it does not have a replaceable battery, which limits its lifespan.

title: Works well with lots of types of CDs, easy to connect to bluetooth
text:
Although I have several CD players, I wanted to get another one to place permanently in my work room to listen to audiobooks. This one looks nice, only takes up a small area on a shelf, and can be controlled using the remote control. Since it will mainly be used in one room, I was glad to see that I don’t have to run it off the battery - it can be powered directly using the power cord that is included for recharging it. I was disappointed that the battery is inaccessible as the picture of the battery made me think you could replace it, but it is good to know the CD player will still function using the power cord even if in the future the battery no longer takes a charge.

This CD player comes with pretty good instructions – 6 pages in English. It has a paragraph on how to connect your Bluetooth headphones that is very helpful and made the process go smoothly, unlike other CD players I own. This plays both audio CD and MP3 CD formats, making it perfect for audiobooks. I haven’t had trouble with any of the types of CDs I have played in it. Speakers are very good for audiobooks – clear and a nice range of volumes. On the negative side, it is one feature that audiobook lovers like to have. You cannot control the speed of the playback to make the narrator talk faster, which is nice to have if you hit a dull or gory part of a book. Also the memory feature, which makes the player start back up where you left off, doesn't always work. This may be more a function of the audiobook than of the player. I found it to work with my MP3 discs but on one of my audio CD books it kept returning to the beginning. Other than that, I am pleased with this CD player.

title: Excellent picture quality, and comes with 3-day free cloud storage
text:
I have several cameras that I use as outdoor security cameras. I always make sure that the camera is wirefree and that it comes with some amount of free cloud storage, as I do not want to have to pay a monthly subscription fee. This camera has both and so was perfect for my needs. It has a rechargeable battery and it has two video storage options: you can either save to a microSD card (not included) or use their free 3-day cloud storage.

Setting the camera up was very easy. The instructions are brief and surprisingly well written and well-illustrated compared to other camera instructions I have had to follow. You use a QR code in the instruction booklet to download their app – it is the O-KAM app, which I already had registered for with another camera - and then you follow the add-a-camera instructions. You need to first scan the QR code on the side of the camera to add it. Since this QR code label will be exposed to the weather, I covered it with clear tape to protect it, just in case I ever need to add the camera again. I also took a picture of it to be extra safe.

The picture quality is very good, even at night, and it picks up the WIFI connection at relatively far distances from my house. I was able to mount it at least 100 feet away from my house, and so far have had no problems with it dropping the WIFI connection. Results will vary depending on the quality of the WIFI & router, and if there are any obstructions. I also like the O-KAM app – it is very easy to use to view live or view the saved-to-cloud videos. The free three-day cloud storage that comes with this is enough for my needs - I doubt I will ever use the microSD card option. I am very happy with this camera.

title: Disaster.... again
text: PowerShot 480. Once again a new Canon camera has failed within weeks. This one, which will be added to the plastic box of 7 other new Canons, has a problem with the deployment of the lens. It creeks and stumbles coming out and creeks and barely makes it back inside the camera when turned off. Battery strength doesn't matter. If the lens doesn't extend properly the pictures are of course out of focus. If the lens won't retract when turned off, well.... what the heck do you do now. I have spent nearly $10,000 on Canon video and still cameras over the years and have relied heavily on Elf products for photo shoots. But even those have expired eventually. The  Canon video cameras have been excellent. I had to sell my Rebel within weeks of paying $1,200 for it because the auto focus and depth of field could never get together sufficiently for me to shoot in focus models from 8 to 12 feet from the camera. If I took 1,000 shots, most would be out of focus. Sooo.... I had to go back to the point and shoots which have great depth of field and sharpness.... WHEN THEY WORK.... I have probably lost at least $3,000 on Canon stuff that broke within weeks of coming out of the box. Next time it's small claims court. I've had enough !!![[ASIN:B001SER4CE Canon PowerShot A480 10 MP Digital Camera with 3.3x Optical Zoom and 2.5-inch LCD (Blue)]]

title: NO LOCAL DIMMING!
text:
samsung is trying to scam us. this tv only has "micro dimming" which is a software that adjust the image for better blacks. by definition, a local dimming tv must physically turn off the LED. samsung is calling this "micro dimming" to make it appear better. only the d8000 has true local dimming, a.k.a. "micro dimming PLUS".

you can tell the tv adjust the brightness level of the WHOLE screen to achieve better blacks. i know this because the menu screen dims when the movie scenes are dark and when there's a credit roll, you can see the credit's font color not being consistently bright. also, you can faintly see that the LED are lit on the black bars on super wide screen movies. samsung only makes edge lit to maintain its ultra thin profile but caused a huge sacrifice in image quality.

the overall picture of this tv is over sharpen, over saturation, over enhanced. the image doesn't appear natural. i know some novice tv buyer would be impress by the vividness of this tv, but this isn't a good tv if you want to reach as close to reference image as possible. i tried calibrating with the built-in expert patterns and the spears & munsil bluray. the result was not too pleasing. you can dial down the color accuracy but you can't overcome it's physical limitation such as bad black levels and poor viewing angles.

they also crippled the analog audio out. if you use external speakers, you can't adjust the volume with the tv remote and all the nice sound adjustment are disabled. samsung is doing this intentionally to "encourage" us to buy their overpriced, under performing audio systems. makes wonder why they even bother adding an analog audio jack.

it also doesn't have "just scan" for image scaling; that's just stupid. the viewing angles are also quite terrible. i can see the backlight bleeding when i sit a couple of seats from the center. the only positive thing i can say about this tv is how aesthetically pleasing it appears and it's able to play many files off of the usb. the internet apps, widgets, and web browser are terrible. not even worth using. get an ipad if you want to web surf on the couch. i am definitely returning this tv.
