title: You need to format the new hard drive first! If you don't it won't be recognized!
text:
I put in a new SSD into this enclosure and connected it to my laptop's USB. At first, my laptop only saw the Sabrent enclosure but not the hard drive. I changed USB ports, even tried it on another computer. Same result, can't recognize hard drive! I was about to return this because I thought it was broke and saw other reviewers having the same problem.

I googled my problem and it was suggested that if this is a new hard drive, which it was, I need to first format it before windows could see it. So I reconnected the enclosure and went to disk management. For windows 10, just type disk management. Google this if you have anything other than Windows 10. I found a youtube video on how to do it. The new hard drive will show up in there! From there,I did a quick format which only took 2 minutes. After that, my new hard drive showed up!

Then I used the free Macrium cloning software to clone my old HDD to the new SSD, swapped them out, and boom! All good. It did take about 3 hours to clone a 256 HDD to SSD tho.

So remember, if you have a new hard drive, please format it first.

title: A good upgrade from the Echo Dot, but not perfect. Sound and Voice recognition review
text:
There's other more in depth reviews on what it can do, but I'm be reviewing the sound, voice recognition and screen. Of course having a screen is a big plus, but I find it small at times being only 5 inches. That's what she said!

Sound:

A step up above the Eco Dot 2nd generation I replaced. But it still only has 1 speaker so sound is in mono, not stereo. However, the one speaker is louder and has more bass. Since this is in my kitchen, I often listen to music while I cook or wash dishes. Music in Mono sounds like crap. So I've plugged a stereo Bluetooth speaker via the aux outlet .

Why did I plug it instead of connecting to Bluetooth? Because Alexa can't go into "follow up" mode if it's Bluetooth connected to a speaker. BUT it can if you use the aux cord. Follow up mode is when you ask Alexa a question and it listens to hear a follow up question. This is very helpful at times. For example; "where's the nearest Pizza Hut?" then follow up and say "Call them" instead of saying "Alexa" twice. Even though the one speaker sounds better, what use is it if it's plugged into a better sounding dual speaker stereo?

Voice Recognition:

It picks up my voice good, but I found that the Echo Dot was better. It could pick up my voice from across the room but the Echo Show 5 missed my voice about 30% of the time. I can live with it because now I just walk closer to it.

Screen:

When playing music, it displays the lyrics. When listening to the news, it displays video. When asking for weather, it also shows it on the screen. This is very helpful. BUT since it's in my kitchen and I move around a lot, cooking or cleaning, I'm often too far away to see what's on the screen. How can it be useful if it can't be seen? Being that it's a touch screen is nice though. At 5 inches, its too small. I mean even my phone has a 6 inch screen.

Final thoughts:

I would've never bought this at $90 but on Prime day, I got it for $25 after trading in my Echo Dot 2nd generation. The screen is helpful but unless you're using it as a night stand clock, it's almost useless as it's too small. I could have used my 8 inch Fire tablet as an Alexa device instead. It can act like an Echo Show in "Show mode."

Overall, 4 stars. Slightly better speaker, but slightly worse voice recognition, has a screen.

title: Great 4K GPS dual dash cam for the price. But no app unfortunately.
text:
[[VIDEOID:268b84471ac8f1244db61e1c45df6086]] I wanted a daul dash cam that records front and rear. But I didn't want to run wires to a separate external rear camera. This fit the bill as both cameras are in one unit.

It comes in a plain white box with only the words "4K UKTRA HD" on it 😆. The build quality is decent. It has 4 control buttons on the bottom and a power button on the side. It has a separate GPS unit attached to the power cord. I like that the car adapter has a built-in USB port, so you can still utilize your car adapter even with this plugged in. It can hold up to a 256GB memory card but I used a 128GB card. The instructions mentioned that you could email them for a free 64GB memory card.

Installation was pretty easy. It doesn't mount with a suction cup but rather, an attached double sided tape. I was hesitant fir a permanent installation. But they include 2 clear stickers that you're supposed to stick between the glass and the dash cam. So you could remove the dash cam easily by peeling off the sticker first, if needed. I noticed that the right angled usb cable to the dash cam is right sided, which made Installation slightly more difficult. See my video for a more detailed explanation.

You can manually pause recording and mute the mic which is nice and missing on cheaper dash cams. You also choose to record, front only, rear only, or both. What i didn't like is that you can only view the videos via the dash cam which isn't ideal because if the small screen. I knew this going in so its fine. Or, you have to download a program onto your computer, then place the micro SD card into your computer to view them. This is also the only way to see the speed and GPS coordinates. Picture quality for the front camera is good enough to read license plates, which is good enough for me. Another reviewer mentioned no night vision for the rear interior camera which is false. I've tested it at night and it automatically switched to night vision.

Overall this is a great 4K dual dash cam with GPS for the price. Even though there's no app for your phone to view recordings, you can still see them on the dash cam in a pinch, so it's only a minor nuisance. Recommended. 5 🌟s.

title: Exactly what I needed. Works Perfectly !
text:
Just got mine today, a day early.

I work from home and spend hours on my computer everyday. I was looking for something simple that I could sit on my desk so that I could keep caught up on news and sports, or don't have to stop working to catch a favorite program.

I looked into DTV adapters or TV cards for my computer...that would have entailed either using one of my monitors for TV, or buying a new monitor to use as a TV...I wasn't too thrilled with either of those options, especially since the reviews on the adapters weren't that great and the good ones all seemed to take up a lot of processor. Besides, I wasn't really sure if I wanted my computer to function as a TV...I have enough stuff going on as it is.

I thought of just buying an HDTV that was the same size as my monitors and mount them all...but still I was looking at at least $250 (on the low end) and a 3 monitor mount...just to watch TV ?

When I started looking at portables, I was looking specifically for one that had decent reviews and had an input for CATV. I never intended to use it as something I would take out of the office, or for emergencies since I don't live in an area that has bad storms or power outages.

The reviews on this unit looked good, most of the complaints seemed to be reception issues based on location..not about the unit itself, and a few days ago the price dropped to $64.99 right in front of my eyes, so I took a chance.

Right out of the box I plugged it in, screwed in the antennae (I live in Las Vegas) and saw that I could get about 13 stations with the included antennae. It took a little adjusting to get them all without any time outs or broken signals, but it picked them up fine.

Note: Mind you, Vegas is a valley surrounded by mountains... the broadcast towers are up high..surrounding the city and there are not too many tall buildings (outside of the strip) and absolutely no hills throughout the city to block the signals. It's pretty flat. I live dead center of the city, so it's a good ways from the towers on Black Mt....probably 12-15 miles, but there are no obstructions. I can see how if you live in an area with a lot of tall buildings in between you and the signal, big trees everywhere, or a lot of hills..over the air digital reception will probably be a pain without an aftermarket antennae. That's not the units fault.

Digital signals are better quality picture and sound..but receiving them over the air is not like it was with the old school signals..you either get a strong signal or nothing..but of course I wanted it to watch cable, so I screwed in my CATV cord (straight from the wall) and hit scan and programmed 70+ stations (it actually said 130). Great ! ESPN, MSNBC, CNN, and all my local stations in HD, and everything else that I normally channel surf.

Picture is very nice, crisp even...and the sound from the speakers isn't really bad at all. I mean it's a small unit..how good can it be? It's definitely loud and clear enough, no distortion..better than my netbook, but of course it's inside on my desk.

title: Don't let the price fool you. This is a quality set and great viewing experience.
text:

Needless to say, I am no longer envious of other people's TV's. I feel like I hit the jackpot my first time out and now it's their TV's that don't look as good as mine.

First of all it was delivered ( on time) by a specialty carrier who not only brought the TV inside, they unpacked it, let me inspect it for damage, put the bottom on, placed it on a [[ASIN:B005HY6R7E Sonax FB-2600 Fiji 60-Inch TV Component Bench, Ravenwood Black]] that I purchased for it, and we turned it on to insure that it was working correctly. When they left, the took the packaging and trash with them. The entire delivery experience was an unexpected bonus!

Once the cable company brought my digital box, set up was pretty easy. For a few minutes I thought something was wrong with it because the picture wasn't what I expected...but then I figured out that I wasn't on HD stations. Once I put it on HD stations (and hooked up the box via HDMI instead of the coaxial cable), it was glorious! The picture crystal clear, sharp, and after a few adjustments it was just how I wanted it. The picture was so nice that I even watched 30 minutes of soccer just because the colors were so vivid.

The sound isn't bad. Better than most newer TVs. But I hooked it up to a Vizio sound bar that I already had and that made it even better.

Setting up my Netflix, and M-Go accounts was painless, although the Amazon App isn't working at the moment...which kind of sucks.

There are a lot more Vizio Apps available than they advertise and I find them all easy to use and even enjoyed some new programming that I didn't even knew existed. It's true that many of the apps are Yahoo apps, but one of them is Yahoo Fantasy Football, so another bonus for this upcoming Football season since I play in that league.
There are a lot of Fox Local News affiliate apps...which is kind of strange.

I did under estimate how big 55" was. I probably would have been fine with 42"-48", but it's not overwhelming. I'm actually glad I went bigger.

It's a real movie experience which I expect to get even better once my new Roku Streaming Stick arrives.

Another unexpected usage was hooking up my laptop via HDMI port. I'd been taking some online classes with a ton of video lectures, and quizzes. It was awesome to be able to do my classes on the big screen from the couch instead of sitting at my desk or holding a laptop.

The user interface is very easy to understand, settings are a breeze, and you don't have to do a whole lot of fiddling and adjusting to get a great picture right out of the box.

I do wish that it came with the QWERTY keyboard remote, but for $12 it wasn't a big deal to just order one.

I don't have any major complaints about this TV. If you are a first time HD Flat Screen buyer like I was, this is the perfect set for you. Especially for the price.

If you are an Audio/Video snob and think that you are going to spend $700 and get a $2500 TV, then don't buy this TV. Go buy a $2500 TV. For my money and needs, this TV is very nice.

UPDATE: Roku streaming stick arrived and it's awesome! The included smart apps on the TV are fine, but adding a Roku to this TV adds so much more entertainment value to it. The user interface is much smoother, and the channel offering is second to none.

I also added a Logitech Harmony Smart Keyboard (Amazon doesn't sell. Got it from Logitech website), which controls the TV, Roku, the laptop I have hooked up to it, my Blueray player, Cable, and the Harmony app lets me use my phone or tablet as a remote. I also added [[ASIN:B0078GCM50 Panasonic SC-HTB20 Energy Star 2.1-Channel 240-Watt Multi-Positional Full HD 3D Audio System (2012 Model)]] for better sound.

I highly recommend the additional accessories. It really improves on the entire experience.

title: Awesome office computer ever.  Some tips for new owners + 6 months later
text:
Came a day early, and I was so excited. Have been wanting to get it for a while now to use as a work computer after reading all of the reviews.
Sadly right out of the box,I thought it doesn't work. First of all it shuts off about a minute after you turn it on for no reason. The second time it stays on, but there's no video signal. Tried every port, suggested troubleshooting. Nothing.

Turns out I'm the idiot, so here's a few tips I wish someone had written down for me before I purchased>

1. [NO SIGNAL] It's a new computer and new install of Windows. All of the ports won't work until you put in the license key and finish the installation. Too see what you're doing, use the HDMI port out of the video card, midway down the back. (see attached image).

2. [Windows Key] DON'T Use metal to scrap the paper sticker. You will tear off the code. I was able to just use my thumbnail to remove the coating and it came off pretty easily to reveal the code underneath. Make sure you run the Windows updater to insure it and Windows Defender are up to date.

3. [No VGA Ports] No, it doesn't have one. It uses Display Ports, HDMI, and DIVI. If you have VGA monitor(s) you can get a VGA to Display Port adapter pretty cheaply. I got these and they work just fine. https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B017Q8OCSY/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

If you were using USB adapters to run multiple monitors, get the display port adapters and use the Display ports.

5. [Disks and Drivers] This machine comes with disks with tools and drivers for your motherboard and graphics card. Update your drivers. Be aware of what you are installing,. If you're a gamer there are lots of tools and addons for gamers. If you're like me and are not necessarily a PC gamer but got this as a work computer you may not want all of those things...but you still need to make sure your drivers are updated.

One of the disks installs Nortons. If you hate Nortons as much as I do, make sure you don't install it with the other stuff.

6. [ Update Windows Again] After you install and update your drivers, run the Windows updater again just to make sure you're all set.

Upgraded to 16G RAM right away. This 2x4GB 2400MHz kit fit the bill nicely. https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00MSOKFJW/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o02_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1

As I mentioned I'm not much of a PC gamer. I'm a work from home web designer and marketer and purchased this as a work computer. Got tired of over the counter "Office" computers that claim to be powerful, but strain to run multiple monitors, and can only handle a minimal RAM upgrade, but still charge top dollar.

This computer fit the bill perfectly. It's quick, responsive, plenty of power to multitask while watching videos, listening to music and so on.

If you're like me and want an office computer with some balls, I highly recommend it. . Can't beat the specs, design, and build for the price and it will handle whatever work can throw at it

After years of purchasing HP's, I was leery buying from a new company, but it was well worth it. I love this machine, and it looks good too.

UPDATE: 6 MONTHS LATER

6 months later and I'm still happy has hell with this computer. One add on I made was a 256GB SSD to boot Windows from, and then installed Linux on the included hard drive so now it can dual boot. Everything still works flawlessly, absolutely no complaints.

One of the best purchases I've made in years.

title: Registering the product to access the software is a nightmare
text:
It took me 5 minutes to install the drive. It took me hours to gain access to the cloning software.

The print on the package is small. The print in the directions is even smaller. You are prompted to register the product by scanning a QR code, which means doing it on your phone. Of course the registration doesn't take your product code. Without registering the product code you can't get the cloning software. This is especially frustrating on a phone.

Checking support to find a solution pretty much amounts to "make sure you're entering the product code correctly".
Go back to the putting in the 13 digit code. The problem is that the code you have is only 10 digits. There are no other codes that it could possibly be, and there are no numbers missing or scratched off. It's only 10 digits;

After about an hour of going in circles with this, I got the idea of looking up the drive in the device manager, and looking at properties. Whataya know, there's another number ( which is not on the box as they said it was) which ended up being what the registration form was looking for. Cool, now I can get access to the software, right? Wrong.

The next email has a link the says that I now need to enter the warranty code to get the software key. Where is the warranty code? On the back of the drive that I already installed.

This is a text book example of how what may be a great product is ruined by horrible, confusing UI, over complicated product registration process that prevents you from actually using the product.

Never been more frustrated on my life. I literally went from excited to hating this company and vowing to never spend another dime on anything they make ever again.

Take my advice. Don't do it. I can guarantee there are easier ways to buy and use an SSD.

title: Worked great for a year. Then it stopped. Fixed it. Finally died after almost 3 years.
text:
When I first got this TV I left glowing reviews. I really loved it. I left it unedited so that you can see how happy I was, and then how quicly disappointed I become. Update below.

UPDATE:
13 months later, it stopped working. First I started noticing little glitches. It would hang and never recover. I'd have to restart it to get it going again. Then one day it didn't recover and system restore was the suggested option. I did that. Worked fine for 2 days, then it said it had an update. Did the update and it never turned on again. The LED is lit, but it will not turn on. TONS of articles and videos about this issue with this TV, I did all the suggestions. Still won't turn on.

Contacted Hisense support. 13 months, so "sorry you're past the 12 months hardware warranty.".
However, the support agent said they could "request" a manual update. Meaning they'd send me a link to download an executable file that's supposed to fix the issue.

Of course, the download for this fix to a KNOW ISSUE isn't posted on their website, so customers can access it easily. After giving them a copy of my purchase receipt, and the TV's serial number, now they want my home address. For a software download. I ask why they need my address for a download link, double-talk ensues. I give it to them. Now I have to wait 24-48 hours for the link. What? I just jumped through every hoop, and you can't just give it to me?
Worst costumer care ever. If this is a KNOWN ISSUE, why do you have to jump through so many hoops for the software fix? Why isn't this a download on the support page of your website like EVERY OTHER electronics manufacturer does?

Suffice it to say I'm not as happy as I was when I purchased it, and now Hisense's handling of this issue and overcomplicated hoop jumping just to get a possible fix adds a level of frustration and ridiculousness that makes me never want to trust this company again. If a year is all you expect out of a TV, then get this model.

UPDATE #2
Finally, 5 days and 3 phone calls later....I got the email with the firmware. It didn't work. Contacted support again and supposedly someone is going to contact me to schedule a service call. TV has been out for a week now.

Update #3
It's about 3 weeks later. Hisense did finally schedule a service tech to come out. He replaced the board, and the TV started up and worked again. It's been about 7 days, and it's still working. Still not sure if it was the update or the board just went out on its own. Tech says it could be either.

Bottom line Hisense did fix it. It wasn't easy, or timely, and the customer support wasn't good..too much run around..but at least I have a TV again. Not sure if I'll trust another update. May just stick a streaming stick in it and stop using its smart features and disconnect it from the internet altogether.

Considering all that has happened, I raised it to 2 stars. Quality control and customer support needs to be better.

Final update- It finally died today. Just kept turning itself off, then will just go black 3 seconds after restart. 6 months ago a huge area of the screen turned brown. It won't factory reset, it won't recognize it won't uninstall any apps, remove my profile...it won't do anything except go in circles claiming a storage issue, but it won't let me uninstall anything.

Hisense support said they'd send me the firmware, but as I mentioned above it's not on their website, they have to send you a link..and lucky me, apparently their systems have been down more than 10 days now.

It's going out with the trash tomorrow. I gave it a shot. Never again.

Watching/Streaming movies/music, playing XBOX...whatever the source it sounds pretty darn great.

I'm no audiophile who nit picks every technical detail, but I know when something sounds cheap and when it sounds good. This sounds awesome! Perfect for how I'm using it, but am pretty sure that it will rock a much larger room with the same clarity.

Very solid sub and it looks great too! Very happy with it.

FYI: Make sure you also order the right cord since none comes with. The back of the sub requires a double male RCA connection ( Left and Right).

title: Works great to provide reliable connection to home office
text:
Like many homes the cable/internet access is in one room...generally the common room ( living room or den) which means if you want signal elsewhere you either need to pay for a second modem connection in a different room, or run Ethernet through the walls to where you need it.

For reference, my main connection is in the family room..open concept with the kitchen, and my office is on the other side of the kitchen wall (same floor). WiFi wasn't cutting it especially considering the amount of devices that I like to run on my own network.

Never tried the power-line thing before.

Set it up as instructed..one end connected via Ethernet to the main modem/router, and plugged into a wall outlet. The other end plugged into a wall outlet in my new office. Although it kicks out it's own WiFi signal and has an Ethernet port, I like to use my own router to create my own network and that's exactly what I did.

I gotta say, it works like a charm!

In my office I run my desktop, console game, smart TV, NAS, and it's the WiFi that connects all my mobile devices. No issues.

Did a speed test just before writing this. I think our plan is 100mbps.
Speed tested:

Ping: 10ms
Download: 75mbps
Upload: 132 mbps

Obviously results will vary. Just wanted to show that I'm not losing much speed over the connection.

I think this works very well. Very happy I tried it.

title: Very nice. LG knocked it out of the park on these.
text:
I've been running multiple monitors for years and thought that was the ultimate in productivity, until I got these. I got two, so when putting windows side by side it's like having 4 monitors, but looks much better and fewer cords.

I like to run different operating systems, sometimes on different machines, and I've always thought input switching on monitors should be easier. A lot of monitors accept multiple inputs, but it's not easy to use them with multiple things because you have to fumble around with too many, unmarked buttons, usually on the bottom or front of the monitors, and do a lot of trial and error to remember which combination of buttons will get you to inputs, which is up/down, which is select....and you have to do it quickly or the settings screen will time out if you take too long to think...then you have to start over.

It's been a crap design /UX flaw of monitors for YEARS.

On these LG's switching inputs is painless. One, centered, joystick control for settings is the way it should be done. I switch between display and HDMI ports easily so that I can have whatever OS I want up and running front and center. Or if running audio through them, the joystick is volume control. This design/feature alone makes these monitors worth trying.
Everyone should adopt how LG does it.

All in all I'm very happy with them, and for this price you can't beat it. Highly recommend.

title: Using it as a webcam mic, plugged into XLR on a Rodecaster
text:
I'd originally purchased a Rode VideoMicro Mic. Wasn't happy with the sound. Lot of white noise and interference. Purchased a shielded cable and that helped some, but not much. Then I saw that you needed a transforming adapter (Rode VXLR Plus XLR to 3.5mm Female TRS Transforming Adapter) to make it work with phantom power from a mixing board. Got that. Still not great. Had to do too much processing and overdo the noise gate setting to get a good sound. I didn't like that.

I gave up and got the Deity. Plugged it into the adapter using the shielded cable, and it sounds great. No white noise, hums, just the normal pickup you'd get from an open mic in an open, untreated room. But most importantly it works great as a boom mic for video conference calls.

Couldn't be happier with it.

title: Exactly what I wanted. I made the installation more difficult than it had to be. A few tips.
text:
First, this is a great product. It's well made, sturdy, and perfect for my needs. Exactly what I wanted.

As mention in other posts, the installation wasn't as easy as I would have hoped, but now that I've done it I understand why, and most of that was me not understanding how it needed to work. It also comes with no instructions, and I couldn't find one YouTube installation video. You are on your own.

As you can see, there are front and back mounting supports. For it to be sturdy and work well, they both have to be attached.

A few tips:
1. If your rack has side panels, you're going to want to remove them. There's no way to make the adjustment needed to mount the back supports from the inside alone. You need access to both sides of the rails.

2. I didn't need to remove both the front AND back mounts to install it. I could have just removed the back
mounts, adjusted the rails, and finished the installation. The front mounts stay where they are regardless of how deep your rack is.

I'm very happy with this product, and will probably buy another.
Hope this helps.

title: Great lighting for WFH video meetings .
text:
My desk faces a wall, with a huge window behind me. When I'm on camera, I need lighting.
I've gone through many iterations of larger lights that I never really liked. They were too large and made my set-up look cluttered and cumbersome, so I've been on the hunt for something small, but powerful. Not a fan of ring lights.

These small rig lights fit the bill. With the included diffuser, it creates decent soft light if directed towards you. I'm using them to bounce light off of white sound panels that are behind the desk. Also using an adjustable aperture camera, so the combination makes the perfect solution for my use case. And when I don't need them, I don't have these large lights mounted on, and looming over my desk.

The app works well enough, but I do have to re-pair the lights if I turn them off by the switch. They don't connect to Bluetooth automatically when I turn them on. Not a dealbreaker, and definitely a better solution than most lighting apps that require you to sign in to the light's Wi-Fi signal in order to control them.

Battery life has been fine. My meetings don't last hours at a time. I've had them a week and have had maybe 5 or so meetings that are 30 mins or less and I haven't needed to charge them yet. So looks like charging them over the weekend will be good enough.

Can't say enough about them. Only wished I'd found them before purchasing larger GVM and Neewer lights.
Thinking about getting 2 more for background lighting.

title: Pretty decent!
text:
I really like these speakers, but feel I need to set realistic expectations.

I already have a decent sound system set up in my office that includes a room shaking sub, and that's what I listen to music, watch movies, and game on. However, for my desk I was using speakers that were quite frankly too large for no reason since I don't use them to do any major audio editing or for entertainment. I just needed something with decent sound for when I needed to hear what was happening on my computer.

These fit the bill perfectly and look very nice doing it.

The sound is clear, and audio quality overall is pretty darn good. I'll never need to turn them up to 100%, so I didn't do any unrealistic testing. They also have some heft to them and overall seem pretty well-made. Have definitely had worse. These deliver, and I can justify the price tag. No issues at all there.

However, some of the reviews talking about how great the bass is, "audiophiles" praising these as miracles in a small package, I don't know where these people are getting that from. Don't get me wrong, these are solid. But if you're like me and like a full sound and that subtle room vibrating bass when you listen to music, these speakers are not all you'll ever need.

If you just need to hear the sound from your computer clearly, maybe light music listening, these are awesome. But they're not going to shake the room and rock your party all night long, and they don't claim to be that.

These are great desktop computer speakers, that are well-made, sound good, look good, and don't take up much room on your desk. If that's what you need, I definitely recommend them.

title: I didn't want to like it, but I LOVE IT! Best tech I've purchased in years.
text:
I'm an Android person, always have been. I was pretty sure Apple made good things, with some exceptions, but always felt they were overpriced for the lack of control, customization, and repairability they offered.

However. I've also been pretty disappointed in 7"-8" tablets since the Nexus 7. Tired of the performance issues, how updates were non-existent...you were pretty much stuck with the version you purchased it with, how quickly Android tablet makers completely abandon them...I could go on.

So, I watched some reviews, saw that it was $100 cheaper, that it was now USB-C...so I decided to give it a try.

The difference is night a day, and I was immediately angry.

Angry at how beautiful apps look and work on the iPad, yet those same exact apps look and behave like crap on Android tablets. How everything is fluid and just works without lag or stuttering. How it doesn't freeze up on certain apps. How responsive it is. How I got an update to iOS 16.1 right away, and it worked.

It's been a week, and here's how I'm using it.

*As a control center for my office automation (Home Assistant)
*As a music center (Tunein radio, YouTube Music, & Jellyfin), Bluetooth connected to my Denon Receiver and speakers.
*As an eReader.
*As a podcast player.
*As a webcam (I also have an M1 Mac Mini)
* Apps I've always wanted to use on a tablet and have them work well like One Note. Google Earth, any Email app, and I've recently started using Milinote for project management, and it works flawlessly. Now I see what's so great about Notion...it actually looks and works nice on the iPad.
* I got an adapter so I could access files from USB and SD cards and I can do light sound and photo editing. no issues. It works.

I can actually search the web on it and don't have to wait for pages to load. I can email on it, and it doesn't freeze up. Things work. Everything looks great!

And I can do many of these things AT THE SAME TIME! This thing is a beast!

I could never do any of these things on my Android tablet. It would be a struggle, or I'd have to constantly restart it, or the app looks terrible, or the battery life is crap, or the version of Android I have....which I just purchased last year and is already outdated and not compatible with certain apps. It's a crap experience.

This iPad is already my favorite tech product, and I use it pretty much all day long.

Yeah, $399 would be a lot for a tablet that barely works, but now that I've used this, it's not too much for a tablet that is reliable and works GREAT!.

Careful not to go down the rabbit hole. Even though the tablet is $399, I've already spent $300 on accessories but, since this is USB C, you now aren't locked into ONLY buying things that work with or convert the lightening port...which opens up A LOT of possibilities and price points for accessories...another reason I decided to give it a shot. If it was still lightening, I wouldn't have.

I was between this and the $299 iPad 10, and I am so glad I got this. More portable size, all the features work, faster more powerful chip, and it uses the new Pencil..which I haven't done a lot with, but from what I've seen does offer some great functions.

I can't be an Android fan boy grinch about it....this is a great tablet. No way around it. I highly recommend it.

title: Sorry. Cannot recommend.
text:
If you're on AMD, Windows 11 (not sure if it worked on Windows 10) and are hoping to use the software, don't bother. Its own software doesn't even see the enclosure or the drives. The user manual is in mostly English, but the really important parts are in what I assume is Japanese.

Can still be used as basically a drive bay. Windows does read the drives, but won't perform any RAID functions....says the device won't allow it.
And since the Yottamaster Raid Manager software doesn't work, you can set the switches in the back all day long and never see that any RAID has been set.

So this is basically a glorified external drive caddy with no other functionality.
I'm pretty disappointed.

Update: I've now started to experience the infamous turning off that others have complained about.
I've since switched to using my M1 Mac Mini as my daily driver, and there isn't even software for an updated Mac. Says right on the website, NOT for Mac OS 11 or higher. At the time of this update, we're on macOS 13.2.1. That's a long time not to update software. Clearly not a priority.

So at this point it's not even a glorified drive caddy. Even if there's some complicated fix, it's not worth it. It had basically one job...read the drives, and it can't even do that.

Sad because I really wanted this to work.

Edit 2: Felt it only fair to update. I did finally get it to work in JBOD mode, and it does not turn off in this mode (so far). Connected to TrueNAS Scale, and running disk management through that. So it's not a total loss and if this holds then it's a nice looking drive caddy, which basically does the same thing as my $49 2 drive Sabrent.

I would not recommend this as a RAID solution and the driver situation, especially for Macs is BS, but as a drive caddy in JBOD mode....probably OK.

I never had these types of reflections. another problem is that the plastic itself is pretty soft and scratches very easily -- meaning more trips to editing to remove them. I'm pretty sure I won't be buying any more of this stuff, at least in black.  White is OK since you expect it to reflect everything.  Not "matte" black. title: Low-res video, terrible audio. Hate it.
text:
While it's advertised as 2k (1920x1080) and the image is that size I think the sensor is MAY be 640x480 -- based on the total lack of detail when O look at a still, the jagged and blurry edges and horrid color accuracy. Typical cheap cameras had firmware that multiplied the actual number of bits to fool you into thinking it’s actually higher. This is worse than the actual 640x480 camera I had before. Second half of a video camera is the audio. That also fails miserably. With a good microphone I see background noise levels of around -60dB. This sucker “sizzles” along at -35dB! Lots of noise, and a sound that makes you like you’re in a barrel. I might tolerate the video because nobody really cares that much, but the audio is terrible. Given the low cost of electret microphones (and generally good quality) I wonder how they could process it to make it sound so bad. How they can advertise "dual noise cancelling microphone" with so much self-noise is beyond me. Also, not stereo. Yes, audio on both channels, but covering either mic grill doesn't change the sound from one ear to the other -- it's bad.
I didn't want to spend much on a camera (hard to find many at this price point) but I have missed my window of opportunity for a return and it’s only now I really looked at the quality in detail.

After that is done, it just takes a minute or two for the units to talk to each other; then both lights will be green- and you have a connection. This line passes everything I have hooked it up to for testing, laptops, media devices like apple TV and rokus. It even passes the DLNA and it works great! The time saved is life saving when it comes to 3 small children, they have no patience anymore. title: Good Sub for Filling In the Low End, Not Shaking the House
text:
Very good fill sub, I bought this to go with the Kanto YU2, after I was let down by the Edifier Luna Eclipse. The Luna's don't have as much bass as everyone says they do, they are missing a LOT of bottom end. The YU2's still needed better low end, but at the size of them you can tell why! The highs on the Luna's are also too sharp, and the bluetooth connection, while it works gets kind of annoying, your device BT has to be off or it will connect automatically.

That said this sub does a great job of filling in bass, it will disappear into the sound and keep up with the small speakers without being too boomy. It is a very small good looking sub, most other subs with sound louder, but this thing has a very small footprint so remember what you are buying. When you crank it with the crossover set to higher frequencies you will hear the enclosure rattle a little and the cone start to slap, but again it is meant to fill in the bass not shake the house.

I am using this for a makeshift studio setup as I had to get rid of my KRK Rokit's to make room for the 27 inch monitor on the iMac. I loved the even sound the KRK's made but they were simply too big, this sub and the YU2's allow you to have almost no footprint while getting a similar sound.

Soundwise, like I stated before it is fairly even and blends well with other speakers, it basically disappears into the sound. Not being able to tell where the sub is through hearing will let you know how good it is at basically doing it's job. I can basically set it and forget it, it is so even throughout it's range. The automatic turn on actually works well, and I haven't had to crank the sound for a bit to get it to turn on. There is a very small almost inaudible click when it turns on and off, but less than other subs. The sub itself runs fairly cool, so you know it's not wasting power.

BTW this is a very good looking sub, something that would look great on a desk or in the corner, they come in a few colors as well.

Bottom line is that if you are looking for a flat, even sounding sub that takes as little room as possible, get this. It would be the perfect sub for an apartment or closed quarters where you don't want to rattle the house. This is the most clean bass you will get out of a sub this size.

title: The Best You Can Get for The Size
text:
These sound great, and look great. For the size they are the best you can get. Really for the size they do not have much bass, but there is a subwoofer out to them, which I use. They are fairly simple and work with PC or Mac. The switching is flawless between the 3.5 jack and the USB connection. They are not as loud as some other speakers I have tested but they are clean and honestly the volume would be too loud otherwise. In a nutshell you will notice yourself near the max of the volume knob, but it is still loud enough for just about anything you need. Sound wise they are very accurate, and basically are a cheaper/more feature packed version of the AudioEngine A2, sound wise they keep up with the AE A2's. There is no noise or hiss when on and not playing either!

The only negative that I can think of is that the volume control is on the back, but that is so minor compared to the accurate sound you can get out of such a small package! I would buy again, but if I had more space I would go for the bigger sizes Kanto offers like the YU3, YU5, or the YUMI; while you would lose the USB DAC, you would gain bluetooth and bigger, fuller sound.

I have to say that this has fully surpassed my expectations. This excels in low light and medium light, very bright and vivid image. When I use my iPhone X, there is shading and shadows in low to medium light, the same as my eyes see it; BUT when filmed with this there are NO SHADOWS/SHADING.

Now with this my daughter has two cameras, one she can take around anywhere and this one where she can use it with me, it's great to share a hobby with her! I help her make instructional videos, we haven't published any just yet, but the editing is fun and she is really coming out of her shell and becoming more social since she is "hosting a DIY crafts channel". She loves that it looks like a mini TV camera, she calls it her professional camera.

This is capable of zoom, digitally, which I prefer as I can't hear a zoom motor like most cameras, and the image is clean enough to start with. This starts up very quickly, which reduces the chance of missing a moment too. Only thing to push it over the edge would be to make a nice case to house everything, I would totally purchase that separately! Overall very impressed with this package and I can't think of anything nicer for even close to the money that would be a better value.

title: This is really an Onkyo product.
text:
Part 1

I previously had an Onkyo receiver that cost much more than this one. It was amazing... for about 2 years. Then for no explanation, it stopped playing anything. I read online that the DSP chips in the Onkyo receivers were habitually crapping out. Well, I went back to my receiver and changed the DSP settings a bit and got it to come back, but only part way. The digital DSP (Dolby Digital) no longer worked, but the Dolby Pro Logic still did. I was frustrated but I put up with it until last week the DSP crapped out again. No sound. I played with it again and got it back, part way again. This time digital services didn't work. No Spotify. No Pandora. Not even USB. So, I got on Amazon to purchase a replacement receiver. I didn't know what I wanted, I just did NOT want another Onkyo product. I looked at this Pioneer, as I had a Pioneer back in the 90's that lasted 20 years without a hitch. I only replaced it because the DSP was woefully outdated. So I excitedly opened the box to my new Pioneer receiver and my heart sank. One of the first pieces of paper I pick up talks about your new Onkyo equipment. @#$%!!! But, I hooked up the receiver anyhow, as per the instructions. I hooked up the microphone and let it make adjustments. Then I go to my DirecTV and for the first time in years, it is reading it as Dolby Digital. Great! I go to my Fire Stick and it is reading as Dolby Digital Plus! Wonderful! and it sounds pretty impressive as well. So, then I want to listen to some music. I always listen to my music in Stereo. I don't like what the DSP does to music. So I go to streaming services, and choose Spotify. Blank Screen! I go to Pandora. Blank screen! I go to Google Chromecast. Blank screen! I read online that the DSP is badly in need of an update. One reviewer even went so far as to test before and after the update and gave it a great review after the update, but he warned the network update isn't working so he had to do it by USB. So I will update the system and see how it goes. I will be honest. I'm not hopeful. I will worry about the DSP chip crapping out the whole time I own this. To me this receiver is deceptive marketing on part of Onkyo.

Part 2

I updated the receiver by USB per the instructions. It was a very simple process only requiring maybe 10 minutes. I then hooked up the microphone and let the receiver run through setup again. I do admit, it does sound better now, although my old Onkyo had a warmer sound that I really enjoyed. However, I am still tweaking the sound of this Pioneer, and I am confident in time I will manage to adjust it more to my liking. As to the 'streaming' services, I was mistaken. I expected the streaming services to work more like on my old Onkyo receiver. I could actually select the service, enter my login information, and the receiver would play the service directly. This 'streaming' on the Pioneer is more akin to a glorified 'bluetooth' connection to your smartphone. You must load a Pioneer app to your phone, and then the app for the streaming service you want to use. Then, you start your stream on your phone and send it to the receiver. And even after that, you must control it through the phone. So basically, your phone is tied up anytime you care to listen to your music service. I may as well just 'bluetooth' my phone to the receiver. An incredibly weak compromise. I am very disappointed with this feature.

Pros: Simple remote easy to use. Wife friendly since not so many buttons.
ATMOS with virtual rear speakers. (Only a pro if you cannot have rear speakers like I can't.)
Auto surround automatically chooses the best form of surround based on the input works well.
Automatic setup works well. I still have to make adjustments although minor.

Cons: Pioneer is now Onkyo...seems deceptive to me
Requires update right out of box
Music steaming services clumsy at best and require smartphone
Remote is not a combo remote. It only controls the receiver.
Detailed manual must be found online, not in box.
I would prefer a bit more power to the speakers.

Last Word: If I had known then what I know now, I would have purchased a different receiver.

My Alexa experience is no better now than it was with the free Alexa App on my phone. I am incredibly disappointed.

Edited a week later.
I'm not sure if it was an update to the app or a firmware update, but now when I get in my car, Alexa pairs with my phone and I can operate without touching the phone. The Echo Auto app does open on my phone automatically, but to see it, I have to unlock the phone, which is not necessary unless I need the navigation function. Is the Alexa Auto perfect? No, I would rather have Apple Car, but as my car is an older car that I plan to keep, it works quite well. Compare the price of the Echo Auto with a whole new entertainment system with Apple Car built in and it is a no brainer to me.

title: Love these Ear Buds!
text:
I just got them today but they're amazing. I charged them up but I really don't think I had to based on the indicator on the case. Yeah, I didn't bother with the instructions. The case has a series of white lights on that I later learned indicted that the box had a full charge which meant the ear buds wee also charged.

I finally put them in and did have an issue with the pairing since I wasn't pairing to the right device. That's when I had to look at the instructions to find the device name. Now I was off and running.

One of the nicest things is that they pair to each other right out of the box, no fiddling with anything. I then just needed to pair to my phone and I was up and running. I loaded up my music app and I was off and running. Now I've been using wired buds for ages and these are easily as good as what I was using, probably better. There was certainly enough bass for my liking and they sounded great.

I did have an issue with the size of the rubber ear inserts but they supplied two other sizes, one larger and one smaller so you have options. I switched to ones that felt best and I was go to go.

The box that holds them is supposed to be able to recharge them a number of times which is nice. Can't say how long the battery will last. I was using them for four or five hours and they were still going strong. The one thing nice about the box is that the buds are held in with magnets so they just click into place.

The only problem I experienced was when I pulled them out to test a phone call. Somehow a turned them off when putting them in my ears. I turned them back on but lost the pairing with my left ear. There's probably something in the instruction on how I could have fixed that but, not being in the mood to read instructions, I just put them back in the box, took them out again and they were paired. When you close the box they automatically turn off and on again and pair, when you take them out. All in all very sweet.

Almost forgot, my test phone call went well. I could ear and I could be heard on the other end. I doubt that I'll use that function much but it's there if you need it. These are going to get a lot of use.

title: Almost perfect!
text:
I live in an area that loses electricity way too often and it's happening more and more lately. It drops often enough that I'm seriously considering buying a Generac to replace my generator. That being said, many of the outages last 5 to 30 minutes. However, when it's night, it is very dark.

I bought a similar unit a couple years ago so that I'd have a readily available light, that I keep handy, so finding other light sources around the house would be easier. I have small, pop up lanterns that I'll place in various rooms until juice if finally returned. My only objection, so far, to this emergency unit is nearly perfect. My only complaint is that it's totally black. My other unit has color and, even in the dark, stands out a lot better than this unit. That's the one of the only complaints so far. In all other ways, this unit is better than my other one which I'm giving to my gf.

The other is that the flashlight on the original is definitely brighter in it's highest setting. If I were using the unit for camping, I'd probably look for a unit that provides higher light output. For my purposes, it's satisfactory.

I read some of the previous reviews to see if there was anything I could add to whatever was written. The biggest complaint was the muli-use of the limited buttons on the unit and the need to "read the manual". To some extent, I agree for those that need to understand every function, one of the reasons I'm keeping this unit and giving the older one to my gf. She's get lost trying to operate this unit. I'm different.

I'll scan the documentation before I lose it, but I haven't even looked at it except to locate the charging port. Seventy five year old eyes don't do well in the little pamphlets they send with this technology. I spent about 15 minutes playing with the thing until I figured out how to use everything I need to be able to access and control. If you're at all tech savvy in this brace new word of electronics, you can probably figure out what you need.

The thing I like best on this type unit is the charging function. Of course you have the solar charging ability that might be nice if you're out camping, letting it self charge during the day so you'll have some level of charge at night. However the hand crank charging I find perfect. You can get the flashlight function on these type units working fairly quickly. I tested that out on my old unit and a handful of revolutions gave me light. It's much better than a flashlight that always seems to need batteries, that you don't have on hand, at the wrong time.

Some have posted that there are better units available, but this more than satisfies my needs and I'm not going to spend hours researching, looking for the best. If the flashlight function is biggest need, look elsewhere but brightness has a energy cost so make sure the battery is large enough to support your needs.

The battery life is about 25% better and the sound of the radio is better if that is something

I'm far from an expert at this point and I'm still missing a few things I need to figure out but it's starting to get dark so I'll work on those tomorrow. I almost wish I had used my phone to get it up and running so I'd have everything working the right way and the car and my phone would be set up. However, my tech challenged gf drives that car more than the other so I used hers and she never set up google assistant, so here we are.

Anyway, after getting it running, the first thing that hit me was we're probably paying more than a thousand dollars for them to be mounted in our dashes. If something goes wrong, you'll pay a fortune to have it fixed. For $300, if it breaks, you buy another one. If you sell your car, you can take it with you. It's a deal!

The screen itself is as nice, if not nicer than the one that I have in my escape. If you have an AUX jack on your car radio, you can plug into it and play through your auto's sound system. If not, you apparently can link by setting up with FM but I didn't try that because there's a jack in the radio and they provide the cable.

Android Auto was a piece of cake if you're familiar with it and I'm sure the Apple App is just as easy, if not easier, for Appleheads.

Probably the best piece of technology of an older car I've seen since they made those early GPS's before they were available on your phone and now here n the Waze app.

If you need it, buy it, you'll love it, my 2012 Versa is upgraded.

title: Not Right for Me But I think it Would Work in the Right Situation
text:
If you look at Youtube videos of the Weenect product it gets pretty good reviews. All were with a different variety tracker and from European reviews. I've had nothing but issues with this one. When I went to register it, they asked for a credit card number which was strange as there was supposed to be a free subscription. After setting up my plan, I went back and found out there was a code I was supposed to provide from one of the boxes it cam in. I immediately sent them an email. A couple days later, I got an email that said they needed the credit card for after the year was over and I wouldn't be charged. I was. I'm waiting for word back on that.

I also live in the woods which I felt would be an issue one the leaves returned so I figured I'd try the premium version which would provide better coverage. However, their site failed on updating that. They said they're working on fixing that.

Then today I got an email saying they were having trouble with the AT&T network and that I should turn the unit off and on again and it should be okay. It wasn't. This afternoon, I got it took hook up and put the unit on my dog and took him for a walk. It was set up for every five minutes so we walked for about 20 minutes and when we returned, there was no sign on the map that we ever left. It was set up for every 5 minutes tracking.

To test out my geofence, I set it at 30 seconds and walked out my 100 yard drive, 50 yards past where I set the fence. Then I returned and walked around my property. Looking at the history, I couldn't even see my movement.

I'll give them a chance to straighten this out, if it's even possible. However, I'm not expecting a positive result here. I hate to be too negative since I don't live in the best of locations for satellite coverage. However, the device does go green so I'm assuming it's making contact. If you live in an open area with good sat. coverage it might be great but it doesn't appear to be working for me.

I shall definitely update if something changes.

UPDATE!!-

I thought I had posted this update earlier today but must not have, so here goes. First, I'd like to the praise support I've received. It's been a rough start but the help I received was excellent.

I ordered this tracker because I have a rescued labradoodle that was two years old when I got him and three months in the process of making him a house pet. He's come a long way but I can't trust him not to run and we've had a couple of scares already. Living in the woods, it wouldn't take much for him to disappear in a matter of seconds. I liked that the ad states various satellite networks but, apparently, the primary network used is AT&T and they are the least powerful in this area. Verizon is slightly better with TMobile the strongest. They do mention TMobile in the Ad but apparently there is just not enough coverage here.

If you would be using this tracker in a strong AT&T area, I think you'd be very happy with this device. I'm not sure if a heavily wooded area would work, particularly once the leaves returned in the Spring. I was just hoping to get good use thru the rest of the winter, just until I had a good grasp on where I was with my boy. Unfortunately, this won't work out for me.

title: It's called Desperation but I finally got to see it!!
text:
Okay, I'm sure this is going to bring a few laughs, but I bordered this projector to have movie nights on my back deck. Of course it's February so it will be a bit before that happens. However, I was excited to take it for a spin. I ordered the screen to use with the projector but it is just too large for placing it anywhere in my house. The weather warmed and I thought maybe it wouldn't be too much longer when snow was forecast and the nights get pretty darn cold. I broke down and bought white sheets that I figured I'd just get a feel for what the projector would do. I finally got to see the projector in action and it's petter than I imagined plus good sound besides. When the weather warms up a bit more and the basement gets into the 60s, I might even set up down there where I can set up everything to get a real appreciation for this thing.

Anyway, I read some of the reviews others wrote and there's still more for me to learn, but my initial adventure into this device was via a 4k Fire TV Stick from Amazon. I plugged it into the hdmi slot and off I went after it did an ungodly amount of updating. Everything was fine until I got to identifying the TV I was running it on. No TV, just a projector. I found a Youtube on how to on a different machine and followed the directions, Just say a TV not on the list. Then it went to sound testing and no sound. It then asked if you were using a receiver or soundbar, nope, not one of them. Tried to use Netflix and got a picture but no sound.

I finally found that the unit doesn't do Dolby and had to find where you shut that off and I had big screen Netflix and followed that up with Disney +.

There's more to learn for sure but, at least I know it works, has a great picture and will be fun once Spring gets here. Now off to find if there's a way to get the Fire TV remote to control the sound on the Fangor!

title: Replaced a Samsung with this
text:
The old Samsung wasn't enough to fill a lager room with sound and the dialog would be horrific at higher volume. Began searching for a quality sound bar at the entry level price. Several reviews pointed to the YAS 207. Now this isn't a low profile sound bar, it's wide, perfect for a larger screen and a little tall, shorter than Sonos. The subwoofer and soundbar pair easily and the bass has plenty of kick. The dialog is where this bar shines, no matter the scene or volume, the dialog is crisp, clean and solid. The DTS 3-D sound is gimmicky, not sure if I can hear a difference. If you want 3-D sound, I don't believe you'll ever achieve that from a bar alone. For the below $300 price this bar is well worth it, I wouldn't use it for a TV below 60" given it's size. I've not had any issues with the bluetooth connection on the sub, the bar and sub are about 20 feet apart, completely to the side of the bar.

Pros:
Price, construction, clarity, decent bass, mobile app, has super thin fiber cable included.

Cons:
Large, 3-D sound is a gimmick, for medium sized rooms.

title: Great device, but not for the non-technical user
text:
This NAS arrives without disks - order them with the drive. Installing the disks in the unit is simple, and a handy diagram helps you with the 'quick start' of getting the drives in, the wires connected and the device powered up. I'd like a tool-less disk and case assembly - though you only need insert a few screws (included with the unit) to secure the drives, and seal the case.

The software installation isn't so obvious. You need to insert a CD and install the DSM operating system over the network. While this was fairly straight-forward, the questions are not going to make sense to a non-technical user. While the installation process gives you a number of useful options, the most obvious (which type of disk configuration do you want?) is not in the setup process. I didn't realize until later that the default setup uses Synology's Hyrbrid Raid configuration for two disks. Nothing wrong with that as a choice, but I would have liked to see other RAID configurations offered during setup.

The web-based configuration screens are very nice - it's an AJAX 'application' type feel to the web site. I'm using 2 2TB Western Digital drives (make sure you order from the Synology compatibility list on their website). The unit spent about a day doing a complete volume analysis and check, but it didn't impact the performance of the unit very much.

I transferred everything from my old Buffalo Linkstation (1TB RAID drive) over my home network (all gigabit) in about a day or so of transfer time. Setting up shared folders with permissions for different two users using Windows sharing was simple.

To use any extra features, you first have to install the application on the device. The NAS is really just a small Linux box, and doesn't have anything other than file and folder sharing installed natively. I installed the Media app without problems, and transferred photos, video, and music to their respective folders. I was disappointed not to have control over the structure of the DLNA accessible folders, but it's not a big deal. (These folders are pre-configured as photo, video, music).

This unit is incredibly quiet. It currently sits next to my Buffalo Linkstation, which huffs and puffs quite a bit as the disks are accessed. The Linkstation is supplied with the disks installed, while the Synology is provided diskless; so I guess the noise level may change based on the disks you install.

Overall speed seems fast, but I haven't done any comparison measurements yet. I can tell empirically that this device is serving files faster than the old Linkstation did.

Definitely a nice unit, but don't expect to use it to the full extent without a good understanding of networking, DNS, firewalls and other technologies.

title: Great device for the money
text:
Great product. The drive included a CD that has drive cloning software on it. However, you do need to buy a disk enclosure to mount the drive in temporarily if you plan to clone your existing system. I bought the Sabrent USB 3.0 to 2.5 inch SATA aluminum hard drive enclosure for this purpose.

Once you've cloned the drive, swap it, and reboot. Done. Now the drive also comes with 'Magician' software that will not work until you've installed the drive and rebooted your machine. In Windows 7, you'll also have to wait while the drivers for the SSD are installed after the reboot. The Magician software (which nags you constantly about an 'update' that in my case just will not install...) allows you to configure the SSD drive for performance or reliability, and configure Windows to work more effectively with the drive.

Remember the downside to SSD drives is that they have a short life span compared to a regular hard drive. There are various tweaks you can do to extend the life - for example, disabling hibernation mode. The Magician software guides you through those tweaks. An SSD drive should be good for several years of normal life, but it is limited on the number of times you can erase and re-write sectors. Eventually, the memory will stop working; so consider that when enabling things like hibernation mode.

Before I installed the SSD, Windows gave my hard drive transfer rate a performance score of 5.9 (using the old 5400 rpm drive). After the upgrade, this went up to 7.6. Other scores didn't change, obviously, so this will not fix problems caused by a slow processor or lack of memory. Don't expect miracles!

Machine now boots a little faster - not by much; and I'm hoping that the battery life will be longer.

title: Great little box if you are looking for a budget home theater system
text:
This is a great purchase if you are looking for a simple streaming solution. Previously I used an old laptop for this purpose. Now I have a full Windows 8.1 machine that is permanently hooked up to my HDTV. The machine works well, but I think a 4GB upgrade (less than $30 from crucial) is a real necessity to make this solution work. Before I upgraded the memory, streaming would work, but I couldn't control the mouse while streaming video - the 2GB memory was completely tapped out. Now, with 6GB of memory on board, this thing works beautifully. I have a VPN service installed as well, and that works smoothly on the upgraded system.

There are a few minor issues. One is that since this box has only flash memory, you have to use SHUTDOWN instead of HIBERNATE to turn it off. This means startup is slower than it otherwise would be. You can use SLEEP of course, but then there's an annoying blinking light on the front reminding you the box is asleep! This box jumps back to life from sleep mode very quickly, but that bright blue light flashing away just bugs me. I'm going to see if I can disable that. The light is built into the ON/OFF switch, so you can't really put a piece of tape over it (which I've done with other boxes).

Another is that it is generally fairly slow to start things like Chrome; but once the window opens, it's certainly fast enough to stream Hulu, Netflix, HBO Go and other content without hiccups or problems.

Overall, this is a MUCH better solution than any of the sticks that you can buy. Having a complete PC hooked up to the TV means I can also do email, browse sites, shop at Amazon :-) - very easily.

The 'support' page directs you to a customer forum, where the same complaints have been made by many people, and there are NO responses from the company. When I tried their 'live chat' it turned out to just be a bot, which is not even remotely smart. And when I tried to email, their online form refused to recognize the model number AC4000, so I couldn't even send an email.

The problem is that randomly, on apps like WhatsApp, SMS and Facebook Messenger, the router stops responding, the connection is dropped, and the phone says it's going back to cellphone data. In four years previously, using a Linksys device, I NEVER had that problem anywhere in the house. The worst issue is that frequently a web page on my PC will fail to load, and I have to refresh it. That's on a wired connection directly into the router. That just shouldn't happen - and again, never was a problem with the old router. So despite the better signal strength in some rooms, the connection is far less stable. Very disappointing.

title: Ubuntu 22 - An OK device
text:
As with a number of similar devices, no thought was given to installing this in a regular USB slot. In my case, they are next to the power cord, and the device is wide enough to partly block the power supply connector. It would be helpful to have a small USB extension cord with this device.

Unlike other reviews, this didn't install automatically. I had to use the included CD disk to display the instructions - the printed instructions are TINY. Having read the included document, I discovered the actual install has to run off Ethernet - or at least, it needs Internet to download the required files. Now in my case, I was trying to install this on a machine where the internal ethernet card isn't working, so it was a catch 22. Buried in a draw I found an old 100Mbps USB ethernet adapter. My system recognized that, so I was then able make a wired connection and then run the command line that was included in the instructions. Using the ethernet connection on the old USB ethernet device, I was able to download the files, then the install started automatically. After that, this BrosTrend device was recognized by Ubuntu immediately.

Once it was up and running, I ran a few speed tests in Firefox. The best I could get was 70.6 download, 10.3 upload. My Internet service provides 300 download.

This device is good enough for what I need, but the install could certainly have been easier, and if your USB sockets are close together, expect the body of the device to cover more than one slot.

title: Great protection with a slight catch..
text:
This is the first screen protector I've put on which used moisture, so I was kind of intrigued. I watched the instructional video on YouTube just to get an idea of how to do it 'properly'. It's actually very easy and I'm now a big fan and would love if all protectors used moisture for application. You do have to have a bit of faith when they say to give it a day or two before any of the 'imperfections' disappear from the moisture under the protector. They also say to give it 24 hrs to settle, but I just let mine sit overnight and all was fine.

In regards to the actual protection this protector provides, I'm absolutely confident my screen is completely protected from scratches and minor dings. It's about the easiest protector I've ever applied to a device and it measures up to my device perfectly.

Now on to the unfortunate downsides..

The material is more rubbery than any other screen protector I've used (and I've used many). This makes it grip your finger just a bit more than a piece of smooth plastic like most people are used to. It's not anything drastic but it's enough that if you're playing games which require you to quickly move/drag your fingers across the screen (Subway Surfer, Dropchord, etc) you'll notice it and it's very likely to affect your game play. Perhaps it's the humidity in my area that makes it so noticeable but it definitely causes problems for these types of games/apps. For normal use you likely won't notice it. It seems to be most noticeable in gaming; especially if your device starts heating up and/or your fingers start heating up and getting sticky.

Another con to the rubbery type material is for anyone with fingernails. While the screen is certainly protected, this is flexible protection not a hard shield. If you run your fingernail across it and make a groove, that groove is there to stay. Over time I imagine those grooves will add up but I can only predict at this point. I suspect as long as you're somewhat careful not to drag your nails across the screen to use your device you'll be fine. This material on a phone however, in your pocket with keys or coins rubbing against it could be an issue. I bought this for a tablet and I don't have long nails so it should be mostly OK in this regard.

Overall I would break down my ratings for this product into several different categories:

5 - Made in USA
5 - Protection
4 - Durability
5 - Ease of Install
3 - Sun glare
3 - Fingerprints
4 - Daily normal use
2 - Gaming use

While my average rating is closer to 4 stars, I'm dropping down to three because I don't think I would buy this again.

The rubbery nature of the shield makes for great protection since it won't tear, peel, flake or scratch but it does grip just enough to be noticeable and it does hold slightly noticeable grooves in the material. If you don't game and/or you use a cover for your device, the protection offered is definitely enough reason to buy this. If you want to play games, live in an area with high humidity, or use your device in direct sunlight then I cannot recommend this protector.

The ability to unplug this from your desktop PC and use it on your laptop or take it with you to a friends house or something makes it wonderful.

This is not a fault of the device but rather a limitation with any and every USB sound device. It's annoying but you learn to live with it.
- My only annoyance with the device is when switching modes. To do so you press down on the circular volume dial however when you do, it's a very noticable 'donk donk' sound (not through speakers/headphones). I'd much rather it be a silent switch, or for that matter, I'd very much rather it just be a simple slider switch or toggle. It takes a bit of care to press it down to make the switch without accidentally moving the dial and accidentally raising/lowering the volume - sometimes by a large amount. A slider switch/toggle would be much easier and quieter. Just personal preference..

You eventually memorize what the buttons are so it doesn't matter, but when you first get the device it's really, really hard to read them. title: Works great on GoPro 9
text:
First the negative.. if you've never installed a screen protector on a phone or other device before, you might be confused as there's absolutely no instructions included with this kit.

Now the positive..

The kit comes with 2 sets of screen protectors, wet wipes, dry wipes and dust removal stickers. Everything is packaged very nicely, each screen protector lens individually wrapped, etc. and in a plastic container.

I applied these on a new GoPro 9 immediately after removing the protective film that shipped with the camera, so I didn't bother with any of the wipes before applying the protective lenses. What worked for me was to put one edge down on the camera screen where you want it to be, and then gently lower the protective lens while keeping it straight. Definitely don't try this after a strong cup of coffee. After you place the protective lens down, you'll see it start to adhere to the camera lens. Take the soft cloth wipe that comes in the box and rub it down to make sure it adheres all over. I can't speak to how easy it would be to remove and reapply if you ended up with air bubbles because it didn't happen to me. I didn't get one tiny little dust particle or something that made its way in, but I can live with it, so again I don't know if you can remove and reapply or if you'd have to go to the extras which were included.

After applying all three protective lenses, there was no visible change in the image quality or responsiveness to the touch screen; everything works great. It also does not impact the ability to place the GoPro 9 in the GoPro underwater protective housing.

I saw a review mention that one of the protective lenses was a tiny bit too big so they were getting air bubbles and ended up just removing that protective lens. It's possible there was a bad size cut at the factory but I'm more inclined to guess that they simply didn't apply it as close to the edge as they needed to. All three lenses I applied fit just fine and not a single air bubble.

Overall the only ding I can give these so far is that there were no instructions included. I didn't need them, but some people might. Just remember to peel the temporary cover of the protective lens off from the bottom (to help avoid dust falling down onto the newly uncovered side that goes onto the camera) and then apply to the camera screen as soon after as you can. I suggest doing the smaller lenses first so you can practice before doing the big one on the back.

Would definitely buy these again, assuming I ever need to since I already have an extra set that came with it..

title: Wanted To Like This
text:
I've had a 4 slot Panasonic charger and needed a charger with more slots due to how many rechargeable batteries I use. I ordered this one and tried using it with a variety of about 20 different nearly new rechargeable AA and AAA batteries by Eneloop (both the white and black ones) and Panasonic. I inserted batteries into all of the slots and after a couple of seconds, almost all of the slots started blinking red (bad battery indicator). I took the batteries out, tried putting them back into different slots, and some would stay red (charging) and most would start blinking again. Again, move the batteries around different slots and same thing. Some would start charging, others would blink. I could take the same battery and put it into each of the 8 slots and get different results every time (even in the same slot).

I reached out to customer service, who was helpful, responded in a timely manner, and sent me a replacement. So the star is for them, not the product.

The replacement I received did the same thing, though not quite as badly. So now I have two chargers and the only way I can charge my batteries is by putting them in, seeing which ones randomly start blinking (supposedly indicating the battery is bad), take those out and start swapping random slots until it decides it wants to charge. I've had situations where I needed to charge 1 battery, had to try all 8 slots then start back at the first slot again, until one of the slots decides to work. So it's not that the slots are bad, because sometimes they work and sometimes they don't. And yes, I'm making sure the batteries are inserted fully and securely into the slots.

I wanted to like these chargers and would have been happy to recommend them if they actually worked properly. But now having experienced two in a row that simply don't work right, I cannot. Look elsewhere, it's not worth the hassle to deal with these.

text: This backup camera is a great device and a super buy. It's easy to install, presents a superb picture, is strong and well made, and works for me almost perfectly. Its night vision is good enough and what it lacks in night sensitivity is made up by its connectivity. The only problem I have with this camera system is its limited use as a rear camera when mounted on a vertical surface. That limitation is the result of the short camera bracket included with the basic kit. The short bracket mounted on the back of our motorhome only supports use as a backup camera. We wanted a rear camera that would function like a rear-view mirror, but the short standard issue bracket limits swiveling to a higher view. Sure, it would work if we mounted it on the roof, but who wants to drill holes in their RV roof? Haloview's answer is an optional long-armed bracket that permits use of the camera in any mode. The only reason I gave this camera kit  4 stars instead of the 5 that it really deserves is that the long bracket should be part of the basic kit, which would provide customers with a full range of mounting options. At the very least, Haloview should clearly advertise the short bracket's limitations and market the product with a choice of brackets.
