text:
The iPad fits snugly and is protected against scratching by a felt-y insert. A cool magnetic strip holds ipad at different angles, wakes the unit upon opening, and holds the case shut. It feels sturdy and protected without feeling too bulky. You get the audible “click” when the iPad hibernates upon closing.

The backlighting is especially sharp against black and all seven colors show nicely. It’s easy to control or adjust brightness and colors with the top-row Fn keys and the directional keys. The backlight hibernates after several seconds of non-use and reactivates at the tap of any key.

My wife has been typing for 35 years and has very very small woman hands. She had this to say:
The caps lock and Shift keys are ‘right where they’re supposed to be.” The delete key (backspace for “old people”) is a bit small, but it’s an easy adjustment to just lift my right hand a bit. title: Great for small ears. Noise cancelling is excellent. Probably the best set I've ever tried.
text:
These came beautifully packaged and are the most attractive and cleanly designed wireless earbuds I’ve tried yet. I’m not an audiophile, I mostly listen to audiobooks and podcasts, and am rather new to wireless, so I’ll stick to what I know!

First and foremost: They are comfortable. I have very-very small ears and have always had to settle in the past for substandard gear just so I could wear them for more than 15-20 minutes. These, I definitely can. I especially like the additional stretch gel, which in addition to comfort, could well-be making them stay put. Because, really, how good can any set be if it doesn’t? And in my ears, most just don’t “stick” unless I jam them in; with these I don’t have to. Also, maybe I have more “oval-shaped” ear canal openings for which these appear to be designed. Who knew?

The neck strap is very comfortable, almost silky against the skin and the weight of the batteries is satisfying.

I’d put good noise canceling next: It does exactly what it’s supposed to. And in that way that you don’t even realize it’s happening until you take them out. “Oh, there’s the birds, and the fridge, and the dog’s toenails.” I’m just sitting with them in my ears right now with no music or podcast playing and it’s kinda nice.

The range is great and I can “wander” a lot more than I used to do “Wired-up,” because the cord isn’t getting caught on everything.

The next items are really just petty, so please take them for what they’re worth.

First, I’d have to second the reviewer on the earring issue. While I like the stem design, I am a daily wearer of earrings and the bud’s oval shape doesn’t allow for twisting to get them out of the way. Most of my earrings are wired (danglies), so I mostly just experience some small ticking sounds. Very minor.

Second, (and here I show my age?): Please give a raise to the employee who decided to put a lovely and easy to read R & L on this set. They do not detract from the appearance at all. It’s the little things.

title: This is the 24" you've been waiting for..
text:
This is the first high quality 24" I have seen for under $500. Yes, this is one of the new 24" TN (twisted neumatic) panels, but don't let that dissuade you. The 22" TN panels have gotten a bad rap due to their poor performance, most of them have issues with bad color banding and lots of light bleeding at the edges. I should know as I have owned several 22" TN panels (mostly Viewsonic VX2235WM).

This 24" TN panel is far and away superior to any previous TN panels I have seen, it is almost laughable how bad my old 22" TN panel looks up next to this one. I would challenge you to put this 24" TN up against any of the more expensive 24" IPS or S-PVA panels and see the difference for yourself, I doubt you will be able to tell which is which unless you are using a specialized image for gamut testing or you are a graphic designer with an extremely keen eye.

The only downsides that some people may find with this monitor compared to other (usually more expensive) 24" panels are: less inputs, no portrait mode. This monitor only has VGA and DVI(+hdcp) inputs, no component or hdmi, this is not really an issue if you are using it as a computer monitor but may turn off some people who wish to hook up other media devices. Also there is no portrait mode like the other 24" samsung 244T series; however, the stand on this monitor is still extremely high quality and height adjustable.

I would very highly recommend this LCD, better yet, I'd recommend 2 or 3. Why buy a 30" when you could have 3 of these for the same price?!

title: Airy, open sound in a sealed design, very nice..
text:
I bought these primarily to use as studio monitors. I have or have had a number of high end cans over the years, Grado, Beyerdynamic, Sennheiser, Etymotic Research, etc.. however for recording purposes I have always preferred my AudioTechnica ATH-M40 due to their sealed design and extremely neutral response compared to most of the aforementioned cans which 'color' the sound in one way or another.

I've had the M40 monitors since they first came out in the early 90's and they were really starting to fall apart so I decided to look for a replacement. I was somewhat surprised by all of the praise for these Denon cans considering that last time I paid attention to the headphone scene Denon wasn't even making headphones. However, after looking at the response curves and reading all the glowing reviews from knowledgeable users on these and the D5000 series I decided to give these a shot as my new studio monitors.

Overall, I would say they live up to the hype. These are definitely the best sealed cans I have heard, the highs are very accurate with an airy presence which feels like you are listening to an open headphone. They do not sound quite as neutral as the M40 to me, primarily due to the punchy low frequency response which can be a bit excessive with certain sources but that may soften up once they are properly broken in. Like any good headphone these will greatly benefit from quality amplification, but I must say they sound quite good unamped compared to some of my other high end cans like the Beyer DT990 which I consider useless without proper amplification.

These are also very comfortable although they could have made them a bit smaller, my head is somewhat small and they just barely fit me on the smallest setting.. all of my other headphones are too tight on the smallest setting so I am not sure what denon was thinking when they came up with the sizing for these.

title: Nice sealed cans but value isn't as good compared to previous generation
text:
The previous generation of these headphones were well regarded among some audio geeks due to their value. Their sound quality compared favorably to many other entries in the <$100 price range, and especially in comparison with other sealed headphones in that price range.

On this new version they have made a number of upgrades and also raised the price quite a bit. Unfortunately, not all of the changes to this version are improvements in my opinion and the higher price puts these in close competition with other headphones in the $150 range which are only slightly more expensive but have significantly better sound quality and construction.

I've never owned the previous version of these headphones but I have a friend who owns them and I have listened to them side by side with the new version. To my ears they sound very similar, both have a great high end and excellent staging for a sealed headphone but they are both bass heavy which I am not particularly a fan of. I would say the aurvana 2 seems to be even more bass heavy than the original so those who like lots of bass will probably enjoy these headphones.

I do like the new removable cord and the fact that the cord is only on one side of the headphones. I'm not really a fan of the red plastic design element, the old version was very nondescript whereas the new model tries to be flashy but looks kind of cheesy in my opinion. I do think the new shape is more comfortable though and also seems to offer improved noise isolation compared to the original model.

Pros:
Nice high end and midrange, good separation and staging for a sealed headphone in this price range
detachable cord w/ built in mic
comfortable design
good noise isolation (recently used them on a plane trip and they worked well)

Cons:
Excessive bass
Cheap looking plastic design elements
Old version sounds just as good and is quite a bit cheaper

title: Excellent Hardware, Decent Software
text:
As a software developer and tech geek who also dabbles in graphic design and photography, good color calibration is an important thing to me. I find it extremely bothersome when looking at a multi-monitor setup where the colors don't match well. I originally bought a spyder 3 some years ago when I started using a 3 monitor setup with two different types of monitors (a 144hz gaming monitor in the center and two 60hz displays on the sides). While the spyder 3 worked well, it was very slow at calibrating which was frustrating when doing a multi-display setup. I think it took around 5-6 hours to do all 3 displays with the spyder 3 (Note that I was using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal, but the Spyder software was equally as slow)

Last year I replaced all my monitors with new ones which are all the same type and I actually never calibrated them because they looked pretty good from the factory and I never felt like spending the time to use the spyder 3.. but when I saw Datacolor had released a new lens-based Spyder with claims of it being much faster and more accurate I knew I had to try it.

I am reviewing the SpyderX Pro, which has the same hardware as the SpyderX Elite but has software limitations locking some features (the most important being the limited calibration options for gamma/white point/brightness). Because those settings are important to me and I have previous experience with DisplayCal, I am using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal software with the SpyderX hardware instead of the default Spyder software. (SpyderX support was just added to ArgyllCMS in the latest version 2.1.0 on 4/10/19)

I haven't done a side-by-side comparison with the older baffle based spyder 3 to say whether the lens-based spyderX is more accurate out of the box.. but I will say that the calibration looked good to me and I can vouch for the manufacturers claims that the SpyderX is much faster than the previous generations.. The SpyderX took around 15-20 minutes per display compared to 90-100 minutes per display with the Spyder3.

Overall I am pleased with the SpyderX and think it is a worthy upgrade over its predecessor.. but I would recommend using it with DisplayCal if you really want the best results Note that both ArgyllCMS and DisplayCal are both Free, Open Source Software so you don't have to pay anything extra if you want to use them... the only downside is that they are more complicated than the Datacolor software which is designed to be very user-friendly.

title: HE-400 vs. Beyerdynamic DT770 80ohm vs. Grado SR325 w/ G-Cush
text:
Source material I use for my opinions:
- Poorly mastered 80s-90s Alternative, Dub Reggae, and old school Punk.
- EBM, Industrial, Industrial Noise
- Progressive Trance, Trip Hop, and other Electronic beats
Schiit Audio stack was used during my review. I already own Beyerdynamic DT770 80ohm & Grado SR325 w/ G-Cush, so I hope this can be a helpful reference point for others.

HE-400 vs. Grado SR325 w/ G-Cush pads:
The HE-400 has a much larger soundstage with far superior vocals; the singer sounds more like a live performance. Bass response is slightly more pronounced and forward. However the Grado SR325 has much crisper, sharper highs. To me, the Grados are a bit too bright. However, sibilance is subtly apparent on the HE400 with cymbal crashes and other fast sharp highs. Overall, with my strange musical tastes, the HE400 sound better. If you listen to well mastered recordings of Jazz and Classical, please seek another opinion.

HE-400 vs. Beyerdynamic DT770 80ohm (velour pads):
Please note that the DT770 at 80ohm is a popular "bass head" set of cans. The other DT770 versions with 32ohm or 250ohm impedances did not have the same pronounced quality of bass IMHO.
Picking a favorite here is really tough, but there is a substantial sound difference between these cans. The DT770 have very prominent drums at the front of the sound stage. You can't miss them. The HE-400 have a great bass response, yet lacks the deep (boosted?) depth of the DT770. Tracks from Einstürzende Neubauten reveal the difference very dramatically with the DT770 playing a much closer match to their live performance. For vocals however, the HE400 holds a slight edge creating a more live sound putting the vocalist in the room with me. Highs on the HE400 also are a bit crisper and more forward. I grab the DT770 if the music I'm listening to has prominent drums or electronic music. The HE400s are great for everything else.

Other noteworthy info about the HE-400s:
Weight: 17.2oz (vs 9.8oz for the DT770 and 9.5oz for the Aluminum SR325 cans) The HE-400 is very noticeably heavier compared to my other cans. I'm a big guy and have yet to experience fatigue due to the weight, but be aware of this difference. Also I have an oval head shape, so again no fatigue due to the headband shape. Read up on Headfi.org on simple mods to the HE-400 headband to make it more comfortable for other head shapes.
Open vs. Closed: The DT770 are closed cans and work well in an office cubicle environment. The Grados and HE-400 are open an open design meaning you'll still hear your cube neighbors and they'll get to listen to your music too.

HE-400 pads and comfort - I was able to successfully install the DT770 velour pads on the HE-400 pad mounts. I did not notice any sound changes, but long wear comfort was improved with the velour pads due to less heat. Also take a look on Headfi.org for other pad mod options.
Update: Ordered Beyerdynamic EDT770VB Headphone Ear Pads (http://www.amazon.com/Beyerdynamic-EDT770VB-Headphone-Pads-Black/dp/B007VCKA64) and was able to easily install them on these headphones. Longer listening session comfort has certainly improved over the original HiFiMan pads.

Please add a comment if you have any questions or need more info. I hope this review helps you!
item_title: HIFIMAN - HE-400 Headphones

title: Fine leather case with ever changing patina
text:

Just be aware that the inexpensive Fintie (other brands too?) cases don't provide as much drop protection as the Amazon Kindle branded cases (see my photo of the case interiors and edge profiles).
Amazon claims this is their lightest case. On my kitchen precision scale (second measurement made in grams):
Premium Leather Case: 4.8oz (135g)
Amazon Kindle Leather Case: 4.9oz (140g)
Fintie case: 3.1oz (87g)
Lighter yes, but by a negligible amount. Fintie case is noticeably lighter with its super thin edges and minimal drop protection.
Total weight with 2014 Paperwhite inserted into this premium leather case is 12.1oz (343g).

I personally thought the leather on the case looked dry. After making the "a to z" mark on my case (see photo), I applied saddle soap to the top of my case. (see photo that shows the darker cover with saddle soap rubbed on it and the untreated back of the case). Notice how the "a to z" mark has almost completely disappeared. My last photo shows how the saddle soap darkens the case, making it a darker walnut brown color. While the case can still easily be scratched, 50-75% of a light scratch can be rubbed out easily and quickly with a finger now that the leather is more moisturized. If you want to experiment with saddle soap (or other leather care products), make sure you test only a small part of the case first and ensure you like the result.

title: A $30 budget mouse masquerading as an expensive MX mouse
text:
I've been using various Logitech MX mice for many years now and was excited when I saw this mouse was released. Disappointment sunk in quickly as soon as I took it out of the box. This is absolutely not a "MX" type of mouse and should be priced at $30, not $95.

Pros:
- Should have a great battery life, but didn't keep it long enough to test. Other recent Logitech mice I've given to my family do have outstanding battery life, so I'd anticipate the same on this one.
- If your hands are small to medium size, this may be a great comfortable ergo mouse for you.
- USB C port for charging.

Cons:
- It has the same cheap feel as the $20-$30 vertical mice sold here on Amazon. I've used many of them in the office to know the difference.
- All of the MX mice I've used previously had hyper-scrolling capability, whereas this one has the typical cheap budget mouse scroll wheel. The product photos show what looks like the MX type hyper scroll wheel; nope, just chrome on plastic. Scrolling pages is a miserable experience on this MX mouse impostor.
- Darkfield tracking was present on all past 2 generations of MX mice, but not on this one. Darkfield tracking works amazingly well on every single surface without skipping or stuttering. Why was this not included?
- Ergonomic disaster for folks with large to extra large hands. I had to curl my fingers even more than as shown in Michael Craig's review photos. (see my included photos, definitely not comfortable for large hands)
- No extra customizable buttons, not even the top most button. (unlike prior MX mice)

Nits:
- Only customization in Windows Logitech driver utilities ("Options") is the mouse sensitivity that can be switched on the top most button. Great for games I suppose, but this isn't even close to a gaming mouse. I set the sensitivity once for a new mouse and never change it again.
- Logitech "Flow Control" is a joke unless you only use Logitech keyboards. Not for us mechanical keyboard fans!
- Logitech "Flow Control" has zero support for Linux computers which is what everyone in my 1000+ employee office is using along with Macs and PCs. "Flow Control" unfortunately won't be able to replace buggy Synergy by Symless because Synergy at least works with Linux AND is keyboard type agnostic.

I gave this mouse to a coworker with small hands who has been using a $5 comes with a desktop mouse and it's a great upgrade for them. OTOH, so would a $20-$30 ergo Anker mouse that has the same feel and quality as this mouse.

For myself, I've ordered a Logitech MX Master 2S as the reviewers state it works well for large hands, has a proper high quality scroll wheel, and precision darkfield tracking. Plus it's currently ~$25 cheaper than this mediocre vastly overpriced mouse.
UPDATE: my new MX Master 2S is working well for me, especially with the proper hyper-scrolling wheel. My coworker has gone back to his cheapo $5 mouse as they struggle with the vertical orientation.

title: Great seal on my cavernous ear canals!
text:
I struggle with getting a proper fit using IEM headphones as my ear canal openings are larger than most. The XL Comply earbud tips just fall out of my ears without getting compressed. I was exceptionally happy to find XXL sized ear tips included with these headphones which gave a proper seal.

Pros:
* Sound quality - These headphones are finally ones that can sound great for everyone. No, seriously!
Everyone hears sounds differently, that's why there are lots of different headphone companies and headphone reviews are incredibly subjective. What sounds great for me may not for you. I like a fun V curve EQ profile, others prefer a flat studio experience. The difference with these headphones is the software app you run on your phone to profile them to your ears and your hearing capabilities. When I first started listening to these headphones, I thought, "mehh, they sound just ok..." Then I tried loading sound profiles from the 20+ professional sound engineers and found a few that made me think, "hmm, much better". Once I ran the Hear ID sound test in the phone app (takes ~ 5 minutes to run), I was completely blown away at the sound improvement. Plus you can apply a custom profile on top of your personalized Hear ID profile to get a flat studio response or something more fun for the music genres you enjoy. Even better, the profile is stored into the headphones, so that profile is always used on other bluetooth devices too. The sound quality of these headphones is some of the best I've ever heard and I can actually say with confidence that it will be the same for you once you've created your own personal Hear ID profile. This is a game changer IMHO!
* Battery life has been great for me so far with the noise canceling enabled. I've been able to listen to music for several hours and the earbuds are still showing plenty of battery power.
* Charging case has a 3 light battery indicator so you know (roughly) how much juice is left. Also there is a light under each earbud that illuminates when the earbud is charging. This makes it easy to know that you have the earbud placed correctly for charging.
* With the included loops to help lock in the earbuds to your ear, the do a great job staying put without being uncomfortable.
* Case feels like a smooth river rock; easy to stash comfortably into a pocket.
* Easy to switch between my phone and my linux laptop for use with these earbuds.

Cons: (more like nits)
* Noise canceling - I set it manually to the "High" setting, but still found it wasn't able to cancel as well as my Sony wh-1000 around ear closed headphones. That said, it's so much easier to pack these earbuds than the giant case for the Sony headphones. Maybe if I had and even better seal with the ear tips or a different ear tip, my experience may be better. Please understand this is a nit as it's not a fair comparison between these two headphone types. The Soundcore ear buds still substantially reduce the volume of loud lower frequencies as found in a vehicle, train, or airplane.
* The slide on the case has worked perfectly so far, but I do worry about its longevity. Time will tell and I'll update this review if I encounter issues.

tl;dr: Best sounding earbuds that I've ever heard and can wholeheartedly recommend them to everyone knowing they will have the same experience.

title: OnePlus phone owners - CAUTION: does not work!
text:
Tried this wireless AA adapter in my 2016 VW GTI that was already working with wired AA and my OnePlus 7T (Android 11). No setting, including all Developer mode settings could get this adapter working with my phone and my car. I tried 3 other different OnePlus phones in the household (all newer models running Android 12), all with the same no-go result. After reading a bunch of articles on XDA, Reddit, and the OnePlus bug reporting forums, this is an ongoing issue with OnePlus. Motorola Tech Support really needs to mention this issue in their support wikis.

Purchased a Pixel 6a phone, factory reset this adapter, and it worked right away in my GTI. During my first usage, input was very laggy; time from a screen press to action being performed was > 1 second. On subsequent drives, the input lag is much less pronounced at ~ 300-500ms. Expect some UI lagginess when compared to running AA with a wired cable.

Overall I'm happy with the device working well other than having to upgrade my phone (which is not Motorola's fault)

title: Porsche - Adds Android Auto option!
text:
If you have a 718/982 or a 991.2 Porsche with PCM 4 Car Play enabled, this adapter will allow Android Auto to work on your center console display!
This isn't a perfect solution and the product is poorly documented, but it works well most of the time and the other times it just needs to be unplugged and plugged back in. If your Porsche is CarPlay enabled, this device appears to the car as though it's an apple phone, then appears to an Android phone as a Android Auto screen device. You can connect your Android phone via a usb cable directly into this device and it will charge your phone (slowly) along with connecting it to Android Auto. Or Android Auto will work wirelessly as well as shown in my photos (the cable connected to my phone is just a charging cable).

Some items of interest I've found:
* If you use wireless Android Auto, there is some latency from the screen press to the actual response. Sometimes the latency is longer than other times; not sure what is the cause. There is minimal Android Auto latency if the Android phone is directly connected to this device using a cable.
* If you get out of the car for a few minutes and lock the car, when you return, sometimes the car's center screen display is blank. Simply unplugging and replugging the adapter fixes the issue.
* To follow the instructions in the owners manual to get firmware updates, connect your phone directly to this device and don't use a wireless connection. It took me a while to make that work, only to discover the device already had the latest firmware.
* The Motorola wireless AA used in one of my other cars works much better if you're simply looking for a wireless AA adapter. The magic with this adapter is to be able to use Android Auto in a car that only supports CarPlay.
item_title: 2023 Carlinkit 4.0 Adapter - Wireless CarPlay & Wireless Android Auto for OEM Factory CarPlay Cars, Fast Connect, Plug & Play, 2 in 1 No Delay, Built in CarPlay

title: Good Card for the Money, Not for High End Gaming
text: I bought this card as part of my upgrade process which included taking an older Dell Optiplex 745 and turning it into a home theater PC.  The onboard video was adequate for Standard Def, but fell short when it came to 720p or 1080p HD content.  I added an 80GB OCZ Vertex 2 Solid State Drive to hold our 64bit Windows 7 Ultimate OS and other applications like XBMC, VLC Media Player, etc.  The PC's secondary (storage drive) is a Western Digital 2TB Green drive which we chose for it's lower power consumption and massive storage space.  This card handles 1080p content flawlessly and is now hooked up via HDMI to our 40" LCD HDTV.  The drivers that came with it aren't completely useless, but they are definitely outdated.  I suggest downloading the latest drivers from the AMD website.  The latest drivers and Catalyst Control Center also include AMD OverDrive, which let you overclock the cards core speed and memory speed, allowing a little bump in performance.  Not for serious gaming, but will handle games that we like (such as the Sims 3) very respectably, even at 1920 x 1080, which says a lot considering I paid $34 for this card and it had a $15 mail in rebate.  I recommend this card to anyone looking to boost the performance compared to the on-board video and highly recommend it for home theater PC's.

title: Those who gave this cable bad reviews most likely don't know what they're talking about.
text: I've read numerous reviews about this cable that say things like "it's junk" or "it's a fire hazard, don't buy".  But then, there's images of things like multiple large SLA batteries hooked up with 8 Gauge wire, and the only thing melted is the wire, not the terminals, screws, etc.  It appears to me that at least that individual was using the wire in a situation where it was grossly underrated for the application.  If that was indeed the case, the wire is not at fault, but the person who installed it IS.  As for those stating that the product is "Deceiving", the ads I see clearly state that the wire is Copper Clad Aluminum (CCA), meaning that it's Aluminum wire with a very thin coating of copper on each strand.  Yes, CCA cable will NOT perform the same as pure copper or Oxygen Free Copper (OFC), but in many cases, it's 40% of the cost of pure copper.  So, if you were to use 8 Gauge pur copper cabling for a given application, I personally would opt for 6 guage CCA to offset the difference in maximum current carrying abilities.  I've used CCA cabling in various forms for YEARS without any issues.  It's all about having the proper knowledge to use it in a proper way.

title: Gen 2 Failure
text:
I have installed three inside and three outside Nestcams through the years and have been quite happy. My oldest inside Nestcam is starting to act it's age, so I bought this new generation2 version. BIG mistake, and I waited too long to install it so now I can't return it.

title: I call it my "James Bond" watch
text:
I've steered clear of smartwatches ever since they came out, mainly because they've looked too much like a Dick Tracy two-way wrist-radio (Yes, I'm dating myself, and yes, Dick Tracy was way ahead of his time). As a professional speaker / trainer, I am up in front of people a lot, and I want to look professional. The look of most smart watches is certainly edgy, but call me old-fashioned, I like a more traditional, classy look. This Michael Kors hybrid smart watch certainly fills the bill for traditional and classy, but with the added bonus of having some useful smart technology. I call it my James Bond watch, in large part because it does cool things without looking like it will do cool things.

Positives:

1) I get email and text notifications! This is the BIG positive. That said, you don't get notified for every email or text. You have to choose who gets the high-priority access to you.

2) The buttons look like regular watch buttons, but they let you take pictures, control music, check the date, and set alarms. (Now, if only I could program it to start my car remotely ...)

3) If you can't find your phone, you can press a button to make your phone ring, enabling you to find it. My thoughts: we all can benefit from this, and with this "call" feature on your wrist, it will save you time!

4) This thing even serves as a fitness tracker (tracking steps & calories burned).

5) It's battery operated -- You don't need to keep charging it.

6) It's classy enough to wear to a formal occasions, yet casual enough to wear every day.

On the downside (for me, anyway):

A) The band overlaps quite a bit on my wrist. My previous watch also overlapped quite a bit, but this band is even longer -- with no way to shorten it. I'm not a small guy, either (215 / 5'11").

B) Gotta change the battery every six months. Yes, you don't have to charge it, and I suppose for all this watch does, a six-month battery life is reasonable, but I'm a tad spoiled ... I also have a Citizen ecowatch that doesn't need batteries at all.

C) Illumination for night viewing isn't all that great. Pretty dim, actually. It'd be nice if one could push a button to get a bit more illumination to tell the time in the dark.

If these downsides don't bother you (and they really don't bother me all that much), then you may enjoy this watch to enjoy a traditional look accompanied by a little bit of James Bond gadgetry.

title: Use beefier screws than what they provide, and you've got a convenient time saver on your desk
text:
This review is for the Legrand WMC220BK Desktop Mounted USB Charging and Power Center. I note that the image and the product described at the top of the Amazon page is not the same unit as the image in the "middle" of the Amazon page. The upper image promotes the WSR320-S, which has three outlets, and the unit I have (WMC220BK) is pictured in the middle of the page. The WMC220BK has two outlets, not three. I will amend this part of the review if/when this apparent error gets resolved.

Regardless, this review is for the WMC220BK.

This is a straightforward unit: Two outlets and two USB ports. The USB ports are 3.1 amps, which is more than what many devices need today. That means this is good for charging almost anything. Really, this design is smart thinking. USB-C will evenually leave USB-2 in the history books, and USB-C is 3.1A friendly. Devices such as an iPad need "only" 2.1A to charge (most phones need only 1 amp, and smaller devices, such as an iPod nano, need only 0.5A). But as things go, more power = more speed and more productivity, so I imagine that in addition to the few devices that are now built around 3.1A charging, more devices needing 3.1A will be forthcoming in the not-to-distant future. That means this unit will be useful for years to come.

Side note: No matter what amperage the port is, you must have a cable that can accommodate the amps needed for your device or the extra available power doesn't matter. Also, if your phone charges at 1A, having 3.1A won't speed up the charging, even if you have a high-capacity cable ... but it will certainly keep the electrons flowing as fast as your device will absorb them. In other words, it won't be slow.

Also note that the electrical outlets on this unit are 12 amps. Don't be thinking you can plug in a 15 amp carpet shampooer and expect everything to be cool.

As for mounting the unit, it's designed so the power cord can come either straight down, or positioned to lead out the backside (which is how I have mine). I like that both option exist.

When getting ready to mount it, I was NOT impressed with the two screws provided. They don't have much "teeth" to them, and I feared that by regularly pressing plugs into those sockets, I would eventually push those screws out the back of my desk. Instead, I mounted this using two 1.5" drywall screws. I set the unit in place, marked the holes with a pencil, and then drilled pilot holes so I wouldn't have to worry about getting everything lined up while simultaneously holding the unit. This worked wonderfully. The screws went in easy, and there's plenty of teeth on them to keep this unit securely in place.

Because they used lame screws in the kit, I'm giving the product 4.5 stars. But the screw problem is easily overcome by using drywall screws. For me, the unit was easy to install, plus it adds a ton of convenience. I'm rounding up to five stars.

title: I think it's a great camera and I highly recommend it
text:
This review is not coming from a gamer, but rather a person who creates instructional video e-learning in many different environments. It's one thing to have a studio in which lights can be situated to create the best look, but being "on location" is a much different story. Thus, the built-in lighting, plus this unit's ease of portability, makes it an excellent choice for anyone who needs to create "talking head" video away from the comforts of an office or studio. In the past I've made do with available lighting, but there are times when it doesn't look the way I'd like. After using this Razer Kiyo, I'll tell you that having the light can make a significant difference.

LIKES:
** No software required on Windows 10. Plug and Play!
** Adjusting the light is EASY. Just turn the ring around the light as if you adjusting the volume knob on a radio.
** Portability. The tripod mounting option is awesome for my needs. It also sits on a flat surface easily without it having to sit precariously. Very user-friendly for recording interviews in someone's office.
** Compatible with OBS. I've been using Open Broadcaster for a while now. It provides awesome technical director capabilities so I can easily create engaging e-learning. I highly recommend it, but I suppose my touting that program is for a different review. As for the Razer Kiyo, anyone familiar with OBS will appreciate the easy interface.
** FPS options. These are not options I've had before in a camera, and I see a lot of value in having them. 1080p / 30fps seems to work well for my head shots, but I did a trial doing a two-person interview, and the 720p / 60fps seemed to work better for that.

DISLIKES:
** Built in mic. It doesn't have a super-professional sound quality. Don't misunderstand -- I'm glad this unit precludes the need for an external mic, and the built-in mic is okay for many of circumstances I need. But after a bit of testing, I can tell there will be times when a separate mic will provide much clearer recording.

That's about it, really, for dislikes. And it's not even a dislike -- more of a "could be better." Overall this is a really nice camera and there is little to dislike about it. For anyone who creates video instruction or does live webinars, I think it's a great camera and I highly recommend it.

title: This projector has everything I need
text:
Let me preface this review by saying I've been doing corporate training in front of senior managers and C-suite executives for 30 years, and I've given thousands of presentations in that time.

Open the box of this ViewSonic PA503W and you're greeted by several plastic bags of cables (VGA & power) and the projector itself, which is securely packed in form-fitted foam. Once you have it out of its wrapping, you'll find a traditional-looking projector, and it has a nice feel to it. That is, it does not feel cheap.

The "thumb wheel" to raise and lower the projector is centered on the machine, and straightforward to use, which I appreciate. I get a tad frustrated with some projectors that have new-fangled ways to adjust the height. There's no guessing on how to adjust the height with this. Also straightforward is the focus adjustment, and there's also a zoom. You'll also find Viewsonic's logo of three Lady Gouldian Finches on the front of the machine, right next to the lens. (For those who don't know, the company's founder selected these birds as his logo because of their beauty and vibrant colors, and he wanted to associate those attributes with his projectors.)

On the back of the machine, above the standard three-prong power connection is an HDMI port plus 1/8" audio "in" and "out" ports. There are also TWO 15-pin VGA receptacles, labeled "computer 1" and "computer 2," plus a 15-pin "monitor out" port. Next to those is a mini-USB port and a 1/8" video jack. There's also a 9-pin RS-232 port.

The remote control allows you to choose the input (computer, video, or HDMI inputs), adjust for keystoning, and adjust the volume, among other features. Those controls I just listed are also available using touch buttons on the top of the projector itself.

If you like, this unit allows to switch to a "SuperEco" feature. It's supposed to reduce power consumption by 70% plus greatly extend the life of the lamp. I find the whites look more grey, but I suppose there are times when it really doesn't matter. Another "if you like" feature is the option to set a password - in case you don't want people using your projector when you're not around.

LIKES:
**The sharpness and the vibrancy of the colors is awesome.
**The "Freeze" button allows me to freeze what's being displayed on screen and then search for a different file on my computer without the audience having to watch me go through my files, then unfreeze the screen once I have a new file open. I *really* like this feature.
**You can magnify the image being displayed to "zoom in" on a particular portion of the slide.
**You can adjust the image brightness. 3600 lumens can be WAY too bright for some situations. You can tone if you like it down to suit your environment. You can also adjust other settings such as contrast and color brilliance, again, as needed to suit your situation.
**The image can project clearly onto a surface that's 36 feet away. With the brightness being capable of 3600 lumens, I may do like a friend of mine does and show movies on my garage door during warm weekend evenings in the summer. :-) I'd just need to hook up external speakers to the "audio out" port and amplify the sound.
**There's a "presentation timer" that you can set to appear on your display. I speak at a lot of conferences, and usually the time frame you are given to speak is set in stone. You MUST be done by a certain time. There have been occasions when the person who's supposed to notify me that I have five minutes left has failed to do so, and that's irritating. With this projector, that problem goes away. You can set it to count up or count down (your choice), plus you can choose to have it display that count during your entire presentation, or just have it appear for the last few minutes (which is my preference). Or you don't have to use the feature at all.

DISLIKES
There really isn't anything I dislike about this projector. That said, there are some features on the remote that are nice, but you have to be in front of the projector to use them -- and they are features I use on a different hand held device. For example, there are "page up/page down" buttons on the remote that *could* take the place of my hand-held Logitech [[ASIN:B002GHBUTK Wireless Presenter R400]] (what I call my "clicker"), but to use the ViewSonic's remote for this purpose I'd have to be standing in front of the projector, which is not always feasible in my training situations. The remote also has a "blank" button, which blacks out the screen and draws all eyes back to the presenter (a very powerful speaking technique, so long as it's not overused). Again, this is something I do w/ my Logitech clicker, but if you don't have one of those, it's nice to have these features on the ViewSonic remote -- so long as you're able to stand in front of the projector.

By the way, I recommend you connect using the HDMI port whenever possible, as it provides the clearest imaging.

This unit also has 3D functions that allow you to watch 3D movies, etc., but I haven't used that feature and therefore can't attest to its effectiveness.

Overall, I love this projector. I've trained for 30 years in front of groups as small as two and sometimes as big as 2,000. In these past three decades I've used hundreds of projectors, and I have to say this one has everything I need. It has a great picture, plus LOTS of options that I'd wished I had in times past. I can't speak to all situations for which you might use a projector, but if you conduct training in front of other people, you really can't go wrong with this projector. I'm compelled to give it five stars, and I'd give it more if I could.

LIKES:

** Very easy to charge. Twist off the top, insert the micro USB connector, then plug the standard USB at the other end of the cable into a charger.

title: Love the freedom!
text:
These Sony SP600N Wireless Noise Canceling Headphones give me excellent freedom to listen to music / podcasts, etc., while working in the yard. I'm finding I get a little over 3 hours of use on a charge if I'm working outside. The unit is "supposed" to hold a charge for six hours, but I'm finding that varies depending on how far I am from the source. If I'm inside, closer to the source, it seems to last a bit longer. Go figure.

I use these with both my phone AND my Kindle fire (bluetooth compatible), and the sustainable range is about 15 feet, maybe 20. After that, the sound starts cutting out.

The ear buds themselves are of good quality material and actually stay on quite nicely! That said, they're not the most comfortable earbuds I own. They're not bad, but I have better. Music and sound quality are surprisingly good. I'm very impressed with that. I also like the way the unit tells you "powering on / powering off / bluetooth connected." Noise cancelling is not for voices --- it's to counter low frequency droning that occurs in airplanes, trains, car trips, etc. For that, I think these do a good job, but not a great job. I haven't found anything that beats BOSE for noise-cancelling.

I really like these a lot, but I'm assigning 4.5 stars and rounding down, mainly because of the combination of the minor issues mentioned above. LOVE the sound quality. LOVE that they're wireless (yay, freedom!). Comfort and range are good, but not top drawer. That said, I still recommend them.

+ There are three brightness levels. Most clocks have only two, if at all.

+ Radio presets? Wow - Every nightstand clock I've ever owned before had only a dial, not presets. This is nice.
+ USB port allows me to charge my phone or kindle overnight without having an extra cord plugged in near the bed.

What I'm not so thrilled with:

Overall, not a bad clock with an easy-to-read screen. The sound quality is not great, but I use this to wake up, not to listen to music. Hate it. I'll climb the stairs rather than yell. However, there are times when a question is urgent. Enter the intercom.

For basic use, the set up is quite intuitive. Just push the talk button and start talking. But if the person you're trying to reach isn't near the intercom, there's a cool "CALL" feature that makes the unit ring like a telephone three times, and somewhat loudly.

There's also a "Group" function, which, if you have more than two machines, allows you to talk to all locations at once. To my amazement, there are 22 channels on this. If you find you're getting static on a one of the frequencies, just change the channel (both units have to be on the same channel to talk, unless you use the "Group" button). My previous intercoms had only two channels. However, there's zero static on the default channel, so I've had no need to change channels.

Amazingly, these units have a one-mile range, which means you could set them up between different houses, or in various buildings on a work site. I've not tested the range, but even if it's half that, I'm still impressed. And, because the power cord is USB, I plugged it into a USB port on my laptop, and it worked fine -- which means it's portable if need be. The fact that the units are small (only about 6" across -- see pic), and have a low profile helps in this regard.

By the way, the units also have a monitor function, so it can act like a baby monitor (or similar). Again, I've not had this feature on any of my previous intercoms. Like I said - this setup has some really nifty features, and they're very useful. Easily five stars.

I sometimes travel overseas and do Skype calls with my wife. I'm thinking this BEISIWO USB Plug and Play provides a better sound quality when I'm 8 - 12" inches from it, but the difference it not that far off. And when you get outside that narrow 4" range, the built-in mic from the laptop actually does better.

That said, let me sing a little praise for this mic. It truly is a plug and play mic. I just plugged it in and my laptop recognized it right away. Nothing to download at all. There's also a 'mute' button on the mic base that's quite convenient.

Where will this mic come in handy? Definitely on any computer that doesn't already have a mic. It's not high quality enough for recording music, and I don't think I'd record a radio commercial on it. But for things like YouTube and/or online chatting, I think it will work fine. But do be sure to stay within that "sweet spot" distance from the mic or your voice will either over-modulate or you will sound far away.

Overall, it's a good camera, but not a great one. Four stars.

title: Adorable unit - easy to use & one charge provides a full-day of play time
text:
This portable Bluetooth speaker is adorable. It’s rechargeable, so no need for batteries. It comes with a USB cable for recharging, and it’s a standard micro USB, so any micro USB cable you have around the house will work. NOTE: the cable comes stored in the plastic that covers the speaker, so be sure not to throw it away accidentally.

LIKES:
+ In addition to Bluetooth, it plays music off a microSD card. You can load MP3 or WAV files onto eight microSD, slip it into the back slot, and you got your own custom playlist.

+ All day playtime! This unit as advertised with a 15 hour playtime, and I’m going to say that’s correct. We ran this over 14 hours cumulative playing time before it needed recharging, and I’m pretty sure it was very close to 15 hours before juice ran out.

+ The “eyes” have it. The unit is so cool in how it tells you what it’s doing. When it’s charging, the eyes are red. When it’s operating off Bluetooth, the eyes are blue. And when it’s playing off the microSD card, the eyes are green.

+ The sound is pretty good for this little unit. Not the clearest, but I’ve heard much worse, in fact, I’d say the sound is “very good.” It uses a sound reflective design that helps spread the sound around the room. Speakers are angled down so the sound reflects out and around the room.

+ If you’re playing music off eight micro SD card, you can skip to the next song or go back into the previous song.

DISLIKES:
- Call me old school, but I wish this unit had a 3.5 mm port so I could connect with a cable instead of using Bluetooth.

- The maximum sized SD card this will take is 32g. That’s still a lot, but if you have 64g cards, they won’t work in this unit.

- No “shuffle” option when using the micro SD card.

Overall, this is a very nifty unit that adds personality to the sound source, instead of having a box-like unit sitting on a counter or shelf. As the writeup for the product says, it would make a great gift for someone. I’m deducting half-a-star for lack of a cable port, but definitely rounding up.

title: Falling in Love all over again...
text:
I have an older pair of SR80 headphones. I have to admit that after my original ear pads desentigrated, I was ready to throw the "old" Grado's away. They certainly did not sound like anything you would wish to own with the ear cushions missing and at the time $25 dollars for replacements seemed a bit over the top considering what I paid for them "new".
After about three years of sitting unused and after having two other pairs of my earphones eaten by the dog and cat, I figured it was time to try something...anything.
I looked on Amazon an low and behold there were a pair of L-CUSH ear cushions. Not the original ones that came with the SR80's but the ones used on the more expensive models. They looked better and they also looked more comfortable to boot. I figured, what the heck I can always send them back...soooo...
My order arrives and I immediately go to my music room to see how they fit and most importantly if my grand ol' Grado's can still make "music".
I have to say I was very VERY surprised! First the ear cushions fit more "over" the ear than just on the ear. As soon as I began to play music through them (the same system, mind you that I use for my reference gear) I couldn't believe how good the old Grado's sounded. Everything was there from top to bottom. The separation of instruments and voices was very good. From the highest highs to the lowest lows, it was all there. Even the bass range was full and much more detailed than I remembered.
The SR80's are by no means the end all and be all in detail and definition but the music is there...all of it. This is what I remember when I first fell in Love with Hi-Fi audio.
I can say that while the tonal color is a bit on the bright side and the midrange a bit forward they do bring out hidden details that only my Revel's and the Quad ESL's (and newer versions) have ever been able to reproduce. This may seem contradictory to what I stated earlier but the SR80's lack in Spatial detail and Depth overall. Can't have it all for $79.
I do attribute a great deal of the bass detail to the "upgraded" cushions. If you own a pair of the SR60's or 80's you MUST get the L-Cushions and see just how good the Grado's can really sound.
Well worth the $20 cost if admission.

title: Still New, More To Come
text:
I was looking at the Shure SE215 to use as an In Ear Monitor, on stage with other musicians. When I first got them I ran them at a moderate volume using tracks with particularly deep bass for about 8 hours. I tried them out and my first impression that from the top to the upper midrange it was all there. Nice detail even at higher volumes (Great for live work). The isolation was very good. They seal into the ear more like fitted In Ears than the usual "stick it in you ear" type.
I've used them for about 15 hours so far and while the bass is detailed and well defined it really isn't that deep. My hope is that whithin the 20 to 30 hour range the IEM's will begin to lossen up a bit and allow for better low end response.
I own a pair of Future Sonics 500-030 Atrio X in ears and the overall tone is much warmer while still having very good detail. I think they are great for music playback while the SE215's will do a bit better with live music.
I think my next try will be with the Future Sonic Atrio 010-045 w/MG7 Pro Technology. These have been designed for live sound and I have heard a lot of good things about them from other drummers.
I'll give an additional review after the 30 hour mark. Stay tuned...=)

title: At this Price, Hard to Beat
text:
At this price point you can't really expect much. That said the Klipsch S3's are by far the best sounding ear phones in their class.

Second - What's Right. We can talk about frequency response, dynamics and bass all day long but what we want to know is what they sound like. Music is very emotional so a good transducer should convey that emotion. Listening to Diana Krall - Live In Paris, A Case of you, almost brought me to tears. Diana pours herself into this song, obviously written about her husband. This is a live performance which was incredibly well recorded. In this song you can hear not only every note of the piano but every mechanical bang, click and clatter. These ear phones reproduce the very essence of the music and conveys the emotion of this piece clear as a bell.
I think this is a very good starting point for any piece of audio gear. Best $16.00 I've ever spent in Hi-Fi.

The bass lines are as deep as you'll find on any CD. you can tell that all of the instruments are "digital" but they don't sound cold through the SR325e. The midrange is amazing. Crystal clear, warm and always very musical. The treble is never to bright or edgy but always detailed and open.
I may chime in with more after a bit of a break in period but so far I believe I made the right choice. Considerations; HiFi Man HW400S - Audio Technica ATH-M350x - SONY MDR-1A - NAD VISO HP50.

title: Excellent sound quality especially for the price
text:
I've seen a few reviews that were, let's say "snooty". Guys these are $65 earbuds. They are not in anyway "high-end". That said...
For $65 you do get very good performance as well as a really nice app which allow active control of the earbuds including a very useful EQ as well as test tones and "Sound Scapes" which are pretty cool. The app also includes the user manual which is very helpful.
Sound quality: Again these cost $65 so I wasn't expecting much, like a freaquency response that goes down to a solid 30Hz. Anyone complaining that the bass response is poor isn't using the correct rubber grommets to seal the ear canal and you're not listening to the right music. If you want to test any music system I suggest Boz Scaggs, "Dig" the last track which is Thanks to You. This track will highlight sub-bass tones excellent mid-range as well as high frequencies. If I have any complaints about the tone it would be the high frequencies which seem a little subdued. Overall sound quality however is very good and they will play loud.
Sound quality during phone calls is very good and the person receiving the call here's me very clearly.
Battery life : I can't really evaluate it because I've been using them for two days and the batteries haven't run out. I would rate the battery life as being very high as I've been listening to music at a high volume as well as placing many phone calls.
I would certainly consider purchasing these again should anything happen to them like my last pair which the dog ate. FYI - dogs eating your earbuds are not covered under warranty.

text: I LOVE this product and have had it for 3 years and purchased one for my in-laws. I love the interface and how simple it is to share pictures and memories. I like the simple design and really appreciate the stiff power cord that doubles as the frame stand. This is where the praise stops b/c the frame was plugged in behind our couch which slid back into the USB plug and broke it. This shouldn't be a problem as with MOST electronics you simply replace the power cable. Nixplay has the power cord hard wired into the frame, so if the USB gets bent it is irreparable. So My $150 frame is completely dependent upon the strength of extremely thin metal housing of a USB interface. Very frustrated as I enjoyed the product but one poor design choice now has me out $150 after just 3 years of use with no option to repair it. Never again will I purchase from this company!

title: Great frame, good app, amazing price
text:
I really like most of the picture frame. My biggest issue is that it did not come with the “kickstand” piece so we currently have it leaning up against another picture. I have contacted support and they indicated they would send one out but we have yet to see anything. I will update this once it is received.

The set up is very easy as it is a touch screen. It made me nervous not having a remote but the touch screen is very responsive so I was extremely happy with that. There also isn’t much set up to do on the frame side. I have had many other digital frames including most recently an expensive Nixplay. I loved my Nixplay frame until the proprietary cord that is hard wired in the back and has a USB on the other end broke and isn’t repairable because it is hard wired in. This frame does not have that problem because the cord plugs into the frame so if there was a similar problem with the plug end (which is frustratingly long as it’s oriented incorrectly if you are plugging it in behind a couch or in a tight area that doesn’t have at least 3-4” of clearance, see picture) I would only be out the cost of a new cord as opposed to throwing away a $200 frame which is what I had to do with my Nixplay.

This frame uses the Frameo app which was pretty simple and does provide some flexibility for comments, and other options. It makes it easy to upload photos from your phone with a few caveats. The downside I have found is that there is no computer interface so getting photos from a computer to the frame is quite a pain as you have to move them to your phone first. It also doesn’t support upload through any of the popular photo hosting apps like Google photos or flickr so I had to sort through and select all of the pictures from google photos and save them back to my phone (defeats the purpose of using a service like google photos to keep large amounts of pictures stored remotely so as not to hog memory space on your phone) and then I had to go back to the Frameo app and select them in order to add them. Ideally I should be able to share them directly from Google Photos to the Frameo app. It also limits you to 10 photos at a time which will be plenty in the future however for the initial set up where I was adding hundreds of pictures was quit annoying!

Again these are minor gripes and overall if the product had shipped with all of the parts or if support had sent them to me it would have gotten a much higher grade. If no replacement part is sent then I plan on returning this one but would buy again as the price was 1/3 that of other frames and the biggest downside is extra time on the front end to set it up, but I love looking through pictures and don’t mind reliving those memories which this frame, once set up, does a great job of displaying at a very good price.

Update: I got the kickstand in the mail which bumps this up to a five star product!! See ya Nixplay!! As the frames I bought my family die out they will be replaced with this quality companies product!

title: Great, Cheap, Foam Tips
text:
Well made, insulate sound well and very comfortable. I use these on my SoundSoul S-018's, they've improved sound isolation, comfort, and bass over the regular silicone tips (like a mechanical keyboard, I can't go back to them now silicone feels awful). So if you think you're not getting the most out of your IEM's, get some foam tips.

I've been using these for a week so far at 8+ hours a day taking them on and off 5+ times an hour and they still look like new with no wear (other reviews have stated they were falling apart first day in-ear, either some kind of defect or fakes probably). Keep your ears clean, and these stay quite clean (obv you should be doing that anyway if you're using IEMs, but less of an issue with silicone tips).

Bought these in place of Comply T-400 tips because they're cheaper (and I'm cheap, c'mon $7 for 6 pair or $15 for 3 pair, no-brainer, 4x cheaper.)

I can't imagine tips get much better than this.

They came in their own little plastic storage box, wrapped in a paper box and look exactly as pictured.

I'll update this review if something happens to them or when I decide they get bad enough to move to the next pair.

Edit: 9/4/17 - They got waxy enough for me to clean them, weren't quite staying in properly for hour (slowly slipped out). A very lightly wet paper towel, rubbed surface with wet then dry, and they're working just like new again. No visible wear so far, still on first pair.

Edit: 9/24/17 - Time to clean them again (I did clean once in-between edits using method above, this new method works better). Took a 2 liter bottlecap, filled it with 3% Hydrogen Peroxide. Took tips and dunked them in for 20 seconds each (you can see the outsides fizzle), followed by running under warm water and wiping with a paper towel, then drying them off, squishing lightly until dry and ready to go again, just like new. No visible wear so far, still on first pair.

title: Well made, but lacking clearance room on top fans and back hdd.
text:
Case looks great, metal is well made it's not cheap and flimsy metal. "Ez" drive bays work good. Cable management holes are decent.

There's not enough clearance once a motherboard is in there to fill the 2 120mm fan slots on the inside. It needs at minimum another inch or two (otherwise you're not getting you 4/8 pin CPU or fan headers plugged in). I had to top mount my 120mm fans (as seen in photo) on top and cover them with a grill.

There's also not enough space on the backside where you plug in sata power to the drives. I had to use some SATA extensions and bend the wire, just off the plug, 90 degrees to get the back panel on. There should at minimum be another 2" of clearance on the backside.

A poor design that would have been apparent if anyone who made it actually tested it. I would *NOT* recommend this to anyone unless you also purchase 90 degree data power adapters for your drives on the back side and try some thin top fans (thinner than 25mm).

However, the fact that I could unplug the earphones from the bluetooth adaptor/main-body on the MW600 won my purchase(as I figured, at places eg., gym-treadmill video/audio, I could just use the earphone by themselves).
My first one died in a month or two, I am not sure why but guess it was a combination of moisture and something else. I reached out to the CS and after almost 3-4 months, got a replacement. Funny thing, the replacement model looked and felt different in the build quality, version and packaging. (update: Yes, it is indeed newer model).

My 2nd one still works to this day, paired with my laptop (Windows 7U, phone (Lumia 920 and earlier iPhone4) and an iPad.

Pros:
1 I use it as a two-in-one (for BT and just the earphones where BT is not available -flights, gyms etc).
2 Works and does what it says will do.
3 Pairing is fairly easy and I could pair it with 4 devices in all (not all 4 work at the same time, mind you).
4 Operating and using it is fairly.
5 BUILT-IN FM!!! THANK YOU SONY!

Cons:
1 INCLUDED EARPHONES ARE SHORT!! But, they are short for my dual purpose use, I used an extension cord for sometime.
2 The BT adapter grip is NOT strong at all, and can easily slip.
3 The placement of the mic and the earphone port needs revision. At least on my 2nd one, it was difficult to position the mic to face my mouth and wrap the cord around my neck properly. Either a bulging loop exists on my neck, or I have to run the main-body further down away from the mouth.
4 The volume control is finicky.
5 Sometimes the display and pairing acts up. Its usually resolvable by restarting the procedure but its annoying in time-sensitive tasks.
6 The mic clarity during phone calls is hit-n-miss.

The 2nd MW600 has different earphones, and unfortunately I had already lost the first ones to compare them both. They have slightly thicker wires and tend to stand up a lot resulting in Con#3 but are much more solid looking without the green logo.

I am ok-happy with the ~$50 I spent on it, given that Sony took that long a time to send a replacement, which apparently some did not get too. I just hope they look into resolving some of the issues like wire length, mic and earphone port positioning, if there ever is going to be a MW600 V2,3,4

The set I originally purchased developed issues where clarity, pairing began to suffer. After contacting Jabra's customer service and getting a replacement one, I was a little skeptical about these. There were periods in between where the headphones were useful just as headphones and not a headset, as in, mic and voice clarity suffered greatly. People had real trouble hearing me and even if they did, were complaining about the quality. I started using them "wired" for any phone calls.
From time to time, I went "wireless" for calls and it worked. So I am not sure if it was the network lag or just the headset. The latest issue with an android phone (running Lollipop) and the voice kept saying "2 devices connected" "disconnected" "2 devices connected" and so on. It was paired to my iPad and phone but the phone kept dropping the connection. Jabra's customer service asked me to reset the headphones and it's back to functioning now.

So, they are generally OKAY. Work and do what they are supposed to do most of the time. The lack of consistency is where I take off one star, though I feel am being a little too generous on it.
---------------

I had to choose between the Revo and the Sony MDR10RBT. I wasn't sure of the on the ear design of the Revo but Sony reviews gave me less cheer. Moreover, these look more appealing too.

I have had them for about 5 days now. So the review period is still very "young".
Pros:
+NFC
+Design
+Clarity
+Ease of Use
+Wired and wireless use
+Multiple-point pairing
+Comfortable
+Box and accessories

Cons:
+White ear pads and head lining
+Unsure of jumping between devices
+Flimsy power button quality (plastic-y)
+Loose fit
+The carrying case

The pairing process was easy but I was disappointed with the quality of the power slider switch. It was slightly transparent and very cheap looking (on a $150+ headphones, come on!). Once I paired it with all the necessary devices (Lumia 1020, iPad 3, Sony Vaio laptop), I wasn't sure how to jump between the devices and which one was active over the other. My other Sony MW600s (with a nice display) allowed me to pick the source, may be that spoilt me.

The quality is decent. I haven't done a ton of music listening on it so I will reserve that for later. Calls were 50-50, one complaint, ne no complaint call so far, so I have to do some heavy talking too. There's audio feedback for different actions which is a nice touch. NFC worked straight out of box (cheer up Lumia users).

My biggest gripe (other than the power switch) is the color. Somehow, the white looks more delicate in hand and am worried about discoloration due to use or dirt. The other is, it fits my head a little loose. I could dislodge it from its perch above my head by 2-3 shakes of the head, which means a no-go for gym or exercise use.

The Grey color might be cheaper but if you are picky about things getting discolored, don't get this one!

title: Outstanding product!
text:
I received this product on Monday and was very excited. We are remote addicts because we have a whole entertainment system set up as well as wireless/WIFI situation going on in our apartment.

At first sight, the ESPN "Ultimate remote" is very sleek and sexy. My husband loves the color red, so this was a wonderful surprise for him as well. The remote also has silver edging. It isn't heavy, but it isn't a tiny remote that you can use while you are trying to go to sleep. Aesthetically... it is gorgeous and the buttons are well thought out. The layout works! There is also a joystick to navigate through the menus which is a welcome change in our household. The screen is rather large and the colors are awesome. It seems like a high end cell phone screen. One part that I rather enjoy is that the screen isn't a touch screen. Our other remote (Sima IR/RF remote) is a touch screen and I am constantly tired of cleaning the scuzzy fingertips off of the surface.

Now onto it's advertised abilities or "claims".... They aren't just claims... this baby does everything it says!!! When you open the package you are surprised to find a one page folded color booklet. I was afraid that it wasn't enough directions. That one page is more than sufficient and takes you step by step to begin setting up your new remote. That is it!! It was easy and effortless. If my 5 year old could fully read, she would have been able to work through it. Everything is on there... from setting up your Plasma/LCD to your old tube television that you would rather no one knows about LOL. You need to have a wireless connection/WIFI set up throughout your home or this remote will not be able to function to its' full capacity. The internet is quick and it does deliver the scores, news, weather, gossip and even a bit of AMAZON shopping! That bought it for me! You can even message.... everything is brought to you from the Click365 network. You do not need a PC to set up your remote. You truly remove it from its box and begin (well you do have to charge it further, per their instructions; even though ours was fully charged).

A function that we fell in love with is the fact that you can channel surf off of your remote without actually turning on your television. You don't actually watch the channels, but you get to see the whole guide and what is currently on. Now that is an amazing feat! Another cool discovery was in the middle of the night, I went into the kitchen and the remote was in it's cradle charging.... all of a sudden the screen lit up. There is motion detection on this bad boy! We can't seem to find a button to turn off the remote though. That isn't an issue because finally we are dealing with a remote that doesn't need standard AA/AAA batteries. It runs off a rechargable Lithium battery which you can charge in its provided dock or from its cord.

There is so much that this thing does that I could go on for days... It can control up to 18 devices in multiple rooms. It found most our devices quickly, we did have an issue with a Sony receiver ( we always do); but eventually found it. IT is a learning remote that can never become obsolete. It can always learn your new devices in the future so you don't have to worry about the cost of this remote because it will pay for itself in the future. You will not have to upgrade.

Now onto the bad... so far it has frozen up 3 times and it had to be rebooted. Maybe it is just my device because I haven't read anyone else complaining of the same issue.

Finally, the reason it isn't a five-star is a major one in our household; this remote isn't IR/RF. What that means is that it cannot control your devices through the walls or floors. We have our system set up in a closet, so that we didn't need to have a hundred things laying around our living room. WE always go for IR/RF remotes so that our devices can be controlled throughout the home without having to actually point at the actual device that we are trying to control. This remote doesn't do that! With everything great on this thing... why couldn't they have implemented that great little function??? WE REALLY LOVE this remote but don't know how we will use it since everything in the living room is stashed away. Hopefully, we will be able to find some sort of extenders that will enable us to use the remote the same as our SIMA remote that I had previously reviewed.

Any suggestions??? WONDERFUL product that you should buy today... I don't know how we lived without it before.... just wish it had IR/RF capability.

text:
Yep... that is what Mom kept on repeating to her kids while wearing these around the house. I have never tried "noise isolating" earphones before so this was truly an experience for me! At first glance... they look simple and I didn't understand what would warrant the MSRP, but after actually trying them out they have made a believer out of me and future buyer (unfortunately because they aren't cheap). I am not an audiophile in any sense... SAHM of 3 kiddies that likes to listen to music while working around the home or working out on the bike. At times I can't blast the surround sound because of the kiddies doing their homework & neighbor's newborn. These came at a perfect time in my life and I patiently waited for their arrival.

Upon arrival, I discovered that there were other sized oval ear-tips provided. This is a great perk considering there are 5 different pairs of ears in our home. When I initially put them in my ear, they were in the wrong ears and I couldn't seem to find the little L & R labels (they are labeled on the underside). Even though they were in the wrong ears they still felt ok (like typical cheap ear phones) but there was any noise "cancellation". I decided to switch them and they fit like a glove!! They sort of suction and when they are in place properly, I could not hear ONE THING! It was funny being able to watch the children speak but not actually hear what they were saying. It was a silent outside world... which ended up feeling a tad claustrophobic. Even speaking to myself I felt the low rumble of my voice and it felt so far and away. If you are looking for peace and quiet, then these will fit that bill. Studying, working out or any scenario where you would like to get in the zone- these accomplish that feat.

The sound is great... at least for my untrained ear.

When removing, I felt the suction feeling that I described above. With other ear phones my ears and the piece of cartilage that holds them into place would have a dull ache. I am happily reporting that with this pair you do not feel anything just the beats of the music & adrenaline rush that it provides.

The bad: You CAN'T HEAR ANYTHING! Right above I just praised how wonderfully the "noise isolation" function performed; it is very much like a double-edged sword. I love that I can't hear anything, but it is also scary to realize that I indeed cannot hear anything. You should not wear these while jogging outside or even walking alone. You will not be able to hear a horn honking or anyone screaming. I had my husband try them out and he too could not hear anything. Another bad point which is probably user error was the fact that my ears/drums hurt afterward. I didn't think I had them loud, but after removing, my ears were hurting a bit. Maybe the isolation truly makes it a quiet world with everything amplified. I don't know...

Highly recommend because they are comfortable, sound great and block out the outside world. If you need a quiet environment then I highly suggest this brand with the understanding that they should be used in certain situations where you do not need to be as alert. Don't forget how silly you look rocking out to a song and singing LOUDLY.... true story!

title: Fluctuating Brightness galore!
text:
One star because it does suffer from Brightness pops and fluctuating brightness! IF it wasn't for the fluctuating brightness then this television would have been rated 5 stars. To anyone reading and considering purchasing any television where consumers complain that there is 'brightness pops' or fluctuating brightness, then I implore you to RUN in the other direction and choose their competitor.

Samsung does not stand behind this product and has still to acknowledge that this is an issue by rolling out an update like Panasonic had done to remedy the same issue. Another slap in the face is the fact that in the SAMSUNG SMART TV apps, Amazon is not included nor supported. Their reasoning is that the televisions in the D line are not recommended for to be able to show the content properly. They think that these expensive televisions cannot stream Amazon videos! What a sham! The Samsung Smart apps are a joke and slow down everything. There is nothing intelligent about the interface.

Aside from the 'pops'... the picture is beautiful/stunning. The colors are amazing and I can begrudgingly agree with my family that the 3D looks great as well. I personally hate 3D and always get a headache from it; but I will admit it is a cool fad. The television was not purchased for the 3D, that was just an afterthought. There have not been any burn issues and we did not bother 'conditioning' the plasma or calibrating. We have owned it since October 2011. We previously owned a Panasonic plasma commercial model from 2004; that television is still beautiful and has been moved to the bedroom.

If you are not sure what fluctuating brightness is... when you are watching a program and the scene changes from dark to bright, or from white background to a darker one, you will notice something like a flashlight popping. Another way to describe it is that the screen dims and brightens to adjust to the new color. At times it is barely noticeable; then there are times that the scenes keep on shifting and you feel as if you are going POP POP POP POP and you scream: DAMN BRIGHTNESS POP! (True story!) In our home after the initial denial that we did indeed notice POPS, then came the depression. Now we are at a point where we announce it to the whole house and mess up everyone's viewing pleasure. Many times I will announce 'POPS' in the middle of a scene and my Husband will become upset because he didn't notice them until I said something. This leads me to believe that EVERYONE'S model is suffering from the same issue but some individuals are more sensitive to it then others. Then again... maybe those people are just in denial because it would be so sad to think that we all spent thousands upon thousands on a product that seems to have a defect.

Does it buzz? Well, for me it never did; until the day I walked right in front of it and couldn't figure out what that annoying buzzing was. I swore it was every other gadget. My husband confirmed by stating that he had heard it buzzing one night when he was napping on the couch and the volume was low. The way around this is to jack up your volume LOL.

So.. it buzzes and it pops and is not a cereal unfortunately. If it wasn't for those defects then it would be perfect. I truly believed that after reading countless reviews and researching on the AVS Forums that maybe I would be a lucky one that received a 'newer' model. NO... there are not lucky ones... just your ability to realize that there is truly something wrong with your television and not your eyes when the brightness fluctuates quickly.

Do NOT RECOMMEND!! Please do not purchase. Samsung will not release an update. IF you would like to research the brightness pops phenomenon, then read all the reviews on Amazon, the internet, page dedicated on Facebook and finally AVS forums. You will regret it the moment you notice that first pop and hear that first buzz.
