title: Brutally fast but will need upgraded!
text:
This laptop is a fantastic value for the price and is brutally fast at 1080p. But going into this you must know that unless you're content with just playing a couple of games, and most people are not, then you're going to need to dole out a bit more money, $100-200, in order to add an additional SSD to the laptop, which it does have a space for a secondary SSD. Now you could go with a 1Gb but I'd really recommend you save up and go for a 2Gb as you will find 1Gb runs out fast. Also the memory at 8Gb is likely borderline in need of an upgrade as well.

But, knowing that going on and you will love this laptop. Setup is seriously easy and fast, I was done just by using my voice to command Cortana to setup Windows 10 in about 10 minutes. There is no bloatware that I found (although if memory serves there was some sort of virus protector trial period which I promptly removed, and I'd recommend you do the same, Windows defender will do you just fine without any subscription fees).

The first game I tested I did run into issues and was unable to get it resolved and that was Doom eternal. It indicated that there was not enough memory in the graphics card to run the game. I thought this was due to it using the integrated (ie slow) graphics card rather than the discrete Nvidia 1650 (which is what you want to use) but even after disabling it I was unable to get Doom to run. A cursory glance around the internet appears that this is an issue with several brands of laptops so I moved on to something else: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020.

Well if you know much about games it is not an easy game to run so if you can run Microsoft Flight Simulator well then you know you've got a keeper. I'm happy to say this game ran it without any issue at all and ran it extremely well. I also was able to run several other modern games without any issue at all and it seems like Doom was just a weird outlying anomaly.

Do be sure when you're running games that you are using your Nvidia card though!

Now, I've been running this laptop for about a week or so and never had it crash once. It boots up super fast into Windows 10, about 11 seconds it seems and is just a joy to use. And I am also driving a 1440p Acer Predator monitor now and games run just great at 1440p I should note. This machine is just a wonderfully light, fast game machine.

All in all this is a fantastic value and appropriately priced. Keep in mind you won't fit a lot of games on the standard 256Gb hard drive and you also should know you don't want to fill up the hard drive completely as Windows 10 will need space in order to install updates and such. Adding an internal hard drive is fairly easy but if that scares you then you can always use an external and this laptop has the ports for it, but know externals do take a slight hit on speed.

I love this machine and plan to use it as my primary machine when I am on the road. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

title: Dinu
text:
I moved to this camera body from a Canon EOS 10D model 2003. That camera served me very well throughout the years, but it had some limitations.
In all aspects this new EOS 50D camera seriously outperforms the other camera on a large margin.
As a sign of excellently built and sturdiness, this camera with a Tokina 12-24 ATX Pro zoom lens and a Speedlight EX-430 flash attached, recently fell on the wood floor of my house, from my tripod. Tripod was faulty and the head separated from the tripod body. I was horrified. To my amazement, nothing happened. I do not know how lucky I was, but I won't ever play with my luck again. I bought a new tripod since.
LCD display: 3" diagonal, bright, high res. LCD display, easily viewable indoors and out, a pleasure to use, compared to the small 1.8" diagonal LCD display of the EOS 10D.
Exposure meter: much more accurate, compared to the older camera. Canon cameras, over the years typically underexposed, when a wide angle lens was used. This one seems to have overcome that issue. Extremely accurate exposures on evaluative metering, with or without flash.
Color accuracy: an improvement over EOS 10D. in order to achieve vibrant, true to life colors, I used to crank the saturation control on the older camera to the max. This one seems to achieve true and vibrant colors on "standard" pic mode... however this "standard" pic mode, also cranks saturation to high :)
Pictures noise: very low noise on high ASA/ISO setting. I read several reviews stating that compared to EOS 40D this camera is more noisy. I do not know the 40D much, but compared to 10D, this camera shines at high ISO settings. I used ISO 3200 and pics are very smooth. At Hi sensitivity setting (presumed ISO 6400), the noise is visually comparable to ISO 1600 settings on the older camera (on a 23"LCD computer screen). I did not try yet the 12800 (Hi-2) setting, but I have heard it is noisy.
Resolution: 15 mpixels... WOW! Images are razor sharp and extremely detailed. I did quite well with 6 mpixels on EOS 10D but this is amazing.
Flash card read/write speed: I am using Sandisk Extreme III flash memory cards. It may be even better with Extreme-IV series. Transfer speed from the camera body to the PC and also using a Sandisk extreme USB 2.0 reader, extremely high. Files simply zap, even 20 MB RAW files... Amazing!
Well done Canon! I am extremely pleased with this camera. I may however be not the most demanding or critical person in reviewing this camera body.
And Amazon did a nice job with a very competitive price (for a US model camera) and by shipping and delivering in just 2 days (with special annual membership plan).
item_title: Canon EOS 50D 15.1MP Digital SLR Camera with EF-S 18-200mm f/3.5-5.6 IS Standard Zoom Lens

title: Good quality Tamron Pro, 2X tele converter
text:
Its fine. But I need to explain one important fact. Most DSLR's will not auto focus with a lens say smaller than F8 (combined aperture). But for 150-600 mm lens which is about f5.6-6.3, using a 2X tele-converter will render a f11.2-12.6 effective aperture, which is below the camera's auto focus capabilities. That is why when shooting with a long tele zoom, and with this 2X tele-converter, the focusing (not the auto-exposure) needs to be set to manual (focus the lens manually).
Exposure may be a different issue, but in most instances, the exposure meter would take into consideration the darker resulting image and would compensate accordingly. However the focus is important. This is not very well understood among photographers.

title: Good quality, sound, and reasonably priced, but output jack got deffective
text:
I received the product a few days ago. Set it up and installed into my car's 12V power outlet. It turned on, I tuned it to an unoccupied FM radio station, and I Bluetooth paired it with my cellphone. The pairing went foolproof. A voice message notified me device paired successfully.
I went on and played songs from Youtube. Sound was good, reception was clear, quality of the audio depending on the quality of the source. All is good, I am happy with the product, but it has a culprit. I did not succeed to set it to play an external audio source, via it's 3.5 mm coaxial port, with the supplied cable. Cable is fine, because I used it to connect my ipod directly to the car radio's aux socket. Source plays fine. However thru this device aux port, there is no sound. when inserted, the sound switches from the Bluetooth to silence...
I contacted amazon technical support. They tried to debug it. After doing their research they deemed the device faulty, and they are sending me new replacement item. But here is the issue... when I play the Bluetooth music thru the device, and I hook the cable from the aux port to the radio aux port, it plays loudly and clear !! So the device may not be defective at all... but here is the question... this is a two way input/output port. It should auto detect the audio source and play it thru the radio FM. But it works as an output, but not as an input. I will get the new item and see if the problem is fixed... if it is the same, then there is a trick that it is not noted in the manual, and I do not know what it is.
Otherwise device is fine.
Edit: I contacted the vendor, Leextek which were kind and very prompt. But they say the "aux" port only works as an input when it receive digital music in formats like mp3, wav, etc. This sounds to me absurd, because I don't know of any audio device that outputs a digital signal, except for fiber optic outlets. But virtually all music player output an analogue signal, thru their audio outlet. So this accepts digital input only, while as output it delivers analogue audio?
This seems absurd...

Edit: Got my replacement unit, that worked like the 1st one. No input via the aux outlet. Product worked well via the aux outlet and via FM. Less that 2 months in service and the output jack started to malfunction. I removed the unit and disassembled it. The output jack un-soldered/broke, and was contacting only one point. Upon examining it, it broke completely. There was no way to solder it, because two out of 4 contacts came off with the flexible cirvuit board, it was soldered to. I reassembled the unit (without the jack) and now it works via the FM radio and Bluetooth only.
The unit was static and was not exposed to vibrations of any kind. I regret to say this is poor, cheap manufacturing and I won't buy this unit again.

Edit: So to make things clear.. the 2nd unit they sent as repplacement, works well on bluetotth and also output good and clear signal from the coaxial jack. I could not use it to accept a sourse input. After a certain port, the coaxial port broke and was unusable. Uppn opening the device, I found out it had 4 contacts, but only two were soldered, and it broke. I continued to use it as a bluetooth only, until I visited walmart and incidentally I found there a similar product. For $29 something. But this also had a USB port for USB sources. I brought it home, installed it and works like a charm. Not to mention that the coaxial port works as output, and also accepts audio input. I am very pleased with the new bluetootk device. The model is ROAV F3. Works as advertised and very well. The Summind product is propably defective at the production line (they forgot to solder 2 pins on the coaxial jacket) For your information.
I reduced the number of stars to only 2. Product is still usable, as bluetooth.

These mechanical parts are manufactured to very tight tolerances. Allowing perfect fit between a Canon or Canon compatible EF or EF-S lens, and the mount on the R camera. Besides there are the contacts, interfacing the contacts on the lens in use, and the matching contacts inside the M50 or R camera mount. These are electric contacts. Allowing full compatibilty, I dont accept other viewers who said this does not provide a good fit. That is not true. The image stabilization is built into the lens itself or camera body, and not into the adapter.
This adapter is a very simple thing. It's just an interface. A ring. But it also makes the lens be mounted at a distance, from an original R lens. This creates a different angle of view. That is all. I will report when I get the camera body and this adapter. But I am not expecting any compatibility problems. With an 1.4X or 2X cconverter, it is different. These are optical converters, including lenses, besides contacts. They impact both the angle of view and the max aperture value.
However aoutofocus capabilities depend very much on ambient light, the maz lens aperture, and the capability of the camera auto focusimg sensor. They dont depend on a mecahnical ring that tramsits the electrical signals. and does not impact the apreture, or signal transmission between the lens and the camera micro processor. Please see these clarifications so you can understand. Thanks.

title: Glorified AC1900 AP in disguise..
text:
I purchased this router mainly for the out of box open source firmware support and to see if it improved throughputs and range over my Asus RT-AC68U in my 3000sqft two story home. I have 30+ 2.4/5GHz devices in my home and plenty of neighboring AP's to contend with so performance can get challenging at times specifically with band selection. My old Asus AP running Tomato has done a great job over the years but coverage deteriorates quickly depending on band congestion.

After reading some reviews on this Linksys, I knew this wasn't going to blow out performance over my Asus but did expect to see improvements for overall throughputs and coverage. Long story short, real world (not sitting next to the AP) performance improvements were minor and for my 2.4GHz devices (PS4, etc) were actually worse then my Asus.

The Pros:
Well built piece of hardware
Readily available open source firmware, tested using OEM and DD-WRT
5GHz throughputs great when next to the AP

The Cons:
Setup process is rather annoying. Requires internet connection (no true offline setup). Linksys insists on creating an online smart account as they do a pretty good job trying to hide their "local setup" option.
2.4GHz performance severely lacking
No improvements on overall range compared to my AC1900

In closing, this is not worth $250 price point considering performance is on par with typical AC1900 AP's for half the cost. If your looking for real world performance and range improvements check out the Netgear Orbi.

title: Tired of poor performing Wireless? Get the Orbi, you won't be disappointed..
text:
I didn't purchase the Orbi on Amazon but did at my local Best Buy to leverage my award points. This is by far the best performing wireless system period.. specifically in regards to coverage, throughputs and competing neighboring WiFi AP's.

I have a 3000sqft two story home with roughly 35 devices and my Comcast modem located at the far end of the house. Furthermore I live in an area with lots of competing AP's, you know what I mean.. your WiFi selection list has more options than McDonalds.

Now with a single AP (no flaky repeaters) I can get decent coverage if my AP happens to be on a non congested channel but regardless throughputs severely lack at the farthest end. Of course this is highly dependent on channel congestion from neighboring WiFi and that always changes throughout the day.

My goto router for the last 3 years has been an Asus RT-AC68U (AC1900) AP running Tomato firmware. It's done a decent job providing wireless service but theres certainly room for improvement.

I have tried a number of different wireless systems which all seem to look like they were props from Star Trek to the not so consumer friendly systems such as the Ubiquiti's UniFi. One thing I have found common on all the current WiFi systems is the lack of improvement for the 2.4GHz band which is important for me. I have a number 2.4GHz devices (home automation, PS4's) scattered at the far reaches of my home. Yes some systems were better in certain areas but lacked in others so couldn't justify the cost on a mediocre upgrade until now.

Hello Orbi, where have you been all my life!? This system is just..awesome. My throughputs at the far reaches of my home are just as good as if I was standing 20ft unobstructed from my previous Asus with zero tinkering with radio settings or channel selections.

Now what really separates this from other mesh systems is the dedicated private band between the AP and the satellite. Its literally like taking a single AP antenna's on an extension cord placed at the other half of your house. Not like a repeater so no band sharing, contention, etc.

The only downside to this awesome system is it's crummy outdated interface. Thankfully it by no means hampers performance but yes it sucks and needs a facelift. I contemplated deducting a star but the performance is just too good.

Now is it worth the price? Heck yes!

Minor issues aside, my wife is thoroughly enjoying her Kindle Touch and the $100 price is frosting on the cake.

title: Excellent Nannycam but . . .
text:
I’m a caregiver who needs to keep continual surveillance over a homebound, wheel-chair confined patient. This camera is perfect.

For $45.99, the 1080p resolution and the infra-red capabilities are spectacular. The ability to view up to four cameras individually or on a quadrant multi-view screen on iPhones and iPads is awesome. These two features alone are worth the price.

This is a stand-alone surveillance system that does not send recordings to outside servers or security companies. This is a very good and important feature to assure in-home privacy.

One good feature to add is the ability to automatically rotate the camera view so regardless which way you horizontally hold the iPhone or iPad, the camera view is right-side-up.

My one disappointment is that there is no WansView app on Apple’s App Store site to download for use with my Mac desktop. WansView offers a workaround but I’m skeptical to download it right now. I plan to contact Apple for their recommendation.

There are a few advertised features that are weak and taints the company’s credibility. The ability of sending and receiving voice communication with people near the camera is underdeveloped and almost of no use. The Alarm notification feature is also underdeveloped. A few onscreen icons were difficult to work with (remote panning) and another icon needs clarification of purpose (mirror imaging). Thanks to Bella, from WansView online support team who acknowledged that some features are still need improvements, my confidence in WansView was restored.

Would I recommend this Wansview camera? Absolutely! As stated in the first paragraph, the 1080p resolution, the night-vision ability, and the multi-view screen option by themselves is worth the $45.99 price. (WansView, if you read this, maybe you could offer a four-camera package deal.)

title: Great GPS for the money
text:
The Garmin 765 is probably the best GPS in this price range. Maps are very accurate, very few lock ups with the software and lots of features like lane assist, bluetooth, traffic, etc. There are a few things that I wish it had but none of them are deal breakers. For example, a mute option from the maps screen would be nice, instead you have to go back to the main menu, enter the volume option and then mute, then go all the way back to the map screen. Same thing for volume adjust. You cannot change the map from 3D to Point North from the map screen either, a little option I liked in my previous GPS. The option to display Direction, ETA, miles to destination, time to destination, current time, are all nice to have. The only problem is that you can only display one at a time. It would be nice to be able to display at least two of these in the main map screen.
These are all minor things that would be nice but I am sure that to many people none of these things would matter. I personally love this GPS and would recommend it. I own a bluetooth device and find that it works better than the built in bluetooth in the GPS. If you already own a bluetooth earpiece, the 755 will be the best bet.

title: My 2nd diaster in upgrading my Netgear wndr3400 with another Netgear product...
text:
This is the second Netgear router that I've tried so as to replace my aging Netgear WNDR3400 N router. I had high hopes for this one, but apparently Netgear is on the wrong hardware/software track!
This router would not play well with android devices, limiting internet access to 10-15% of what my internet provider serves. I had near wired speeds to my windows computers on the wireless 5G, and pretty good speeds on 2G to those same windows machines. LAN (Network) speeds were very nice for both android and windows devices, but I was unable to solve the android creeping, glacial internet speeds with any available solution.
I didn't like it, but had decided to live with it so as to have the signal strength improvement in my home and to capture the 5G AC benefits as well. Today, after 3 days of working with this thing, I woke up to find the the wireless transmitter on the 2G band was cycling on and off. Resetting it stabilized it for a little while, but it started the cycling business again. This was tearing up my network for the devices that needed 2G, rendering them useless! That was the final straw, and this thing is going back to Amazon!
Note that I had also tried the 1900 Nighthawk router as well. That was another nightmare...not so much nighthawk, I'll tell you. My impression is that Netgear's implementation of the beam-forming technology, or the AC 1300 transmission rates, or both is just not doing the job! Neither of these routers were able to serve up internet speeds above a crawl to the various mixes of wireless devices. LAN rates and signal strength on both were very nice improvements over my old N router's 300 mbps, but neither has been able to deliver consistent, lasting, speedy internet connections!?! What happened?
Other pros: The speed of the USB 3.0 HDD access through the router, and the smooth functioning of the DLNA server for the drive's content. I wish that the whole router worked as well! If a router can't route the internet signal, what good is it?
The WNDR3400 is a workhorse that is dead cold reliable, and extremely fast on every connected device that I own(android included). I expected so much more from Netgear, but I am done!

WHAT HAS HAPPENED TO DLINK?

So, Amazon's great customer service functioned once again. They got me a new router to replace the nightmare below, and they did it quickly. After it arrived, here is the rest of the story on the brand new replacement:

NEW REPLACEMENT ROUTER:

Glacially SLOW android connect speeds, even with router dumbed down to just basic router functions (no Smartconnect, no QoS priorities selected (not able to turn it off!!), no USB sharing, and firewall functions both on and off with no effect).

This required yet another factory reset and a manual reload!!

UPDATE FOR PARAGRAPH ABOVE: DLink engineer indicated that if the QoS boxes are NOT populated, QoS is off; even though there is no positive switch in the firmware to verify that. Also, if you reload the config file that you've saved, THE FIRMWARE DUMPS YOUR PASSWORD BY DEFAULT! When you see the password box, just hit enter to start the firmware! This is not documented at all!!!

LAN speeds and signal strength profile match the failed router, but internet speeds remain suppressed. It required 4 full system resets to get even the wired speeds up to the provider's purchased speeds. That means reset the wired computer, the router and the cable modem. Finally, the speeds came up from 1/6 of purchased to full speed on a WIRED COMPUTER! Now, at least, the windows machines, both wired and wireless, are running at or near internet provider speed. Ancillary air flowed over the router, temps declined about 1C and the 2.4G radio came back on. By then, I'd already set an old 2.4G router as an AP, so had the function somewhat restored. Now I have 2 distinct 2.4g signals. Transmitter temp is now 39C, and the signal has been steady for hours.
It is illuminating to note that this router had an overtemp failure of the same transmitter when it was about 3 weeks old. I added a usb fan blowing up through the router, and it has remained trouble free till now. HEAT is the enemy, and the 3200 doesn't provide for that in its design!!
I am still going to replace it with the 5300 since I need a dead cold reliable router....But I don't like it one bit!!!

The wonderful difference is that my android devices are getting full speed (58-60 mbps) downloads from my Comcast provider. Since I receive 60 mbps from the wired desktop (rated speed for my service), that is a HUGE improvement for the android OS devices-READ 80% BETTER! Note that this is with QoS active. That leaves competing devices sucking wind! This ASUS QoS really works, and that is very refreshing!

I really like the firmware interface, but you should know that you'll have to do manual updates to get the latest firmware...AND YOU DO WANT IT!! It is really slick, and should address even complex situations requiring specific configurations.

I initially tried N only, but I lost use of my wireless Canon printer. I then tried Legacy, and that restored the printer access. I figured, why not try Auto again; but dump the b/g. It worked!!

Finally heard from ASUS, but the info provided didn't help AT ALL! Here's what they suggested:
1. Please login to your Router page.
2. Select the USB Application Tab under General.
3. Then you can select Network Place (Samba) Share / Cloud Disk.
4. Enable the Share option.
5. Under the USB Application- ftp share Enable FTP.

While dinking around trying to get things working, I figured it out. First, to really access the tabs that are mentioned with the latest firmware, just select 'Media Services and Servers' under the General/USB main tabs. Select the SAMBA tab, and 'Enable Share.' DO NOT select the ftp tab unless you have another goal than SAMBA LAN only file sharing. Just temporarily, select 'Allow guest login.' In the lower window, add a file share account (NOT admin) by hitting the '+' symbol on the left of the lower pane. Give it a name and password. Add a file/folder (or several, if needed) using the '+' key on the right side of the lower window. Ensure that they are read/write folder permissions. Using Windows Explorer, go to your newly created folders and put your data into those containers. Disable guest access. Refresh Explorer, reselect the folders that you've just populated, and login in using the account and password you just made. Your files will be there waiting!
Note that I also tested the transfer rate through the router with some really large files. I got 19-23 mbs, which is about 45% of what I'd expect with the drive hooked directly to my computer's USB 3.O ports.

title: Here's the nuts and bolts to make this card sing!!
text:
Be sure and download the latest driver/capture software and manuals from the Aver site. I didn't even take the cd out of the package, as the material was dated. Here's the files you'll need:
C027_MCS.1.7.9.91.15030401_Drv_1.54.x.82_150317.exe
QuickGuide.pdf
UM_EN_C027_AVerMediaDarkCrystal HD Capture Pro_MCS1.7.9_121204_ww.pdf
Also, know that you'll need to reboot after running the .exe to install the driver and etc.

Once you've got it installed, it works really well on non-capture protected (hdcp) hdmi input, and all the non-hdmi modes work as well. If you are trying to capture any hdcp hdmi, you'll need a splitter/stripper, since the software WILL NOT record such material for time shifted viewing. A device such as the 'CKITZE BG-520 HDMI 1x2 3D splitter v1.3 HDCP 2 ports switcher' will solve the problem. That is available on Amazon, and is very useful.

Another job that you'll have to do is to segregate and mark the 9 wire bundle--ie. composite/S video bundle (4 leads with 2 channel sound), the 2 audio leads (also used with component recordings), and the component video RGB leads (3 leads). Trying to do it standing on your head and working behind the computer is not so fun, so get them all split out before you install them. Further, be sure that you get the multi-lead DONGLE into the proper hdmi slot on the card!! The HDMI plug closest to the motherboard is the one for the dongle ONLY!!

The capture software is really well done, but remains less GUI like than some will appreciate. It does, however, work like a charm! Read the manual if you hit any road blocks, and you'll be fine. The unattended/scheduled mode is really useful for a set it and forget it job. Such things as digitizing old Hi8 tapes takes 2 hours per tape in real time. You are able to set up the 2 hour time blocks and walk away. Cool!

Finally, as to settings. H 264, which is MP4, is a universal recording format, but that is something one needs to research and select. 480 by 720 is fine for Hi8 S video, while component settings will vary depending on quality of input from your device. Just know that high quality video there will provide all the card is able to do in terms of quality. Of course, most of us will select the very highest quality for all our hdmi recordings. Be sure that you use your largest disc for the working space/video storage, unless your default C: drive is a monster. These are really large files! Just be sure that you do this piece of work before your first recording.

title: Needs a couple of tweaks, but what a great design!!
text:
The only additions that we made to the delivered product were star washers...several needed to hold tilt and level. With those added, my 83 pound tv is rock solid in the mount!
As to the mounting process itself, I encountered a local problem with my particular wall. My studs were on 16" spacing--well enough. However, the wall center was 1" from a stud!! That meant that this mount's 24" spacing (nor the other mount made by them for a 24" spacing stud pattern) would do. The tv was entirely too heavy to mount on a single stud, so I had to fabricate a 2X4 'bridge' for the mount to be attached to. It was cut at 34" on 2 boards fastened to the wall with 3 lag bolts in 3 studs on each of the boards, using the template for spacing. Don't forget to countersink the bolt heads on the center lag bolt to avoid mounting problems. I also used a fender washer on the outer 2 bolts to give even more stability to the 2X4's.
It is rock solid, and solved a problem that was perplexing at first!

title: Great Laptop!
text:
UPDATE!!
I've now owned the laptop for some time. The problems outlined below required a full default restore and reinstall of ALL programs. That always was/is a pain. All drivers were updated after the restore operation and before programs were put in place. Plus, research revealed how to turn audio and visual alerts of caps lock and num lock key changes on (See Accessibility options). That really helped make the absence of the lights a non-issue.
After the latest updates, the fingerprint reader is working very well. Occasionally, one must try several times, often with a sliding motion to get it to read; however, it reads every time!
At this point (and NO THANKS to Acer!!), this is the laptop that I wanted when I purchased it! Acer should be proactive in highlighting these items so as to save their customers hassle. Hopefully, this will help others to get the machine doing what is expected...
_____________________________________________________________________________________________________

After just less than 3 months of ownership, the camera is inoperative. It shows the green 'on' light for a second (when activated), then fails with the error, 'media capture failed event.' It seems to be hardware, since every recommended software fix fails.
Additionally, after the latest update to Windows 10, it nows fails with the 'BSOD (bluescreen of death)' failure. SFC /scannow (with the prerequisite DISM /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth) and CHKDSK FAIL to fix the error.

Star Addition...the fingerprint reader is running reliably after the last software update!!
Now, if there was only a way to see caps lock status...it would be perfect.

So, this laptop is an astounding value! The screen is bright, battery life is unexpectedly long (follow the battery break in instructions!), and the ergonomics of the device are very nice indeed!
Eval of Speed under stress-this baby flies! The web access is faster than my provider service, and access to my NAS screams! Boot up and recovery from sleep are really fast, computing tasks sing along, and any video playback is flawless.
The SSD is a little small for my needs, but doubling it was easy, using the provided cage and connector (Note that I stayed with another generic SSD so as to preserve the overall speed). So far, the 8 GB of provided RAM have been sufficient. Even complex multi-operations don't get above 62% of available RAM.

The bad? There is no CAPS or NUM LOCK light! This is a minor, but needless shortcoming. The FINGERPRINT READER by Elan--Wow it is BAD! When it works, it is a dream. Problem is, multiple times a day, the driver gets bent and it just stops. One can access Device Manager and uninstall/reinstall. Sometimes, that will fix it. Other times, the driver will stay dead for a couple of days, then restart. Nothing mechanical here, just the driver is notorious for this behavior across several brands. I took off one star for these two issues.
If Acer would fix the reader, I'd up it to 5 with no reservations, since the Caps/Num Lock thing is so minor.
ACER, DO YOU HEAR YOUR CUSTOMERS??

title: Body sensors and battery life broke the deal!
text:
So, this headline, 'Body sensors and battery life broke the deal!' says it all!

THE BAD:
-Blood Pressure was an advertised feature--it wasn't working on USA versions of the watch, per the FDA. That tells me that the function is a non-starter, and Samsung can't make a major sales point workable!
-ECG measurements were highly erratic and did not match other medical sensors.
-Battery life was a constant area of concern, especially when on the go all day and away from the 'special' charger.

THE GOOD:
-Sleep monitor worked very well, though with the noted deficiencies, I am now not certain what that signifies. Snore monitor was perfect!
-PO2 sensor was always within 1 %.
-I liked the vib when a phone call came in, and the fact that it could be answered or rejected from the watch without diving for the phone!
-Viewing alerts from the watch was also a nice touch.
-I loved the bezel for moving through the various functions of the watch. This is a great feature!
-I liked the customizable watch faces, but longed for one that had aviator/navigation timekeeping functions forward. The kid stuff faces were a waste for this old dog...
-After reading a number of reviews, I DID NOT test the waterproof ability of the watch. The horror stories convinced me that it was a very dark area.

I think that Samsung has a potential winner here, but there are several areas that need cleanup before this is a $300+ watch...at least, in my opinion. I had to return mine, albeit with some regret!

title: Great little speakers with a pleasing mid-forward sound.
text:
First let me say the 1000+ 4.5 star reviews on Amazon for the COVO-S speakers are not wrong. These are great little speakers. They provide a warm, mid-forward sound that is not harsh or fatiguing. That said, given their size you should not expect any true bass or brilliant high notes. If you don't want to read this entire review, here is my take home message - seamless integration as Atmos/surround with my Klipsch LCR, perfect for desktop setup, I love them and will be buying another set.

My set-up:
Receiver - Denon x4500h
Power Amplifier - Monolith 3 x 200W
L/R - Klipsch RP 600
C - Klipsch RC 64-iii
Sub - SVS PB-2000 Pro
Speaker wire for the Miccas - AmazonBasics 14-Gauge Audio Speaker Wire Cable - 99.9% Oxygen-Free Copper
Banana Plugs - FosPower Banana Plugs
Micca wall mounts - Jumbl SINSB7B ProGrip Ultra Stainless Steel Speaker Wall Mount Bracket

COVO-S Specs:
Impedance: 6-8 Ohms
Sensitivity: 83dB 1W/1M
Frequency Response: 90Hz-20kHz (Typical In-Room)
Dimensions: 5.1” (H) x 4.2” (W) x 5.1” (D)

As seen in the pictures, the first thing I did was A/B test the Miccas v. the RP-600’s because I already had the 600s and was curious. For stereo listening (2.1) the COVO’s are placed 7 feet apart, the internal crossover in the Denon was set to 100Hz and I connected the sub. Center imaging was well focused but there wasn’t much height or depth to the soundstage when compared to the RP600s (not a surprise). Dynamic swings were also not as in your face compared to the Klipsch but I actually really liked the COVOs relaxed demeanor. Even with the COVO’s limitations they made a wonderful pairing with the sub, and mid way through my A/B testing my wife said, “Is that sound from the little speakers? Wow!” Powered by the Denon on its own and then with the Monolith, the COVO’s sounded surprisingly good using both amps. The main difference I noticed was that in order to get the same volume from the COVOs using the Denon compared to when powered by the Monoprice amp, I needed to turn up the volume a bit more (about 4db) with the Denon. I should mention my typical listening level is 75-85db. Fidelity and dynamics were about on par when comparing playback using the Denon v. Monolith. And when pushed beyond 85db with either the Denon or the Monoprice the COVOs started to lose their composure. Given the COVOs size, sound signature and volume output, like many reviews have stated, I agree they would be great on a desk when paired with a little sub.

For me, the main purpose for buying the COVO’s was to act as front height and surround channel speakers. I have them connected to the Denon. To achieve the same level of sound as the Klipsch speakers (L/C/R) which are being powered with the Monolith, I had to increase the COVOs by +3db in the receiver. The fact that they are not timbre matched to the Klipsch L/C/R was not an issue for me as I thought they integrated well to my non-audiophile ears. And, given the alternatives for surround speakers is MUCH more than $50/pair (think $100’s more), the COVO’s are a steal at twice the price. I wall mounted them using the preinstalled 1/4 inch screw plug (see pictures).

So, if you find your use case the same as mine (home theater surround/Atmos on a budget) then buy the COVO-S, you won’t be disappointed. And if you don’t like them, return them, it’s a win win. Heck, if you're just starting your audio/HT journey and want to explore the world of budget separates v. the alternatives (I’m looking at you soundbars) then get 2 pairs of these for Front L/R and Surround L/R duties. Get a decent center channel (80% of movies comes from the center speaker anyway), and then use the COVOs for atmos as you upgrade.

I love these little speakers and will be buying another set for my rear height channels as soon as they are back in stock.

My only negative - 2 out of the 4 speakers had a loose 1/4 screw plug. I had to remove the speaker and use a socket with an extension to hold the internal bolt inside the speaker box while tightening the external nut of the wall mount with an adjustable wrench.

title: Such a deal!
text:
Bought the 8000s for $1098/pr. from Sound Distributors May 2022 to replace a pair of RP-600Ms as front L/R. They arrived on time, double boxed and in perfect condition.

First I listened to music via Bluetooth from my iPhone to my Denon AVR-4500 using Spotify. The Denon settings for 2-channel listening is as follows (Speakers set to large, SW mode LFE+Main, Crossover 40Hz).

There was an immediate, stark contrast comparing the 600s to the 8000s. The 8000s present a taller and wider soundstage. Their center image is larger and easier to achieve (due to their smaller size I found the 600s shoot a smaller beam of sound from the tweeter and therefore require more exact placement to achieve a perfect center image).

Given my space I have them set 8 feet apart and 14” from the front wall with slight toe in.

If you already have speakers from the RP line then you will know the Klipsch tweeter provides crisp clear detailed sound. I don’t find it fatiguing but I like speakers on the more forward side (especially for movies). The only difference I could hear was the 8000s tweeter has a wider dispersion and is less “beam like” which helped when listening to movies in a 3.1 configuration as sounds coming from the left and right were less localized.

I sit 8 feet away from the speakers and had no issues hearing voices/dialogue when watching movies in a 2.1 set up.

Regarding mid-range, mid-bass and low bass there is no comparison. The 8000s best the 600s in every way. But given their size and crossover tuning they should be. Mid and low base is larger than I expected, tight and controlled. Those with more space will have an easier time regulating bass output from the 8000s.

Next I added my Monolith 3x200watt amplifier into the line up. While listening to music the added power was most evident in the increased fullness and added control/articulation of the mid-range, and mid-bass/low bass. In my opinion the separate amp added an increased sense of scale to both music and movies, especially during low volume listening.

Given their reported sensitivity I think the 8000s sounded great with the Denon alone. I think you can get 90% of the way to their full potential without an external amplifier.

I will repeat what many have stated in the reviews - If you have the money and space buy the 8000s. They present music and movies with a level of detail and energy that is addicting. And given the small improvements speakers make year to year I foresee living with these speakers for a very long time, making the initial $1100 investment a bargain in the long run.

title: Wonderful sound in a small package!
text:
I was looking for a small desktop amp to power a pair of Klipsch RP 600Ms in a nearfield/desk setup. Originally I had the 600s as LR for a home theater powered by a monolith 3 channel power amp providing 200 watts to each speaker. Having never owned or even listened to a tube amp I was wary about how they would sound with such a small “low power” tube-pre-to-class-D amp.

Set Up - Macbook Pro to T20 via audio jack to RCA, then the T20 to 600s using 12AWG monolith speaker cables. I turned the system on and was prepared to be let down.

Sound - The T20 + 600s sound amazing and lack nothing. I especially love having tone controls. Yes the tone controls work and their presence really helped tame the brightness of the 600s with nearfield listening. Needless to say this little amp filled my 13” x 13” office with amazing sound, no sub required (bass heads will of course want a sub).

Speaker Hiss - If I put my ear directly to the tweeter I can hear hiss, but from even a few feet away I cannot. Simply playing music at any volume covers any hiss, so for me this is a non-issue.

Tube Rolling - On the advice of the reviews I exchanged the stock tubes for the Riverstone Audio JAN 5654W tubes. The sound quality improvement to a warm, full sound was apparent within a few minutes of listening. This warmth really helped the 600s sound more full bodied and scaled back the high top end without the use of tone controls. It was like getting a new pair of speakers for $28 bucks!

Nob Feel - All three nobs have small clicks (40 stops) built into them and they give a nice smooth satisfying click when turning them.

Bluetooth - It worked great with my iphone and ipad but I had to make sure only 1 device was active at a time otherwise the T20 would have difficulty connecting. Also, the overall volume output of the speakers and effectiveness of tone controls was a touch diminished via bluetooth (This is common when comparing volume differences with bluetooth v. direct connect).

Heat - The device itself only got warm to the touch after several hours of listening at 75-80 db. The tubes obviously get quite warm.

Closing - If you are looking to dabble in a tube preamp and have a small budget like me, I say go for the Fosi T20 + Riverstone tubes. They make for a wonderful combo. We live in amazing times where you can buy a small home audio system for less than $200 (plus speakers of course) and try it out in the comfort of your home. I highly recommend this little powerhouse!

title: Great for the price - just don't expect to always be able to read plates
text:
This is my second dash camera, the first was a mirror one (Abeo HDVR-150)that I originally loved, but I didn't like the fact of how bulky that one was and how it got in the way of the passenger's visor when down. Also I wanted one that would stay on for a period of time if unplugged. The mirror one wouldn't but this one will, I tested it last night and unfortunately it only lasted 20 minutes on a full battery then went dead. A few minutes after going dead there was an accident that happened right in front of me, I wasn't involved but was a witness and wanted to give a video but couldn't as the battery didn't last as long.

One of the issues I have with this is it does get hot when used for an extended period of time, true I had hot air blowing on the windshield but with this right next to the mirror one, same height, the mirror one was only luke warm while this seemed to be over 100F (wish I would've had my IR gun with me to accurately measure).

After receiving this one I used this one in conjunction with the mirror one for two weeks as I wanted to see a side by side comparison. Here is what I noticed, the HDR (High Dynamic Range) of this camera as it got dark did a great job of showing objects in low light as my mirror one showed black. Although during the day time it (TaoTronics cam) would darken almost too much due to bright sky, this can be resolved by aiming the camera more down to where you can see part of the dash, you still see all the road and everything needed to but this way it is picking up the majority of the ground exposure than the sky. What would be great is if you could choose your exposure area such as bottom third, center, etc.

One area this camera fails in is in the motion sensor. My mirror cam would turn on with any movement in front and would stay on as long as I was moving, this one will stop recording quite often even while moving down the freeway with cars passing me and me passing others.

Comparing video quality of the two:
TaoTronics - Great resolution and picture, license plates are mostly blown out (bright white) and therefore are harder to capture most of the time unless close. You can zoom in with it up to 4x so this helps but still if someone hits you and takes off and you can't catch up to get a good view of the plate this one will more than likely not be able to help you there except show the vehicle.

Mirror cam - Although at night it is almost impossible to see the lines on the road it is easier to make out license plates, yet with both of these cameras unless I'm behind them with my lights off I can't read a plate.

If anyone has suggestions please give them as I've even reduced exposure on my TaoTronics by -2 and turning HDR off yet still can't read plates often.

I still want to find a dash camera that can capture all plates during day and night but I fear that might be asking too much.

I will keep this review as a review in progress and keep posting every so often if I discover anything else about how to make this work better or if there is an issue with it and how customer service is about handing any issues with the item.

If you currently are looking at a dash camera or have one, I highly recommend once a month you take the card out and view it on the computer, this is not watching the whole thing but starting at the very last few seconds of every file to ensure when the next one starts that a file hasn't been skipped as this is your warning sign the unit might not record an accident and might be time to look for a new unit or file a warranty claim if still within the time limit.

I'm not a fan of how much wider these are then the A118. I don't take mine out as assuming goes for most people, but the value of these can make it a target for theft so having a sleeker design is better to be less conspicuous - I though wouldn't mind trying it again but I purchased this on the Amazon Prime Day 2016 deal but since I had to return it I couldn't get the deal again so I haven't purchased another yet. title: A Monsterously Powerful GPU
text:
I purchased the Founders Edition partly because it was momentarily available from Amazon itself (at MSRP) and because I prefer a blower cooler and the FE is likely the best blower style cooler of them all. There are many, many reviews online of this GPU already so I don't need to elaborate on it too much. Coming from an AMD Radeon HD 7000 series, GCN 1.0, mid-range GPU I laughed when I first cranked up this card. It's obscenely powerful by comparison. It even stays cooler, and doesn't use much more power than my old AMD card when playing the same games. This is a very efficient card considering its compute capacity. I've always bought AMD, and I'm still secretly rooting for the underdog, but I couldn't deny the performance of the GTX 1080.

At stock settings the card runs about 69C-70C (stock fan curve) in taxing games such as The Witcher 3 (everything on ultra, @1440) so there is definitely still some thermal overhead before you hit the limit (84C for me). I haven't played with OC'ing too much yet but 1900 boost clock should be doable for most people. You really don't need to OC this beast anyway, unless you're trying to set records. Just enjoy the raw performance straight out of the box. I don't do any GPGPU stuff or CUDA computing so I can't speak to it capabilities there, but applications like PS CS6 are able to utilize all available 8gb of vram.

I also purchased this card with the anticipation that in a year or two I may get in to VR gaming. I am waiting to see how the market matures before committing to a VR platform, but no matter what, this card will deliver.

Paired with a solid CPU, such as an Intel i5, i7, or Xeon, or an AMD 8 core FX series you will have great results. Any less than this and your games may be CPU limited and you won't reap all the benefits of this GPU. Though I doubt anyone purchasing a GPU in this price range is running a Pentium or i3.

The Founders Edition is a great card in my small form factor set up. If you have a large tower you'll probably prefer one of the other cooler designs for even greater OC potential. If you're in the market for a high end GPU, don't hesitate, just purchase this beast, you won't be disappointed.

title: Good but not great
text:
The Logitech K830 accomplishes what it aims to do, bring keyboard and mouse control to the couch in a single device. However having used other Logitech devices I have to say I was a little disappointed by the fit and finish of this particular keyboard. I was hoping the K830 would be just like the K810 with a trackpad, unfortunately this is not the case. The K830 connects via bluetooth or 2.4ghz via Logitech's proprietary Unifying USB receiver. I use bluetooth, but if you don't have bluetooth, you can use the usb dongle. I don't use this for gaming so I can't speak to it's performance for that. I use the [[ASIN:B0041RR0TW Logitech Gamepad F710]] for casual gaming.

I'll review the keyboard and touchpad separately.

The Keyboard:
Previously I was using the [[ASIN:B0099SMFVQ Logitech K810 Bluetooth Illuminated Wireless Keyboard for PCs, Tablets, Smartphones - Black]] and [[ASIN:B00DR8LA6U Logitech Ultrathin Touch Mouse T630 for Windows]] in the living room which using a regular mouse in the living room is not ideal. However, the build quality of these two devices is top notch, they absolutely changed my opinion of Logitech. The K810 as a keyboard is far superior to the keyboard of the K830. The backlight of the K810 responds to touch and proximity, as in, if you just get close to the keyboard it lights up. This product, the K830, however, does not. You must touch the touchpad or press a key to light up the backlight which essentially makes the backlight worthless as you have to click the mouse or random keys just to see critical buttons like pause/play, volume, mute. Also the K830 doesn't remember it's backlight level and reverts to the lowest setting every time you activate the backlight. Which is one reason I returned my first K830, as the backlight at it's lowest level caused the keyboard to emit inverter/coil whine that was positively unbearable. The second K830 produces a slight whine but it's not obtrusive. As for the quality of the light, it is nice, white and even. The light only illuminates the printed letter of each key. It does NOT illuminate around the edges of the keys like most backlights. Also, the Function Keys only illuminate their "alternate" function (pause, play, next) not the F1-12 so if you need to see F1-12 in the dark, you're out of luck. Also the Fn key doesn't light up so even if you memorize which F key is which you'll be hunting for the Fn key in the dark. And just to rub salt in the wound, the spacebar doesn't light up, once again due to the fact the light is only emitted through the printed letters on the key caps and not the perimeter of each key.

The keyboard of the K830, for typing purposes, is decent, however once again the K810 is far superior. The keys of the K830 are chicklet style, but the key caps are completely flat, and the spacing between the keys is quite narrow. This leads to a situation in which you absolutely cannot use the keyboard by feel. This is made worse by the fact that the backlight, as mentioned above, doesn't illuminate around the edges of each key. So what you have is a keyboard you can't see or feel in the dark. The K810 on the other hand is an island style keyboard with indented key caps and slightly more space between keys which lends to the all around better keyboard experience.

Fit and finish of the K830 is good compared to your average $10 usb keyboard from walmart. Compared to other premium products though it lags behind. It's almost as if two totally separate design departments at Logitech designed the K830 and K810 because the K810 is once again far superior. The K830 is nice, smooth plastic without any large seams, gaps or visible screws. It is of moderate thickness, thicker than I was expecting but overall it's not bad. The K810 again destroys the K830 in build quality and finish. It is made of aluminum, feels much more solid, and is considerably thinner.

The touchpad:
The design of the touchpad of the K830 is somewhat of a mystery. The touchpad of the older [[ASIN:B01F5U5OZ0 Logitech Wireless All-In-One Keyboard TK820 with Built-In Touchpad (Certified Refurbished)]] is much, much larger and doesn't have separate clunky mouse buttons. Compared to most new laptops the touchpad of the K830 is average in size and feel. It is responsive enough, however I find myself often wishing it was larger seeing as there is so much wasted space below the touchpad for mouse buttons and blank space. Compared to using the T630 ultra thin mouse on the couch it is generally a better experience. It lacks some of the gesture support of the T630 but that's ok, the gestures are mostly important for web browsing which I don't do too much of on the couch. The mouse buttons of the K830 are, a mystery as to why they're included, nonetheless they're there. They cheap feeling, wobbly plastic, clicky buttons. They could have been omitted for a larger clicky touchpad like the TK820.

Battery life:
I haven't really had to recharge it more than once in a couple weeks of sporadic use. I believe bluetooth uses slightly less power, but this will mostly vary according to use. The one, and really only one, area this keyboard improves over its predecessor (the TK820) is the battery. Gone are the days of hunting for AA and AAA batteries and tossing them in the trash when they're spent after just a few weeks of use. The K830 (like the K810 and T630) uses an internal rechargeable Li-Ion battery that is easily recharged using a standard micro-USB charger you probably already have lying around for your phone. I honestly don't know why any wireless devices still use AA and AAA batteries anymore when lithium batteries are so light, compact and ubiquitous.

Overall:
If you've never used a mouse and keyboard in the living room you'll probably be pleased. If you've experienced some of Logitech's superior products you'll be underwhelmed. The K830 gets the job done, but with lower quality fit and finish, and some odd design choices compared to other Logitech products. It won't disappoint but it won't leave you speechless either.

title: Good performance but it runs hot
text:
I purchased this to replace an older Arris Sb6141. Comcast no longer officially supported the older modem. I could connect but would frequently lose connection and wouldn't be able to get an ipv4 or ipv6 address so I'd have to call Comcast to reconnect. So I decided it was time to just get a new modem. I originally ordered the sb6190, but after doing some reading I discovered that the chipset inside that modem is notoriously bad, leading to frequent packet (data) loss and frequent latency problems. I immediately canceled that order and went for this, the top tier product that does not have the Puma 6 chipset issues. I figured even though I don't yet have gigabit home internet service, I may someday so this will be somewhat, "future proof", hopefully.

I called Comcast, gave them the Mac address and after about 30 mins I was up and on the internet. However I noticed jittery performance, resulting from 30% packet loss, and very high latency. I called Comcast, they issued me a new public IP and remotely reset the modem. Checked the downstream channels and upstream channels, I had exceptional power and signal to noise ratio. So as far as I could tell my Connection to Comcast was solid. Things were fine for about an hour or two after that. But the packet loss and latency came back. I noticed anytime there was sustained traffic in or out of the modem, the packet loss would shoot up. Stop the load and latency and packet loss would stop. I tried connecting a pc directly to the modem in case my router was the issue, but the packet loss persisted so it was clearly the modem. I rebooted it a few times, still having issues. Factory reset. Still have issues.

During all this I noticed the modem is insanely hot. The outer plastic shell was probably 50C, so I assume the chipset inside is probably around 70-80C. This is with the modem out in the open sitting on top of a table in an well air conditioned room. I thought, maybe the chipset inside is throttling back performance due to being so hot. I crudely attached an 80mm PC fan to the side of the modem using some electrical tape. I powered the fan with this https://smile.amazon.com/gp/aw/d/B000MGG6SC/ref=yo_ii_img?ie=UTF8&psc=1

And this https://smile.amazon.com/gp/aw/d/B007S3T4O0/ref=yo_ii_img?ie=UTF8&psc=1

I didn't open the casing of the modem to attach it as that would void the warranty. I simply attached the fan to the outside, blowing in to the modem.

After a few minutes with the fan running the air pouring out of the modem started to feel cool. Ran some speed tests, downloaded large 500GB files, streamed 4k content, pinged dozens of servers with large packets of data, everything I could do to load up the modem. No packet loss and no increase in latency even when maxing out my connection. It seems my hunch about the modem performance being poor due to overheating may have been correct.

I don't know why Arris would cram such high performance components in a modem only to handicap it by letting it overheat. There is small array of fins inside the modem acting as a heatsink but without a fan to move the air it clearly doesnt help. Arris could have easily added a tiny laptop fan inside to cool things down. Adding my own fan made a big difference. It's sad that I had to do this to get proper performance out of the modem, especially given its price.

If you have a gigabit connection you'll want this modem, but be sure to put it somewhere it can breath, don't let it overheat, or performance will suffer.

title: Better than almost any stock cooler
text:
I have an EVGA GTX1060 SC, which had a pretty good cooler straight from EVGA. However it still reached 70C+ in demanding games with an aggressive custom fan curve. Due to the variable nature of GPU Boost 3.0 that means the boost clock would drop from 1950mhz down to 1800mhz. Even using overclocking utilities like Afterburner the clocks would still drop as power draw and temps rose. All the while the fan was pretty loud.

Enter the Accelero Xtreme III. I had seen these before but a few reviews on YouTube convinced me it was worth it. Installation instructions aren't the best, maybe watch a video or two and look at pictures from other users to make sure you've got it right. I don't recommend using the included glue for the vram and vrm heatsinks included with the kit. I purchase thermal adhesive tape and cut it to size for each vrm chip and vram module. That way they're not permanently glued on! I also removed the stock fans from the Accelero which are held on by simple plastic clips and mounted some nice, silent Noctua fans with standard wire mounts for fans. I also used my own thermal paste, Thermal Grizzly Cryonaut, one of the best non-conducting thermal pastes available.

As for performance? It's nuts. With this Accelero Xtreme III my GTX 1060 never goes over 50C. That means greater power efficiency and better boost clocks. Now my GPU runs at 2150mhz almost constantly in all games. Occasionally it dips down to 2050mhz due to power limits. That's 19% more performance over the original boost clock with the stock cooler. This translated into ~15% improvement in frame rate in most games. That's pretty significant in my opinion. Plus, the Accelero can be moved to a new gpu whenever you decide to upgrade in the future (another reason not to glue those heatsinks on!)

If you're deciding between the Accelero III vs IV, I'd say go with the III. AFAIK the III includes all the little heatsinks you need, the IV doesn't from what I've read. The III doesn't have a bulky backplate/heatsink that protrudes and may get in the way like the IV does. Otherwise the coolers should perform the same.

title: Not as fast as claimed. But still good UHS-I card
text:
I was surprised to find this card for the same price as the Extreme Pro 95MB/s that had been available for a while. Almost double the read speed for the same price? Awesome! Not so fast there...

If you read the fine print on SanDisk's website or the product packaging you'll see that it requires proprietary technology to achieve the full 170MB/s read. Otherwise it maxes out at around standard UHS-I speeds of 90MB/s read, 80MB/s write. (It's called a standard for a reason.)

At first I thought my laptop's integrated card reader just wasn't up to par so I tried an external one, same results. It seems the only device capable of achieving these speeds is SanDisk's own USB 3.0 card reader, and other certified/participating devices (which so far includes nothing else). Normally I'd be upset about this but, at the time of writing, this model is almost the exact same price as the 95MB/s model, only a few cents higher. title: Amazing! Simply Amazing
text:
Wow. Positively amazing. This was an upgrade to an older Haswell era i7. I thought, sure it'll be a bit faster. No..oh no...It's like the first time you experienced a SSD versus a HDD. This is an absolute MONSTER of a CPU. I've been using it at the heart of a workstation for Next Generation Sequencing analysis, where 8 cores is about the minimum necessary, and I was blown away by the speed of this CPU.

I'm running this AMD 2700 cpu on an ASROCK B450M Pro4 motherboard
with a Noctua Nh-L12 cpu cooler
with 64GB of DDR4 2933MHz vengeance LPX memory from Corsair.
a 500GB WD Black SN750 nVME M.2 SSD
a 1TB WD blue SATA M.2 SSD
an old Radeon HD7750 GPU for basic display out purposes
with the OS being Ubuntu 18.04 LTS

First thing was first, I overclocked it. It's a bit more difficult with Linux as the benchmarking software is lacking, but using Blender I was able to dial in a stable all core OC of 4.1GHz at 1.36v. With the Noctua NH-L12 (with a NF-A12x25 fan, great fan!) I'm getting peak load temps while OC'ed around 72C with the fan at 100% (surprisingly tolerable noise level). At stock, not OC'ed, it was more like 3.6GHz all core, and 58C. If I didn't already have this cooler lying around I'd have gone for the NH-C14S, but for now this is fine because it cost me nothing extra.

Most people running the particular scientific programs around getting around 300-400 millions reads mapped per hour (at best) on their Xeon E5 based professional OEM workstation systems, meanwhile with the consumer grade Ryzen 7 2700 I'm getting ~800 million paired end reads mapped per hour. Most people say that hyperthreading isn't very useful for many of these scientific programs. However, I found AMD's implementation of simultaneous multithreading to be much more effective than Intel's hyperthreading and it was actually beneficial to use multithreading on AMD where it made almost no difference on Intel.

Paired with 64GB of RAM this thing is a beast. I wish it was possible to use 128GB as intel has supposedly allowed on their consumer platform using double capacity memory (which is so expensive it may as well not exist), but unfortunately memory capacities like that are only available on Threadripper for AMD.

A few programs a limited to a single CPU thread. In these cases it did boost up to 4.1GHz at stock, but would rarely hold there for long and would spend far more time around 3.6GHz. Manually overclocking in BIOS ensured the CPU will be around 3.9-4.1GHz all the time. Makes the system extremely responsive. Intel still reigns supreme at single thread workloads though with single core clocks of over 5GHz. Hopefully the next generation of Ryzen 3000 cpu's will address single thread speed a bit more.

Overall, I couldn't be happier, well maybe if I'd gone with Threadripper, but for the money, this CPU can't be beat.

title: Absolute monster cpu
text:
I was running a R7 2700 overclocked to 4ghz in a workstation for scientific data analysis (next generation sequencing). I thought it was a pretty good setup. I had been thinking about the new Ryzen 3000 cpu's but figured the upgrade probably wasn't worth it. Couldn't stop wondering if it'd speed up my work so I finally just did it. And am I glad I did!

The amazing thing is it stays above 4ghz even fully loaded. I expected it'd really slow down when hammering the cpu but it stays around 4.1ghz with all 24 threads crunching away.

Compared to my 16 thread 2700, the 24 thread 3900x has cut the time to complete one particular workload in half. Seriously impressive, from 36 minutes down to 16 minutes.

The 3900x only runs about 7C warmer than my old 2700. Using a Scythe Mugen 5 Rev B. Granted this is a workstation so the fans are not set to silent. But it tops out around 70C with all cores loaded.

Do be aware if you're upgrading an existing b350/B450 or x370/x470 board from an older Ryzen cpu, upgrade your bios to the "lowest" or "first" bios which will support the Ryzen 3000 cpu first. Then install the Ryzen 3000 cpu. Once you confirm that it works, then go ahead and update to the newest bios available. Don't try to update to the newest bios with the old cpu though. That can cause problems. I had issues and had to mess around with upgrading and downgrading the bios until finally got everything working. Save yourself the headache and do as I mentioned above. Or follow your motherboard vendor instructions closely.

Overall, really pleased with the upgrade.

Now, it's interesting to note the remote for the Chromecast with Google TV does have an ability to control a TV - it can run through standard codes and deal with power and volume. If all you have is a TV and that's it, you probably don't need the Sideclick. However, we have some odd setup stuff (TVs that don't control the sound bar through HDMI, etc.) where having the extra few buttons that can learn is really key. Plus, I'm not totally sure how sophisticated the Chromecast remote is, like, I don't think it can "learn" from an existing remote in the event the TV code isn't found for your TV.

Anyway, we got this and it's a great fit. Highly recommended if you want to control a receiver _and_ a TV, or the TV _and_ a sound bar, or even if you just want some additional buttons beyond power and volume for your TV.

title: Died in 5 years.

Those junk capacitors strike yet again! I can not begin to express my hate for the cheap capacitors that are a plague to the world. Almost anything electronic that fails, you can bet that an electrolytic capacitor usually from China is the culprit! So is the case with this brand sub woofer also. I wish I know which brand products make the effort to get better capacitors before buying an expensive product like this. 5 years is not acceptable, even though I have had some products where the caps died in less than 2 years.
I have already found 3 bad capacitors and still have not fully fixed this yet. Got it to have its red power light actually come on, but can't get it to go green yet. The power supply is fine, but the amplifier board is the problem area. I will still give it 3 stars as it lasted more than 2 years and sounded better than the one that had capacitors failing in less than 2 years.

title: It is much faster than my previous WiFi
text:
I am using this NetGear router as an Access Point paired with my ASUS router which I left as my main router. I have the old router in the basement connected to my modem and this new router upstairs with a wired connection to other router.

My main objective for this router was to have an extremely fast WiFi connection to my Oculus Quest 2 VR headset to use it wireless with my Rift games. The good news is that it works Great!

This router offers 3 independent WiFi radios with each offering 2.5 and 5G frequencies. I set up one that I only connect my VR to. The great thing about the others is that I set up my other devices to use either one of the other channels of this Access Point or the other router. The two routers do not seem to interfere with each other.

The only issue I had was reconnecting the setup web page in this new Router/AP after initial setup. I had to figure out the IP address it was given from the other router so that I could get to the web page. I am all good now and have it set up as a favorite in my browser now.

Just glancing out the router features, it seems pretty full featured like my other router if you use the advanced settings pages.

The range seems really great on this WiFi. Maybe it is because I have it upstairs.

My WiFi connection to VR headset is reporting 1.2 Gbit. That is faster than my wired Ethernet connections! And it is almost as fast as the wired USB 1.6 Gbit connection to VR headset and I can not tell the difference in performance.

So I am happy with this NetGear router used as Access Point so far.

title: Came with non-US plug.  Yet useful for me.
text:
The unit I received did not have a US plug even though the product pictures a US plug. In my first picture you can see the plug it came with on left and on the right is the adaptor that did not come with it which I had to use in order to plug it in. I could have replaced the plug and still might. Maybe they sent this wrong one only to Vine testers?? Just be aware of this possible issue.

It also came with all the output adaptors shown in second picture which is a nice collection. They are on a nice rubber holder and fit output jack with good tightness. However, the tip is always positive with no way to switch that. They store back on the rubber holder with good fit to keep the parts together. Wouldn't it be nice if they could be stored on the adaptor itself?

The voltage adjusting knob has an off click position. The voltage readout is clear in real life. Camera catches a flicker I can not see in real life.

Finally I tested this with a load and test equipment The following are my results:
Max setting display = 24.1 (volts). Measured = 23.7v with 70ma load.
with 1amp load display = 24.0. Measured = 23.5v.
with 2 amp load display = 18.0. Measured = 17.5v.
Note that I could draw 1.35amp before voltage dropped at 23.5v measured.
With supply set at 9.00v. Measured 8.87v at 80ma.
with 1amp load display = 8.98. Measured = 8.74v.
with 2 amp load display = 8.96. Measured = 8.61v.
With supply set at min = display at 3.71. Measured = 3.66v at 30ma.
with 1 amp load display = 3.63. Measured = 3.46v.
with 2 amp load display = 3.53. Measured = 3.26v.

The last picture shows my test setup.

Note that the unit is current protected and drops the voltage to 0 on display and output if you try to pull more than 2 amps. This is good!

I took a star off because it came with wrong AC plug.

Other than that I like this unit. I do wish it had a polarity reversing switch in order to make the tip negative for devices that require that.

Also I might be a little concerned to use this on a device that only requires 3v because my unit only goes down to 3.5v even when pulling 1amp and I am afraid that might over power a 3v device. I almost took another star off since they advertise it goes down to 3v and mine does not. 3v is common for some devices and some people might want to use it for that.

title: Very light and compact.  Glides easy on desk.  BT and dongle modes.
text:
I really like the two interface modes this mouse has. Blue Tooth or use the included USB 2.4G transmitter. Only one can be used at a time. There is a switch on bottom of mouse that has 3 positions. Off/BT/2.4G. You have to select one position of that switch. But it will remember last BT device paired with.

This mouse feels very light and glides across the desk very smooth. I am really enjoying this for a change from my heavy gaming mouse. I just have both hooked up now.

There are 3 DPI settings that you toggle through with button on top of mouse. There is not much difference at all in these 3 DPI setting. You can tell which setting you are in if you closely notice the flashing blue light each time you push the button. One flash for lowest DPI and 3 for highest. I notice the blue flash on left side of mouse most.

The buttons are quite, but the response is a bit sluggish and not the same on both buttons. This is NOT a gaming mouse in any stretch of the imagination. Fine for solitaire and jigsaw though.

The scroll wheel is small and finger slips sometimes without wheel turning. Probably the scroll wheel is my biggest complaint.

The switch on the bottom is very hard for me to operate even with my small hands. It is recessed which I understand is needed. But the opening is too small to reach finger into.

I normally just leave it on, because it will shut itself off after around 10 minutes without use. To use it again, just click a button and it pops right on almost instant.

When I wanted to change device I had the BT paired with, I could not add new device until I removed the pairing on old device from the old device. Not sure how you would do that from the mouse and instructions were not clear on if there was a way to reset the mouse pairing from the mouse itself.

I am updating my review and taking off a star because I have charged this 3 times now and only averaging 4 days on a charge where the description says 30. Not even close. I leave the switch on, but the auto shutdown works in 10-15 minutes and I could never use the tiny hard to reach switch all the time.

You can not turn OFF the LED lights when using mouse as far as I can figure out and I sure tried. This might be a big negative for some people.

title: Found a way to use this for larger electronics.
text:
Reviewing Digital Microscope with 7" screen and 32GB SD card from Zeberry:

I needed something better to examine circuit boards while I worked. The magnifier lamps were not good enough. I got this with the knowledge the base it came with would not work as it is way too small.
I was not sure if the unit would be able to focus if it was much further from the board, but it turns out it can do it very well and has great range!

So I can say now that magnifying power is adjusted by how close you put the camera to what you are viewing. The focus is handled by a multi turn ring on the camera shaft itself. There must be a lens inside that is moved up and down.

You can see by my picture I found a way to mount it in an old adjustable work lamp. This works really well. So much better than trying to look into a magnifier lens/lamp. I can now sit back and just look at the screen. So much better!

I played with this a bit with the stand it came with looking at stamps and coins and my finger and such. It is really neat. But the picture on the box shows someone looking at bacteria or something. You can't do that with this, it is not really a microscope and you can't use backlit slides, nor would this magnify enough. But for stamps and coins and pulling a splinter out and stuff, it is great and way more powerful than any magnifier I have used and much more stable.

I must say that I am not too wild about the little lights. The flexible sticks they are on are too short to maneuver the lights well and move away from the subject enough to not reflect too much. Sometimes the LEDs inside the camera reflect off what you are looking at and you have to turn them down and find another way to light the subject or the picture is a little grainy with low light.

The 7 inch screen is very clear. The build seems like good quality.

You do not have to install any software on you PC or phone to use this and that is a big plus. It comes with some sort of software on a CD, but I did not install it as it is not needed. I am VERY happy they did not force me to install some software or drivers. Worked with windows 10 to display on bigger screen if you want or download pictures from SD card.

You can record stills or video on the SD card if you want.

What more would I like...A way to change the zoom/power without moving it closer to the object. But that would require more lenses I guess. Maybe a little laser pointer to show where I am looking on the board. Guess I could add that, but it might be dangerous if it reflected into your eyes.

Overall for the money and now that I have another mounting option for the work bench (I can also still move it back to stand it came with very easy), I am really thinking this is a great value for me and I think I will get a lot of use out of this.

I am taking off a star for the goofy advertising they show on the product page and the box. It is misleading and to be honest, I think it is silly. But the product has good uses and good build quality and I am very happy with it.
