title: Could not get to work.
text:
Reviewing 1080p Color Security Camera - Wired Full Time Video:

I got this because I am tired of the huge delay to see real time video on the WiFi app based cameras. I own Blink camera and by the time I get a video of who is at the door, they have left!!!!

I figured I would come up with a way to have this video on a monitor instead of buying a DVR. The add for this camera says it supports 4-in-1 TVI/CVI/AHD/CVBS and says the camera is preset to 1080p@30fps HD-TVI, and acts like you can change it. But there is nothing in the instructions on how to change and there are no switches on the unit. I even opened up the unit and no switches on the circuit board either. The instructions have specifications that say PAL/NTSC and all sorts of resolutions. How the heck do you change these settings!!!

I am retired electrical engineer, so have some knowledge. I was able to power up and the lights flash once on power up...so think I have that right. They specify 12v but don't mention plug polarity. So I just tried. One way the lights flash, the other way they don't. Assuming the flashing way is correct. I tested using the video composite input on 3 different monitors and got nothing. I tried the VCR video input on an old security camera monitor and that showed an out-of-sync video signal while the camera was powered, so something was coming out of the video output. I don't have time or interest in putting the video signal on a scope at this time and try to see what sort of output this is. I am also not familiar with all the possible video specifications. Since there is not way to change the video output, I am not sure I will have any use for this camera.

If you happen to have the "Correct" DVR, maybe this camera will work for you. Taking 2 stars off because the add for this product acts like it has a flexible video output, but it appears that it does not. The only thing that I can imagine is that the DVR protocols have some way to talk back to cameras and change the video settings....if I have time in the future, I might try to dig into this technology more.

At this time, I certainly can not recommend this product even though the price is reasonable if it happens to work with your DVR.

title: Great value.  Low noise.  Simple control.  Sizes as advertised.
text:
Reviewing Qirssyn 120mm USB Fan with 3 spd with Hydraulic Bearing

Let me by clear that this is the version with hydraulic bearing Not the dual ball bearing version.
I have ordered both versions and the hydraulic bearing version was better and a dollar cheaper.

They now have the reviews separated, So I removed the picture and most comments about the ball bearing ones that I returned which were louder with vibration and had weak cord connection to fan.

The rest of the review below was from my experience with cheaper hydraulic bearing fan that was sent to me through Vine program:

I am very happy with this simple control. I opened it up to see what was inside and it is basically just two resisters and the switch. The resistors give you the low and med speeds. Off is no voltage and Hi is full 5V. The fan itself is a 5vDc fan. USB outputs provide 5V. So this is pretty simple and if you want, you could cut off the USB plug and power it another way.

The cord is pretty short at 39"....but the seller is clear on this, so you get what they say. I plan to use this and buy more for arcade machines that need cooling and replacement of noisy fans. I will have to buy some USB wall warts for machines that don't have 5v available, but most machines have 5V. This is such a minor current draw, I am not worried about overloading the power supply.

The seller is very clear on the specs also at the different speeds. I do have to say the difference between 19 and 23db is significant, but that makes sense since db to sound level is logarithmic.

The only negative thing I noticed is at low speed, the fan was a little slow at getting started which makes me wonder if that will ever be and issue. I will probably just use these on medium though and that starts up quickly and is not much louder. It does provide noticeable flow difference though which is good.

I am very happy with the value of these fans.

title: My experience with these headphones was not a good one
text: I don't know if I received 2 sets from a bad batch of these or what, but my experience with these headphones was not a good one. The first pair arrived and I plugged them up to my laptop via my dac/amp and every time a bass note hit at 50% volume or above, they distorted severely and rattled like both cans were blown. The only way to make it go away was to turn the individual bass sliders all the way down, which leaves these headphones with barely any bass whatsoever. Now, I've heard Beyerdynamic headphones before that have sounded amazing, so I thought these sounding bad had to be a fluke. I tried plugging in my Sennheiser IE80 ear buds to be sure the amp wasn't causing the issue, but they sounded perfectly fine. So, I decided to have Amazon replace them with another set of the Custom One Pro Plus instead of a refund. That new set sounded the exact same as the first, with static and a rattle whenever a bass note was played at 50% volume or higher. I've already boxed the 2nd set up and dropped them off at UPS on the same day I received them. I'm just not willing to risk a 3rd pair, so this time I'm going with the refund and I'm going to find a different pair of headphones. I've still given these 2 stars even after both were bad because the comfort was remarkable, and even though I didn't get the opportunity to use it, the customization of these was a pretty big feature in my original decision to buy them. I'm actually disappointed that my time with these headphones was this bad after reading all the great reviews and seeing so many videos about them. Definitely not what I'd hoped for.

title: Best bang for your buck!
text:
I own/have owned a ton of headphones, from entry level to audiophile quality. IEM's to over-ears. But I have never enjoyed as much "bang for your buck" goodness as with the HFI-580 from Ultrasone. They are on par with headphones costing 3 to 4 times as much, both in build quality and sound. I'm an admitted basshead, but I also want the rest of the sound spectrum in my headphones, and the HFI-580's deliver all of it. Clean and deep sub bass, quick mid bass, slightly recessed mids (easily EQ'ed) and super clean and bright highs with a slight roll off at the top end. They do benefit from a burn in period of 80-100 hours. Keep in mind, these are closed back headphones, so they won't have the sound stage of an open back design. But these use a technology called S-Logic Plus which makes the sound stage very large for a closed back set. (Read about S-Logic Plus here: [...]) Very comfortable out of the box, but I bought some Brainwavz HM5 replacement pads and they are now the most comfortable pair I've ever owned. I can wear them hours on end with no fatigue. I bought them thinking they would be my portable over-ears, however, they are now my everyday headphones. I use them with my Laptop>DAC>Amp setup at home and my Android>portable DAC/Amp for on the go. They don't require an amp to sound great, but they come to life hooked up to one. Truthfully, I've not heard anything better than these Ultrasone HFI-580's in this price range. Buy with confidence, I don't think you could be disappointed.

*Included pictures show the HFI-580 with the blue Brainwavz HM5 replacement pads.

title: Solid HD alternative to a full blown camcorder
text:
While I already own a HDV camera, I have found that it's not always practical for personal use because of its size. If I wear shorts with cargo pockets, I can fit it into a pocket if I really want to, but it's still bulky and heavy for casual use like on vacation. After looking at the Kodak Zi6, the Flip and another "pocket video camera", I settled on the Kodak and have been pretty happy with in thus far.

The main factors that sold me were the price (it's cheaper than the other models), the reviews of its picture quality (it's been rated better than the others), and its use of SD cards for memory instead of built-in (I like the fact I can use up to a 32GB card and switch out if I need to record more). My Kodak still camera came with a long-lasting rechargeable lithium battery and the Zi6 comes with rechargeable AAs instead, which is good in a way as you can use standard AAs in a pinch.

My only complaint is that I use a Mac Book Pro and I cannot plug into the USB port with the power supply connected because the USB connector comes out at a right angle to the camera, which then blocks the power supply connection. Right now I have to unplug the computer to hook up the camera, but I've ordered a cheap USB hub to see if that will help and it may not be a factor for other computers depending on where their USB ports are located.
item_title: Kodak Zi6 Pocket Video Black Camera

title: Build your own camera bag
text: This bag is nice because it has a ton of pockets that are very roomy. The addition of a slot specifically for tablets is a nice feature for photographers that use their iPad to clear out memory cards and/or view photos as they're shooting. The bag is designed to configured as you need it using spacers that adjust with velcro. This can be a good or bad thing. While it gives you flexibility, other bags may seem more secure with set configurations that hug your camera and lenses tightly with compartments built specifically for them. If the ability to configure the inside of the bag the way you want is what you're going for or you use a tablet hand in hand with your camera, this may be a good bag for you.
item_title: Lowepro 250 Urban Photo Sling (Black)

title: Strong Volume and Bass for Small, Lightweight Speakers
text:
I've tried a lot of portable Bluetooth speakers and so far the Goal Zero Rock Out 2 has the most "oomph" in terms of volume without distortion and bass.

It charges up quickly using a build-in USB cable, but also has the benefit of solar panels for charging on the go. There is also a built in "line in" cable for connecting directly to an audio source with a standard 3.5mm mini stereo plug. Apparently you can also use the mini cable to connect to other Goal Zero Rock Out speakers to amplify your sound. What's nice about both of them is that they're built in so you won't lose it and they coil neatly into slots; the drawback of both are that are very short.

The speakers paired quickly with both my iPhone and iPad with little effort. Just hold down the power button to make it discoverable, go to your Bluetooth menu and pair. There were some glitches or delays in the sound initially, but the more I used it the less this happened.

Another nice feature is that they use the space behind the speakers inside the case to provide a small netted compartment, perfect for storing a MP3 player or smart phone. If you have a dedicated iPod or something like that, you can store it *in* the speakers so again you don't lose it.

The one thing I wish the speakers did however is charge a mobile device using the solar panels as well. These speakers would be killer if you could plug your smart phone or MP3 player into the speakers and charge along with the speakers, or even just charge the device while not using the speakers. While it is nice that you can recharge the speakers using the sun, what good does it do you if the battery on your audio source goes dead?

All in all, these are great speakers for their size, perfect for hiking, camping, boating or being out on the deck where you can take advantage of the solar recharging. They have good sound, but could benefit from longer built-in cables and the ability to also charge a connected audio source.
item_title: Goal Zero 94014, Green

title: Not pretty to look at, but delightful to listen to
text:
Aesthetically, you can tell these were designed by Germans and not Jony Ive as they're not the most visually appealing item to have sitting in your living room. This is fine if you have your audio equipment in a closet or rack, but something to consider if these are going to be sitting out in your living room for all to see. Most of the bulk comes from the headphones, so it's less intrusive when in use.

Setting up and using these headphones are a cinch. Most of the controls are on the headphones themselves including power, volume and mode, though you can adjust balance and mode back at the base unit as well. There are two means of audio in, either 1/8" mini or optical audio, though they sound great even using the mini jack with an iPad as a source. While it comes with multiple plug options for the power adapter, this may have caused the one thing I don't like about the unit which is the size of the power adapter at the plug in. It won't fit nicely into a power strip as it's wide and long. The headphones are powered by two AAA rechargeable batteries which sit inside the earpieces and are charged when the headphones are put back on the base unit. It took about 12 hours for the initial charge out of the box; I'll have to report back on how long they last. Haven't tested out the range, but I have been able to walk around and use them in another room without too much of an issue so far.

The sound is rich and the headphones comfortable, so I can see myself using these in several applications. Our living room acoustics aren't great, so I can see myself using these when watching an action movie or playing Playstation by myself. I can also foresee using them when discretion is warranted and I want to listen to music but don't want to disturb others.
item_title: Sennheiser RS 195 RF Wireless Headphone Systems for TV Listening with Selectable Hearing Boost Preset

text: I've bought several of these cables to replace worn Apple cables with mixed results. Some cables work great without an issue, others get the "This accessory is not compatible with this device" error after a few weeks or months of use. title: Massive well designed backpack holds a lot; great for the pro, may be too much for casual use
text: Not for the faint of heart or small of frame, this Pro-DSLR backpack is MASSIVE and not for casual use or most amateur photographers. If you just want a bag for your DSLR, its accessories and an extra lens to take hiking or out and about, this is not the pack for you. If however you have a massive DSLR with a ton of lenses and want to take multiple mobile devices with you, then this is exactly what you want. You can store your camera with a huge zoom lens attached, eight additional lenses, a latpop, a tablet, your charger, memory card readers, extra cards in the compartments along with a place to strap on a tripod. It sits on a hard plastic base, which gives you stability and moisture protection if you put it down on the ground. I can see either using this as "one stop storage" that is moderately portable or for the hardcore photographer who must have everything they own with them when out in the world.
item_title: Case Logic KDB-101 Kontrast Pro-DSLR Backpack (Black)

title: Rugged case, less than intuitive installation
text:
I bought Otterbox Defender cases for gifts twice, so when I got a new iPhone 6s I wanted to get one for myself. Next time, include instructions because without this video (http://youtu.be/IacGHCKHO_s) I would have been lost even though I bought previous models. It was hard to find a place to pull back the rubber without being afraid to break something. I finally got a finger hold around the camera lens opening. Not as intuitive as it could be.

Once past the installation, it's a solid case if you're tough on your phone or use it in situations it may get wet or subject to impact. It is not a good case if you want to get your phone out regularly. My wife took her phone out frequently and over time the rubber stretched and ripped. If you're going to use a case like this, prepare to leave it in.

title: Make your iPad Mini into a MacBook Air for typing on the go
text: An iPad Mini isn't very big, so any keyboard meant to go with it can't be all that big either. Despite its petite size, this keyboard is easy to adapt to and works well with responsive keys. Power comes from an included USB cable to recharge the battery that lasts for a while with a system that only turns the keyboard on when it's locked into position for typing. Pairing was a breeze without any complications; just turn on Bluetooth, find the keyboard in your utilities app and pair. If you need to do a lot of typing and want to use your iPad like a laptop, this is a great solution for you as it doubles as a case to fit in your briefcase or bag. If you mostly use your iPad for browsing, games, etc. the added bulk of the keyboard being always attached may be too much for you. That said, the iPad pops in and out with ease if you want to use it on its own without the weight.
item_title: Logitech FOCUS Protective Case with Integrated Keyboard for iPad Mini 4, Black

title: Ingenious design for keeping your cords untangled
text: We all have wires to deal with -- phone cords, headphones, computer cables -- and Cloop cable keepers are an ingenious way of keeping them organized. A small loop in the middle of the keeper slides on the cable so you don't have to worry about losing it when not in use. The pack includes six keepers total, three large (good for wrapping cords up to a dime's width) and three small (for bundles the width of a pencil), making it a pretty good deal at under $4 a keeper. I've paid more for cable keepers with fewer features that ended up getting lost because they didn't have a good means to stay on the cable.
item_title: CLOOP Cord Keeper – 3 Small & 3 Large Set Magnetic Cable Organizer – Charging Cord Organizer – Ideal for Cable Management, Headphones, USB – Patented – Practical and User-Friendly – (Assorted Colors)

title: Well designed cables to reduce clutter, not sure about the base
text: These cables keepers are ingenious. They attach to your cable so you won't lose them, can clip onto your clothes to keep your headphones from going all over, and are a good value with a pack of six (three large, three small) to handle a range of cable organization needs. I'm not entirely sold on the base though. A strong magnet with an included adhesive strip is supposed to attach to a surface like a desk or a bedside table for the cable keepers to attach to so your phone doesn't fall off the desk or keeping the cable in reach when you need it. The fact that they use magnets makes this good in concept as like Apple's magnetic laptop cables, if you trip over the cord it will give way rather than launching your item across the room. However in this case it's necessary to adhere the base onto a surface which is at very least limiting (you can only do it in one location) and I'm not sure I want to glue things to my furniture. Personal preference would lead me to buy the set without the base which is about $10 cheaper.
item_title: CLOOP Cord Keeper – 3 Small, 3 Large & 1 Base Set Magnetic Cable Organizer – Charging Cord Organizer – Cable Management, Headphones, USB – Patented – Practical and User-Friendly – (Assorted Colors)

title: Large capacity UBS drive for carrying a massive amount of data, inconsistent experience pairing it with mobile devices
text:
Works great as a large capacity USB stick, however I had issues using it with my mobile devices.

Making sure that I downloaded the right app per the instructions on the stick, while I could connect to the device with my iPhone, I couldn't download files. I attempted to backup my photos, but I got caught in an endless loop of it asking me to create a destination folder then telling me it couldn't create the folder. Also couldn't' get it to connect to my home wi-fi network, though I could connect to the stick's wi-fi network. Kept telling me my password was wrong, however I checked and double checked to make sure I was putting it in correctly. I could access files however from the stick and read the instructions PDF on my phone.

Oddly, I didn't have most of these problems on my iPad, though I still had an issue connecting to my home wi-fi network. I was not only able to access files on the stick, but backed up photos from my iPad that appeared on the stick when I connected it to my computer. The app also seemed to run fasted on my iPad though it's an older model while I have a brand new iPhone 6S.

All in all I can't complain about the shear number of files I can store on this drive as it has higher capacity than many hard drives I own. That said, the connectivity part of it is still a little wonky for me and I'l have to play around with it more. Obviously it works since I can access most of the features on my iPad, I just need to find out why I'm not having the same success on my iPhone. Unfortunately, like most products these days, documentation consists of a "Getting Started" one page guide without any serious documentation or instructions, but hopefully I'll find my answer on SanDisk's web page.
item_title: SanDisk 200GB Connect Wireless Stick Flash Drive - SDWS4-200G-G46

title: Camera does a little bit of everything for times using a smartphone isn't practical or wanted, but has its limitations
text:
You may wonder why you'd need something like the ZAGG Now Cam when most people can take photos, record video and play music on their smartphone, especially when there's no screen to preview or review shots? I can see myself using this camera in situations I don't want to risk using my phone but may still want to record a moment either as a still or video. It also has a high capacity with space for up to 30 minutes of 720p HD video or 1,600 photos, which may be more than your phone or tablet can hold

Since the ZAGG Now Cam is water resistant (and fully waterproof with an additional case) and attaches to a lanyard (includes three: one for your neck, one for your wrist and keychain), I can take this fishing for instance and not have to worry about it getting wet but still get that picture of the fish I caught. Or maybe you use it when you're doing something active outside but don't want to take a chance that you'll drop your phone. The lack of screen also keeps you more in the moment as you can't take time trying to frame that "perfect shot", but rather snap the photo hoping you got it. This may be one of those things that the instant gratification of digital cameras have spoiled us with, as we never knew with film cameras whether we "got the shot" until we got the film developed.

An optional mounting kit is available for attaching to anything with a bar like a bicycle, motorcycle, stroller, Segway, what have you like a Go Pro. There's a magnet built in for attaching to metal surfaces and if you a strong magnet shirt pocket, you could conceivably use this as a body cam. That's the strength I think of this camera is that you can use it in nontraditional ways if you just get creative enough, especially with creative uses. For instance the "six second burst" feature is clearly meant for use with Vine, so a social media manager could give this to staff members with no experience to shoot video without having to worry bout editing it down.

The camera has built-in connectivity for mobile devices with Bluetooth and generates its own wi-fi network that you can use to access photos and videos through an app on your phone or tablet. These are a little slow with larger files, so you will probably want to use the app mostly to check if your photo/video came out but use the included USB cable to download onto your computer. While it functions as a Bluetooth speaker, I didn't find much better than those on my mobile devices
item_title: ZAGG Now Cam Social Video, Camera, and Bluetooth Speaker - Gray

This means you need to carry two cables with you if you're an Apple device user, one to charge your battery and a Lightning cable to hook the battery to your device. text: This wi-fi extender is truly plug and play. All I had to do was open the box, turn the power switch on and run the simple setup wizard to connect it to my network. I particularly like that it has a Gigabit Ethernet port for hardwiring a computer, smart TV or game console and comes with a cable to do so. While it's a little big, it's designed in such a way it won't block the other outlet.
item_title: TP-Link AC1200 Wireless Wi-Fi Range Extender (RE350K)

title: Better suited for the suburbs or cities, very particular
text: We live out in the country on top of a mountain, so I've been searching for an over-the-air antenna that would allow me to cut the cord with DirecTV. No such luck here. While we may be in the boonies, we are within 50 miles of several broadcast towers but therein lays the first rub with this antenna: it's very finicky about what direction it's pointing. Throughout the instructions, it says you have to point at the tower, but what if they're in different directions? We have a PBS station 10 miles to the south, a NBC affiliate and another PBS station 30 miles to the north and NBC, CBS, ABC, FOX and PBS 50 miles east. None of them came in. It's supposed to mount to a window or wall, but that didn't work for me either as it wouldn't stick to the nearest window. The 12' cord also isn't particularly long if your television is in one place but the best location for the antenna isn't near. In the end, I reverted back to cheap, unpowered "rabbit ears" which pick up eight channels compared to none with thr Clearstream. I'm going to try again in the suburbs near my office to see if it works any better there, as I want this to work as it has potential given its small size and easy hook up.
item_title: Antennas Direct ClearStream Eclipse Amplified TV Antenna, 50+ Mile Range, Multi-Directional, Grips to Walls, 15dB In-Line Amplifier, 12 ft. Coaxial Cable, Power Adapter, Black or White (ECL-A)

title: Makes your Apple TV much more practical and easy to use
text: The Sideclick remote solves two problems: keeping track of your Apple TV remote and controlling the TV you use it with. Apple didn't design it's remote very practically; yes, it looks nice but it's so slim and small, it's easy to misplace. By mounting it into the Sideclick, the remote has enough heft and size so you don't lose it, but not so much that it's bulky or cumbersome. The universal remote attachment quickly and easily pairs with your remote by learning it's functions through infrared, saving you the hassle of having to program it manually with codes. I do wish the universal remote could be mounted on either side since it is removable as the buttons aren't as intuitive as I thought they'd be for me being righthanded. For some reason it just feels like the buttons should be on the right for me. The limited number of buttons also means you're channel surfing with up/down buttons, rather than inputting numbers to go to specific channels. Neither of these are fatal flaws and I appreciate being better able to keep track of my Apple remote and not have to use my TV remote for basic functions like power, volume etc.
item_title: Sideclick Remotes SC2-APG3K Universal Remote Attachment for Apple TV

title: Long, durable cable for high-definition hookups
text: Long fabric covered cable is a great alternative to HDMI for hooking up a high definition source to a television when you need added length with durability. My only complaint is that the color coding at the ends are just little dashes visable on only two sides, with the red on the audio and video looking very similar, but it's not like most people are fiddling around with the connections frequently. Other than that, while it may be "basic", it seems well constructed and does the job.
item_title: Amazon Basics RCA Component Video Cable with Audio - 15 Feet

title: Inexpensive solution for basic entertainment setup
text: A serviceable television stand for its price, but because of that price don't expect too much. Made up of six recycled particleboard pieces laminated to give it the appearance of wood, it's fairly straightforward to construct but the multiple bolts and dowels will take up your time putting it together. The instructions are better than you usually get with "assemble yourself" furniture and there's a phone number and email address for assistance. Because it's particleboard and laminate, it can be easy to nick or dig the corners and edges, but nothing that black touch up paint wouldn't fix. The manufacturer says its rated for 60 pounds, but I'm not sure how much I trust it, so I'd be conservative with the weight of the television you put on here.
item_title: Furinno JAYA Large Entertainment Stand for TV Up to 55 Inch, Blackwood

title: My Apple Keyboard is now complete!
text: Perfect addition to to my Apple Bluetooth keyboard, which I wouldn't have purchased if I knew it lacked a numeric keyboard. This keyboard more than makes up for this deficiency by giving me the number pad I need for data entry and gaming, while also including four additional function keys, page up/down, home/end, and delete. Set up and pairing was simple and quick; just add two AA batteries, turn it on, go to the "Bluetooth" menu and pair.
item_title: Belkin YourType Bluetooth Wireless Keypad

title: Strong, resilient cable for iOS devices with Kevlar protection on the inside (nylon on the outside)
text: Works fine with my iPhone 6s and iPad Air 2, cord length is a good compromise (not too short, not too long), and black color compliments my iOS devices which are also black. Be aware though that the Kevlar is on the *inside* of the cord to help insulate the wires from damage without compromising flexibility. The braided cable jacket however is nylon, so if you were hoping for Kevlar protection from outside wear (or in my case pet chewing), that's not the case.
item_title: Belkin MIXIT DuraTek Lightning to USB Cable - MFi-Certified iPhone Charging Cable for iPhone 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro Max, XS, XS Max, XR, X, 8/8 Plus and more (4ft/1.2m), Rose Gold

title: Quiet and compact, questionable durability and construction
text:
Not particularly well constructed, but functional and reasonable for its price point. Very lightweight (though adding batteries would offset that) with average construction, it doesn't feel very well made or durable, but does blow and strong stream of air fairly quietly. The fan stays closed or upright by using a ratchet type hinge, but I have a feeling this will wear out with use and a latch to keep it closed would have been a good feature here. The switch is kind of cheap and also seems like it will wear out at some point. While a USB cable is included, they should have designed this to work with a standard USB-mini USB cable since many electronic accessories use them, making it possible to carry just one cable and replace it easily if you lose it. Finally, a carrying bag would have been helpful again to help keep it closed and the cable from getting lost.

Why the 3-stars after saying all that's wrong with it? Because it fulfills its function of blowing air and is relatively compact, so I could see this being useful at the office or while traveling on a plane or train. If it had been priced any higher, I probably would have given it an even lower rating, but for its cost I think it's worth it if you need a portable fan.
item_title: Treva 5 Inch Portable Fan, Battery Operated or USB Connected Cooling for Travel, Outdoor, Car, and Office. Compact Folding and Tilting Design for Directional Air Flow (Grey)

title: Hefty digital storage option for extreme conditions
text: Having accidently dropped my keys in water with a USB stick on them in the past, I like the idea of a waterproof, shockproof, etc. option. I was a little worried about the cap as often they are hard plastic and either become loose or crack, eventually falling off. This cap however is snug fitting rubber which will keep water out while keeping the cap on. The only drawback is that it is a little hefty -- which is good for sturdiness -- so getting it on and off a key ring might be a little of a chore as the loop is pretty fat. Other than that, it's a great digital storage option if you think your USB stick will be exposed to the elements.
item_title: Lexar JumpDrive Tough 32GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive – LJDTD32GABNL

title: Easy to set up, rich deep sound for television and other audio sources
text:
I've been in the market for a sound bar and this has been a great solution for me. Easy to set up, all you have to do is plug in the speaker, plug in the subwoofer and connect your television to the speaker via the included optical audio cable. It's also extremely versatile with optical audio in, 1/8" analog audio in (I use it to connect to my satellite radio), Bluetooth (paired easily with my iPhone) and USB in. The sound is a vast improvement over my television speakers with a lot more depth. What's nice about it connecting with optical audio from the television is that I don't have to find ways of also having to connect the Blu-ray player or satellite receiver.

The only reasons I'm not giving it 5-stars are: it says to also connect to your television with an HDMI cable but doesn't include one (they're cheap enough to include, I hate finding out I need something else like a cable or specific batteries after a purchase), the necessary volume can vary greatly depending on the audio source (can set low for my television, but need to jack it up for analog) and it's hard to read what input you're if the speaker lays flat instead of being mounted.
item_title: Sony HTCT390 Ultra-slim Sound Bar with Bluetooth

title: Heavy with too many adjustment points to be practical
text: I got this as a more portable tripod than the one that came with my astronomical binoculars and while it may fold up more compactly, it's not more practical. It's heavy for a "travel" tripod, which you'd think would be lightweight to take on the go. The design is clunky with way too many points of adjustment to have to lock down. To extend the legs for instance you have to twist open each joint, extend the section, and lock it down with a twist four times each leg, meaning twelve times for the whole tripod. To pack up, you have to do it all again in reverse. Not the most convenient or quick set up. Most of all though I hate that the legs aren't connected to keep them equidistant and stable. Other tripods/monopods I've seen have been able to retain having a brace connecting all the legs without making it overly bulky or complicated. It gets two stars because it will hold a camera or binoculars and is portable, but the design is horrible and not at all intuitive.
item_title: Amazon Basics 63-Inch Lightweight Aluminum Travel Tripod/Monopod with Bag

title: Durable, compatible and cheap
text: I don't ask much of a patch cord, just that it: has a durable cord, has a durable junction where the meets the jack, has good sound without distortion or crackles and can plug into my phone while the case is on. This cord does all of those things while being a good value, making it ideal for hooking your phone to an auxiliary in jack or connecting other devices to speakers or a stereo.
item_title: QualGear 100% OFC Copper, Gold Plated Contacts, 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Premium Auxiliary Stereo Audio Cable - 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male - 4' Black (Qg-Acbl-4ft)

title: Sleek and smart design with great sound
text: Comfortable, well made with a simple, minimalist design. No "on/off" button, the headphones turn themselves on and off when you put them on your head. Requires additional power for amplification, but no batteries...just charge using the included USB-to-USB Micro cable in 3-4 hours for a 12-hour charge. Lights on the side let you know whether it's charging, fully charged or needs recharging. Also included are a 1/8" mini-to-mini 1.2-meter audio cable with Apple iPhone/iPad controls and microphone, regular 3 meter 1/8" mini-to-mini audio cable and 1/8" mini to 1/4" stereo adapter. title: Good inexpensive starter scope, needs upgrades in some areas
text:
A generous 4-stars based on the fact that this scope does what it's supposed to in terms of being inexpensive, easy to assemble and use, and can be used for both astronomical and terrestrial viewing as a refractor. As such, it's a good starter scope for someone who wants to dip their toes into stargazing but doesn't want to spend a lot of money.

The image you get once you get it set up and use it is pretty good for its price given it's all-inclusive. Beginners may not mind some of the parts being subpar compared to what you'd get with telescopes that are even marginally more expensive, but if you get serious about your astronomy you'll probably want to upgrade eventually. In particular, the spotter scope isn't that great, nor is the diagonal or Barlow lens, though the tripod and eyepieces are fairly good for what they are. Given that this telescope is under $200 and these are easy to upgrade, I'm willing to give them a pass on this.

Where this scope is severely lacking is documentation. There is only a folded 8-page largely pictorial instruction sheet included and half of that is in another language than English. Other than showing you how to assemble it, there's nothing included to really help you use it or get the most of it. There also isn't much in terms of support information; initially one of the tripod turnscrews were missing (it had fallen off and was buried in box) and other than the website address, there's nothing on the documentation for who to contact if you're missing a piece or need help.

If you're not sure you want to get into astronomy, may not use it much or just want something inexpensive for a kid to play with, this scope will do the job for you. For a little bit more though if you're more certain your money may go farther with a more traditional brand like Celestron, Meade or Orion as their components are a little more universally solid.

text: I have read through the reviews and I understand some of the complaints and can see why they did not rate this as high. I purchased these with the headers already attached and a different companies with the headers that would need to be soldered in by me.  Since I did not purchase from either of these companies before I was not sure which way to go.  I was not sure how the quality would be for pre installed headers and the soldering quality,  The cost happened to be less for this one with the headers all ready installed.  Both versions worked fine. Sometimes you may need to make sure the board and Ports selected in the IDE before trying to load a sketch.  I sometime needed to load the program a couple of times but just check to make sure everything is selected manually first.  Since both of the companies I selected both use the CH340G IC,  IDE will not detect the board type the indicate which port it assigned it to.  So you manually need to select the board and check the ports and if it displays more than one port pick the last one in that list.  Then try to down load the program once or twice.  Once I did that in never had the problem to load a program again.  So sometimes when testing boards and you feel you only go two or three board out of 5 to work , it may be the IDE may have dropped the Board and Port information and needs to be manually reset.  The complaint of using the white non antistatic foam could be a concern and they should look into it to make sure this product will not be damaged using this to protect the pins and not sure how these boards are fixture before soldering the headers in to make sure they get soldered in straight so they will always line up with a solderless breadboard.  Otherwise the rating will be lower.  Since the cost was less I gave them 5 stars as I did not see any direct issues with my boards .  But  the quality need to be a top concern.  If the White Foam for protecting the pins is not antistatic with low humidity could be a concern of damage to the boards.

I only rated the Seller 4 stars because of the AD I purchase what wasto be a very good used SA speakers but it looked like I received the AVX speakers (New not Used). AD indicate the exact power ratings but when you get the speakers as I have purchased the SA previously. They look the same at first glance but the SA rates theirs at 80 watt RMS and the AVX rates theirs at 100 watts Music Power Now to be fair I do not know if they both are correct as I have not run an RMS Rating on either one yet. But I took off one star as what I ordered and which one I recieved was different and the add claime 80 watt RMS for both speakers but the Box claims 100w Music power. Since there is no spec on defining Music Power it is hard to know. So the sellers need to be transparent and be straight up with the customers.
Work to the customers is do not go by strictly a the speaker has a lot to do with the loudness as speakers are rated at so many db's at 1 Watt at 1 measured at 1 meter away with a db meter. so if you get a 4 " speaker with 84 db sensitivity vs. 10" speaker rated at 96 db for the same 1W power mean that you would have to drive the 4 " speaker at 16 W to have it be the same volume at the 10" speaker at 1 W so the rule of thumb is every time you double the power into the speaker it will be 3 db louder. So when looking for speaker you also need to look at the speakers sensitivity rating.

Update (02/22/13)
I just wanted to post a picture of my setup. I used aluminum flat bar from the local hardware store and built a customer mount with a brushed finish.
[...]

Update (01/28/13)
My TV stand has a mesh back and I was able to mount the sound bar to that ([...]) but it left much to be desired. It was behind the TV and did not change direction when the TV could so I decided that I needed to move it somehow. There are some L-shaped mounts on here for $30-$50 and mixed reviews about functionality which allow mounting to to the top or bottom. They looked cheap and flimsy so I decided to make my own custom mount.

Update (01/15/13)
While walking someone else through it, I found that the optical tuning off and on did not work while the HDMI did. It's quite possible this is due to having a newer model or that I have some power save function turned on/off. Will update once we figure it out.

Original (01-13/13)
Ok, so there are those with issues and those who have workarounds but I'm going to set things straight. First, I purchased the HW-E450C (Costco). Second, I have a Samsung SMART TV (E6000 series). Now, to address the issues some have had, solutions, and review.

Remote issue with volume control: If you into the TV settings and set the sound to external speakers the remote automatically switches to the sound bar and you control the volume.

On/Off issue: First, let me state that the on/off with TV works with both optical and HDMI connections. Also it's HDMI out that should be used and the same source setting switches from optical to HDMI. The other HDMI is not the sound in this case.

As stated previously, connecting the sound bar to the HDMI (ARC), turning Anynet on does control the power with the TV. The reason for setting the 'Auto Turn Off' setting off is because with the setting on, turning off the TV send a hard power off to the sound bar. That's why when the TV is turned back on the sound bar doesn't turn on. Allowing the sound bar to time out (20min with no signal) sends it into standby mode, not a hard power off. To use the sound bar in this manner, Anynet must be on for both the TV and the sound bar (there's a button on the remote), Auto Turn Off is off, and Receiver is on.

Now for the optical. The TV power off can shut off the the sound bar and turn it back on. To do this, on the sound bar, turn off Anynet (TV can be left as is) and turn on the 'Auto Power Link' on as well. Now when the TV is turned off the sound bar is as well and as soon as there's a signal (light source) the sound bar comes on.

You can also connect both HDMI and Optical and switch between them by turning the Anynet on/off on the sound bar.

Review: This has Dolby Digital and DTS support. If you're looking the shake the house you want a full theatre system 5.1 and above with the full receiver, processing, etc. and shouldn't be shopping for a sound bar. If you want great sound (much than TV) in a small footprint, this is for you. The HW-E450 supports HDMI, Optical, Bluetooth, and 3.5mm so any device you have can be connected. It has volume leveling and sound modes but the box doesn't say it. The sound modes are similar to what's on the TV but there's a couple extra ones. The subwoofer is also set to 0 by default so if you don't hear base, turn it up. It does have sound setting for night and has 3D surround which has both a high and low.

I had an old Logitech 5.1 (no Dolby, or anything) PC speaker system I attached with 3.5 to RCA to an adapter I found here on Amazon. I ran a few tests and although the 5.1 was somewhat louder it wasn't as clean. I wasn't really in the market, but saw a great deal and thought I'd give it a try. The sound bar was crisp, clean and with toying with some of the setting got some serious room shaking sound. I was very impressed with this sound bar and am sold on it. I tested using the Bluetooth and the 3.5mm connection and they worked great with my iPhone. I connected the iPod via 3.5mm and it worked fine as well (don't know why some had issues).

There is an issue of mounting if you don't want to put it on the wall. There are 3 bracket/mounts here on Amazon with mixed reviews that allow mounting at top or bottom using the wall mount kit included with the sound bar. There was another type I saw in a search but it was on one site only and no longer in stock. I saw a mounting kit at the local electronics stores but that's a custom Samsung display mount and can't be found anywhere. I talked with a nice employee and HHGREGG and we managed to get some specs. It's a metal plate about 9" x 6". It's using the 2 lower holes where the stand would have been attached (2 small holes) and has cutouts (similar to wall mount racket) to allow the sound bar to be attached. The plate won't need use of the wall bracket but needs some skilled work to make it properly (cut out). I could machine it if I had the tools but alas, I do not. The employee mentioned something else that got me brainstorming though. The local hardware stores sells shelf track (I think hobby shops have something similar) which is a long piece of metal with holes in it. You can grab that, measure out a length to allow 2" space below the TV, cut and paint black. You can attach that to the TV and the wall mount bracket using some small nuts and bolts. Good luck and let me know if you manage to get something nice worked out.

title: Tried both Sizes - Larger is better
text:
Apparently Amazon's review system is broken. While it shows you should review the other item it will only allow one review. So I'm updating this review to reflect both.

Smaller-
The backspace positioning on this keyboard is much better (even though out of place) due to the size of the keys on the compact keyboard. I really did like the feel and after some getting used to, it was actually not too bad.

The issue for me was going back and forth from any normal (full size) keyboard causes and adjustment period. Muscle memory usually wins so it takes a several sentences to clear things up and get comfortable.

Also the number keys are small to typing numbers feels a bit weird (I know it's a compact keyboard) and with the 4 shortcuts on each key (normal=#, shift + number=symbol, function=function keys, shift+function=shortcut) makes it too busy to work with quickly.

I ultimately settled with their full size keyboard.

Larger-
After a lot of testing, I ultimately settled on this. We will have to see how long it lasts or if there are any issues but here's what I think so far.

Some of the other keyboards (janvoo, iclever, etc.) have the backspace in the correct position but it is so small compared to the backslash that it makes things harder. Also, the smaller version of this, while correcting the backspace position was a little busy on the small number keys and not as easy to transition from a regular full size keyboard.

While the keys on the outside may be smaller, the actually letter and number keys are spaced the same as a normal full size keyboard. This makes transitioning a lot easier. While it's a bit bigger, when folded, it's still not that bad.

As a full keyboard the keys are in the correct position and you have your own normal size number keys. The function keys are smaller setting the shortcuts as default and F1-12 as used with the function key.

Pairing was easy although no model number is listed so making the distinction between this and it's smaller friend a little hard to figure. It's still better than "keyboard" or "bluetooth keyboard" (I like to know what's plugged in). It does have it's sleep mode (I didn't time how long before sleep) but while typing I didn't have issues turning away for a minute and coming back. For longer periods, a couple taps on any key woke the keyboard up and I was back at typing.

title: Seems good, time will tell
text:
Typically use other brands but they weren’t available for the a7 lite so went with this. Now for the bad and the good.

The first try was a no go. The stickers didn’t adhere and the protector came off that while removing the film to stick. That was a pain. Got a replacement set and adjusted my approach (see below) and it went good with no bubbles or issues (left it alone for several hours). Only time will tell if the adhesive stays and if it doesn’t peel.

I did not use their cleaner, dust strips, etc. (read reviews about particles and other brands are the same) and put on some no powder nitrile gloves). I used some eye glass cleaner, then my own cleaning cloth (doesn’t leave fibers). With the screen crystal clean, I set the tablet on a box so the edge would slightly hang over (elevated for the sticky tape). Next positioned the screen protector to the proper alignment and carefully (not move) placed all three tape strips (top, middle, bottom) on the protector first (pressed down to stick), then rolled it over the edge and under the tablet. Now I had to reposition the tablet so that flipping the screen protector was level with the tablet (used a thicker mouse pad). Confirmed placement again and ensured tape was secure. Flipped the protector onto the mousepad and carefully pealed off the film. Then flipped it over without pressure. title: Love my Wind!
text:
I researched Netbooks for a few weeks (read until my eyes burned!) before making a decision on one. What I wanted was something inexpensive, super portable and simple to use, especially when traveling.

One of the reasons I chose this model is because the RAM can be upgraded, which I did (took 5 mins). Adding 1GB of RAM cost me $15 (from a local store). I searched YouTube and followed along with a simple, informative video. You will need to puncture a sticker over one of the screws to remove the back cover which states your warranty will be void, but MSI says they will still honor the warranty as long as you don't modify anything else inside.

The boot up is so quick compared to my desktop. I also cleaned out some of the unnecessary programs from the start-up to make it boot up and run even faster. With the extra RAM, I'm running Norton Internet Security just fine. I prefer Windows XP, so I wont be installing Vista any time soon. If you want to upgrade to Vista, you'll NEED to upgrade the RAM first in order to run it. I don't care for IE so I installed Firefox, no problems. A trial version of Office 2007 comes preloaded, but I downloaded Open Office (free office suite) to use instead and that's also working fine.

Yeah, the speakers stink. I knew that before purchasing it though. My headphones work and sound fine with it. Make sure you visit the MSI website and update your drivers. I've read many times that they're needed especially for the touchpad, wireless and Bluetooth functions.

My battery is lasting 4-5 hours with regular use, there is an Eco setting to get more life out of your battery (Fn F10 while unplugged, power LED turns green). Don't forget, Fn-F11 to turn ON the wireless, which is not automatically on when you first take it out of the box. However, thereafter it does stay on unless you turn it back off OR remove the battery pack. Pressing Fn-F11 again engages the Bluetooth. There are 4 options here, keep pressing the Fn-F11 keys until you get the combination of wireless and Bluetooth that you want, as indicated by the LEDs. I pick up an 'excellent' signal from my router all over the house and outside. I just recently traveled with it for the first time and was able to pick up other wireless signals as well as public WiFi with no problems.

I purchased a small (Rocketfish - Best Buy product) laser mouse with a nano USB adapter for what I thought was a decent price... Love It! The USB adapter is nice and small, sticks out the side of the unit only 1/4" as opposed to the other ones that stick out probably 1.5" - 2". However, when I downloaded the Synaptics touchpad driver, I was unable to utilize the advanced functions of the touchpad. I read in the FAQs on the Synaptics website that if a secondary mouse is installed, the advanced functions on the touchpad would be disabled. Their resolution was to uninstall the secondary device. Well, I like my wireless mouse, so I'll forgo the extra functions (left side corner options) on the touchpad. Right side corner-tap functions works fine though, for engaging the scroll feature. Maybe there is a way to make the touchpad work to it's full ability along with my wireless mouse installed, but I was not able to figure that out.

I really like the matte screen, great color and clarity with no glare! The screen is wide enough to display the full width of a web page, but shorter than a standard monitors view. Another reason I chose this model was for the keyboard. It's larger than other brands and I'm able to type on it just fine. The smaller size period and comma haven't been much of an issue so far. The touchpad IS super sensitive but can be turned off (Fn-F3) when you are doing a lot of typing or while using a mouse. Yet another reason I chose this one was because it's white. No pesky finger prints, looks nice and clean all the time. And so cute!

I'm always surprised to read when others are shocked to find no CD/DVD drive in these netbooks, and therefore give the unit a lower rating for this reason. Read the specs and know what you are buying! You can purchase an external optical drive if you must have one, but another option is to network your netbook and your desktop, then share the desktop's CD drive with the network. That's what I did, works perfectly and cost me $0. It's not quite as convenient to require the desktop for installing software from a CD, but -- it's free.

I'm extremely pleased with my Wind U100-279. It's exactly what I wanted, very portable and plenty efficient for my needs. I definitely recommend it. My only complaint with MSI and their product in general is the lack of comprehensive, written instruction. Not everyone buying one of these is tech-savvy (myself included). Even the "manual" (pdf format) contained very little information. The good thing is, the information IS out there on the net if you look for it. Otherwise, in regards to functionality, this machine is great!

title: Very Happy with this pc
text:
Best price around at the time and it arrived in 3 business days (direct from Amazon, $439). Included was a wired mouse and a wired keyboard, both very basic with no extra features. Love this smaller sized tower, effortlessly carried it upstairs under one arm, and I'm a gal. Set up was fairly easy, would be nice if Microsoft included some standard information about the operating system (comes with Windows 8.1) considering most times us common folks are getting a newer version than the one being replaced (and this version is very different from the last). If you need help learning Win8, go to the Microsoft website, they have some 'getting started' videos. I had read that you don't HAVE to create a Microsoft account, but figuring out how to use a "local" account wasn't obvious. Must have done it right since I never did create a MS acct. Very minimal junk to uninstall, which was nice! Came pre-loaded with 6mo of McAfee and a trial version of MS Word -- dumped both. Subsequent installations including an internet security program, OpenOffice, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox and Thunderbird all went smoothly. Likewise, no problem installing my wireless printer (it initially recognized the printer and actually printed, but then printing failed and the software had to be manually installed).

Took some time figuring out how to customize and configure the general settings. Not a fan of this OS, but I appreciate that the Metro screen and the standard desktop are both easily accessible. Toggle between them using the MS icon at the bottom left where the Start button used to be, or the Windows key on the keyboard. When you can't figure out how to close something, hover your cursor at the top right corner of the screen, the red X will appear. Hovering at the bottom right brings up a menu that includes search and settings. (Wish you could return to Win7? See UPDATE #2 below)

This machine runs VERY quietly, though the optical drive is a bit noisy when installing from disc. A pleasant surprise -- 8 USB ports: 4 [2.0] + 2 [3.0] in the rear and 2 [2.0] in the front. The processor is definitely more snappy than my previous dual-core (and if you're considering the less expensive i3 instead... don't). But do note, Amazon's lists this as 3.2GHz, it's not -- it's actually 2.9GHz (with turbo boost to 3.4?). Apparently the RAM is expandable to 16GB, but as-is, this is a very good processor/RAM combo for the price. I didn't have any luck with the MS Easy Transfer program present on both pc's, couldn't get them to communicate (probably user error, maybe a firewall issue). Therefore, I manually transferred important files (photos, documents, music, etc) via my home network and then used a thumb drive to move stored email items. Overall, I'm extremely pleased with this purchase. Unlike another reviewer, I've experienced absolutely no issues with the WiFi while running several devices on the home network.

UPDATE #1: Using the Dell Backup and Recovery app, I successfully created a bootable backup on a 16GB USB thumb drive, actual space needed was just over 10GB. Then created a utilities and drivers backup on a separate 8GB USB, actual space needed was <1GB (so a 2GB thumb drive would be sufficient). Each process formats/erases current content so you can't use the same thumb drive for both, or at least I wasn't able to figure out how to do so. Regardless, very easy and quick to do, took about 20mins + <1min to complete both.
UPDATE #2: Following the suggestion of fellow reviewer K. O'Meara, I did some reading and decided to download "Start8" from Stardock(.com). Completed the 30-day trial, then purchased for $4.99. It causes your OS to look/run just like the Win7 design (doesn't actually change the OS) with a traditional desktop, Start button and Start Menu. It can be configured to boot up to this desktop instead of the Metro screen (which is still accessible via a button within the start menu or the 'Windows' key on the keyboard). All the familiar items are there within the start menu -- plus you can pin quick launch items to it, or to the task bar, just like Win7. Very cool. No more struggling trying to find stuff, makes Win8 bearable! I have since heard of another program called Classic Shell (classicshell.net) which is said to be similar, but I have not personally tried that one.

title: Great little laptop!
text:
I would give this Dell 2-in-1 (Pentium quad-core version) 4.5 stars if that were an option – it's almost perfect for me. I've been wanting another compact laptop for a while, especially for travel, so the sleek appearance of this is what originally caught my attention. Been using it for several months now and really, really like it. I understand the internal configuration isn't designed for heavy gaming and such. Even though I'm only a casual user, doing mostly basic computing tasks, I still want a laptop that performs well. Here are my thoughts and observations so far:

Several reviews claim this machine is slow, and a few noted that after a short while, performance seemed to improve. This was my experience also. During that first day, I was pretty certain I'd be returning this model. I had cleaned it up of unwanted programs, didn't load it down with new ones, and didn't install a heavy security program. Yet, it didn't behave new and snappy, I was extremely disappointed. However, a day or so later, things seemed to clear up and from then on it's been fine. The likely cause of this is all the Windows and Dell updating the computer goes through when it's fresh out of the box (there were 50+ Windows updates needed on mine, plus driver updates). Therefore, new owners, be patient and don't give up on it too quickly. Run the Windows Update (and restart) a few times before doing anything else. Beyond that, I haven't had any issues with the other recurring complaints: Wi-Fi stays connected (but I am not currently using bluetooth); touchpad works fine after some personal pref adjustments; touch screen responds relatively well to taps and swipes (after calibrating), has pervasive function, and rotates properly in tablet mode; LCD is clear and bright; hard drive seems fine; it's a little warm at the rear but not hot; power cord is recognized and charges quickly (though I did see the dreaded non-Dell warning on the in-store unit I inspected); decent battery life; hinges are sturdy and functional; keyboard and all keys are fine (little bit of flex). Can't comment on the camera, haven't used it.

In addition to all that, here's what I like about this particular laptop:
1) The 2-in-1 feature! Very portable laptop + a large tablet in one unit. Because it's so thin, it folds nicely into tablet mode, albeit heavier/larger than a typical tablet. No question, Android apps selection is better, but leaving my tablet home and having one less thing to carry on a plane is OK by me. No more bulky laptop bag, this easily fits into a mid-size shoulder bag or purse.
2) I have never been disappointed with Dell. Every Dell product I've owned, and there have been many, has out-performed and out-lived all the others.
3) This is a very upgrade-friendly unit, particularly for a novice. I've decided to swap out the HDD for a SSD for these reasons: less chance for disk damage, less heat, more energy efficient (aka battery life), and faster boot/response times. Additionally, the wireless LAN card can be upgraded to dual band (recommended if you plan to use bluetooth) and the RAM can be upgraded from 4 to 8GB (single stick). There are how-to videos available on YouTube depicting these upgrades.
4) This is the first time I've not immediately reached for a wireless mouse. The touch pad works surprisingly well for me and is very customizeable. That, along with the touch screen, makes navigation easy.
5) Many folks dislike Windows 8. While I don't love it, I am adapting, primarily because of the touch screen which makes Win8 a bit more bearable. If this were a standard laptop, I'd probably install one of those programs that cause the OS to look and run like Win7 (such as Classic Shell or Start8). For instruction on how to use Win8, go to the Microsoft website, they have some “getting started” videos that are helpful.
6) Some aren't happy with the placement of the power button (on the side), but I actually quite like it. This allows the pc to function nicely as a desktop / work-station unit (in conjunction with an HDMI compatible monitor, wireless keyboard and mouse). Just turn off the sleep response to a closed lid. This feature is something I've long been looking for in a laptop.
7) It runs VERY quiet (and basically silent with the SSD installed). Even the fan isn't very noisy.

A few things to note: There is no optical drive, you'll need to use an external drive or download your software from the net. An iPearl Mcover hard shell is probably a good idea, this model is said to scratch easily. There are also skins available that can help protect the top cover and palm rest area (esp when in tablet mode). I left the clear adhesive film on the bottom cover for protection of that surface.

A few complaints: That initial sluggish behavior is, understandably, off-putting. Aside from that, my PC runs very smoothly with ONE exception - the 'automatic' Windows updates still bog down the system, no other programs or processes have this effect (this was remedied with the SSD upgrade). Occasionally, my touchpad won't recognize two-finger swipes for page scrolling and I have to use the touch screen instead (which turns out to work better, but still). Wish there was a Fn-key for quicker enabling/disabling of the touchpad. The touch screen is sometimes less responsive in tablet mode compared to the same actions made in laptop mode. Also, the touch screen wont recognize some check-box and dialog-box taps, forces me to use the touchpad and pointer. When in tablet mode, the LCD dims and brightens for no reason (with no obstruction or interference to the sensor). The touch screen is not stylus-friendly at all, add the matte screen protector that I applied and my stylus has been rendered completely useless. New users -- definitely go to the Dell website and update your drivers, particularly for the touchscreen and touchpad.

UPDATE / UPGRADES:
#1 After receiving the Samsung 850 EVO SSD ($100), I cloned my HDD using the included software (via an external optical drive). Many advise the use of better cloning software, but being inexperienced, I opted to adhere to the manufacturers directions for my first time. Everything went fine. Follow the directions provided and consult online instructional videos if needed. But before you begin the upgrade, I suggest that you first create a bootable backup onto a flash drive via the Dell Backup and Recovery app. The Samsung migration software does NOT clone the recovery partition of the HDD for some reason (others consistently report this and my experience was the same). That said -- I can attest to the much improved function and performance of the new SSD over the original HDD. Applications and programs engage quickly, pages load faster. From being completely powered down, start-up takes about 10 seconds to completely up and running, shut-down takes about 5 seconds to lights-off. Also, the amount of heat generated near the rear of the unit feels to be only about half as much as before. Highly recommend this upgrade!
#2 Never had any issue maintaining an internet connection, but speed test results for this laptop were only about half that of my other PC's (a laptop and a desktop, both wireless). So I purchased and installed a dual-band wireless card. The cost was under $30 and it brought the speeds up to par with my other PC's. Another recommended upgrade. Just be sure to buy the proper item: "7260NGW Intel Dual Band Wireless-AC" (802.11ac Wi-Fi + Bluetooth 4.0). Be careful with cheaper options, some don't have bluetooth.
#3 I went several months using the original 4GB of on board RAM before deciding to upgrade. The main reason for doing so is because the Samsung SSD that I installed has a RAPID Mode feature that uses 4GB of RAM all on its own. Also, my word processing program was a little slow to engage and I use it frequently. After installing an 8GB RAM stick ($38), everything is engaging and running even faster.

title: Pleased so far
text:
Original Review 8/20/21 [5 stars]: Took a chance on this "renewed" item. So far, so good. Out of the box it looked brand new. Updated the maps, which only took about 35 mins, and then used it for a trial run in familiar territory around Lake Michigan: MI, IL, WI, out to MN, back through the UP, and then down to where we started -- about 1800 miles. It preformed just fine, even while spending hours on the dash in the hot August sun. The only issue I had was an occasionally stubborn screen within the settings menu. Not sure if that's an issue in general with this model or not. That said, the screen is FAR more responsive when manipulating the map than my previous Garmin (a nuvi 1450 which lasted probably 13 years, so no complaints). The included attachment fit the dash mount I already have. GPS boots up and finds satellite connection quickly. There seems to be more ways to customize this model, I set it to show gas stations, hotels and restaurants. This was really helpful while we traveled rural county highways. It gives a tone and visual warning when a reduced speed zone is ahead (including school zones), I appreciate those. The curved road warnings I can do without, they can be pesky but I suppose may be useful after dark on a rural road. My old unit gave a visual indication of how many lanes split off on the interstate, this one gives verbal instruction, like "be in any of the 3 right lanes". I like that change. But if audible sounds become bothersome, there's a shortcut tools icon on the map (which can be customized) where muting the narrative or other other adjustments can be done easily. Didn't do anything to set up the traffic feature (thought I read that it needs to be enabled?), just worked automatically. It warned of construction, accidents, and other delays, including how much time to expect the delay to be. There were a few warnings of construction delays that didn't exist so I'm glad we didn't reroute on those. Overall, we found the maps to be accurate and the unit to be helpful while traveling. That's the goal. I considered other, less-expensive models, but am very glad I stuck with Garmin. It's a quality, reputable product. Amazon offers a 90 day return policy on this renewed item, that makes it worth trying IMO.
Review Update 3/12/22: Months later, and beyond the return window, my GPS is starting to have some issues. Others have complained about the short battery life, true. But worse, mine goes dead within a week of not being used. Previous model could sit for months on a shelf between uses and still have some charge left. This is very annoying when needed for a spontaneous jaunt -or- when I want to program it at home before a trip. Need to charge it first, which takes HOURS. Also, the screen has become considerably more temperamental. No longer responsive to light touches, now I have to basically smash it. Again, don't know if these issues are typical for this model or because its a "renewed" unit. I'm bummed. Down to 3 stars as it does technically work as a GPS very well.

title: First unit was a dud, replacement is perfect
text:
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
A great 2.4ghz router... not so much at 5ghz though.

I could say this is a one-star review, but "half the router" does indeed work great. So Ill give it 2 stars, which means "I dont like it" on the Amazon review scale.

So basically it looks like I got a dud. The wired and wireless G connections are strong. Any 5ghz connection (N and AC) isn't dependable at all. In fact, the rare moments where the 5ghz band isnt instantly dropping out, I cant even get my N devices to connect to the 5ghz band.

The included picture is what I had running, with the neighbors networks blocked out. The red being my G network, and the blue and yellow the N/AC.

Im disappointed. This really looked like it was going to be a winner based off other reviews.

UPDATE 7-12-15:
Ive been in contact with Netgear support even before this review was posted.

To their credit, the Netgear customer support was quick to reply and offer solutions. Of course some of the solutions really didn't have anything to do with the problem, but there is nothing new about that. Every company's customer support tends has their "checklist" to go through to narrow down the issues.

After trying out a few of the applicable suggestions offered by support, it ultimately confirmed my unit was defective.

I received my replacement router today, and it is working perfectly out of the box.

title: Dont believe the hype
text:
This antenna was used in an attic install. I am well within the 35 radius to the Milwaukee-area transmission towers. There aren't any tall trees or building blocking me, and the section of attic I installed at didn't have any shingling or anything other than wood and siding blocking it.

I bought this antenna expecting it to perform better than an old pronged-aerial (approximately 3 feet long, and 1 foor wide) my Dad had given me when I mentioned I wanted to cut the cord. Who knows how old that aerial was, he had found it hidden in his basement.
It didn't perform better than that old-as-dirt aerial, it performed the same... maybe even a bit worse in all honesty.
I then as a test I put a powered generic "leaf" style antenna in the attic, and that worked better than both passive antennas.

So what did I learn today? If you are installing in an attic, you likely will need some sort of powered antenna or add-on preamp, unless you are ridiculously close to the transmitting towers. Passive just wont cut it.
If you do still feel a passive antenna is good enough, you can get something cheaper that works the same as this. This one doesn't live up to the hype. It was no better than whats been on the market for generations. It IS less of an eyesore, but you don't need a "prettier" antenna if its going into the attic, especially when the performance isn't improved upon.

Regarding the antenna itself:
I bought mine at the big-box blue & yellow electronics store on Black Friday for substantially less than offered here on amazon. Theirs also comes with the add-on VHF antenna and mounting pole. At the time, it was a significantly better buy than what was offered here.
It assembles fairly easily, and it does look "prettier" than the old-style pronged antennas (which doesn't matter if you are stuffing it in an attic.) Being pretty only gets you so far in life though, you gotta perform at some point too!
Its light and easy to install.

So my review is 2 stars. It DID work, but it was no better than much cheaper antennas you can get anywhere. For the money, it isn't worth it if you are looking to do an attic install. Don't believe the hype.

title: Above Average All Around Headset
text:
I have several stereo bluetooth headsets that I use for different activities - but the pair I use the most often are my Motorokr S9's. Here are my thoughts on the product:

Pros:

+ They fit my head pretty well and I can get them on/off with one hand
+ The play/stop volume controls work with all of the iP* devices I have tried (iPhone 3GS, 4, iPad, iPod Touch)
+ Zero issues pairing with all devices I've tried [ including iPhone 4 ]
+ The buttons are easy to find and use
+ The unit has been durable for me, I've had mine for a few years without any functional hiccups
+ They use a standard mini-USB jack to charge, so losing the original charger isn't a huge issue (laptop charges work well)

Cons:

- The blinking light at the back that shows it is connected is unnecessary and a distraction at night
- The USB port cover broke off a few years ago - still functions fine though
- While they are great for walking around/sitting, you can't lay down with these headphones
- If anyone is working a microwave within 50ft you may as well turn them off
- They aren't 100% stationary on my head while running [probably varies head-to-head]

Overall I'm pleased with the headset. I've run into strangers on the street that have told me their pair broke and Motorola sent them a newer version, but mine have been just fine. The only real issue is not being able to use them when resting. I know that headsets are incredibly subjective [ sound quality, ear fit ], but I would buy these again and recommend them to others.

Unmodified, I found two magnification levels that resolved well when I put the light ring directly on the slide: appx 56x and appx 140x - I DON'T understand why there are 2 such levels that resolve. I suspect that I could cut the ring off and lose some lighting concentration but gain magnification range.

I haven't really applied it to my primary purpose yet - my intent is to non-rigorously count bacteria - it will work fine for a low cost, I need at least 50x and more mag is nice. EDIT well I probably need 400x! We'll see, I'll update.

Comfortable (if you can tolerate in-ear buds) but this is not the noise-cancelling I am looking for. In a quiet environment, these sound fine. At least they were cheap. I guess I'll keep them.

I suspect but do not know, that CVC 6.0 is a specification/implementation for noise reduction in the mouth-microphone only. I can NOT detect ANY active-noise-reduction/noise-cancelling in the ambient sound level. I do hear the passive noise reduction and it is not enough for my noisy office or Metrorail-train-trip. Another clue is that there are NO instructions or button to turn ANC on or off.

When used with phone-Waze-GPS, the brief voice navigation directions fade-in so you miss the beginning of the instruction. This is a minor issue, but does not occur with my other bluetooth headsets.

They're regular in-ear headphones.

Remote control of audio source seems limited - shortpress to volume-control, , pause and play. Longpress to skip-forward, skip-back. I did not find that it can skip-tracks. I did not find a way to simulate google-home/assistant-button. I'm not sure about call functions but they use the pause/play buttons.
